label: Pitfall: universal-negative claim vs mutual exclusivity direction
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is a universal negative ('somatic CALR mutations are not present in ANY MPN patient with nonmutated JAK2'), and analysts confuse it with the textbook statement that CALR and JAK2 mutations are mutually exclusive, which is the opposite conditional (CALR absent in JAK2-MUTATED patients). CHECK: build a patient-level 2x2 table of JAK2-mutated (yes/no) by somatic-CALR-mutated (yes/no) and read the JAK2-nonmutated row specifically; count how many JAK2-nonmutated patients carry a somatic CALR variant. IF FOUND: even one credible somatic CALR mutation in a JAK2-nonmutated patient contradicts the claim, zero among a reasonable number of profiled JAK2-nonmutated patients supports it; no statistical test of association is needed and an enrichment p-value does not answer the question. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7000472/ and https://www.hemonc.theclinics.com/article/S0889-8588(20)30153-2/fulltext

label: Pitfall: absent MAF row is not the same as profiled wild-type
text: PITFALL: In a cBioPortal-style MAF (data_mutations.txt) a sample with no row for a gene is either wild-type or simply not profiled; samples with zero called mutations are absent from the MAF entirely, so 'JAK2 nonmutated' cannot be defined from the MAF alone without knowing which samples were sequenced. CHECK: compare the set of SAMPLE_IDs in data_clinical_sample.txt with the set of Tumor_Sample_Barcode in data_mutations.txt; check whether every clinical sample has a non-missing TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS and SOMATIC_STATUS (evidence it was sequenced), and whether the MAF looks exome-wide (many genes, silent rows present) rather than a targeted panel. IF FOUND: define the denominator as sequenced samples only; treat a sequenced sample with no JAK2 row as JAK2-nonmutated, and report separately any clinical samples missing from the MAF rather than silently counting them as wild-type for both genes. SOURCE: https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/5000 and https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/

label: Pitfall: defining JAK2-mutated vs nonmutated
text: PITFALL: 'JAK2 mutated' is defined too narrowly (V617F only) or too broadly (any JAK2 row). MPN JAK2 drivers are V617F (exon 14) plus exon 12 indels/missense around codons 537-547, and a MAF can also contain silent, intronic or UTR JAK2 rows that are not mutations in the sense of the claim. CHECK: list every row with Hugo_Symbol JAK2 with its Variant_Classification, HGVSp_Short and Mutation_Status; also read the study's own per-sample annotation column 'JAK2/MPL mutation' in data_mutations.txt (it is a sample-level label repeated on every row of that sample, not a per-variant field) and tabulate its unique values. IF FOUND: classify JAK2 status per patient using nonsynonymous somatic JAK2 rows AND the curated 'JAK2/MPL mutation' column, flag any disagreement between the two, and run the conclusion under both definitions; the answer should be the same under both before you trust it. SOURCE: https://www.hemonc.theclinics.com/article/S0889-8588(20)30153-2/fulltext and https://doi.org/10.1111/bjh.17766

label: Pitfall: finding CALR exon 9 indels in a MAF
text: PITFALL: CALR driver mutations are exon 9 indels (commonly a 52-bp deletion 'type 1' and a 5-bp insertion 'type 2', plus >50 rarer variants) and they are missed when the analyst searches for a specific protein-change string, filters to Variant_Type SNP or Missense_Mutation, or drops indels; the same indel is annotated differently by different pipelines (e.g. L367fs*46 vs L367Tfs*46, K385fs*47 vs K385Nfs*47) and indel positions shift with left/right alignment. CHECK: select rows by Hugo_Symbol == 'CALR' (and as a backstop by Chromosome 19 with Start_Position inside the CALR locus, roughly 13.049-13.055 Mb on GRCh37) with NO filter on Variant_Type or Variant_Classification, then inspect Variant_Classification, Variant_Type, HGVSc/HGVSp, 'DNA Change' and 'Protein Change' columns for each. IF FOUND: count CALR by gene and by frameshift/indel class, not by exact string match; keep INS and DEL rows in every filter. SOURCE: https://www.ensembl.info/2020/05/26/normalising-variants-to-standardise-ensembl-vep-output/ and https://doi.org/10.1111/ijlh.13282

label: Pitfall: somatic vs germline and frameshift vs in-frame CALR
text: PITFALL: The claim is about SOMATIC CALR mutations, but a MAF can hold germline or unvalidated calls, and non-frameshift CALR variants (in-frame exon 9 indels, missense, silent) are usually germline polymorphisms or non-drivers; only +1 frameshift exon 9 indels are established pathogenic MPN mutations. CHECK: for each CALR row look at Mutation_Status, Validation_Status, the clinical SOMATIC_STATUS (Matched vs unmatched), and the study-specific columns 'Germline reads' and 'Germline allele percentage (%)' versus 'Tumor reads' and 'Tumor allele burden (%)'; confirm the variant is absent or near-zero in the matched germline and is a frameshift in exon 9. IF FOUND: count as somatic CALR only variants with tumour support and no germline support; report in-frame/missense/silent CALR rows separately and state whether the conclusion changes if they are included. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8038093/ and https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/bjh.14512

label: Pitfall: long CALR indels are under-called in exome data
text: PITFALL: Short-read exome pipelines have poor sensitivity for long indels: reads carrying a 52-bp CALR deletion are often soft-clipped or mismapped, so a CALR-negative exome is weaker evidence than a CALR-positive one, and 'no CALR rows in JAK2-nonmutated patients' can be a false negative of the caller rather than true absence. CHECK: see whether the MAF contains any indel longer than ~20 bp at all (compare lengths of Reference_Allele/Tumor_Seq_Allele2 for DEL/INS rows) and whether CALR indels appear with a Validation_Method or manual-curation flag; note how many JAK2-nonmutated patients have no CALR, JAK2 or MPL row. IF FOUND: positive CALR calls can be taken at face value (false positives for a validated 52-bp deletion are unlikely), but absence should be reported as 'not detected' with this caveat; do not convert absence of long-indel calls into strong support for a universal negative. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9808503/ and https://jcp.bmj.com/content/71/5/473

label: Pitfall: low-burden JAK2 V617F missed by exome sequencing
text: PITFALL: Exome sequencing at ordinary depth cannot detect low-burden JAK2 V617F (NGS detection limits are roughly 2-5% VAF versus 0.01-1% for allele-specific PCR), so a patient labelled JAK2-nonmutated from the MAF may carry a small JAK2 clone; reported CALR+JAK2 double-positive cases typically have low-burden JAK2 V617F. CHECK: look at the distribution of 'Tumor allele burden (%)' / t_alt_count for JAK2 rows to see the lowest burden the study reports, and compare MAF-derived JAK2 status with the curated 'JAK2/MPL mutation' sample label, which may reflect a more sensitive clinical assay. IF FOUND: prefer the curated label where it disagrees with the MAF rows, and state that 'nonmutated JAK2' means 'not detected at this assay's sensitivity'; this affects which patients fall into the JAK2-nonmutated group but not the logic of the test. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.15761/hmo.1000191 and https://doi.org/10.1111/bjh.17766

label: Pitfall: unit of analysis is the patient, not the MAF row
text: PITFALL: The claim is about patients, but MAF rows are per variant per sample; a patient can have several samples, one variant can appear as duplicate rows, and the sample-level 'JAK2/MPL mutation' label is repeated on every row, so row counts or sample counts overstate or misassign status. CHECK: test whether PATIENT_ID and SAMPLE_ID are one-to-one in data_clinical_sample.txt; collapse the MAF to one record per patient with boolean flags (has somatic nonsynonymous JAK2, has somatic CALR frameshift indel, has MPL) before cross-tabulating; check Tumor_Sample_Barcode values all map to a clinical SAMPLE_ID. IF FOUND: a patient is JAK2-mutated if ANY of their samples has a JAK2 mutation and CALR-mutated if ANY sample has a somatic CALR mutation; report counts of patients, not rows. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/

label: Pitfall: when 'Not verifiable' is and is not justified
text: PITFALL: Analysts choose 'Not verifiable' because there is no clinical column for JAK2 or CALR status, or choose a label from prior belief about MPN biology instead of from the tables. The mutation table itself is the relevant variable: gene-level rows for JAK2 and CALR plus the sample list are sufficient to test a presence/absence claim. Also the claim conditions only on JAK2, not on MPL, so MPL-mutated patients belong in the JAK2-nonmutated group unless they also have JAK2. CHECK: confirm that Hugo_Symbol contains both JAK2 and CALR and that the cohort is MPN (CANCER_TYPE / ONCOTREE_CODE in data_clinical_sample.txt); count JAK2-nonmutated profiled patients so the reader sees the denominator. IF FOUND: 'Not verifiable' is appropriate only if CALR was not assayed or cannot appear in the data at all (e.g. the MAF had no indels or no CALR coverage and no JAK2-nonmutated patients exist); otherwise decide True or False from the patient-level cross-tabulation. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/ and https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/12323

label: Tiny mutant group: asymptotic log-rank unreliable
text: PITFALL: In a small cohort (the clinical tables here have under 80 patients) a rarely mutated gene gives a mutant group of only a handful of patients, and the asymptotic chi-square log-rank p-value does not keep its nominal size when group sizes are very unequal or events are few (type I error can be inflated or the test can be badly anti-conservative/conservative). CHECK: Tabulate n patients and n deaths in the BRCA2-mutant and wild-type groups among patients with usable survival data; flag if the mutant group has fewer than about 10 patients or about 5 events. IF FOUND: Do not rely on the default log-rank p alone; compute a permutation/exact log-rank p-value (permute the mutant label many times, or enumerate all assignments if the group is tiny) and report both, with group sizes and event counts; treat any p near 0.05 as fragile. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1111/j.0006-341x.2003.00132.x ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2950789/ ; https://jsr.isrt.ac.bd/wp-content/uploads/53n2_1.pdf

label: Monotone likelihood in Cox with rare mutation: use Firth
text: PITFALL: With a very small or event-sparse mutant group a standard Cox model can hit monotone likelihood (hazard ratio diverging to 0 or infinity, huge standard errors, non-convergence warnings), and Wald confidence intervals and p-values are then meaningless. CHECK: Look for convergence warnings, |log HR| larger than about 5, or a group in which all or none of the patients died or whose deaths all precede/follow every death in the other group. IF FOUND: Use Firth-penalized Cox regression (R coxphf, or a penalized fit in Python) with profile-likelihood confidence intervals, or report the exact/permutation log-rank test plus Kaplan-Meier estimates instead of an unpenalized HR. SOURCE: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.0006-341X.2001.00114.x ; https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/coxphf/coxphf.pdf

label: Define BRCA2-mutant by protein-altering variants, not any MAF row
text: PITFALL: Counting every MAF row for the gene as a 'mutation' misclassifies patients, because a study MAF can contain silent and non-coding calls (Silent, Intron, 3'UTR, 5'UTR, 3'Flank, 5'Flank, IGR, RNA) that cBioPortal-style analyses exclude when defining a gene as altered. CHECK: Filter data_mutations.txt to Hugo_Symbol == BRCA2 and tabulate Variant_Classification (and Consequence/IMPACT) per Tumor_Sample_Barcode; also check that one patient with several BRCA2 rows is counted once. IF FOUND: Define the mutant group as patients with at least one protein-altering BRCA2 variant (Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift_Ins/Del, In_Frame_Ins/Del, Splice_Site, Translation_Start_Site, Nonstop) as the primary analysis, and state how many patients change group if silent/non-coding calls are included. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/ ; https://groups.google.com/g/cbioportal/c/tqVhYFqWvwo

label: Wild-type denominator: only sequenced patients; 78 patients vs 77 samples
text: PITFALL: The wild-type group is silently mis-built when the three tables are joined carelessly: a patient absent from the MAF is wild-type only if their tumour was actually sequenced, and patient-level survival must be linked to sample-level mutations through the sample table. Here the patient table has one more data row (78) than the sample table (77), so at least one patient appears to have no sequenced sample. CHECK: Compare the sets of PATIENT_ID in data_clinical_patient.txt, PATIENT_ID/SAMPLE_ID in data_clinical_sample.txt and Tumor_Sample_Barcode in data_mutations.txt; list IDs present in one and missing in another, and check for multiple samples per patient. IF FOUND: Restrict the analysis to patients with a sequenced sample (in the sample table / with mutation calls); do not label un-sequenced patients as BRCA2 wild-type; collapse to one record per patient; report the final N. SOURCE: https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/blob/master/docs/File-Formats.md ; https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/

label: Parse OS_STATUS correctly; blank OS_MONTHS must be excluded, not zero
text: PITFALL: Survival fields are mis-parsed or missing values are mishandled: OS_STATUS is a string such as '0:LIVING' / '1:DECEASED' (event = 1 only for DECEASED), and some patients have a blank OS_MONTHS (the first data row of the patient table is LIVING with no OS_MONTHS); treating blanks as 0 months, as events, or comparing raw OS_MONTHS means/medians with a t-test or Mann-Whitney ignores censoring and biases the comparison. CHECK: Count patients with missing OS_MONTHS or OS_STATUS overall and within the BRCA2-mutant group; confirm the event indicator sums to the number of DECEASED rows; check for zero or negative times. IF FOUND: Drop patients lacking time or status from the survival analysis (state how many, and whether any were BRCA2-mutant), use censoring-aware methods only (Kaplan-Meier, log-rank, Cox), and report how many mutant patients remain evaluable. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6110618/

label: BRCA2 mutation confounded by hypermutation / MSI / TMB
text: PITFALL: BRCA2 mutation status is confounded by hypermutation / mismatch-repair deficiency: BRCA2 is a long gene with coding mononucleotide tracts, so in MSI-high or high-TMB gastrointestinal tumours BRCA2 mutations (often frameshifts) are frequently passenger events, and MSI-high / high-TMB gastric cancers tend to have different (usually better) prognosis; a naive mutant-vs-wild-type comparison may then reflect TMB/MSI rather than BRCA2, and can even point in the opposite direction to the hypothesis. CHECK: Compare TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS and DNA_REPAIR_STATUS (and per-sample mutation counts from the MAF) between BRCA2-mutant and wild-type patients; see whether mutant patients are concentrated among the hypermutated/repair-deficient tumours. IF FOUND: Report the unadjusted result as primary but add a sensitivity analysis stratified by or adjusted for DNA repair status / TMB (or restricted to non-hypermutated tumours), and say explicitly whether the direction of the effect survives. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12088398/ ; https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/PO.21.00531 ; https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2156-7-3 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7805270/

label: Adjust for stage sparingly: events-per-variable limit
text: PITFALL: Prognostic-marker comparisons are confounded by standard prognostic factors (stage, age), but in a small cohort over-adjusting is as harmful as not adjusting: a Cox model with more than about one covariate per 10 deaths gives unstable, biased coefficients. CHECK: Cross-tabulate BRCA2 status against STAGE, CLIN_M_STAGE, AGE and SUBTYPE; count total deaths to get the events-per-variable budget. IF FOUND: Keep the univariable log-rank/Cox as the primary test, and add at most one or two pre-chosen covariates (e.g. stage) or a stratified log-rank as a sensitivity analysis; do not build a many-covariate model and do not let a covariate-selected model replace the primary result. SOURCE: https://journals.plos.org/plosmedicine/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pmed.1001216 ; https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5969114/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4122484/

label: Check direction AND significance; low power is not 'Not verifiable'
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is directional and asks for significance ('significantly shorter survival'), so two separate things must both hold: the mutant group must do worse (HR > 1, lower Kaplan-Meier curve / shorter median) and the difference must be statistically significant; a two-sided p < 0.05 with mutant patients living longer contradicts the claim, and a non-significant p in a small cohort is weak evidence, not proof of no effect. CHECK: Report the direction (HR with 95% CI, medians, which curve is lower), the two-sided p-value, and the number of deaths in each group (power depends on events, not patients). IF FOUND (non-significant or wrong direction): Say plainly that the data do not show significantly shorter survival and give the CI so the reader sees how wide it is; note that the task reserves 'Not verifiable' for data lacking the relevant variables, not for an underpowered comparison whose variables are present. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9365504/ ; https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.d3340

label: Crossing curves / unreliable tails: check PH, use RMST as sensitivity
text: PITFALL: The log-rank test and a single Cox hazard ratio assume roughly proportional hazards; if the Kaplan-Meier curves cross or separate only late, the log-rank test loses power and one HR misdescribes the data. Curve tails and medians based on one or two patients at risk are also unreliable (median may be 'not reached' or have an unbounded CI in the small group). CHECK: Plot both Kaplan-Meier curves with numbers at risk, look for crossing, and run a Schoenfeld-residual test where there are enough events; note whether the mutant-group median is estimable. IF FOUND: Add a sensitivity analysis that does not need proportional hazards (restricted mean survival time difference up to a time where both groups still have patients at risk, or a weighted/Wilcoxon-type test) and describe the result as depending on time; do not base the conclusion on raw medians alone. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3287712/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8802494/ ; https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9081686/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3932959/

label: Pre-specify the BRCA2-mutant definition; avoid forking paths
text: PITFALL: With a handful of mutant patients the result can be flipped by analyst choices (which BRCA2 variants count: all protein-altering vs truncating-only vs excluding missense variants of uncertain significance; which patients are kept; which test), and trying several until one is significant inflates false positives. Most BRCA2 missense variants are of uncertain significance and monoallelic somatic hits may not inactivate the gene, but the hypothesis as worded says only 'BRCA2 mutations'. CHECK: Before looking at survival, fix the primary analysis (any protein-altering BRCA2 mutation vs none, overall survival, two-sided log-rank); then run truncating-only and other definitions as labelled sensitivity analyses and see whether the conclusion changes. IF FOUND (conclusion depends on the definition): Base the label on the pre-specified primary analysis that matches the hypothesis wording, and report the sensitivity results and their disagreement rather than picking the significant variant. SOURCE: https://journals.plos.org/plosmedicine/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pmed.1001216 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6752316/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8161351/

label: TMB panel-vs-WES: first confirm a WES measurement exists
text: PITFALL: A panel-vs-WES TMB comparison needs two independent measurements on the same tumours, and a panel-only study export may contain no whole-exome measurement at all; every TMB-like column (here the headers show MUTATION_RATE and TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS in data_clinical_sample.txt) may be derived from the same targeted-panel mutation calls. CHECK: tabulate GENE_PANEL in data_clinical_sample.txt and all three columns of data_gene_panel_matrix.txt for any exome/WES/WXS value; tabulate Center, Sequencer and Sequence_Source in data_mutations.txt; count distinct mutated genes per sample and overall (panel data stay within a few hundred panel genes, exome data span thousands of genes); look for any clinical column naming exome/WES or a second sample per patient sequenced on a non-panel platform; recompute mutations-per-Mb from data_mutations.txt and see whether each TMB column is reproduced from panel calls alone. IF FOUND (no WES-derived variable): there is no second measurement to correlate, so the claim cannot be tested by a paired analysis on these tables; do not substitute one panel-derived column for WES, and apply the task's own rule for data that lack the relevant variable. SOURCE: https://jitc.bmj.com/content/8/1/e000147 ; https://groups.google.com/g/cbioportal/c/VIgmkfgPZ5o

label: TMB: same-source columns correlate by construction
text: PITFALL: Two TMB columns computed from the same mutation list (for example a mutation rate per Mb and a nonsynonymous TMB per Mb, or a panel TMB simulated by subsetting calls to panel genes) correlate near 1 by construction; this part-whole or same-source correlation says nothing about agreement between a targeted assay and independently sequenced WES. Published 'in silico' panel-vs-WES comparisons work this way and are known to overstate real-world concordance. CHECK: compute the ratio of the two columns per sample and see whether it is constant within each panel version (a constant ratio means one is a rescaling of the other); check whether both can be regenerated from data_mutations.txt. IF FOUND: treat the two columns as one measurement, not as panel vs WES, and do not report their correlation as evidence for or against the hypothesis. SOURCE: https://jitc.bmj.com/content/8/1/e000147 ; https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pcbi.1008332

label: TMB correlation: long tail and outliers inflate Pearson/R2
text: PITFALL: Pearson r and R-squared between panel TMB and WES TMB are inflated by the long right tail of TMB; a few ultra-high-TMB (hypermutated) tumours can produce a high R-squared that collapses when they are removed (R-squared dropped by more than 0.25 in 16 of 24 cancer types in one TCGA analysis). CHECK: if paired panel and WES values exist, plot them on raw and log scales, report Spearman rho alongside Pearson r, and recompute both after log1p transformation and after dropping the top few TMB values. IF FOUND (correlation driven by outliers): base the conclusion on Spearman rho and the log-scale correlation with bootstrap confidence intervals, and state the sensitivity result. SOURCE: https://jitc.bmj.com/content/7/1/206 ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-021-00626-7

label: TMB: correlation vs agreement, expected panel bias
text: PITFALL: Correlation is not agreement. Cancer-gene panels systematically read differently from WES (panels of cancer genes usually overestimate TMB per Mb because of positive selection and hotspots; in other pipelines panel TMB is consistently lower), so a slope different from 1 or a constant offset is expected even when the two are strongly correlated. A hypothesis worded as 'do not correlate' is about association, not interchangeability. CHECK: if paired values exist, report the correlation coefficient with a confidence interval separately from bias (Bland-Altman mean difference and limits, regression slope and intercept). IF FOUND (bias but strong correlation): do not read the bias as absence of correlation; answer the correlation question with the correlation coefficient and report bias as a separate finding. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10446118/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11256552/ ; https://jitc.bmj.com/content/8/1/e000613

label: TMB: panel sampling noise and range restriction attenuate correlation
text: PITFALL: Panel TMB is noisy because a panel covers only about 1 Mb (3 to 5 percent of the exome): its coefficient of variation falls with the square root of panel size and of TMB level and is about 35 percent at 10 mutations/Mb for 1.1 to 1.4 Mb panels, so correlation with WES is attenuated in low-TMB or range-restricted cohorts and in small paired subsets. A non-significant correlation in a small or narrow-range subset is not evidence of no correlation. CHECK: report n of paired samples, the TMB range, and a confidence interval for the correlation; compare the correlation in the full range with that below about 10 mutations/Mb. IF FOUND (small n or restricted range): describe a weak or non-significant result as inconclusive rather than as support for 'no correlation', and only call the hypothesis supported if the interval excludes any meaningful positive correlation. SOURCE: https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534(19)45993-0/fulltext ; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30238975/ ; https://doi.org/10.1002/uog.122

label: Pitfall: 'high' mutation frequency needs an external benchmark
text: PITFALL: 'High' median exonic mutation frequency is a relative claim with no built-in threshold, so a team may call any non-zero rate 'high', or call the claim 'Not verifiable' because no cut-off column exists. CHECK: compute the cohort median in mutations per Mb and place it on published scales: across 27 tumour types the median varies >1,000-fold, lowest in haematological and paediatric tumours and highest in carcinogen-driven melanoma/lung (overall average about 4.0 nonsilent coding mutations/Mb over ~30 Mb covered; per-tumour prevalence spans ~0.001 to >400/Mb); common adult cancers sit at about 1-10/Mb; paediatric histotype medians are about 0.02-0.8/Mb (0.17/Mb AML and Wilms to 0.79/Mb osteosarcoma in a 1,699-case paediatric pan-cancer set that included neuroblastoma); the clinical 'TMB-high' cut-off is >=10/Mb. IF FOUND: judge the median against these external benchmarks and state which benchmark was used; a per-Mb rate variable plus a benchmark makes the claim testable, so 'Not verifiable' is not the default just because the data carry no 'high/low' flag. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3919509/ ; https://www.nature.com/articles/nature12477 ; https://www.nature.com/articles/nature25795 ; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41568-024-00684-9 ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41571-024-00932-9

label: TMB: MSK-IMPACT panel versions have different denominators
text: PITFALL: MSK-IMPACT has several panel versions with different footprints (341, 410 and 468 genes; one source gives coding denominators of 0.896665, 1.016478 and 1.139322 Mb, others quote about 0.98, 1.06 and 1.22 Mb), so raw mutation counts are not comparable across versions or with exome counts, which are divided by roughly 30 to 38 Mb. Sample IDs ending -IM3, -IM5, -IM6 and the GENE_PANEL column mark the version. CHECK: tabulate GENE_PANEL; confirm that any TMB column is per-Mb and uses a version-specific denominator by dividing each sample's mutation count by its TMB value. IF FOUND (mixed versions or raw counts): compare per-Mb values, not counts, and repeat any correlation within each panel version or with panel version as a stratum. SOURCE: https://github.com/chris-kreitzer/IMPACT_Prostate ; https://aacrjournals.org/cancerdiscovery/article/10/12/1808/2595/Tumor-Mutational-Burden-as-a-Predictive-Biomarker

label: Pitfall: counts vs per-Mb rate and the covered-bases denominator
text: PITFALL: A mutation count per sample is not a mutation frequency; frequency needs a per-megabase denominator, and a nominal exome size (30 or 38 Mb) differs from the bases actually covered well enough to call mutations in each tumour-normal pair. CHECK: in data_clinical_sample.txt use COVERED_BASES; recompute (NUM_NONSILENT_MUTATION + SILENT_MUTATION) / COVERED_BASES * 1e6 per sample and confirm it reproduces TOTAL_PER_MB (first row: 15 mutations / 28.58 Mb = 0.52); look at the spread of COVERED_BASES and whether it differs by PLATFORM. IF FOUND: report the median of per-sample mutations per Mb using each sample's covered bases, not a median raw count and not count/30; if covered bases are missing or implausible for some samples, state the denominator used and show the result is stable under 30 Mb vs covered-bases normalisation. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3919509/ ; https://jitc.bmj.com/content/8/1/e000147 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9347149/

label: Pitfall 1: cohort tumour type may not match the hypothesis (ccRCC vs colorectal/IBD data)
text: PITFALL: Testing a hypothesis about one tumour type (clear cell renal cell carcinoma, ccRCC) on a study whose samples are a different tumour type; the file headers in /biodsa-data show columns such as IBD, INTERVAL_FROM_LAST_COLONOSCOPY_TO_CAC_DX, PRIMARY_SITE='R Colon' and a first row labelled Colorectal Cancer / COAD, which suggests an IBD/colitis-associated colorectal cohort rather than a kidney cohort (the library read headers only and did not tabulate). CHECK: Tabulate CANCER_TYPE, CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED, ONCOTREE_CODE (ccRCC is OncoTree code CCRCC, parent RCC, tissue KIDNEY), PRIMARY_SITE and TISSUE_SEQUENCED in data_clinical_sample.txt and count samples and patients that are kidney/ccRCC. IF FOUND (zero or near-zero ccRCC samples): do not compute an ITH measure on the other tumour type and transfer it to ccRCC, and do not answer from background knowledge of the literature; the label must rest on whether the supplied tables contain the relevant population and variables, per the task's own definition of 'Not verifiable'. SOURCE: https://github.com/cBioPortal/oncotree and https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/blob/master/docs/File-Formats.md

label: TMB: variant-class definition mismatches
text: PITFALL: TMB definitions differ between sources: cBioPortal's TMB (nonsynonymous) counts only nonsynonymous variants (cBioPortal does not store synonymous mutations; for exome studies it is the nonsynonymous count divided by 30 Mb), some assays count synonymous variants too, and a panel MAF can include non-coding calls such as promoter (5'Flank, e.g. TERT), splice-region or intronic variants that an exome-based count would not include. Germline leakage, low tumour purity and VAF thresholds also shift counts. CHECK: tabulate Variant_Classification and Mutation_Status in data_mutations.txt; recompute per-sample counts with and without non-coding classes and compare with the supplied TMB column. IF FOUND (mixed variant classes): use one explicit definition (coding nonsynonymous SNVs plus indels) for every count you compute, and say which definition the supplied column appears to follow. SOURCE: https://groups.google.com/g/cbioportal/c/VIgmkfgPZ5o ; https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/ ; https://www.mdpi.com/1422-0067/23/9/5097

label: Pitfall: TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS is count/30 and excludes silent mutations
text: PITFALL: The cBioPortal-derived column TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS is not the study's exonic mutation frequency: it is the nonsynonymous mutation count divided by a fixed 30 Mb for exomes and excludes silent mutations, so it is systematically lower than a total (silent + nonsilent) rate per covered Mb and the two must not be mixed or compared to benchmarks defined the other way. CHECK: confirm TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS == NUM_NONSILENT_MUTATION / 30 (first row: 13/30 = 0.4333) and compare its median with the median of TOTAL_PER_MB and of TOTAL_PER_MB - SILENT_PER_MB. IF FOUND: take 'exonic mutation frequency' as all coding somatic mutations (silent + nonsilent) per covered Mb (TOTAL_PER_MB) as the primary measure, report the nonsilent-only rate as a sensitivity check, and match the variant classes to whichever benchmark is quoted (clinical TMB cut-offs are usually nonsynonymous; pan-cancer frequency plots usually count all exonic mutations). SOURCE: https://groups.google.com/g/cbioportal/c/VIgmkfgPZ5o ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6350758/ ; https://www.jmdjournal.org/article/S1525-1578(24)00115-6/pdf

label: Pitfall 2: ITH needs multi-sample-per-tumour design; one sample per patient is inter-patient heterogeneity
text: PITFALL: Intratumour heterogeneity (ITH) is a within-tumour property and is only directly measurable with several spatially separate samples of the same tumour (multi-region sequencing) or with per-mutation cancer cell fractions; a table with one sample per patient shows inter-patient heterogeneity, which is not ITH. CHECK: Count samples per PATIENT_ID in data_clinical_sample.txt; for patients with more than one sample, read SAMPLE_TYPE, TISSUE_SEQUENCED and METASTATIC_SITE to see whether they are regions of one primary, primary-versus-metastasis pairs, or time-separated samples; check whether any ITH/clonality column (CCF, clonal/subclonal flag, region ID) exists. IF FOUND (mostly one sample per patient, no clonality columns): a per-tumour 'ITH present yes/no' call cannot be made for those patients and the fraction 'tumours with ITH' must be computed only over tumours with at least two same-tumour samples, reporting that denominator explicitly. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7867630/ and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6837753/

label: TMB: pairing unit and non-independent samples
text: PITFALL: Correlation assumes independent pairs measured on the same unit. A panel-vs-WES comparison is only valid when both values come from the same tumour (ideally the same specimen); patients with several samples (IDs such as -T01, -T02, -T03) give non-independent rows, and pairing a panel value with a WES value from a different specimen or time adds tumour heterogeneity that lowers correlation for reasons unrelated to the assay. CHECK: count samples per PATIENT_ID in data_clinical_sample.txt; if a WES value exists, establish whether it is keyed by patient or by sample and which specimen it came from. IF FOUND (repeated samples or mismatched specimens): keep one pair per patient, state the pairing rule, and treat a lowered correlation as a lower bound on assay concordance. SOURCE: https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5079093/ ; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.annonc.2021.09.016

label: Pitfall: the MAF omits silent mutations and may include non-exonic calls
text: PITFALL: Counting rows of data_mutations.txt per sample under-counts exonic burden, because cBioPortal does not store synonymous mutations (calls are taken as published and only re-annotated), and the MAF may also carry non-exonic classes (intron, UTR, flank, IGR, RNA) for whole-genome samples. CHECK: tabulate Variant_Classification in data_mutations.txt (is 'Silent' present? any non-coding classes?), and compare per-sample MAF row counts with NUM_NONSILENT_MUTATION and with NUM_NONSILENT_MUTATION + SILENT_MUTATION from the sample table. IF FOUND: prefer the study-reported per-sample rates (TOTAL_PER_MB, SILENT_PER_MB) for the exonic frequency and use the MAF only as a cross-check of the nonsilent count; if the MAF is used, restrict to coding classes and say explicitly that silent mutations are absent. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/ ; https://github.com/cbioportal/cbioportal/blob/master/docs/user-guide/faq.md

label: TMB: linear regression of panel on WES is heteroscedastic
text: PITFALL: Mapping panel TMB to WES TMB by ordinary linear regression is biased at low TMB (counts cannot be negative and variance grows with TMB), which produces apparent cancer-type differences in slope and prediction limits that widen with TMB; a regression fitted on pooled data can look good or bad for reasons of distribution shape rather than assay performance. CHECK: if paired values exist, inspect residuals against fitted values for a fan shape and compare results on the raw and square-root or log scale. IF FOUND (heteroscedastic residuals): use rank correlation or a variance-stabilising transform for the association test, and do not rely on raw-scale R-squared or regression p-values alone. SOURCE: https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pcbi.1008332 ; https://jitc.bmj.com/content/8/1/e000147

label: Pitfall 3: under-sampling hides ITH; non-detection is not homogeneity
text: PITFALL: Detected ITH rises with the number of regions sampled and a mutation that looks clonal in one biopsy can be subclonal or absent elsewhere, so failure to see heterogeneity in a tumour with one or two samples (or on a small gene panel) is absence of evidence, not evidence of a homogeneous tumour. CHECK: For every tumour scored 'no ITH', record the number of samples, the number of genes/mutations compared and the sequencing depth; ask whether heterogeneity could have been detected at all. IF FOUND (the 'homogeneous' tumours are the thinly sampled ones): do not count them as counter-examples to a universal claim; treat them as uninformative and say so, rather than labelling the hypothesis False on their account. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6489174/ and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4298374/

label: Pitfall: zero-mutation samples vanish from MAF-based medians
text: PITFALL: Samples with zero called mutations have no rows in a MAF, so a median computed by grouping the MAF by Tumor_Sample_Barcode silently drops them and is biased upward; samples can also be listed in the clinical table but not profiled. CHECK: compare the set of Tumor_Sample_Barcode values in data_mutations.txt with SAMPLE_ID in data_clinical_sample.txt and in data_gene_panel_matrix.txt (clinical has 240 samples, the panel matrix 239); count samples absent from the MAF and samples with missing or zero TOTAL_PER_MB. IF FOUND: build the per-sample table from the list of profiled samples and fill true zeros for profiled samples with no calls; exclude (do not zero-fill) samples that were never profiled; report N used. SOURCE: https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/3067 ; https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/5000 ; https://mskcc-epi-bio.github.io/gnomeR/articles/data-processing-vignette.html

label: Income exposure variable must exist - headers show none
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis exposure is community-level average income, but an association cannot be estimated if no income-type variable exists; the library's header listing of /biodsa-data found the patient table has only PATIENT_ID, AGE_AT_DIAGNOSIS, AGE_AT_PROCUREMENT, RACE, SMOKING, PSA, M_STAGE, VITAL_STATUS, DISEASE_EXTENT and the sample table only PATIENT_ID, SAMPLE_ID, TUMOR_SAMPLE_HISTOLOGY, TISSUE_TYPE, SAMPLE_TYPE, GLEASON_SCORE, ONCOTREE_CODE, CANCER_TYPE, CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED, SAMPLE_CLASS, GENE_PANEL, SOMATIC_STATUS, 8Q_ARM, TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS, and a case-insensitive grep for income|ancestry|zip|census|admixture across all seven files returned nothing. CHECK: Re-list every column (including the # description lines) of both clinical tables and the headers of the mutation, SV, CNA, seg and gene-panel files and confirm for yourself whether any income, zip code, census tract, deprivation index or other socioeconomic field is present. IF FOUND (i.e. if absent): do not run a regression on a stand-in variable and call it a test of income; apply the task's own label definitions for the case where the relevant variable is missing, and say explicitly which variable is missing. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2965888/

label: Pitfall 4: false ITH from technical noise, purity and depth differences between paired samples
text: PITFALL: Apparent 'private' mutations between samples of the same patient are often technical: in a replicate study 34-80% of discordant somatic variants that would be read as ITH were noise, and cancer-only pipelines gave about 69% false-positive somatic calls; low purity or low depth in one sample makes a shared mutation look absent there. CHECK: For each mutation called in sample A but not in sample B of the same patient, compare TUMOR_PURITY and MEDIAN_COVERAGE/SAMPLE_COVERAGE of the two samples and the mutation's t_alt_count and VAF in A; ask whether B had the power to detect it (expected alt reads = depth x VAF_A x purity_B/purity_A). MAF files list only called variants, so absence of a row is not a genotype of zero. IF FOUND (discordance concentrated in low-VAF calls or low-purity/low-depth partners): count as heterogeneous only discordances that the partner sample was powered to detect, and report both the naive and the power-filtered result. SOURCE: https://www.cell.com/cell-reports/fulltext/S2211-1247(18)31635-8 and https://perspectivesinmedicine.cshlp.org/content/8/4/a028316.full

label: Pitfall: platform mix (WGA exome, native exome, WGS) can drive the median
text: PITFALL: The cohort mixes sequencing sources (PLATFORM/DATA_SOURCE values such as Exome_WGA = whole-genome-amplified exome, native exome WXS, and WGS), which differ in sensitivity and artefact rate; whole-genome amplification before exome capture adds amplification-only variants (in one comparison only 74% of variants were seen in both amplified and unamplified DNA and about 11% of WGA calls were not in unamplified DNA), and low coverage or low tumour purity lowers sensitivity for low-allelic-fraction mutations. A pooled median can therefore reflect platform mix rather than biology. CHECK: tabulate samples by PLATFORM (and gene panel matrix WXS/WGS) and compute the median and IQR of TOTAL_PER_MB and of COVERED_BASES within each platform; test for a platform difference (Kruskal-Wallis). IF FOUND: report the pooled median together with per-platform medians and base the conclusion on whether every platform stratum falls on the same side of the benchmark; do not let one platform's inflated or deflated stratum drive the verdict. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3883664/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3833702/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9103036/

label: Race is not a valid proxy for income/SES
text: PITFALL: Using self-reported race (or smoking, PSA, stage) as a proxy for an unmeasured socioeconomic exposure is invalid: race bundles ancestry, culture, discrimination and economic position, socioeconomic indicators correlate only weakly with each other within race groups, and in this hypothesis race is the adjustment covariate, so it cannot simultaneously be the exposure. CHECK: If an analysis plan uses any column other than a real area-level income measure as the 'income' term, flag it; a RACE-vs-8q result answers a different question. IF FOUND: report the race-vs-8q association only as descriptive context, never as support for or contradiction of the income hypothesis. SOURCE: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK215756/ ; https://www.nyc.gov/assets/doh/downloads/pdf/epi/epiresearch-SES-measure.pdf

label: Pitfall 5: mixed gene panels - not profiled is not wild type
text: PITFALL: Samples in one study can be sequenced on different targeted panels (the gene panel matrix here lists IMPACT341, IMPACT410, IMPACT468 and a FoundationOne panel file exists); a gene absent from a sample's panel is 'not profiled', not wild type, so comparing two samples of a patient across panels manufactures private mutations and fake heterogeneity. CHECK: Join data_gene_panel_matrix.txt to the sample table; for each within-patient sample pair check whether the panels are identical, and get each panel's gene list (data_gene_panel_FoundationOne.txt is supplied; IMPACT lists are not, so use the union of genes mutated on that panel as a lower bound or restrict to the smallest panel). IF FOUND (pairs on different panels): restrict the comparison to genes covered by both panels before calling any mutation private; the same applies to data_cna.txt and data_sv.txt. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/ and https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/blob/master/docs/File-Formats.md

label: Pitfall: skewed burden - use median with CI, not mean or outliers
text: PITFALL: Per-sample mutation burden is strongly right-skewed with occasional hypermutated outliers (paediatric pan-cancer work flags hypermutators as >3 s.d. above the histotype mean), so the mean, or a statement that 'some tumours have many mutations', misrepresents the typical tumour; the hypothesis is about the median. CHECK: plot or tabulate the distribution of TOTAL_PER_MB (min, quartiles, max, mean vs median, number of samples above 1/Mb and above 10/Mb). IF FOUND: answer with the median and IQR plus a bootstrap confidence interval for the median, and optionally a one-sample Wilcoxon signed-rank test against the benchmark value; never substitute the mean or the maximum, and do not drop outliers to change the median. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/nature25795 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3919509/

label: Pitfall 1: mutation-frequency denominator (profiled vs in-MAF samples)
text: PITFALL: In cBioPortal-format data the mutation file (data_mutations.txt) lists only samples that have at least one called mutation, so using the samples present in the MAF as the denominator drops mutation-free tumours and inflates (and can differentially distort) per-group mutation frequencies; conversely a sample not profiled for the gene must not be counted as wild-type. CHECK: Build the denominator from data_clinical_sample.txt joined to data_gene_panel_matrix.txt (column 'mutations' not NA); count how many clinical samples are absent from the MAF, and confirm every panel ID in the matrix (e.g. IMPACT341/410/468) covers BRAF exon 15. Join MAF Tumor_Sample_Barcode to SAMPLE_ID; read clinical files by skipping the 4 leading '#' lines rather than assuming none. IF FOUND: Frequency = (unique profiled samples with the variant) / (all profiled samples in that subtype group), with MAF-absent profiled samples counted as wild-type and unprofiled samples excluded. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/ ; https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/ ; https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/5000

label: Pitfall: absolute 'high' vs within-neuroblastoma comparison; no risk column
text: PITFALL: 'High' can be misread as 'higher in high-risk than in lower-risk neuroblastoma'. The clinical tables have no explicit risk-group or stage column (headers show MYCN_AMP, AGE, GRADE, MKI, HYPERDIPLOID only), so an internal high-risk vs low-risk contrast may be impossible, and a team may then wrongly conclude the absolute claim cannot be tested, or build a contrast on proxies that does not answer it. Mutation burden also rises with age at diagnosis, so within-cohort trends do not speak to whether the level is high. CHECK: look for any risk/stage column and for the cohort description in the table headers; tabulate MYCN_AMP and AGE (years) to see whether the cohort is homogeneous; test whether TOTAL_PER_MB varies with AGE and MYCN_AMP. IF FOUND: treat the hypothesis as an absolute statement about the cohort median judged against external mutation-rate benchmarks; use MYCN/age strata only as sensitivity analyses showing the median is on the same side of the benchmark in each stratum. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/nature25795 ; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41568-024-00684-9 ; http://kidsgenomics.org/genomic-landscape-pediatric-cancers/

label: Pitfall 6: unmatched/pooled-normal and Foundation calls leak germline variants
text: PITFALL: Calls made without a patient-matched normal contain germline variants that sit at VAF near 0.5 or 1.0 in every sample of a patient, inflating apparent shared/clonal content and distorting VAF-based ITH scores; the mutation file header here shows rows with Matched_Norm_Sample_Barcode like 's_Normal_Pooled_FROZEN', Mutation_Status 'SOMATIC_VS_POOL', and Foundation rows with Variant_Type UNK and Verification/Validation status 'unknown'/'likely'. CHECK: Tabulate Center, Mutation_Status, Matched_Norm_Sample_Barcode and the SOMATIC_STATUS column of the sample table (Matched vs Unmatched); for unmatched samples look at the VAF histogram for a spike at 0.5 and at n_alt_count and the ExAC/1000G frequency columns. IF FOUND: run the analysis on matched-normal samples separately, or drop variants with population allele frequency above about 0.1-1% and unknown-status Foundation calls, and state that unmatched samples cannot support clonality claims. SOURCE: https://www.cell.com/cell-reports/fulltext/S2211-1247(18)31635-8 and https://www.jmdjournal.org/article/S1525-1578(19)30084-4/fulltext

label: Ancestry adjustment needs germline data not in somatic files
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis requires adjustment for race AND genetic ancestry; quantitative ancestry needs germline ancestry-informative SNP genotypes (matched normal or unfiltered tumor pileups) projected on reference panels, and cannot be recovered from a filtered somatic mutation file, gene-level CNA matrix or seg file, where germline variants have been removed. CHECK: Confirm whether any ancestry-fraction column exists (header listing found only a self-reported RACE column, SOMATIC_STATUS suggests matched-normal filtered somatic calls) and inspect RACE for small or Unknown/Other categories. IF FOUND: do not claim an 'ancestry-adjusted' estimate; self-reported race alone is at best partial adjustment and must be described as such, and do not attempt to infer ancestry from somatic calls. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9811156/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11521331/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8246846/

label: Pitfall 2: V600E-specific vs any-BRAF mutation
text: PITFALL: Counting any BRAF mutation as 'BRAF V600E'. In lung adenocarcinoma only roughly 35-50% of BRAF mutations are V600E (class I, the BRAF/MEK-inhibitor-targetable one); the rest are non-V600 class II/III (G469, G466, K601, L597, D594, N581) or VUS, so a gene-level 'BRAF mutated' frequency can give a different ranking of groups than V600E itself. BRAF fusions (data_sv.txt) and amplifications (data_cna.txt) are also not V600E. CHECK: Filter data_mutations.txt to Hugo_Symbol==BRAF and tabulate HGVSp_Short; the primary event is exactly p.V600E (hg19 chr7:140453136 A>T, c.1799T>A). Also inspect any other row at codon 600 (Protein_position 600, e.g. V600K, V600_K601delinsE, dinucleotide calls) and report them separately. Count unique samples, not MAF rows. IF FOUND: Base the verdict on p.V600E-only counts per group; show gene-level BRAF and all-codon-600 counts only as sensitivity analyses and say whether they agree in direction. The absence of a ready-made 'BRAF V600E' clinical column does not make the claim unverifiable, since it is derivable from the MAF. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12568928/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10166262/ ; https://pcm.amegroups.org/article/view/5933/html

label: Pitfall: exonic vs genome-wide rate, germline leakage, duplicates
text: PITFALL: 'Exonic' mutation frequency is the coding-sequence rate; for whole-genome samples a genome-wide rate (all SNVs / ~3,000 Mb) or a covered-bases value that refers to the whole genome is a different quantity, and non-somatic calls (germline leakage in unmatched tumours) inflate burden. Duplicate MAF rows or more than one sample per patient also distort per-sample counts. CHECK: for WGS samples verify COVERED_BASES is on the exome scale (~30 Mb) like the exome samples; confirm SOMATIC_STATUS is 'Matched' for all samples; check Mutation_Status in the MAF; check one sample per PATIENT_ID and de-duplicate MAF rows on sample + chromosome + position + alleles. IF FOUND: restrict to coding calls and exome-scale denominators for WGS samples, exclude or separately report unmatched samples, and summarise one value per patient. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/nature25795 ; https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534(21)04495-1/fulltext ; https://townsend-lab-yale.github.io/cancereffectsizeR/articles/MAF_filtering_tips.html

label: Pitfall 1: silent/intronic rows inflate gene mutation frequency
text: PITFALL: The MAF in this kind of cBioPortal study can contain non-protein-altering rows (the first rows of data_mutations.txt are Variant_Classification=Intron), so counting any row for a gene as 'mutated' inflates per-gene frequency, most of all for genes with long introns/UTRs. CHECK: tabulate Variant_Classification over the whole file and for each gene of interest; recompute the per-sample nonsynonymous count and see whether count/TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS from data_clinical_sample.txt is a constant (it tells you which classes the study itself treated as nonsynonymous). IF FOUND: define 'mutated' as >=1 protein-altering variant (Missense_Mutation, Nonsense_Mutation, Frame_Shift_Del/Ins, In_Frame_Del/Ins, Splice_Site, Nonstop_Mutation, Translation_Start_Site) and drop Silent, Intron, 3'UTR, 5'UTR, 3'Flank, 5'Flank, IGR, RNA, exactly as cBioPortal and maftools do by default; report the all-rows number only as a sensitivity figure. SOURCE: https://groups.google.com/g/cbioportal/c/tqVhYFqWvwo ; https://github.com/PoisonAlien/maftools/issues/103

label: Pitfall 7: VAF is not CCF; correct for purity and copy number before calling subclonal
text: PITFALL: Raw variant allele frequency is not the fraction of cancer cells carrying a mutation; VAF depends on tumour purity, local total copy number and mutation multiplicity (including copy-neutral LOH), so calling low-VAF mutations 'subclonal' without correction mislabels clonal mutations in impure or amplified/deleted regions, and single-sample ITH methods disagree widely with each other. CHECK: If single-sample clonality is attempted, compute CCF = VAF x (purity x CN_tumour + 2 x (1 - purity)) / (purity x multiplicity) using TUMOR_PURITY and segment copy number from data_cna_hg19.seg, with a binomial confidence interval from t_alt_count and t_ref_count; check that pathologist purity is not missing or implausible (compare with the highest clonal-looking VAF). IF FOUND (purity missing, panel-only log-ratio segments without allele-specific copy number, few mutations per sample): treat single-sample subclonality calls as low-confidence, call a mutation subclonal only if the upper CCF bound is clearly below 1 under all plausible multiplicities, and do not rest a universal claim on them. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7867630/ and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5538405/ and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6837753/

label: Arm-level 8q gain: use 8Q_ARM, not MYC amp or ad hoc seg thresholds
text: PITFALL: Arm-level gain is not the same as gene-level amplification, and re-deriving 8q gain from panel seg files is threshold-dependent: there is no consensus definition (ASCETS default is |log2 ratio| 0.2 over at least 70% of the covered arm with a minimum breadth-of-coverage filter; others use 0.1/50% or >90% of arm), and focal MYC amplification in data_cna.txt does not equal 8q arm gain. CHECK: Use the curated 8Q_ARM column in data_clinical_sample.txt as the outcome (tabulate its levels, e.g. Gain/Neutral/Loss and any missing); if you recompute from data_cna_hg19.seg (hg19 8q roughly chr8:45.6Mb-146.4Mb) compare with 8Q_ARM in a confusion table. IF FOUND: prefer the provided arm call as primary outcome, define the binary as Gain vs not-Gain, state how Loss and missing are handled, and treat any seg-derived call as sensitivity analysis only. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8388019/ ; https://github.com/beroukhim-lab/ascets ; https://www.jmdjournal.org/article/S1525-1578(21)00255-5/fulltext

label: Pitfall 3: histologic subtype group definition and stray categories
text: PITFALL: Mis-defining the three histologic groups. Lung adenocarcinomas are grouped by predominant pattern as lepidic (LEP, low grade), acinar/papillary (ACI/PAP, intermediate) and micropapillary/solid (MIP/SOL, high grade); cohorts often also contain tumours outside these groups (invasive mucinous, colloid, other variants, or missing subtype) and silently lumping them into a comparator, or dropping a group through a string mismatch, changes the proportions. CHECK: Tabulate SUBTYPE_GROUP against PREDOMINANT_HISTOLOGIC_SUBTYPE in data_clinical_sample.txt, including NA/blank; strip whitespace before matching (the group label is written like 'Micropapillary/ Solid' with a space after the slash); confirm each predominant subtype maps to exactly one group and note any category outside the three. IF FOUND: Use the provided SUBTYPE_GROUP column for the three groups, exclude (and report the n of) samples that belong to none of them, and do not rebuild groups from scratch unless the column is inconsistent. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4272758/ ; https://www.jto.org/article/S1556-0864(20)30468-8/fulltext

label: Pitfall 2: frequency = distinct mutated samples / all profiled samples
text: PITFALL: Mutation frequency is computed with the wrong unit or denominator: counting mutation rows instead of samples (one tumour with several hits in a gene counted several times), or dividing by the samples that appear in the MAF instead of all sequenced samples, which inflates frequency when some profiled samples have no (qualifying) mutation rows. CHECK: compare the set of Tumor_Sample_Barcode values in data_mutations.txt with SAMPLE_ID in data_clinical_sample.txt; for each gene compute n_distinct_mutated_samples / n_profiled_samples and also list the number of rows per sample per gene. IF FOUND: use distinct mutated samples over all profiled samples from the clinical sample table (the cBioPortal 'Freq' definition), never rows; state numerator and denominator explicitly. SOURCE: https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/5000 ; https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/

label: Pitfall 8: MATH-type scores on panel data are unstable and make 'all tumours' trivially true
text: PITFALL: VAF-dispersion heterogeneity scores such as MATH (100 x MAD/median of VAFs) are sensitive to the mutation caller, purity and copy number, are unstable or undefined with the handful of mutations a gene panel yields (samples with 0-1 mutations get a score of 0 by convention, which is 'undefined', not 'homogeneous'), and are positive for almost any sample, so 'score > 0 in every tumour' makes a universal ITH claim trivially true. CHECK: Count mutations per sample; see how many samples have fewer than about 5-10 mutations; if a continuous score is used, fix the threshold for 'ITH present' before looking and test how the proportion changes across reasonable thresholds. IF FOUND: do not use a continuous score with an arbitrary cut-off to affirm or deny 'ITH in all tumours'; prefer discrete evidence (a mutation or copy-number event confidently present in one same-tumour sample and confidently absent in another). SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-018-29154-7 and https://journals.plos.org/plosmedicine/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pmed.1001786

label: Purity and sample type bias arm-gain calls
text: PITFALL: Log2 ratios shrink toward zero as tumor purity falls (a one-copy gain is log2(1.5)=0.585 only at 100% purity), so arm gains are under-called in low-purity samples; purity differs systematically between primary biopsies and metastatic samples and between tissue sites, giving differential outcome misclassification that can create or hide an association with any patient-level covariate correlated with sample type. CHECK: Cross-tabulate 8Q_ARM by SAMPLE_TYPE, TISSUE_TYPE and GENE_PANEL (IM5 vs IM6 visible in sample IDs) and compare the distribution of 8q seg.mean across those strata. IF FOUND: include sample type (and panel if imbalanced) as covariates or stratify, and do not interpret raw gain frequency differences across groups with different sample-type mix. SOURCE: https://cnvkit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/calling.html ; https://cnvkit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/heterogeneity.html ; https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534(19)31355-9/fulltext

label: Pitfall 4: pooled vs pairwise comparison of three groups
text: PITFALL: The claim 'MIP/SOL lower than LEP and ACI/PAP' is a three-group statement, and testing only MIP/SOL versus the pooled other two groups can hide that one comparator goes in the opposite direction (collapsing categories can reverse or mask a group-specific pattern), while testing only the overall 3x2 table says nothing about direction. CHECK: Report n mutated / n total and percentage for each of the three groups separately; then run (a) MIP/SOL vs LEP, (b) MIP/SOL vs ACI/PAP, and (c) MIP/SOL vs LEP+ACI/PAP pooled, noting direction in each. IF FOUND: Treat the hypothesis as supported in direction only if the MIP/SOL frequency is lower than each comparator group, not just lower than the pooled one; if the pairwise directions disagree, say so explicitly and let the per-group table, not the pooled test, drive the verdict. With three groups, a closed-testing approach (overall test then pairwise) controls error without heavy Bonferroni penalty. SOURCE: https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/00031305.2021.2002188 ; https://people.stat.sc.edu/hansont/stat205/lecture20.pdf

label: Pitfall 3: raw recurrence vs background mutation rate and gene length
text: PITFALL: In high-mutation-burden cancers (UV-driven cutaneous SCC is among the highest) raw recurrence is not evidence of a gene being a real, selected target: long, late-replicating or low-expressed genes (TTN, MUC16, RYR2, CSMD3, olfactory receptors) top the 'most frequently mutated' lists purely from background mutation, so a gene can look 'frequently mutated' by chance. CHECK: rank all genes by fraction of samples with a protein-altering mutation and see where the genes of interest fall relative to known passengers (TTN, MUC16, FLAGS genes) and relative to coding length (mutated-sample fraction per kb of CDS, or nonsynonymous vs synonymous counts within the gene); if possible run a background-aware test (dNdScv, MutSigCV-style, or a simple binomial/Poisson expectation from each sample's burden and gene length). IF FOUND: report both the raw frequency and whether it exceeds what burden and length predict; do not call a gene 'frequently affected' on raw percent alone if passengers of similar length reach the same percent, and say explicitly which definition (raw prevalence vs excess over background) the verdict rests on. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3919509/ ; https://doi.org/10.1186/s12920-014-0064-y ; https://github.com/im3sanger/dndscv/blob/master/vignettes/dNdScv.Rmd

label: Pitfall 9: universal claims - denominators, rule of three, counter-examples
text: PITFALL: A universal claim ('present in all tumours') is not established by n-of-n in a small cohort and is refuted only by a well-supported counter-example; with 0 exceptions in n evaluable tumours the 95% upper bound on the exception rate is about 3/n (rule of three; exact Clopper-Pearson lower bound for the proportion is 0.05^(1/n), e.g. 0.74 for n=10). CHECK: State the number of evaluable tumours (correct tumour type, at least two same-tumour samples, comparable panels), the number with ITH, and the exact binomial interval; for each apparent exception check pitfalls 3-5 before accepting it. IF FOUND (n evaluable is zero): the proportion is undefined and the data do not address the claim; (n small, all positive): report support as limited to the cohort with the interval; (credible exception): that single tumour is what decides against a universal claim, so document its sampling depth. SOURCE: http://www.pmean.com/01/zeroevents.html and https://arxiv.org/html/2109.02516v4

label: Disease stage is mediator/confounder for 8q gain - overadjustment
text: PITFALL: 8q gain frequency in prostate cancer rises steeply with progression (grade, stage, metastatic and castration-resistant disease), and socioeconomic position affects stage at presentation, so disease extent is plausibly a mediator between a socioeconomic exposure and 8q gain; adjusting for DISEASE_EXTENT, M_STAGE, GLEASON_SCORE or SAMPLE_TYPE is overadjustment for the total association, while not adjusting leaves an association that only reflects who presents late. CHECK: Tabulate 8Q_ARM by DISEASE_EXTENT, M_STAGE, SAMPLE_TYPE and Gleason group; fit the model both without and with these clinical variables. IF FOUND: state the adjustment set up front (the hypothesis names only race and ancestry), report the minimally adjusted model as primary and the clinically adjusted model as sensitivity, and never read covariate coefficients from the same model as if each were itself adjusted (Table 2 fallacy). SOURCE: https://aacrjournals.org/clincancerres/article/16/1/56/197734/Chromosome-8p-Deletions-and-8q-Gains-are ; https://journals.lww.com/epidem/fulltext/2009/07000/overadjustment_bias_and_unnecessary_adjustment_in.4.aspx ; https://www.jclinepi.com/article/S0895-4356(22)00143-3/abstract

label: Pitfall 5: rare-event comparison, test choice and zero cells
text: PITFALL: BRAF V600E is a rare event in lung adenocarcinoma (about 1.5-3% of tumours), so each subtype group will hold only a handful of positives or zero; chi-square is invalid with expected counts below 5, and Fisher's exact test is conservative and has very low power, so a large p-value is nearly guaranteed even when a real difference exists. CHECK: Compute expected cell counts; count the total number of V600E-positive samples and how many sit in each group; give exact (Clopper-Pearson or Wilson) 95% CIs for each group's proportion, and for a group with 0/n events use the rule-of-three upper bound of about 3/n. IF FOUND: Use exact tests (scipy.stats.fisher_exact, plus the more powerful unconditional scipy.stats.barnard_exact or boschloo_exact, or mid-p) instead of chi-square; report the effect as proportions with CIs, do not report an odds ratio of 0/infinity as if it were an estimate, and state plainly how many events the conclusion rests on. SOURCE: https://aliquote.org/pub/3531_ftp.pdf ; https://www.biostathandbook.com/small.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4367599/

label: Pitfall 4: pooled frequency across RDEB/sporadic and TMB strata
text: PITFALL: The cohort mixes etiologic subgroups with very different mutation burdens (clinical columns HERED_DISORDER e.g. RDEB vs None, IMMUNE_STATUS, and TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS ranging from <1 to >50 per Mb), so a pooled per-gene frequency can be produced entirely by a handful of hypermutated UV-type tumours, or diluted by a low-burden subgroup; the pooled number may describe neither subgroup. CHECK: for each gene, list the mutated samples with their TMB, HERED_DISORDER and IMMUNE_STATUS; compute frequency within each subgroup and within TMB strata; test whether mutated status simply tracks TMB (e.g. Mann-Whitney of TMB in mutated vs unmutated samples, or logistic regression on log TMB). IF FOUND: report subgroup-specific frequencies alongside the pooled one, state which population the claim 'in cutaneous SCC' is being judged on, and treat mutations confined to the highest-TMB samples as weak evidence of the gene being a recurrent target. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3919509/ ; https://www.cell.com/cell/fulltext/S0092-8674%2817%2931142-X ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6131170/

label: Pitfall 10: primary-vs-metastasis or longitudinal discordance is not the same as within-tumour ITH
text: PITFALL: Differences between a primary and its metastasis, between synchronous primaries, or between samples taken at different times (for example before and after therapy) are inter-lesion or temporal heterogeneity and are often conflated with intratumour (within one lesion) heterogeneity; some authors include them under ITH and some do not, so the result depends on the definition. CHECK: For each multi-sample patient classify the pair using SAMPLE_TYPE, TISSUE_SEQUENCED, METASTATIC_SITE and sample ID suffixes (T01/T02) as same-lesion regions, primary-metastasis, or longitudinal; also confirm the samples are clonally related (share at least one somatic mutation) rather than independent primaries. IF FOUND (only primary-metastasis or longitudinal pairs): state which definition is used, report same-lesion and cross-lesion results separately, and do not present cross-lesion discordance as proof of heterogeneity within a single tumour. SOURCE: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/medicine/articles/10.3389/fmed.2018.00234/full and https://www.cell.com/cell-reports/fulltext/S2211-1247(18)31635-8

label: Sparse-data bias and separation with small race groups
text: PITFALL: Institutional clinical-sequencing cohorts are heavily imbalanced by race, so logistic regression of a binary arm-gain outcome with small race categories suffers sparse-data bias or separation: maximum-likelihood odds ratios drift away from the null or become infinite as covariates are added, and Wald p-values become unreliable. CHECK: Print the full cross-table of outcome x exposure x RACE; flag any cell under about 5-10 and any coefficient with |log OR| > 3 or a huge standard error, and watch whether estimates move further from the null as covariates are added. IF FOUND: use Firth penalized logistic regression with profile-likelihood intervals (or exact/stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel), collapse or drop tiny race categories with the decision stated, and report likelihood-ratio rather than Wald tests. SOURCE: https://www.bmj.com/content/352/bmj.i1981 ; https://doi.org/10.1093/aje/kwx299 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10165217/

label: Pitfall 6: interpreting non-significant small-sample differences and label choice
text: PITFALL: Mislabelling because of how a non-significant rare-event result is read. A p>0.05 from a small sample is not evidence that the frequencies are equal ('absence of evidence is not evidence of absence'), so it does not by itself contradict the hypothesis; equally, a lower percentage resting on one or two cases is fragile. Also, 'Not verifiable' in this task means the needed variables are missing, not that power is low. CHECK: Decide the rule before looking at p-values: (1) are the variables present (subtype group and V600E calls)? (2) what is the direction of the observed frequencies versus each comparator? (3) how strong is it (one-sided exact p for 'lower', CI for the difference)? (4) fragility: would moving one V600E case between groups flip the direction? IF FOUND: If variables exist, choose between True and False on the observed direction and magnitude of the frequency difference together with its robustness, and report the p-value and CI as a statement of uncertainty rather than letting 'not significant' alone force False or Not verifiable; say in the reasoning when the conclusion is descriptive rather than statistically significant. SOURCE: https://www.bmj.com/content/311/7003/485.full ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9365504/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5726092/

label: Pitfall 5: small n, exact intervals, pre-specified 'frequent' criterion
text: PITFALL: The cohort is a few dozen tumours, so each gene's frequency rests on a handful of samples; one or two samples move it by several percentage points and a point estimate with a normal (Wald) interval is misleading. 'Frequently' has no fixed threshold, so choosing the cutoff after seeing the numbers lets the label go either way. CHECK: for each of the four genes report k/n with a Wilson or Clopper-Pearson 95% interval; fix the criterion before looking (e.g. the gene's percentile among all genes in this cohort and its frequency relative to accepted cSCC drivers), and check that the verdict is the same under a stricter and a looser criterion. IF FOUND: if the verdict flips with +/-1 mutated sample or with the choice of threshold, say so and base the label on the relative criterion (rank among all genes and versus positive-control drivers) rather than an absolute percent; the claim is a conjunction, so each of the four genes must pass on its own. SOURCE: https://www.stat.cmu.edu/~brian/720/week01/Binomial-StatSci.pdf ; https://doi.org/10.1002/pds.1081

label: Null result vs untestable: absence of evidence
text: PITFALL: A non-significant p-value is not evidence that a hypothesis is false, and a missing variable is not a null result: 'contradicted' needs an estimate from the actual exposure whose confidence interval excludes meaningful effects, whereas no exposure variable, or a wide interval, means the data cannot settle the question. CHECK: Before choosing a label, write down (a) which column is the exposure, (b) which is the outcome, (c) the adjusted effect estimate with 95% CI; if (a) cannot be filled with a real income measure the analysis has not tested the hypothesis at all. IF FOUND: distinguish three states - supported (real exposure, CI excludes null in the stated direction), contradicted (real exposure, CI tight around null or opposite), not testable (exposure or required covariate absent) - and do not let a null result on a proxy variable be reported as contradiction. SOURCE: https://www.bmj.com/content/311/7003/485.full ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4877414/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5726092/
