label: Pitfall 7: one sample per patient, count patients not MAF rows
text: PITFALL: Wrong unit of analysis. Sample IDs in this kind of MSK-IMPACT cohort carry tumour indices (e.g. -T01-, -T02-, -T04-), so a patient may contribute more than one sequenced sample, and a MAF can list the same variant more than once per sample; counting rows or samples instead of patients double-counts a rare event and breaks the independence assumed by exact tests. CHECK: Test whether PATIENT_ID is unique in data_clinical_sample.txt; check for duplicated (Tumor_Sample_Barcode, HGVSp_Short) BRAF rows; compare the number of samples in the clinical file, the gene panel matrix and the patient file. IF FOUND: Analyse one sample per patient (standard practice is the first sequenced or the primary resection sample), count a patient as V600E-positive once, and confirm the conclusion is unchanged at sample level. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1182/blood-2022-158783 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11747808/

label: Pitfall 6: calibrate against positive- and negative-control genes
text: PITFALL: With no in-cohort calibration it is impossible to say whether, e.g., 10% is 'frequent' for this tumour type; cutaneous SCC has established recurrent genes (TP53, NOTCH1, NOTCH2, CDKN2A, HRAS, FAT1 and others, many also mutated in sun-exposed normal skin) and well-known passengers. CHECK: compute, with the identical pipeline, the mutated-sample fraction of positive controls (TP53, NOTCH1, NOTCH2, CDKN2A, HRAS, FAT1) and negative controls (TTN, MUC16, an olfactory receptor, a length-matched random gene set for each target gene) and place the four hypothesis genes on that scale. IF FOUND: if the four genes sit with the length-matched random genes rather than with the positive controls, raw frequency does not support 'frequently affected'; if the positive controls themselves come out implausibly low or absent, the pipeline (filters, symbol matching, denominator) is wrong and must be fixed before answering. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11352924/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4367811/

label: Area-level income: ecological fallacy, misclassification, clustering
text: PITFALL: When an area-level income measure (zip code or census-tract median household income) is available it is a contextual variable, not individual income: agreement with household income is poor, coefficients can be biased or even change sign (ecological fallacy), zip codes mismatch census areas, patients in the same area share one value (clustered errors), and area income is strongly correlated with race so the two are hard to separate. CHECK: If such a column exists, look at its granularity (how many patients share each value), its distribution by RACE (overlap/positivity), and whether it is continuous or pre-binned. IF FOUND: interpret as neighbourhood-level association only, model income as given (quantiles or per-unit on a log scale, not an arbitrary median split), use cluster-robust or multilevel standard errors if area IDs exist, and check the income-by-race overlap before trusting a race-adjusted estimate. SOURCE: https://academic.oup.com/jnci/article/115/5/488/7076612 ; https://doi.org/10.2105/ajph.92.7.1100 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10165486/

label: Pitfall 8: confounder adjustment with sparse events (separation)
text: PITFALL: Over-adjusting or mis-adjusting a rare outcome. Histologic subtype groups differ in smoking history, stage and sex, and BRAF mutation type is related to smoking, so an analyst may try a multivariable logistic regression; with only a few V600E events this gives separation (infinite or absurd odds ratios) and sparse-data bias, and the adjusted model can then be wrongly taken as the answer. CHECK: Count events per candidate covariate (well under 10 events per variable means ordinary logistic regression is unreliable); look for zero cells in subtype-by-covariate-by-V600E tables. IF FOUND: Keep the unadjusted per-group frequency comparison as the primary analysis, because the hypothesis is a descriptive statement about frequencies; if adjustment is shown at all, use Firth penalised logistic regression or a stratified exact test as a sensitivity analysis with at most one covariate (e.g. SMOKING_HISTORY), and never report maximum-likelihood odds ratios from a separated model. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1093/aje/kwx299 ; https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.i1981

label: Pitfall 7: multiple tumours per patient and repeated identical variants
text: PITFALL: Samples are not all independent patients: the clinical tables contain more than one tumour from the same person under separate IDs (e.g. Patient9 and Patient9_2), and related tumours can share clonal or leaked germline variants, so the same event is counted twice. CHECK: find patients with more than one sample (also by ID stem such as '_2'); for the genes of interest check whether the mutated samples include such pairs and whether the identical variant (chromosome, position, alleles) appears in both, or in many samples across the cohort. IF FOUND: report frequency per patient (a patient is mutated if any of their tumours is) as well as per sample, and count an identical variant shared by tumours of one person once; an identical variant recurring across many unrelated samples should be inspected as a possible germline/artefact call rather than counted as recurrence. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8514156/

label: Selection bias in clinical sequencing cohorts
text: PITFALL: Patients in a single-centre clinical tumor-sequencing cohort are selected on referral, advanced disease and access to care, all of which relate to socioeconomic position and race, and to 8q gain through disease stage; conditioning on being sequenced can therefore induce or mask an SES-genomics association (collider/selection bias) and under-represents minority and low-income patients. CHECK: Describe the cohort mix (RACE counts, DISEASE_EXTENT, SAMPLE_TYPE, one sample per patient or not - both clinical tables have about 2068 data rows) and note whether advanced disease dominates. IF FOUND: present any association as holding within this selected cohort only, analyse one sample per patient, and consider stratifying by disease extent to see whether an association is consistent within strata. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41698-023-00351-6 ; https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2766816 ; https://www.esmorwd.org/article/S2949-8201(25)00006-2/fulltext

label: Pitfall 9: tumour purity and false-negative calls across subtypes
text: PITFALL: Differential detection sensitivity. Hybrid-capture panel calls depend on tumour purity and depth; about 10% of BRAF hotspot mutations in clinical samples have variant allele fraction below 5%, and low-cellularity tumours (lepidic-pattern tumours tend to have low tumour content) can produce false negatives, which would bias a between-subtype frequency comparison. CHECK: For each BRAF V600E call compute VAF = t_alt_count/(t_alt_count+t_ref_count) and depth; compare across groups the share of samples with zero called mutations and, if available, purity proxies (e.g. FGA_FACETS of exactly 0 or missing, very low TMB) as a sign of low-purity samples. IF FOUND: Note it as a limitation and run a sensitivity analysis excluding samples with no detectable somatic alteration at all; do not change the primary denominator on this basis alone. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-017-01470-y ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3826759/

label: Pitfall 8: call quality sensitivity (VAF, read counts, germline leakage)
text: PITFALL: Low-confidence calls (few supporting reads, very low allele fraction, alt reads in the matched normal, known dbSNP germline sites, FFPE artefacts) can add or remove the one or two samples that decide a gene's frequency in a small cohort. CHECK: the MAF has t_ref_count, t_alt_count, n_ref_count, n_alt_count and dbSNP_RS; for every protein-altering variant in the four genes compute VAF = t_alt/(t_alt+t_ref), tumour depth, n_alt_count, and whether dbSNP_RS is filled; check Matched_Norm_Sample_Barcode/Mutation_Status to see whether calls are tumour-normal or tumour-only. IF FOUND: rerun the frequency with a conventional filter (e.g. t_alt_count >= 3-5, VAF >= 0.05, n_alt_count <= 1) as a sensitivity analysis and report whether the conclusion survives; do not silently drop variants in the main analysis since the deposited MAF is already the study's filtered call set. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7586657/ ; https://www.gimjournal.org/article/S1098-3600(21)00974-6/fulltext

label: Data structure of the PTEN/BRAFi melanoma study tables
text: DATA STRUCTURE (headers only, no analysis done): 66 patients with exactly one tumour sample each (61 metastasis, 5 primary); all 66 sample IDs appear in data_cna.txt, data_mutations.txt and data_gene_panel_matrix.txt. Patient table has PFS_MONTHS (no missing values) but NO PFS status/event column; OS_STATUS exists and OS_MONTHS is described as measured from initial diagnosis. AGENT is mixed: 48 vemurafenib, 6 dabrafenib, 8 dabrafenib+trametinib, 3 vemurafenib+cobimetinib, 1 'Vem+cob (leukemia patient)'. data_cna.txt has 59 genes including PTEN with values only -2/0/2 (no -1/1). Gene panel matrix has only a 'mutations' column with three panel versions (bait_v3 n=10, bait_v4 n=11, bait_v5 n=45) and no gene lists. Mutation file has 816 rows, 218 genes, mostly missense, with t_ref_count/t_alt_count and a Hotspot column. Covariates available: ECOG_STATUS, M_STAGE, STAGE, BRAIN_METS, LIVER_INVOLVEMENT, RECIST_BURDEN_OF_DISEASE, NUMBER_OF_SITES, GREATER_THAN_3_SITES, IMMUNE_TREATMENT, CHEMOTHERAPY, TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS; no LDH.

label: Pitfall 9: gene symbol matching and meaning of zero rows
text: PITFALL: Genes are missed or over-matched when looked up by symbol: Entrez_Gene_Id is empty in this MAF so Hugo_Symbol is the only key; symbols may be outdated aliases (EP300 = p300/KAT3B; PBRM1 = BAF180/PB1; CHUK = IKKA/IKK1/IKBKA/TCF16; USP28), carry stray case/whitespace, or be matched by substring so antisense/readthrough loci (e.g. EP300-AS1) are counted; a gene with zero rows can mean 'no mutation' or 'named differently'. CHECK: exact, case-insensitive, whitespace-stripped match on Hugo_Symbol; also search the alias list and regex 'EP300|PBRM1|USP28|CHUK' to see every symbol variant present; confirm hits by chromosome band (EP300 22q13, PBRM1 3p21, USP28 11q23, CHUK 10q24) using the Chromosome/Start_Position columns. IF FOUND: merge true aliases into the gene, exclude antisense/readthrough symbols, and if a gene has no rows under any name report it as 0/n (evidence against 'frequently'), not as 'Not verifiable' - the mutation table covers the exome, so absence of rows is data. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7856679/ ; https://www.genenames.org/help/faq/

label: PITFALL: PFS has no event indicator
text: PITFALL: PFS_MONTHS comes with no PFS event/censoring indicator, so analysts either borrow OS_STATUS as the PFS event flag (wrong: death is not progression, living patients have usually progressed, and OS_MONTHS is measured from initial diagnosis, not from therapy start) or silently drop to a non-survival test without saying what was assumed. CHECK: confirm there is no PFS status column; verify PFS_MONTHS <= OS_MONTHS for everyone; flag patients who could still be progression-free at last follow-up (OS_STATUS LIVING with very long PFS, RESPONSE_GRADE Excellent, COMMENTS text). IF FOUND: make the primary analysis 'every PFS time is an observed progression' (Kaplan-Meier/log-rank/Cox with all events=1, cross-checked with a Wilcoxon rank-sum on PFS_MONTHS), then run a sensitivity analysis in which the plausible ongoing responders are treated as censored; never use OS_STATUS as the PFS event and never substitute OS for PFS. Report whether the direction and conclusion are the same under both. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3071962/ ; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jtho.2021.04.004

label: PITFALL: directional claim, check sign of effect
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is directional (PTEN loss-of-function -> LONGER PFS on BRAF inhibitor). A significant two-sided p-value alone does not support it; the effect must be in the claimed direction, and a difference in the opposite direction (shorter PFS in PTEN-altered) contradicts it. Also, per the task text, 'Not verifiable' is reserved for data that lack the relevant variables, not for a small or underpowered comparison. CHECK: always report the direction explicitly: median PFS per group, hazard ratio for PTEN-altered vs wild-type with 95% CI (HR>1 = shorter PFS), and group sizes; state which group is the reference. IF FOUND (effect opposite to the claim or no benefit for PTEN-altered): the claim of increased PFS is not supported; judge on direction + CI, not on p<0.05 alone, and do not re-label a wrong-direction result as 'inconclusive' merely because n is small. SOURCE: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4877414/ ; https://lakens.github.io/statistical_inferences/09-equivalencetest.html

label: PITFALL: small unbalanced biomarker group
text: PITFALL: The PTEN-altered group will be a small minority of 66 patients; the asymptotic chi-square log-rank p-value and Cox Wald test are inaccurate (often anti-conservative) with small, unbalanced groups and few events, and Cox estimates can be unstable. CHECK: count PTEN-altered vs wild-type patients and events in each; if the smaller group is below roughly 10-15 patients, the asymptotic p-value should not be trusted on its own. IF FOUND: add a permutation (exact) log-rank test (shuffle PTEN labels >=10,000 times), use the Cox likelihood-ratio test or Firth-penalised Cox rather than Wald, show the Kaplan-Meier curves and medians, and report the HR confidence interval so the reader sees how wide it is. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6690426/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2950789/ ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-024-64573-9

label: LoF = mutations + deep deletions + SVs
text: PITFALL: Counting only truncating point mutations undercounts loss-of-function (LoF) of tumour suppressors in sarcomas, where TP53/RB1/ATRX are often inactivated by homozygous deletion or disruptive structural rearrangement rather than SNV/indel (a sarcoma WGS series attributed more drivers to disruptive SVs and homozygous deletions than to SNVs). The study's data_sv.txt does contain TP53 and ATRX rearrangement rows. CHECK: for each gene build, per patient, three flags: (a) truncating mutation in data_mutations.txt, (b) value -2 (deep deletion) in data_cna.txt, (c) any row in data_sv.txt with the gene in Site1_Hugo_Symbol or Site2_Hugo_Symbol; report mutation-only frequency and the union frequency side by side. IF FOUND (union >> mutation-only): state both; the hypothesis says 'mutations', so decide the label on the mutation-only definition AND check it does not flip under the union definition; if it flips, say so explicitly in the reasoning. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11368954/ ; https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5693358/

label: TP53 missense counts as LoF; RB1/ATRX missense does not
text: PITFALL: TP53 is unusual among tumour suppressors: most inactivating hits are missense mutations in the DNA-binding domain, which saturation-mutagenesis studies show act by loss of function / dominant-negative effect, not as neutral variants. Excluding all Missense_Mutation rows from 'loss-of-function' can cut the TP53 frequency by roughly half; including missense for RB1 or ATRX would wrongly inflate theirs (ATRX/RB1 missense are mostly of uncertain significance; only frameshift/nonsense/splice are safely LoF). CHECK: tabulate Variant_Classification separately for TP53, RB1, ATRX; compute TP53 frequency (i) truncating only and (ii) truncating + missense (optionally restrict missense to DNA-binding domain codons ~100-300 or known hotspots R175, G245, R248, R249, R273, R282). IF FOUND (TP53 missense are numerous): report both definitions, treat TP53 DBD missense as LoF in the primary analysis, and keep RB1/ATRX to truncating classes. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6168352/ ; https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aax3649 ; https://www.oncokb.org/gene/TP53/Truncating%20Mutations

label: Filter MAF Variant_Classification before counting LoF
text: PITFALL: The MAF (data_mutations.txt) holds non-protein-altering rows too (its first data row is a TERT 5'Flank promoter variant), so counting 'any row for the gene' overstates LoF. Standard truncating/LoF classes are Nonsense_Mutation, Frame_Shift_Del, Frame_Shift_Ins, Splice_Site, Translation_Start_Site (and Nonstop_Mutation); In_Frame_Del/Ins and Missense_Mutation are protein-altering but not automatically LoF; Silent, Intron, 3'UTR, 5'UTR, 3'Flank, 5'Flank, IGR, RNA and Splice_Region are low-consequence and must be excluded. CHECK: print value_counts of Variant_Classification for the three genes before filtering, and confirm no Silent/Intron/Flank/Splice_Region rows are being counted. IF FOUND: filter to the truncating list (plus TP53 missense per the TP53 pitfall) and count each patient once per gene even with several mutations. SOURCE: https://rdrr.io/bioc/maftools/src/R/validateMaf.R ; https://docs.gdc.cancer.gov/Encyclopedia/pages/Mutation_Annotation_Format_TCGAv2/

label: Pitfall: define GCB subsets by COO x CLUSTER, not all samples
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is about two subsets WITHIN GCB-DLBCL, but the sample table carries a genetic CLUSTER label assigned across all DLBCLs plus three cell-of-origin columns (COO_GEP from arrays, COO_LYMPH2CX from NanoString, ANY_COO combined), with NA for unprofiled cases and an 'unclassified' class; comparing clusters over all samples, or re-clustering yourself, answers a different question, and GEP and Lymph2Cx calls disagree in a minority of cases. CHECK: Cross-tabulate CLUSTER by ANY_COO (and by COO_GEP and COO_LYMPH2CX separately), list the levels of CLUSTER (look for an unassigned/0 level), count NA and unclassified COO, and identify which clusters hold most GCB cases. IF FOUND: Define the two subsets as the GCB-enriched clusters, run the outcome comparison both for all cases in those clusters and restricted to COO=GCB cases, and repeat with each COO column as a sensitivity analysis; never treat NA COO as non-GCB. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1182/blood-2013-11-536433 ; https://haematologica.org/article/view/8236

label: Denominator = profiled samples from gene panel matrix
text: PITFALL: Wrong denominator. In cBioPortal-format data a sample with zero called mutations has NO rows in data_mutations.txt but is still profiled; using 'samples appearing in the MAF' (or in the CNA matrix) as the denominator inflates frequency, and counting un-profiled samples as wild-type deflates it. The authoritative list of who was profiled for what is data_gene_panel_matrix.txt (columns mutations, cna, structural_variants; NA = not profiled); samples here span panel versions IMPACT341/410/468 (IM3/IM5/IM6 suffixes). CHECK: denominator per data type = samples with a non-NA panel in data_gene_panel_matrix.txt; compare that count with clinical-sample rows, MAF unique barcodes and data_cna.txt columns; confirm TP53, RB1 and ATRX rows exist in data_cna.txt with non-NA values for every panel version (a gene absent from a panel shows as NA, not 0). IF FOUND (counts differ): use profiled samples/patients as the denominator per gene and per data type; for the union of mutation+CNA+SV use samples profiled for all three. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/ ; https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/5000 ; https://groups.google.com/g/cbioportal/c/u3pHrsXP9WY

label: Pitfall: asymptotic log-rank p unreliable for small/unbalanced clusters
text: PITFALL: The standard chi-square (asymptotic) log-rank p-value from R survival or Python lifelines is anti-conservative when groups are small or unbalanced or have few events, which is exactly the situation when comparing cluster-derived tumour subgroups; in a benchmark, 30 of 37 'significant' asymptotic p-values were too small versus exact permutation p-values and about 8 percent lost significance. CHECK: Count patients and events (PFS and OS separately) in each of the two GCB subsets; if any group has fewer than about 20-30 events or the groups are very unequal, compute a permutation log-rank p-value (shuffle group labels 10,000+ times) next to the asymptotic one. IF FOUND: Base the conclusion on the permutation p-value and the hazard ratio with confidence interval, not on the asymptotic p alone. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6690426/

label: Count per patient, not per sample
text: PITFALL: Samples are not patients. Sample IDs in this study carry T01/T02/T03 suffixes, so some patients may contribute more than one tumour (e.g. primary and metastasis); counting samples double-counts those patients and violates independence in a prevalence estimate. Large MSK-IMPACT cohort analyses pick one representative sample per patient for this reason. CHECK: compare number of unique PATIENT_ID with number of SAMPLE_ID in data_clinical_sample.txt and list patients with >1 sample. IF FOUND: compute frequency per patient (patient altered if any of their profiled samples is altered, or use one pre-specified sample per patient) and report the per-sample figure only as a sensitivity check. SOURCE: https://www.cell.com/cell/fulltext/S0092-8674(22)00003-4 ; https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/23723556.2022.2065176

label: Pitfall: non-significant survival difference is not evidence of no difference
text: PITFALL: A non-significant survival difference between two small genetic subsets is not evidence that outcomes are the same; power of the log-rank/Cox test depends on the number of events, not patients, so an underpowered comparison can wrongly be read as contradicting the hypothesis (and a visibly separated KM curve with p just above 0.05 wrongly dismissed). CHECK: Report number of events per group, the hazard ratio with 95 percent CI, and KM estimates at fixed times (e.g. 2 and 5 years); ask whether the CI excludes clinically meaningful hazard ratios such as 2 or 0.5. IF FOUND: If the CI is wide and includes both no effect and large effects, say the outcome part is inconclusive rather than refuted; call it contradicted only if the CI is tight around 1 or the direction is opposite to the claim. SOURCE: https://www.bmj.com/content/311/7003/485 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9365504/

label: Restrict cohort to ULMS histology
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is about uterine leiomyosarcoma only, but the clinical sample table has CANCER_TYPE = 'Uterine Sarcoma' with separate CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED / CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED_CODE / ONCOTREE_CODE columns, so the study may mix histologies (do not assume every sample is LMS). Pooling other uterine sarcoma subtypes, which have different driver profiles, would bias the frequency. CHECK: value_counts of CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED and ONCOTREE_CODE in data_clinical_sample.txt (skip the 4 '#' lines). IF FOUND (more than one histology): restrict all numerators and denominators to ONCOTREE_CODE == ULMS / 'Uterine Leiomyosarcoma'; optionally report other subtypes only as contrast. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/ (clinical data columns); observation from the file header.

label: Pitfall: confounding by treatment, cohort and IPI in pooled DLBCL outcome analysis
text: PITFALL: The patient table pools several cohorts (COHORT column, including trial and non-trial series) and has an R_CHOP_LIKE_CHEMO flag; outcome differences between genetic subsets can be produced or hidden by differences in treatment, cohort (different eligibility, age range, follow-up) and IPI rather than by the genetics, and not every sequenced patient has outcome data. CHECK: Tabulate COHORT, R_CHOP_LIKE_CHEMO, IPI and age by subset; count patients with non-missing PFS/OS per subset; run the survival comparison restricted to R-CHOP-like-treated patients, then a Cox model adjusted for IPI and stratified by COHORT. IF FOUND: Use the R-CHOP-treated, outcome-available set as the primary analysis population, report both unadjusted and IPI-adjusted/cohort-stratified hazard ratios, and state the patient flow (N sequenced, N with COO, N treated, N with outcome). SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3362085/

label: Pre-specify 'uncommon' threshold; Wilson/exact CI per gene
text: PITFALL: 'Uncommon' is a qualitative claim, and the hypothesis is a conjunction over three genes; an analyst can reach any label by choosing the threshold after seeing the numbers. Small cohorts (<100 patients) also give wide intervals, and the Wald interval is unreliable there. CHECK: before computing, fix a rule (e.g. 'uncommon' = upper confidence bound below ~10%; 'common' = lower bound above ~20%); then for each gene report altered/profiled patients, the proportion and a 95% Wilson or Clopper-Pearson interval; state results per gene, not only pooled. IF FOUND (interval straddles the threshold, or genes disagree): say which genes drive the label; the claim that all three are uncommon is contradicted if any of them is clearly common, and is supported only if each is clearly rare. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1214/ss/1009213286 ; https://fingertips.phe.org.uk/static-reports/public-health-technical-guidance/Basic_statistics/Proportions.html

label: Pitfall: double dipping when testing alterations between genetically defined clusters
text: PITFALL: Clusters were defined from the genetic alterations themselves, so testing whether mutation or SV frequencies differ between clusters on the same data is circular ('double dipping'): classical Fisher/chi-square p-values are extremely inflated and a significant genetic difference is guaranteed by construction, so it is not independent evidence that the subsets are 'distinct'. CHECK: Ask for each test whether the variable was an input to the clustering (mutations, SVs, copy number were; PFS/OS and COO were not). IF FOUND: Use genetic comparisons only descriptively (which alterations characterise each subset, with effect sizes), and rest the inferential weight on variables not used to build the clusters, chiefly outcome; do not cite tiny enrichment p-values as proof. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11036349/

label: Panel CNA/SV calls under-detect; -2 only, frequencies are lower bounds
text: PITFALL: Targeted-panel calls are a LOWER bound on LoF frequency. Discrete CNA value -2 is a 'putative' deep deletion; low tumour purity pulls log-ratios toward 0 so true homozygous deletions get called -1 or 0, and panels only see SV breakpoints that fall in captured exons/selected introns. A low observed frequency is therefore weaker evidence for 'uncommon' than a high observed frequency is against it. Also -1 (shallow loss) is not by itself LoF and should not be counted. CHECK: in data_cna_hg19.seg look at seg.mean for segments overlapping TP53 (chr17:7.57-7.59 Mb), RB1 (chr13:48.88-49.06 Mb) and ATRX (chrX:76.76-77.04 Mb), hg19; list samples with strongly negative seg.mean (e.g. < -1) that are not -2 in data_cna.txt, and note how many samples are -1. IF FOUND: report the strict frequency (-2 only) as primary and a relaxed one as sensitivity; if the strict frequency is already high the conclusion is robust, if it is low say explicitly that under-detection could not be ruled out. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5027494/ ; https://www.jmdjournal.org/article/S1525-1578(22)00103-9/fulltext ; https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/

label: Pitfall: multiplicity across cluster pairs, endpoints and COO definitions
text: PITFALL: With about five clusters, two endpoints (PFS, OS), three COO definitions and optional treatment filters there are dozens of possible pairwise survival comparisons; picking the pair or endpoint with the smallest p-value inflates the false-positive rate, and an overall k-group log-rank test does not say which pair differs. CHECK: Before looking at survival, fix the primary comparison (the two GCB-enriched clusters, primary endpoint PFS in treated patients, OS secondary) and count how many other comparisons you ran. IF FOUND: Report the pre-specified comparison as the answer; treat all other pairwise comparisons as exploratory with Holm or Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment (e.g. pairwise_survdiff-style correction). SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7015042/ ; https://doi.org/10.1002/sim.8016

label: ATRX on chrX: check CNA coverage, single hit suffices
text: PITFALL: ATRX is X-linked and subject to X-inactivation, so a single truncating hit can abolish function, and copy-number pipelines often handle chrX differently from autosomes (chrX may be missing from the seg file or the discrete CNA matrix, or be coded as 'X' vs '23'). Treating a missing ATRX CNA row as 'no deletions' silently biases ATRX downward relative to TP53/RB1. (The panel-pipeline part of this is the librarian's inference, not a documented fact about this dataset.) CHECK: confirm ATRX has a row in data_cna.txt with non-NA values, and whether chrom X/23 occurs in data_cna_hg19.seg; check SEX in data_clinical_patient.txt. IF FOUND (ATRX CNA absent or all NA/0): base the ATRX frequency on mutations + SVs only, label it a lower bound, and do not compare it naively with the other two genes. SOURCE: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/molecular-biosciences/articles/10.3389/fmolb.2024.1434398/full ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10137841/

label: Pitfall: MAF hygiene, denominators and tumour-only germline leakage
text: PITFALL: The mutation table (MAF) is not ready for gene-frequency comparison: it contains Silent and other non-protein-altering rows, variants annotated with dbSNP rs IDs, multiple rows per gene per sample, and the cohort mixes tumours with and without a matched normal (SOMATIC_STATUS), where tumour-only calling leaves residual germline variants and inflates mutation counts; samples with zero mutations in a gene do not appear in the MAF at all. CHECK: Filter Variant_Classification to nonsilent coding classes, collapse to one flag per sample-gene, take the denominator from data_clinical_sample/gene_panel_matrix (all WXS-profiled samples) rather than from samples present in the MAF, and compare the matched/unmatched proportion between the two subsets. IF FOUND: If matched status is unbalanced, repeat the gene-frequency comparison in matched samples only or restrict to recurrently mutated significant genes (data_mutsig q<0.1) and hotspots, which are robust to germline leakage. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41698-021-00164-5 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4561496/ ; https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/

label: Somatic status, ID joins and external sanity check
text: PITFALL: Not every row is a confident somatic call. data_clinical_sample.txt has a SOMATIC_STATUS column (Matched vs possibly Unmatched) and the MAF has Mutation_Status; tumour-only samples can carry unfiltered germline variants, and data_sv.txt has an SV_Status column. Also sanity-check the result against other cohorts: published sarcoma exome studies of OTHER datasets found TP53, RB1 and ATRX to be the recurrently mutated genes in leiomyosarcoma (e.g. TP53 mutated in about half of LMS), so a near-zero TP53 frequency here should first be suspected as a filtering or join bug (e.g. sample-ID mismatch between files), not accepted at face value. The label must still come from this study's data. CHECK: value_counts of SOMATIC_STATUS, Mutation_Status and SV_Status; verify sample IDs in the MAF/CNA/SV files all match SAMPLE_ID in the clinical table. IF FOUND (unmatched samples or germline-flagged rows): rerun excluding them as a sensitivity analysis and report whether the frequency changes materially. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9172914/ ; https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5693358/

label: Pitfall: exome SV calls are incomplete; no CNA table
text: PITFALL: Structural variants (BCL2, BCL6, MYC rearrangements) here are called from capture/exome sequencing, which misses a substantial share of rearrangements compared with FISH (reported NGS sensitivity roughly 58 percent for MYC and 74 percent for BCL6, near 100 percent for BCL2), and data_sv.txt lists only positives, often with two rows per event (reciprocal fusion calls in the same sample); the study also ships no copy-number table, only per-sample counts such as NUM_DRIVER_SCNA. CHECK: Collapse data_sv.txt to one flag per sample and gene (search both Site1 and Site2 gene columns), use all WXS-profiled samples as denominator, and note that specific copy-number alterations cannot be examined. IF FOUND: Treat SV-negative as 'not detected', compare SV frequencies between subsets as lower bounds (the bias is roughly equal across subsets so differences in direction remain interpretable), and do not claim absence of a rearrangement class or of copy-number targets in a subset. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11251499/ ; https://doi.org/10.4149/neo_2024_240527n236

label: Pitfall: operationalising 'targetable' alterations
text: PITFALL: 'Targetable alterations' is not a column in the data and is easily mis-operationalised: either every driver mutation is called targetable (too loose), or the claim is declared untestable because no drug-response variable exists (too strict). Actionability frameworks such as OncoKB grade a gene/alteration by level of evidence (1-2 standard of care, 3 clinical evidence, 4 biological evidence), and the share of 'actionable' tumours changes several-fold with the level chosen. CHECK: State up front which genes/pathways count as targets with available or investigational inhibitors (for B-cell lymphoma e.g. epigenetic regulators, BCL2, PI3K, JAK/STAT, BRAF/MEK-ERK pathways) and then tabulate, per subset, the frequency of nonsilent mutations/SVs in those genes. IF FOUND: Judge the 'targetable alterations' half of the hypothesis on whether each subset carries a characteristic, different set of alterations in such genes; say explicitly that the data can show presence of candidate targets but cannot test drug response. SOURCE: https://www.oncokb.org/therapeutic-levels ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10784742/

label: TERT promoter calls may be absent or partial in exome MAF
text: PITFALL: The mutation table of an exome-based (WXS) cBioPortal study may hold no TERT promoter calls at all, or only a partial set, because the promoter is non-coding (labelled 5'Flank, the one non-coding class cBioPortal keeps, and only for TERT) and in TCGA-style cohorts TERT promoter status often came from a separate targeted assay or WGS that was never loaded into the MAF. CHECK: in data_mutations.txt select Hugo_Symbol==TERT (Entrez 7015) and tabulate Variant_Classification, Start_Position (hg19 hotspots chr5:1295228 'C228T' and chr5:1295250 'C250T', on the minus strand so shown as G>A), and the number of distinct Tumor_Sample_Barcode; also scan the clinical sample/patient headers for any TERT status column. IF FOUND: if there are zero promoter (5'Flank/hotspot) rows and no clinical TERT column, the mutation variable does not exist and the label is 'Not verifiable' rather than True; if promoter rows exist, the variable exists and the test can proceed, but only the mutant calls are trustworthy (see the wild-type pitfall). SOURCE: https://github.com/cBioPortal/datahub/issues/154 ; https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/895 ; https://groups.google.com/g/cbioportal/c/5vpH1mp5_Qc

label: Pitfall 1: PTC comparator may be absent from the data
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is comparative ('compared to PTCs') but the study tables may contain only advanced thyroid cancers (the patient table has a PDTC_DEFINITION column; sample rows show Anaplastic Thyroid Carcinoma), so there may be no PTC comparator group in the data; CYTOLOGICAL_PHENOTYPE values such as 'tall cell variant' describe the cytology of an advanced tumour and are NOT a PTC sample group. CHECK: tabulate CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED and ONCOTREE_CODE in data_clinical_sample.txt and confirm whether any sample is actually a papillary thyroid carcinoma; do not build a PTC group from CYTOLOGICAL_PHENOTYPE or GROWTH_PATTERN. IF FOUND (no PTC samples): say explicitly that only the advanced-cancer half (prevalence and clonality of TERT promoter mutations in PDTC/ATC) is measured from the data and that the PTC side is not in the tables; do not silently import a PTC number from memory as if it were data, and choose the label by the task's own definitions (Not verifiable is defined as 'no relevant variables or tables', which is different from 'one comparator arm is external'). SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/

label: No TERT promoter call is not wild-type
text: PITFALL: Treating every sample without a TERT promoter call as wild-type. The TERT promoter is >80% GC and poorly captured by exome kits, so a missing call usually means 'not covered / unknown', not wild-type; low tumour purity also hides calls. True TERT promoter mutation frequency in glioblastoma is about 70-80%, so a 'wild-type' group built from no-call samples is mostly hidden mutants, which pulls any mutant-vs-rest expression difference toward zero. CHECK: compute the fraction of mutation-profiled samples that carry a TERT promoter call and compare with the expected 70-80%; look at t_alt_count/t_ref_count depth on the called rows to see how thin coverage is. IF FOUND (call rate far below 70%): describe the comparison group as 'no call detected', not wild-type; state that misclassification biases toward the null, so a non-significant result cannot be read as support for 'no correlation', whereas a significant higher expression in called mutants despite the dilution is strong evidence against it; add a sensitivity analysis (e.g. restrict the comparison group to samples with independent evidence of an alternative telomere mechanism such as IDH1/ATRX mutation). SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8756133/ ; https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0204912 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4247168/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3833702/

label: Pitfall: Cox over-fitting and non-proportional hazards in small subgroup
text: PITFALL: Cox models on a small GCB subgroup are easily over-fitted and the proportional-hazards assumption can fail (curves crossing, early versus late events), making a single hazard ratio or log-rank test misleading; the rule of thumb is at least 10 events per covariate. CHECK: Count events in the analysis set; test PH with scaled Schoenfeld residuals (cox.zph in R, check_assumptions/proportional_hazard_test in lifelines) and look at whether KM curves cross. IF FOUND: With few events, adjust for IPI as one ordinal or grouped term (not five separate factors) and put COHORT in strata rather than as covariates; if PH fails, report KM survival at fixed landmarks or restricted mean survival time instead of relying on one HR. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7941573/ ; https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-patched/library/survival/html/cox.zph.html

label: Pitfall 2: TERT promoter rows are 5'Flank, lost by coding filters
text: PITFALL: TERT promoter mutations are non-coding, so any filter on protein-changing variants (Missense/Nonsense, non-empty HGVSp_Short, 'nonsynonymous') silently deletes them and gives a prevalence of zero. In a GRCh37 MAF they sit at chr5:1295228 (C228T, c.-124C>T) and chr5:1295250 (C250T, c.-146C>T), usually with Variant_Classification 5'Flank and Consequence upstream_gene_variant, empty HGVSp, and plus-strand alleles G>A; rarer promoter variants include tandem CC>TT at 1295228-229 / 1295242-243 and c.-57A>C. The two hotspots are mutually exclusive and heterozygous. CHECK: list every row with Hugo_Symbol==TERT in data_mutations.txt with Start_Position, Variant_Classification, Reference_Allele, Tumor_Seq_Allele2, t_ref_count, t_alt_count. IF FOUND: define TERT-promoter-mutant by genomic position/5'Flank class, keep it separate from any coding TERT variants, and never run the MAF through a nonsynonymous-only filter first. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/oncsis201539 ; https://aacrjournals.org/mcr/article/14/4/315/132821/Understanding-TERT-Promoter-Mutations-A-Common

label: Restrict to samples profiled for both mutation and RNA-seq
text: PITFALL: Mixing samples that were never sequenced, or never RNA-sequenced, into the comparison. In cBioPortal data the expression matrix, the mutation table and the copy-number table cover different sample sets (RNA-seq is often a small subset), and a sample absent from the MAF may be unprofiled rather than unmutated. CHECK: build three sets - RNA-seq column IDs, samples with mutations != NA in data_gene_panel_matrix.txt (profiled), and samples with a TERT promoter row - and report the size of each intersection; confirm sample IDs match exactly (TCGA-XX-XXXX-01) and that there is one sample per patient (SAMPLE_TYPE primary vs recurrent). IF FOUND: restrict the analysis to samples that have RNA-seq AND are mutation-profiled; drop samples with mutations == NA instead of calling them wild-type; report n per group, since the usable overlap may be small. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/ ; https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/ ; https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/12323

label: Pitfall: parsing cBioPortal clinical/survival coding and patient-sample merge
text: PITFALL: cBioPortal-format clinical files are easy to mis-parse: four '#' metadata lines precede the header, status fields are strings like '0:LIVING'/'1:DECEASED' and '0:Not Progressed'/'1:...' (the event is the leading 1, not the text), missing values appear as NA or blank, outcome lives in the patient table while CLUSTER and COO live in the sample table (join on PATIENT_ID, check for patients with more than one sample), and the meaning of OS/PFS start time can differ by study. CHECK: Read with comment='#', parse the event indicator from the prefix before ':', confirm one sample per patient after the merge, and print event counts and missing counts for PFS and OS. IF FOUND: Drop (do not zero-fill) patients with missing time or status, deduplicate to one row per patient before any survival test, and analyse PFS and OS separately. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/ ; https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/

label: Pitfall 3: prevalence denominator and sample/patient mismatch
text: PITFALL: Wrong prevalence denominator. A MAF only has rows for samples with at least one called mutation, so counting distinct Tumor_Sample_Barcode undercounts profiled tumours; in this study the '#sequenced_samples' header line of data_mutations.txt, data_gene_panel_matrix.txt, data_clinical_sample.txt and the .seg file do not obviously list the same sample set (e.g. P-0000174-T01-IM3 is in the panel matrix and seg file but was not seen in the sequenced_samples header). Patients can also have more than one sample, which double-counts. CHECK: compare the sample sets across clinical_sample, gene_panel_matrix (mutations column), the #sequenced_samples line and the MAF; confirm every sample's mutation panel covers the TERT promoter (panel names like IMPACT341 do; a WES or NA panel may not); count samples per PATIENT_ID. IF FOUND: use profiled samples (panel matrix mutations != NA) as the denominator, report prevalence per patient and per histology (PDTC, ATC, pooled 'advanced') with exact binomial CIs, and state how the result changes under each plausible denominator. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/ ; https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/5000

label: Only hotspot 5'Flank TERT rows are promoter mutations
text: PITFALL: Defining 'TERT promoter mutated' as any row with Hugo_Symbol TERT. Coding TERT variants (missense, silent) are not promoter mutations, and non-hotspot upstream variants or the common germline promoter SNP rs2853669 (which lowers, not raises, TERT expression) are not the activating C228T/C250T events; the two hotspots may also differ in effect size. CHECK: list every TERT row with Variant_Classification, Start_Position, alleles and HGVSc; keep only 5'Flank rows at hg19 chr5:1295228 or chr5:1295250 (plus rare neighbouring activating changes such as 1295228 C>A or the 1295242-243 CC>TT tandem) as promoter mutants. IF FOUND (other TERT rows present): exclude coding-only TERT samples from the mutant group (do not place them in mutant; note them), and report results for C228T and C250T pooled and separately if numbers allow. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1038/bjc.2014.538 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4496380/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5248652/

label: Pitfall 4: clonality needs CCF (purity + copy number), not raw VAF
text: PITFALL: Calling clonality from raw VAF. VAF depends on tumour purity and local copy number, so a fixed VAF cut-off (e.g. VAF>=0.4 is clonal) labels clonal mutations in low-purity tumours as subclonal; advanced/anaplastic tumours are often heavily diluted by stromal and immune cells, so this bias runs against the hypothesis. The standard quantity is the cancer cell fraction: CCF = VAF * (purity*N_T + 2*(1-purity)) / (m*purity), with N_T local total copy number and m the mutation multiplicity (heterozygous diploid: CCF = 2*VAF/purity). CHECK: compute VAF = t_alt_count/(t_ref_count+t_alt_count) for each TERT promoter call and plot it against TUMOR_PURITY from data_clinical_sample.txt; a clonal heterozygous mutation should lie near VAF = purity/2. IF FOUND (VAF scales with purity): judge clonality on CCF (or on a within-sample relative measure), not on VAF, and report the fraction of TERT-mutant tumours whose CCF is consistent with 1. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7867630/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8542635/

label: Pitfall 1: acetyl site vs parent protein abundance
text: PITFALL: An acetyl-site value from enrichment TMT data rises and falls with the amount of its parent protein, so a 'histone acetylation' difference between Wnt-active and Wnt-inactive tumours can be only a histone (or chromatin/proliferation) abundance difference. CHECK: for each histone acetyl site in data_acetylprotein_quantification.txt, look up the parent protein in data_protein_quantification.txt (row ids are 'GENE|GENE'), correlate site with protein across samples, and test whether the parent protein itself differs by Wnt status. IF FOUND: test the site adjusted for protein (site ~ Wnt + parent_protein, or residual of site on protein, or site minus protein) and report both raw and protein-adjusted results; if the exact histone paralog is absent from the protein table, adjust with another measured paralog of the same histone family or say the adjustment could not be done; only call it an acetylation relationship if it survives adjustment. SOURCE: https://vitek-lab.github.io/MSstatsPTM/index.html ; https://www.biorxiv.org/content/biorxiv/early/2023/07/05/2023.07.05.547780.full.pdf ; https://www.creative-proteomics.com/ptms-proteomics/resource/acetylome-troubleshooting-guide.htm

label: TERT expression is low and zero-inflated: use rank tests
text: PITFALL: TERT mRNA is very low and zero-inflated in bulk RNA-seq (mean below 1 TPM in most cancer types; brain tumours are among those with 25% or more samples at zero), with a bimodal expressed/not-expressed pattern, so a t-test or Pearson correlation on raw RSEM values is driven by a few outliers and can miss or invent a difference. CHECK: pull the TERT row (match on Entrez_Gene_Id 7015, since Hugo_Symbol can be blank or duplicated) from data_mrna_seq_v2_rsem.txt, and look at the fraction of zeros, the range and the shape of the distribution in each group. IF FOUND (skewed, many zeros/ties): use a Mann-Whitney/Wilcoxon rank-sum test as the primary test on RSEM or log2(RSEM+1), report medians and a rank effect size (AUC or rank-biserial) with a bootstrap CI, and add a Fisher exact test on TERT detectably expressed vs not; do not rely on a raw-scale t-test alone. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8070023/ ; https://doi.org/10.1038/ng.3781 ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13059-022-02648-4 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2857732/

label: Pitfall 5: purity column may be biased; use driver-VAF ratio as cross-check
text: PITFALL: The purity value itself is unreliable. Pathologist-estimated purity agrees poorly with sequencing-derived purity (R2 about 0.35; within 10 points in only 45% of tumours; histology tends to overestimate), and an overestimated purity pushes every CCF down and makes clonal mutations look subclonal, while an underestimate gives CCF > 1. CHECK: find out what TUMOR_PURITY is (range, missing values, round numbers suggest histology); as a calibration, compute CCF for the known truncal driver in each tumour (BRAF V600E, NRAS/HRAS/KRAS hotspot) - if those come out far from 1 the purity column is biased. IF FOUND: add a purity-free analysis: compare the TERT promoter VAF with the VAF of the truncal driver (or the highest/median VAF of the other somatic mutations) in the SAME sample - a ratio near 1 means TERT is as clonal as the founding driver; exclude reference mutations in copy-number-altered or LOH regions (e.g. TP53 with 17p loss) and be careful with unmatched samples (SOMATIC_STATUS) where a germline variant at VAF 0.5 can masquerade as the top somatic VAF. Report both the purity-based and the relative result. SOURCE: https://modernpathology.org/article/S0893-3952(22)00261-7/fulltext ; https://www.modernpathology.org/article/S0893-3952(22)01806-3/fulltext ; https://cnvkit.readthedocs.io/en/stable/heterogeneity.html

label: Pitfall 2: defining Wnt activation from mutations
text: PITFALL: Defining 'Wnt signaling active' as any non-silent mutation in any Wnt gene (CTNNB1, APC, AXIN1/2, RNF43, ...) mislabels tumours, because in endometrial carcinoma the activating events are CTNNB1 exon 3 degron missense/in-frame mutations (codons D32, S33, G34, S37, T41, S45) while POLE-ultramutated and MSI-hypermutated tumours carry many passenger mutations in long genes such as APC. CHECK: in data_mutations.txt list CTNNB1 rows with their HGVSp/protein position and Variant_Classification and count how many are exon 3 hotspot codons 32-45 versus elsewhere; cross-tabulate any 'Wnt gene mutated' flag against GENOMICS_SUBTYPE / POLE_SUBTYPE / MSI_STATUS and LOG2_VARIANT_PER_MBP in data_clinical_sample.txt. IF FOUND: make CTNNB1 exon 3 hotspot mutation the primary Wnt-activation variable, treat non-hotspot CTNNB1 and other Wnt-gene mutations in hypermutated tumours as unclassified (sensitivity analysis with them excluded and with them included), and do not let a pathway-level 'any mutation' flag stand in for Wnt activity because it mostly measures mutation burden. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5797067/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6354055/ ; https://pathsocjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/path.5372 ; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-025-02496-5

label: Prefer RSEM over z-score files for the TERT comparison
text: PITFALL: Using the cBioPortal z-score files as if they were tumour-vs-normal or normally distributed values. Both z-score files are computed against tumour samples only (all samples, or only samples diploid for that gene); the source data are not normal, 'z>2' thresholds are arbitrary, and the diploid-referenced file shifts with the gene's copy-number pattern and can be NA for genes with little variation. cBioPortal itself recommends the all-samples version; sample ranking is the same in either. CHECK: confirm TERT is present and non-NA in each expression file; confirm a rank-based test gives the same answer on RSEM and on all-samples z-scores. IF FOUND (TERT NA in a z-score file, or answers differ between files): take data_mrna_seq_v2_rsem.txt as the primary expression measure, use the all-samples z-scores only as a cross-check, and do not define 'elevated' by a z>2 cut-off as the only analysis. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/z-score-normalization-script/ ; https://groups.google.com/g/cbioportal/c/MnHuBhjt368 ; https://groups.google.com/g/cbioportal/c/fbSZMjCzoTI

label: Pitfall 6: low depth at GC-rich TERT promoter; use CI-based clonal rule
text: PITFALL: Read-count noise at the TERT promoter. The promoter is >80% GC and is captured less efficiently than exons in hybrid-capture panels, so depth there can be much lower than the sample median; a single-locus VAF from few reads has a wide binomial interval, and a point-estimate threshold (CCF >= 0.8 etc.) will then misclassify in both directions. CHECK: for each TERT promoter call compare t_ref_count+t_alt_count with the median depth of that sample's other mutations, and compute a binomial 95% interval for the VAF, propagated to CCF. IF FOUND (low depth / wide intervals): use the interval rule that is standard in the field - call a mutation clonal when the 95% CI of its CCF includes 1 (equivalently P(CCF>0.95) high), subclonal only when the upper bound is below 1 - and report how many calls are simply uninformative; do not report 'all clonal' when the intervals are too wide to exclude subclonality. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8756133/ ; https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4636056/

label: Pitfall 3: Wnt activity score must be target-gene footprint, validated on CTNNB1 mutants
text: PITFALL: The clinical sample table has PATHWAY_ACTIVITY_* columns for EGFR, hypoxia, JAK-STAT, MAPK, NFkB, PI3K, TGFb, TNFa, TRAIL, VEGF and p53 but none for WNT, so a continuous Wnt activity has to be built, and building it from expression of Wnt pathway MEMBERS (ligands, receptors, CTNNB1 mRNA, the Hallmark WNT_BETA_CATENIN set) is unreliable: pathway-member expression does not track pathway activity, whereas downstream target-gene footprints do, and even single targets such as AXIN2 are context dependent. CHECK: build a target-gene score from data_mrna_seq_rsem.txt (z-score then average feedback targets such as AXIN2, NKD1, LGR5, RNF43, ZNRF3, NOTUM, LEF1, TCF7, SP5, APCDD1, those present) and verify it is clearly higher in CTNNB1 exon 3 hotspot-mutant tumours than in wild-type; a score that does not separate the mutants is not measuring Wnt. IF FOUND: use only a score that passes this positive control as the continuous Wnt variable, alongside CTNNB1 hotspot status as the binary one, and require the two definitions to agree in direction before concluding; do not use CTNNB1 mRNA/protein level alone, since activating mutations stabilise rather than transcriptionally induce beta-catenin. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5750219/ ; https://wnt.stanford.edu/signaling-components-wnt-targets ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7697568/ ; https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4200060/

label: Wild-type group is heterogeneous: IDH/ATRX/ALT and TERT copy number
text: PITFALL: The TERT-promoter-wild-type group in glioblastoma is biologically mixed, which can either inflate or hide the mutant-vs-wild-type expression difference. IDH-mutant / G-CIMP / ATRX-mutant tumours maintain telomeres by ALT and have near-absent TERT mRNA, while about half of IDH-wild-type, TERT-promoter-wild-type glioblastomas raise TERT through rearrangements upstream of TERT, and TERT amplification and promoter methylation also raise it. CHECK: cross-tabulate TERT promoter status with IDH1_MUTATION and G_CIMP_METHYLATION (clinical sample table), ATRX mutation (MAF), and TERT copy number (data_cna.txt GISTIC value and data_linear_cna.txt). IF FOUND (imbalance between groups): keep the unadjusted mutant-vs-rest comparison as the primary answer, because the hypothesis is about correlation, then repeat it within IDH-wild-type / non-G-CIMP samples and with TERT copy number as a covariate (or excluding TERT-amplified samples); call the result robust only if direction and rough size hold in the stratified analysis. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5970234/ ; https://doi.org/10.1038/ng.3781 ; https://www.mdpi.com/2072-6694/13/5/1147 ; https://doi.org/10.1186/s40478-019-0732-4

label: Pitfall 7: copy number / multiplicity at TERT locus shifts VAF
text: PITFALL: Ignoring local copy number and multiplicity at TERT (chr5p15.33). 5p gain or TERT amplification, or LOH, changes the expected VAF of a clonal mutation: a mutated allele that is gained gives VAF above purity/2 (CCF>1 if m=1 is assumed), a mutation on the non-gained allele gives a lower VAF and looks subclonal. The discrete values in data_cna.txt (-2..2) are thresholded calls, not absolute copy number, and seg.mean in data_cna_hg19.seg is a log2 ratio NOT corrected for purity (low purity compresses it toward 0). CHECK: for every TERT-promoter-mutant sample, look up the seg.mean of the segment covering chr5:1295228 and the data_cna value for TERT; convert with n = (2*2^seg.mean - 2*(1-purity))/purity. IF FOUND (segment not near 0): compute CCF under each admissible multiplicity (m=1 and m=gained copies), cap at 1, and flag samples whose clonal/subclonal call flips with m; if the segment is near 0 the simple diploid formula CCF=2*VAF/purity is adequate. SOURCE: https://cnvkit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/calling.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10832148/

label: Pitfall 4: genomic subtype / histology confounds Wnt associations
text: PITFALL: CTNNB1 mutation / Wnt activation in endometrial carcinoma sits almost entirely in endometrioid, copy-number-low (NSMP) tumours and is rare in serous / CNV-high tumours, so a pooled Wnt-versus-histone-acetylation association can be just the endometrioid-versus-serous or genomic-subtype difference (which changes thousands of proteins and PTMs) rather than anything about Wnt. CHECK: cross-tabulate Wnt status against GENOMICS_SUBTYPE (data_clinical_sample.txt) and HISTOLOGIC_TYPE and grade (data_clinical_patient.txt); test whether the histone acetyl sites differ by subtype/histology on their own. IF FOUND: repeat the Wnt test (a) within endometrioid tumours only and within CNV-low only, and (b) in a linear model with GENOMICS_SUBTYPE and histology as covariates; base the conclusion on the stratified/adjusted effect, and report if the association exists only in the pooled data. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/nature12113 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9072012/ ; https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/oncology/articles/10.3389/fonc.2022.1009345/full

label: A null claim needs effect size and CI, not just p>0.05
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is a claim of NO correlation, and a non-significant p-value in a small overlap of samples is not evidence for it (absence of evidence is not evidence of absence); equally, a tiny but significant difference is not automatically 'elevated'. CHECK: report group sizes, the effect size (median difference or fold change, AUC/rank-biserial) with a confidence interval, and the direction; ask whether the CI excludes a biologically meaningful increase (reporter and tumour studies describe roughly 2- to 4-fold higher TERT transcription with promoter mutation, so about 2-fold is a reasonable smallest effect of interest). IF FOUND: label 'False' when called mutants show clearly and significantly higher TERT expression; label 'True' only if the estimate is near zero AND the interval excludes a meaningful increase (equivalence/TOST logic) with adequate n per group; if the test is non-significant but the CI is wide or a group has only a handful of samples, say the data are underpowered rather than claiming support, and decide the label from the direction and size of the estimate plus the sensitivity analyses. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5502906/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4877414/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12567074/ ; https://doi.org/10.1038/bjc.2014.538

label: Pitfall 8: purity-driven false negatives bias prevalence downward
text: PITFALL: Detection sensitivity depends on purity and depth, so observed TERT promoter prevalence is a lower bound and differs between groups for technical reasons: variant callers lose sensitivity quickly when purity is below 50% or VAF is below about 10%, and the GC-rich promoter adds dropout. Low-purity advanced tumours with no TERT call may be false negatives, not wild-type. CHECK: compare TUMOR_PURITY, specimen type (SPECIMEN_PRESERVATION_TYPE frozen vs FFPE) and number of called mutations between TERT-mutant and TERT-wild-type samples and between histologies; look for samples with purity so low that even the truncal driver was not called. IF FOUND: report prevalence both in all profiled samples and restricted to samples with adequate purity / a detected driver, and treat the all-sample figure as conservative; do not interpret a prevalence difference between histologies without checking it is not a purity difference. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8506910/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8756133/

label: Pitfall 5: finding and reading histone acetyl sites
text: PITFALL: Histone acetylation rows are easy to miss or mis-read in data_acetylprotein_quantification.txt: histones use the OLD gene nomenclature (HIST1H2BB, HIST2H2BF, HIST1H4G, HIST2H4B, HIST3H3, H3F3A, H2AFZ, H2AFX, H2AFY, H1F0, HIST1H1B ...), not H3C1/H4C1 or 'H3'/'H4'; a peptide shared by many identical paralogs is assigned to one arbitrary paralog gene; residue numbers may be offset by +1 from textbook marks if the initiator methionine is counted; and neighbouring lysines on one tail (H4 K5/K8/K12/K16, H3 K9/K14, K18/K23, K27/K36, H2B N-terminus) are measured on the same or overlapping multiply-acetylated peptides, so their values are positional-isomer mixtures and strongly correlated. CHECK: select histone rows by GENE_SYMBOL patterns ^HIST, ^H1F, ^H2AF, ^H3F3 (about 130 site rows over about 30 gene symbols), list the site ids, compare the site numbers with canonical marks to detect an offset, and compute the correlation matrix among histone sites. IF FOUND: treat paralog labels as histone-family labels (H2B, H3, H4, H2A, H1, macroH2A), do not over-interpret a single named lysine, do not count correlated neighbouring sites as independent confirmations, and keep linker histone H1 and macroH2A sites separate from core-histone tail acetylation when summarising. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6161106/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12974565/ ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13148-022-01371-y

label: Pitfall 9: external PTC numbers are not assay-comparable; define criteria first
text: PITFALL: Treating any outside PTC figure as comparable. Published PTC cohorts were mostly exome-sequenced, and exome capture kits do not target or only weakly cover the TERT promoter (systematic kit-specific coverage gaps cause false-negative calls; TERT promoter status had to be added to exome studies as a separate curated attribute and is assessable only in a subset of cases), so PTC prevalence and VAF/clonality from another assay are not like-for-like with deep panel data. Also the hypothesis has two parts (clonal AND highly prevalent) and both need a pre-stated criterion. CHECK: confirm whether the study tables hold any PTC rows or any TERT-status clinical attribute; write down in advance what 'highly prevalent' and 'clonal' will mean (e.g. prevalence with exact 95% CI per histology; proportion of mutant tumours with CCF CI including 1). IF FOUND (comparison must lean on outside knowledge): label that part clearly as background, not as a result of the analysis, keep the in-data evidence (prevalence and clonality in PDTC/ATC) separate, and note assay non-comparability as a limitation rather than testing it statistically. SOURCE: https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0204912 ; https://github.com/cBioPortal/datahub/releases

label: Pitfall 6: multiple testing and correlated histone sites
text: PITFALL: With roughly 130 histone acetyl sites and several possible Wnt definitions, reporting whichever site/definition pair reaches p<0.05 manufactures a 'relationship' (about 6 sites are expected at p<0.05 by chance), and because histone sites are strongly inter-correlated, counting significant sites or permuting features gives badly inflated set-level significance. CHECK: fix the Wnt variable(s) and the histone-site family before looking at p-values; apply Benjamini-Hochberg across all histone sites tested; get a set-level p-value by permuting SAMPLE labels (e.g. 10,000 permutations of Wnt status, statistic = mean absolute t or number of sites below p<0.05) so inter-site correlation is preserved; compare the histone-site result with the background of all ~10,800 acetyl sites. IF FOUND: conclude 'supported' only if sites survive FDR or the sample-permutation set test is significant, with consistent direction across related sites; a few nominal hits that fail FDR are not support, but equally do not call the hypothesis contradicted on an underpowered test - report the group sizes (number of Wnt-active tumours among 95) and effect sizes with confidence intervals. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3458527/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2922896/ ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/1471-2164-11-574

label: Pitfall 7: TMT plex-structured missing values and batch
text: PITFALL: The proteomic tables are multi-plex TMT data (PROTEOMICS_TMT_PLEX and PROTEOMICS_TMT_BATCH in data_clinical_sample.txt); a site not picked in a plex is NA for every sample of that plex, so missingness is plex-structured, not random, and filling NA with 0 or the minimum, or dropping to complete cases, distorts correlations and group tests; plex effects can also mimic biology if Wnt-active tumours are unevenly spread over plexes. CHECK: per histone site count non-missing values overall and within each Wnt group; tabulate missingness by plex; cross-tabulate Wnt status by plex; run a PCA of the acetyl matrix coloured by plex. IF FOUND: do not impute zeros; test each site on its observed values only and require a minimum per group (for example at least 5 Wnt-active and 50 percent of samples overall); if Wnt status is unbalanced across plexes or plex drives a principal component, add plex as a covariate or blocking factor; state how many histone sites were actually testable. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6773557/ ; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1359644623001770 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10949645/

label: Pitfall 8: tumour purity confounding
text: PITFALL: Bulk tumour pieces differ in tumour-cell fraction, and stromal/immune cells have different histone content, histone marks and Wnt-target expression, so both a Wnt target-gene score and histone acetyl levels can co-vary simply through purity, giving a spurious (or masked) association. CHECK: correlate the Wnt variable and each histone acetyl site with PURITY_CANCER, PURITY_STROMA, PURITY_IMMUNE and ESTIMATE_STROMALSCORE / ESTIMATE_IMMUNESCORE in data_clinical_sample.txt (and TUMOR_PURITY in data_clinical_patient.txt). IF FOUND: include purity (or stromal and immune scores) as covariates in the site ~ Wnt model, or use partial correlation, and report whether the association survives. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms9971 ; https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/genetics/articles/10.3389/fgene.2021.642759/full ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8453244/

label: Pitfall 9: relative centred PTM values and global shifts
text: PITFALL: The acetyl values are log-ratios to a pooled reference that have been centred per sample, which assumes most sites do not change; this is relative quantification, so (a) values cannot be compared between different sites, only the same site across samples, and (b) a genuine global rise or fall in histone acetylation in one group can be partly removed or pushed onto other sites by the centring, and a per-sample mean over histone sites is a contrast against the rest of the acetylome rather than an absolute level. CHECK: look at per-sample medians and distributions of the acetyl table (are they all near 0?), and test whether the histone-site average differs by Wnt status relative to the non-histone-site average. IF FOUND: phrase results as relative site-level differences, prefer site-wise tests plus a sample-permutation set test over an 'average histone acetylation' number, and do not re-normalise (quantile or z-score across sites within a sample) before testing. SOURCE: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/phosphonormalizer/inst/doc/vignette.html ; https://doi.org/10.1101/012203 ; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31816396/?dopt=Abstract

label: Pitfall 10: test measured histone acetyl sites, not proxies; prior sites from CBP/p300 mechanism
text: PITFALL: Substituting a proxy for the thing the hypothesis names, or choosing the label 'Not verifiable' when the variables exist: the data DO contain measured histone lysine-acetylation sites (histone rows of data_acetylprotein_quantification.txt) and Wnt variables (CTNNB1 mutations in data_mutations.txt, Wnt target genes in the mRNA table, CTNNB1 protein/phosphosites), so the hypothesis is testable; mRNA or protein levels of HATs/HDACs (EP300, CREBBP, KAT2A/B, HDAC1-3) or acetyl sites on non-histone proteins (EP300/CREBBP auto-acetylation sites, CTNNB1-K666/K671) are supporting context, not histone acetylation itself. CHECK: confirm histone site rows and CTNNB1 mutant samples overlap in the same sample ids (sample columns are patient-style ids such as C3L-00006) and count them. IF FOUND: make the primary test 'histone acetyl sites versus CTNNB1-hotspot status / validated Wnt target score', give H2B N-terminal and H3/H4 tail sites priority as pre-specified, and report HAT/HDAC abundance and non-histone acetylation only as secondary evidence. label: PITFALL: defining PTEN loss of function
text: PITFALL: 'PTEN loss of function' gets mis-defined: either every PTEN row in the mutation file is counted (including missense variants of unknown significance, which are frequent UV passengers in high-TMB melanoma, plus 5'Flank/Intron/in-frame calls), or only mutations are used and deep deletions in data_cna.txt are forgotten, or PTEN CNA value 2 (amplification) is counted as an alteration. Standard definition (OncoKB): truncating mutations (Nonsense, Frame_Shift_Ins/Del, Splice_Site) and homozygous deletion (CNA = -2) are loss of function; missense counts only if a known inactivating variant (e.g. phosphatase-core residues such as C124, G129, R130, R173). CHECK: list every PTEN row in data_mutations.txt (Variant_Classification, HGVSp_Short, Hotspot, t_alt_count/(t_alt_count+t_ref_count)) and the PTEN row of data_cna.txt; build a patient-level flag = truncating mutation OR CNA -2 (primary), and a broad flag = any nonsynonymous PTEN mutation OR CNA -2 (sensitivity). IF FOUND (the two definitions classify patients differently): report results under both and base the conclusion on the strict definition, noting whether the direction is the same. SOURCE: https://www.oncokb.org/gene/PTEN/Truncating%20Mutations ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5986715/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC379112/

label: PITFALL: not profiled is not wild-type
text: PITFALL: In targeted-panel cBioPortal studies a sample with no recorded alteration in a gene is not necessarily wild-type; it may be 'not profiled' if that gene was absent from the panel version used. Here samples were sequenced on three bait versions (bait_v3, bait_v4, bait_v5), the panel matrix has only a 'mutations' column (no CNA column) and no gene lists are supplied, so PTEN coverage per version cannot be read directly. CHECK: tabulate PTEN mutation and PTEN deep-deletion calls by bait version, and confirm PTEN (or neighbouring common genes) has calls in samples from every version; confirm every sample is in the CNA header and the mutation file (already verified: all 66 are). IF FOUND (a bait version with zero PTEN calls and no sign PTEN was covered): do not count those samples as wild-type without comment; rerun excluding that version as a sensitivity analysis. If PTEN calls occur in all versions, treating absence as wild-type is reasonable. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/ ; https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/blob/master/docs/File-Formats.md ; https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/5000

label: PITFALL: undetected PTEN loss in wild-type group
text: PITFALL: The 'PTEN wild-type' comparison group is contaminated with undetected PTEN loss. The CNA table holds only -2/0/2 calls (no hemizygous -1), panel-based deep-deletion calling loses sensitivity in low-purity samples, and PTEN protein can be lost without any detectable genomic lesion (epigenetic/other mechanisms; IHC and genomic deletion are discordant in a meaningful fraction of tumours). Such non-differential misclassification biases the PTEN effect toward the null. CHECK: note that no purity, hemizygous-loss or PTEN protein/expression variable exists in the tables; look at variant allele fractions (t_alt_count/(t_alt_count+t_ref_count)) of driver mutations such as BRAF V600 per sample as a rough purity proxy and see whether PTEN deletions are only called in high-purity samples. IF FOUND: there is no fix inside these tables; treat a weak or null PTEN effect as possibly attenuated, state it as a limitation, and do not describe CNA=0 samples as 'PTEN intact'. A clear effect that survives this dilution is, if anything, conservative. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1158/1538-7445.am2025-2406 ; https://www.nature.com/articles/modpathol201688

label: PITFALL: BRAFi monotherapy vs BRAF+MEK combination
text: PITFALL: Treatment is not uniform. About 12 of 66 patients received a BRAF+MEK inhibitor combination (dabrafenib+trametinib, vemurafenib+cobimetinib) and the rest BRAF-inhibitor monotherapy; combination therapy gives clearly longer PFS than monotherapy in the randomised trials, so an imbalance of regimen between PTEN groups can create or hide a PTEN effect. One patient is annotated 'Vem+cob (leukemia patient)'. CHECK: cross-tabulate PTEN status by AGENT collapsed to monotherapy vs combination (Fisher exact); compare PFS by regimen. IF FOUND (imbalance or a regimen effect on PFS): report a log-rank test/Cox model stratified by monotherapy vs combination, and a sensitivity analysis restricted to BRAF-inhibitor monotherapy (the population the hypothesis names); check the conclusion does not hinge on the leukemia patient. SOURCE: https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaoncology/fullarticle/2694878 ; https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1904059
