label: PITFALL: confounders and over-adjustment
text: PITFALL: Confounding by baseline prognosis, and the opposite error of over-adjusting. PFS on BRAF-targeted therapy is strongly driven by baseline LDH (not in this dataset), ECOG status, number of organ sites with metastasis, tumour burden and M stage; in a retrospective cohort of 66 a chance imbalance in these can drive the PTEN result. But with at most ~66 events a Cox model supports only about 4-6 covariates (10 events per variable), and RESPONSE_TO_TARGET_THERAPY, BORR, RESPONSE_GRADE and OS are post-treatment outcomes, not confounders; adjusting for them or stratifying by them removes the very effect being tested. CHECK: compare ECOG_STATUS, M_STAGE, GREATER_THAN_3_SITES/NUMBER_OF_SITES, RECIST_BURDEN_OF_DISEASE, LIVER_INVOLVEMENT, BRAIN_METS between PTEN groups; count missing values per covariate. IF FOUND (imbalance): give the unadjusted estimate first, then one parsimonious adjusted Cox model with 2-4 pre-treatment covariates (e.g. ECOG, sites >3 or RECIST burden, regimen), using Firth penalisation if unstable; never include response variables; state LDH is unavailable. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1016/s1470-2045(16)30578-2 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6093349/

label: Pitfall: non-significant is not support for null
text: PITFALL: A 'not associated' hypothesis gets labelled True because a small-sample test gives p>0.05; absence of evidence is not evidence of absence, and with only a few dozen paired patients almost any test is underpowered. CHECK: count the informative units (patients who were ERBB2-amplified before trastuzumab and have a post-trastuzumab sample), report the proportion whose post sample lost amplification with an exact (Clopper-Pearson) 95% CI, and compare it with the expected background discordance (~7-12% without anti-HER2 therapy) rather than relying on a p-value alone. IF FOUND: do not treat non-significance as support for the null; base the label on the effect size and its CI versus background (loss well above background contradicts 'not associated'; loss at or below background with a tight CI supports it; say so explicitly if n is too small). SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC351831/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4877414/

label: Pitfall: purity dilution mimics loss of ERBB2 amplification
text: PITFALL: Low tumour purity in the post-treatment biopsy dilutes the ERBB2 log-ratio below the panel's amplification threshold (MSK-IMPACT calls AMP at fold-change >=2, i.e. log2 ratio ~>=1; FC 1.5-2 is 'borderline'), producing a false 'loss of amplification'; NGS-vs-IHC/FISH discrepancies occur mainly with low tumour content and HER2 heterogeneity. CHECK: for every post-treatment sample called non-amplified, look at (a) the continuous ERBB2 value (HER2_IMPACT_LR and the data_cna_hg19.seg segment covering chr17:37.84-37.89 Mb hg19), (b) whether the rest of that sample's seg profile is flat (small spread of seg.mean, other CNAs from the paired pre sample gone too), and (c) somatic VAFs t_alt_count/(t_alt_count+t_ref_count) of mutations shared with the pre sample (e.g. TP53) as a purity proxy. IF FOUND (flat profile, shared-mutation VAFs collapsed): treat that pair as indeterminate, not as loss, and run a sensitivity analysis excluding it; count as true loss only when truncal mutations/other CNAs persist at comparable level while ERBB2 falls. SOURCE: https://www.jmdjournal.org/article/S1525-1578(16)30233-1/fulltext ; https://www.jmdjournal.org/article/S1525-1578(15)00045-8/fulltext ; https://cnvkit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/heterogeneity.html

label: Pitfall: spatial heterogeneity vs temporal selection
text: PITFALL: HER2 is spatially heterogeneous in gastro-oesophageal cancer, so a pre/post difference in ERBB2 status can be sampling of a different region or site, not treatment-driven selection: pooled primary-vs-metastasis HER2 discordance without therapy is ~7% (strict definition) to ~12% (broad), and biopsy-sized samples have a ~24% false-negative rate for HER2-positive tumours. CHECK: for each pair record whether pre and post samples are the same site or primary vs metastasis (SAMPLE_TYPE, SITE_OF_TISSUE_BIOPSY, BIOPSY_OBTAINED); if the data contain same-patient pairs that are both PRE-TX (multi-region/untreated pairs), compute their ERBB2 discordance as an internal background rate. IF FOUND: judge the post-trastuzumab loss rate against that background (internal or the 7-12% literature figure), stratify by same-site vs different-site, and word the conclusion as 'consistent with selection of a non-amplified subclone' rather than proof. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-017-03304-9 ; https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534(19)37150-9/fulltext

label: Pitfall: PRE-TX/POST-TX is not necessarily pre/post trastuzumab
text: PITFALL: The sample column IMPACT_PRE_POST (PRE-TX / POST-TX) is not guaranteed to mean pre/post trastuzumab; it may mean pre/post any systemic therapy, and only HER2-positive patients received trastuzumab (patient TREATMENT '...+BIOLOGIC', DETAILS_FIRST_LINE_COMMENTS mentioning tras). Comparing ERBB2-AMP frequency in all POST-TX vs all PRE-TX samples across the whole cohort (341 samples, mostly HER2-negative, chemo-only) answers a different question and is confounded by who gets re-biopsied. CHECK: restrict to patients with baseline HER2 positivity and documented trastuzumab exposure (HER2_RESPONSE / HER2_TTP_ON_1ST_LINE_MONTHS / HER2_TX_STATUS not NA, or trastuzumab in treatment details) and confirm the POST-TX sample post-dates trastuzumab. IF FOUND: analyse only the trastuzumab-treated, baseline-amplified cohort with within-patient pairs; treat the cohort-wide unpaired PRE vs POST comparison as, at most, supporting context. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1002/ijc.30408 ; https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/

label: Pitfall: pair by patient, use paired tests
text: PITFALL: Treating samples as independent, or mis-pairing them. The study has ~341 samples from ~305 patients; about 34 patients have 2-3 samples, and sample IDs come in several styles (P-xxxx-T01-IMx, YJ-her-00x-P1/M1a, s_YJ_her_0xx_P/M/X) so string matching on sample ID can miss pairs; some same-patient pairs may be two PRE-TX regions rather than pre/post. CHECK: build pairs from PATIENT_ID in data_clinical_sample.txt (not from sample-name parsing), tabulate each multi-sample patient's IMPACT_PRE_POST combination, SAMPLE_TYPE and HER2_IMPACT, and confirm every sample has a column in data_cna.txt and rows in the seg file. IF FOUND: make the patient the unit of analysis; use paired methods (exact/mid-p McNemar on discordant pairs for binary AMP status, Wilcoxon signed-rank on the paired ERBB2 log-ratio); never use chi-square/Fisher across pooled samples as if independent; keep PRE-PRE pairs separate as a heterogeneity control. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3716987/ ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00265-020-02916-y

label: Pitfall: discrete CNA 0 is not diploid, NA is not 0
text: PITFALL: Misreading the cBioPortal discrete CNA matrix. In this study data_cna.txt holds only -2, 0, 2 and NA: 0 means 'no high-level amplification/deep deletion called', NOT diploid (low-level gains and borderline amplification, FC 1.5-2, are coded 0), and NA means the gene is not on that sample's panel version (IMPACT300/341/410/468), not copy-neutral. CHECK: confirm the ERBB2 row has no NA for the paired samples; cross-check the discrete ERBB2 call against sample-level HER2_IMPACT (AMP/DIPLOID), HER2_IMPACT_LR and the seg.mean of the ERBB2 segment, and flag disagreements. IF FOUND: analyse the continuous log-ratio alongside the binary call (a drop from high-level to borderline is partial loss / mixed population, not 'unchanged' or 'diploid'); exclude NA rather than coding it 0. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/ ; https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/ ; https://www.jmdjournal.org/article/S1525-1578(16)30233-1/fulltext

label: Pitfall: define baseline amplification from the pre-treatment NGS sample
text: PITFALL: Baseline misclassification and one-way change. Patients enter a trastuzumab cohort because they tested HER2-positive by IHC/FISH, so status can only move toward negative on retest (regression to the mean), and a tumour that was IHC/FISH-positive but never ERBB2-amplified by NGS at baseline will look like 'loss' if clinical HER2 status is used as the pre value. In published paired series HER2 loss after trastuzumab was far commoner in baseline IHC 2+ than IHC 3+ tumours (80% vs 14%). CHECK: define the pre value from the pre-treatment sequenced sample itself (HER2_IMPACT = AMP, ERBB2 = 2 in data_cna), cross-tabulate it against HER2_IHC_OR_FISH / IHC_HER2, and stratify loss by baseline IHC score and baseline ERBB2 log-ratio. IF FOUND: count 'loss' only as NGS-amplified pre -> non-amplified post on the same assay; report separately the patients who were clinically HER2-positive but not amplified by NGS at baseline (these bear on primary, not acquired, resistance). SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1002/ijc.30408 ; https://doi.org/10.1002/sim.1957

label: Pitfall: acquired vs primary resistance
text: PITFALL: Answering a different question - confusing acquired resistance with primary resistance or with baseline predictors of benefit. Acquired (secondary) resistance means progression after initial benefit on trastuzumab (response or durable stable disease, e.g. >=~4 months); primary resistance is progression at first assessment. An analysis of pre-treatment ERBB2 level/heterogeneity versus PFS or response tests primary resistance and cannot settle a hypothesis about subclone selection under treatment. CHECK: use HER2_RESPONSE (CR/PR/SD/POD), HER2_TTP_ON_1ST_LINE_MONTHS and HER2_TX_STATUS to classify each paired patient, and check that the post sample was taken after progression rather than while still responding (ON TREATMENT). IF FOUND: make the primary analysis the within-patient pre->post change in ERBB2 amplification among patients who progressed after benefit; report best-response=POD patients and on-treatment samples separately. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1158/1078-0432.ccr-17-2781 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5506279/ ; https://doi.org/10.1002/ijc.30408

label: Pitfall: operationalising 'subclone selection' in bulk panel data
text: PITFALL: Bulk targeted-panel data cannot show a 'subclone' directly, so analysts either over-claim clonal selection from a single lost call or wrongly declare the question unanswerable because no column is named 'subclone'. The accepted operational evidence for selection of a non-amplified subclone is: paired samples are clonally related (shared truncal mutations such as TP53 in data_mutations.txt at comparable VAF), other clonal CNAs persist, and the ERBB2 amplicon (ERBB2 plus co-amplified 17q12 neighbours on the panel, e.g. CDK12) is high pre-treatment and absent post-treatment. CHECK: for each pre/post pair list shared vs private mutations with VAFs, and the 17q12 segment seg.mean in both samples. IF FOUND (shared mutations retained + amplicon lost): count it as evidence of selection for an ERBB2-non-amplified population; if the pair shares no mutations or the post sample has no tumour signal, drop the pair as uninformative. Before choosing 'Not verifiable', confirm whether these three ingredients (pre/post pairs, per-sample ERBB2 copy number, trastuzumab exposure/outcome) exist. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7867630/ ; https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-022-02600-6 ; https://doi.org/10.1002/ijc.31184

label: PITFALL targeted mutation rows are a fixed locus list, no allele counts
text: PITFALL: The '-targeted' rows of data_mutations.txt are not per-sample detections: within each patient every targeted sample lists the identical set of loci (verified for all 15 patients), and t_ref_count/t_alt_count are empty in every row of the file, so targeted samples carry no between-sample signal and no allele frequencies exist anywhere. Counting or comparing targeted mutations between tumour and xenograft will always show 100% identity and wrongly look like 'no clonal change'. CHECK: per patient, compare the (chrom,pos,alt) sets across targeted samples and confirm the read-count columns are blank; TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS for targeted samples is derived from the same rows. IF FOUND: exclude targeted rows and targeted TMB from any tumour-vs-xenograft comparison; only the 30 '-whole_genome' samples (mutation presence/absence, data_cna_hg19.seg, data_log2_cna.txt) are informative, and clonal-prevalence (VAF/CCF, PyClone-style) methods cannot be run because they need allele counts plus copy number and purity. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7867630/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4864026/

label: PITFALL private mutation calls between paired samples are largely detection noise
text: PITFALL: Mutations called in one WGS sample but not its pair are mostly a detection problem, not proof of a new or lost clone. With independent per-sample calling, only 36-78% of somatic variants were reproduced between technical replicates of the same DNA and 34-80% of discordant ('heterogeneous') variants were technical noise; without matched normal ~69% of calls were false positives. CHECK: for each patient compute tumour-only, xenograft-only and shared WGS mutation counts, and build a noise baseline from xenograft-vs-xenograft WGS pairs of the same line (SA429 X2A vs X5A, SA501 X1A vs X5A) and from the distribution across patients; ask whether tumour-vs-xenograft discordance clearly exceeds that baseline and whether it is structured (large blocks of private mutations in both directions) rather than a thin scatter. IF FOUND that discordance is small or no larger than baseline: do not read it as clonal selection; rely on evidence that is robust to call noise (large reciprocal private sets, private mutations co-located with segmental copy-number changes) and state that presence/absence alone cannot quantify clone frequencies. SOURCE: https://www.cell.com/cell-reports/fulltext/S2211-1247(18)31635-8 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4482059/

label: PITFALL purity increase at engraftment mimics clonal selection
text: PITFALL: Tumour purity jumps at first engraftment because human stroma is rapidly replaced by mouse stroma whose reads do not count toward the human genome; a purer xenograft yields MORE detected mutations and LARGER log2 copy-ratio amplitudes than the patient tumour with no change in clonal composition (a one-copy gain is log2=0.585 only at 100% purity and shrinks toward 0 as purity falls). Published work explicitly attributes larger patient-vs-PDX than PDX-vs-PDX copy-number deviations to stromal dilution of the patient sample. CHECK: per tumour/xenograft WGS pair, put both seg profiles on common bins and regress xenograft log2 on tumour log2: a high correlation with slope >1 is pure amplitude scaling; also check whether xenograft-only mutations outnumber tumour-only in nearly every pair (the purity signature) and whether TMB is systematically higher in xenografts. IF FOUND: do not use fixed gain/loss thresholds (e.g. +/-0.3) or raw mutation-count/TMB differences as evidence of selection; use scale-invariant comparisons (correlation, or rescale the tumour profile by the fitted slope) and look for bins that deviate from the fitted line (state changes), and treat tumour-only mutations (lost in the purer sample) as far stronger evidence of clonal change than xenograft-only ones. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9981214/ ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41588-020-00750-6 ; https://cnvkit.readthedocs.io/en/stable/calling.html

label: PITFALL mouse read contamination creates false xenograft-private variants
text: PITFALL: Mouse DNA in xenograft samples creates false 'xenograft-only' somatic calls and copy-number artefacts: mouse reads align to ~49% of the human genome (409 cancer genes) and PDX samples can contain up to 70-80% mouse DNA; mouse-specific alleles then look like mutations gained on engraftment. CHECK: among WGS mutations present in a xenograft but absent from its tumour, test recurrence across unrelated patients (identical chrom/pos/alt or the same genes in xenografts of different patients, never in any tumour sample); true private somatic mutations are patient-specific, mouse alleles and mapping artefacts recur. Also look for xenograft-only narrow seg segments recurring at the same coordinates across patients. IF FOUND: remove recurrent xenograft-only variants/segments before measuring tumour-vs-xenograft divergence, and report divergence with and without them. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6844030/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5946891/ ; https://doi.org/10.1186/s12920-019-0551-2

label: PITFALL selection vs bottleneck/drift/spatial sampling at engraftment
text: PITFALL: A genomic difference between the sequenced tumour piece and the xenograft is not by itself fitness-driven selection: PDX establishment imposes a bottleneck in which the graft often represents a single subclone of the region it came from, and large studies found patient-vs-PDX copy-number differences comparable to multi-region variation within one patient tumour, with random fragment-splitting drift a major contributor. Selection versus sampling/drift is normally separated by independent replicate engraftments showing the same clone winning reproducibly. CHECK: look for replicate transplants of the same tumour with informative data (sample IDs with letter suffixes such as X1A/X1B/X1C); in this dataset WGS exists for only one xenograft per passage and replicates have only the uninformative targeted rows, so reproducibility probably cannot be tested. IF FOUND (no informative replicates): state explicitly which meaning of 'clonal selection' the conclusion uses - a change in clonal composition between tumour and engrafted xenograft (testable here) versus deterministic fitness selection as opposed to drift/spatial sampling (not separable here) - and do not claim more than the data can show. label: PITFALL: analytic flexibility and cut-points
text: PITFALL: Analytic flexibility manufactures or erases a result in a small biomarker study: trying several PTEN definitions, several endpoints (PFS, OS, response, RESPONSE_GRADE), data-driven PFS cut-points (e.g. 'PFS > 6 months' chosen after looking) and subgroups, then reporting whichever is significant. Minimum-p-value cut-points inflate false positives severalfold. CHECK: before looking at outcomes, fix one primary analysis: strict PTEN loss-of-function flag vs PFS_MONTHS as a time-to-event/continuous outcome in all 66 patients; list every other analysis as a labelled sensitivity analysis. IF FOUND (results differ across definitions or endpoints): base the label on the pre-specified primary analysis and report the others transparently; do not dichotomise PFS at a data-chosen threshold, and do not switch the endpoint to OS or response rate because the hypothesis is about PFS. label: PITFALL seg profiles differ in segment count and scale; rebin before comparing
text: PITFALL: Segment-level copy-number comparisons are not like-for-like: in data_cna_hg19.seg the xenograft WGS samples have roughly 1.5-3x more segments than the patient tumours (tumours about 4,000-11,000 rows, xenografts about 9,500-19,800), breakpoints do not align between samples, and quantitative CNA comparisons are known to be sensitive to the gain/loss thresholds, baselines and dynamic range used. Counting segments, breakpoints or thresholded 'altered genes' will show xenografts as more altered purely from noise/oversegmentation and purity. CHECK: per sample tabulate segment count, share of segments with small num.mark, and the median/centre of seg.mean (baseline shift); then re-bin every sample onto common fixed bins (e.g. 1 Mb, length- or marker-weighted mean), drop tiny segments, sex chromosomes and bins missing in either sample. IF FOUND: compare pairs on the common bins with a purity-robust metric (correlation, or discordance after rescaling and re-centring each profile) and require a discordant region to be large (multi-Mb / arm-level) before calling it a copy-number difference; published DNA-based analyses that did this still disagree on magnitude (median ~10% of genome discordant in one re-analysis vs 'comparable to multi-region variation' in another), so report the size of the effect, not just its existence. label: Rank-sum/Kruskal-Wallis is not a median test
text: PITFALL: Rank tests are not tests of medians. Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney and Kruskal-Wallis test stochastic ordering, Pr(X1<X2)+0.5*Pr(X1=X2), and can be significant with equal medians or non-significant with different medians unless the group distributions have the same shape and spread; latency intervals are right-skewed with unequal spread. CHECK: if latency data exist, plot/compare the per-group distributions (IQR, range, skew) and report each group's median with n. IF FOUND that shapes/spreads differ: back the 'median is lower' claim with a median-targeted analysis (Mood's median test or permutation test on the median difference, bootstrap CI for the difference in medians, or quantile regression) alongside the rank test, and say which estimand each p-value refers to; Mood's test is robust but low-powered at small n. SOURCE: https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/00031305.2017.1305291 ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Median_test

label: Conjunction hypothesis: test both pairwise contrasts, not only omnibus or pooled
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is a conjunction (RT-AS lower than RT-MPNST AND lower than RT-UPS), so a significant 3-group omnibus Kruskal-Wallis p-value, or a single test of AS versus pooled MPNST+UPS, does not establish it: the omnibus can be driven by one pair, and pooling lets the larger UPS group mask a null AS-vs-MPNST comparison. CHECK: run both pairwise comparisons separately (AS vs MPNST, AS vs UPS), check the direction of each median difference, and report n per group. IF FOUND: require both pairwise tests to be significant in the stated direction (intersection-union logic: each at alpha 0.05, no extra penalty needed for a conjunction), and also report Dunn or pairwise Wilcoxon p-values with Holm adjustment after the omnibus so the verdict is shown not to depend on the adjustment choice. SOURCE: https://alexisdinno.com/files/Dinno2014b.pdf ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4432262/

label: Small MPNST group: exact tests and effect sizes
text: PITFALL: Small, unbalanced groups. In radiation-associated sarcoma series angiosarcoma and undifferentiated sarcoma are each about 40% of cases while MPNST is only about 6%, so an MPNST group may have a handful of patients; asymptotic p-values and Mood's median test are unreliable/underpowered there, and a non-significant result at n<10 is weak evidence. CHECK: count patients (not samples) with non-missing latency per group; note ties. IF FOUND that any group has fewer than about 10: use exact or permutation p-values (e.g. scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu method='exact', permutation_test), report effect size with CI (Hodges-Lehmann shift or bootstrap median difference), and state the group sizes in the reasoning so the reader can judge power. SOURCE: https://www.redjournal.org/article/S0360-3016(19)30173-7/abstract ; https://www.biostathandbook.com/kruskalwallis.html

Radiation-associated sarcoma criteria (Cahan and modifications) require a minimum latent period (variously 6 months, 2 years, 3-4 years), the start point may be first day of RT, end of RT, or primary-cancer diagnosis, and units may be months or years; patients with several RT courses have several possible start dates. CHECK: read the column description for start/end events and unit; look at the minimum, any zero/negative/implausibly small values, and whether all groups share the same floor; confirm one value per patient. IF FOUND mixed units or definitions across rows: harmonise before testing; if a minimum-latency floor is visible, note that medians are conditional on that floor and compare groups only under the same definition. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2373580/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6143936/

label: Histology confounded with primary site and era
text: PITFALL: Histology is confounded with primary tumour site and treatment era. Radiation-associated angiosarcoma arises mostly after breast-conserving RT for breast cancer and shows short latency (about 7-8 years versus about 15 years for other radiation-associated sarcomas), and RT-angiosarcoma only appears in series after the mid-1980s, so an AS-vs-other latency gap can reflect site/era rather than histology. CHECK: cross-tabulate histology against primary cancer / irradiated site, sex and year of RT if such columns exist. IF FOUND strong imbalance: still report the unadjusted comparison the hypothesis asks for, but add a stratified or adjusted analysis (e.g. restricted to non-breast cases, or quantile/rank regression with site as covariate) and say whether the difference persists. SOURCE: https://www.redjournal.org/article/S0360-3016(19)30173-7/abstract ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6143936/

label: Right truncation biases case-only latency comparisons
text: PITFALL: Right truncation in case-only latency data. When only patients who have already developed the second tumour are sampled and the exposure date is found retrospectively, observed latencies are biased toward short times, and more so for groups whose radiation exposure was more recent (they have had less time to show long latencies); a naive comparison of medians can therefore manufacture a 'shorter latency' group. CHECK: if RT dates/years or diagnosis years are available, compare the calendar distribution of RT year and the maximum possible follow-up (data cut-off minus RT date) between groups. IF FOUND that the short-latency group was irradiated more recently: flag the comparison as truncation-biased and, if dates allow, use right-truncation methods (reverse-time Kaplan-Meier/Lynden-Bell estimator, or Cox regression for right-truncated data such as R package coxrt) or restrict groups to a common RT-era window. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9465556/ ; https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1989.10478780

label: cBioPortal clinical file parsing and patient-vs-sample level
text: PITFALL: Parsing and unit-of-analysis errors in cBioPortal clinical files. The clinical tables carry 4 leading '#' metadata lines (display name, description, datatype, priority) before the real header; latency is a patient-level attribute but a patient can have several samples (primary, recurrence, metastasis), so merging onto the sample table duplicates values and inflates n; missing values appear as blank, 'NA', 'n.d.', '[Not Available]' and numeric columns may load as strings. IF FOUND duplicates or non-numeric codes: analyse one row per patient and report how many patients were dropped for missing values. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/

label: PITFALL zero-mutation samples are absent from the MAF - ctDNA-negative denominator
text: PITFALL: In cBioPortal-format data a sample that was sequenced but had zero detected mutations has no rows in data_mutations.txt, so 'ctDNA-negative' patients are invisible if you build the cohort from the MAF; conversely counting only samples in the MAF makes everyone look ctDNA-positive. Discrete CNA values of NA mean 'gene not profiled/not called', not 'no alteration'. CHECK: take the sample denominator from data_clinical_sample.txt / data_gene_panel_matrix.txt (panel ACCESS129 for mutations, CNA, SV), then count samples with no rows in data_mutations.txt, no non-zero non-NA value in data_cna.txt and no row in data_sv.txt; also check samples-per-patient (IDs like P-xxxxxxx-T0n-XS1) so the unit of analysis is the patient. IF FOUND: define ctDNA status explicitly (any somatic alteration detected vs none) from the full profiled denominator, state the definition, and analyse one record per patient (e.g. first plasma sample) rather than per sample. SOURCE: https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/3067 ; https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/blob/master/docs/File-Formats.md

label: PITFALL ctDNA status misclassification - clonal hematopoiesis and low shedders
text: PITFALL: ctDNA-positive/negative status from a plasma cfDNA panel is misclassified in both directions: clonal-hematopoiesis variants (DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1, also TP53, JAK2, PPM1D etc., usually low VAF) are real mutant molecules in plasma but not tumour-derived, so they create false 'ctDNA+'; low-shedding or early-stage tumours and a small panel create false 'ctDNA-'. A 'ctDNA-' group is therefore a mix of truly low-burden disease and assay misses. CHECK: in data_mutations.txt look at Mutation_Status / matched-normal columns (n_alt_count, Matched_Norm_Sample_Barcode) to see whether calls were WBC-filtered, tabulate how many 'positive' patients are positive only through canonical CH genes at low VAF (t_alt_count/(t_alt_count+t_ref_count)), and see how ctDNA status varies by CANCER_TYPE. IF FOUND: run a sensitivity analysis with CH-gene-only patients reclassified as ctDNA-negative, and report whether the conclusion depends on the ctDNA definition. SOURCE: https://aacrjournals.org/clincancerres/article/24/18/4437/80899/False-Positive-Plasma-Genotyping-Due-to-Clonal ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7462123/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10813828/

label: PITFALL non-significant is not 'no benefit' - read the CI and event count
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is a claim of NO benefit in a subgroup. A non-significant p-value for anticoagulation among ctDNA-negative patients is not evidence of no benefit; with few VTE events the confidence interval is wide and still compatible with a clinically meaningful reduction. Power in time-to-event data is driven by the number of events, not patients. CHECK: count VTE events in each cell (ctDNA- x anticoagulated yes/no); report the hazard ratio (or risk ratio) with its 95% CI and ask whether the CI excludes a meaningful benefit (e.g. HR <= ~0.7-0.8), i.e. an equivalence/non-inferiority style reading. IF FOUND (CI spans both no effect and meaningful benefit): the data are inconclusive for the claim rather than supportive; say so in the reasoning and weigh direction and CI, not p>0.05 alone. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6412612/ ; https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5726092/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12567074/

label: PITFALL subgroup claims need an interaction test, not separate p-values
text: PITFALL: Concluding that anticoagulation helps ctDNA-positive but not ctDNA-negative patients because one subgroup is significant and the other is not is invalid; the difference between significant and non-significant is not itself significant, and the ctDNA-negative subgroup has a lower baseline VTE rate and therefore fewer events and less power. CHECK: fit one model with anticoagulation, ctDNA status and their interaction (anticoag x ctDNA) and report the interaction estimate with CI and p-value; also compare absolute risk differences, since the same relative effect gives a smaller absolute benefit at low baseline risk. IF FOUND (no clear interaction): the subgroup effect in ctDNA-negative patients cannot be distinguished from the overall effect; describe the ctDNA-negative estimate with its CI rather than asserting heterogeneity. SOURCE: https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMsr077003 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5687944/ ; https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/full/10.1177/25152459241304347

label: PITFALL confounding by indication for anticoagulation
text: PITFALL: Anticoagulation is not randomised. Patients are anticoagulated because they already had a VTE, have atrial fibrillation, or are judged high-risk (confounding by indication), so a naive treated-vs-untreated comparison can show anticoagulated patients with MORE VTE and falsely suggest no benefit or harm; prevalent users also differ from new users. CHECK: look for variables on prior VTE, indication (prophylactic vs therapeutic), timing of anticoagulation start relative to the blood draw, cancer type, stage and treatment; compare baseline risk profiles of anticoagulated vs not within the ctDNA-negative group. IF FOUND: restrict to patients without prior VTE where possible, adjust or stratify for cancer type/stage and other VTE risk factors (multivariable model, propensity score or IPTW), and state plainly that residual confounding by indication limits any causal 'benefit' reading. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9121653/ ; https://www.ejves.com/article/S1078-5884(23)00707-4/fulltext ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8252086/

label: PITFALL immortal time bias when anticoagulation starts after baseline
text: PITFALL: Immortal time bias. If anticoagulation starts after cohort entry (the plasma draw) and patients are labelled 'anticoagulated' from baseline, the time before starting is VTE-free by construction and is wrongly credited to treatment, exaggerating benefit; the bias grows with the length of that gap. CHECK: see whether the exposure variable is 'on anticoagulation at blood draw' (baseline) or 'ever anticoagulated during follow-up', and whether start dates exist; check that time zero, eligibility and exposure assignment coincide. IF FOUND (exposure defined after baseline): treat anticoagulation as a time-varying covariate in a Cox model, or use a landmark analysis with exposure fixed at the landmark, instead of a baseline yes/no group. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1093/aje/kwm324 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9627261/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3732313/

label: PITFALL death as competing risk for VTE
text: PITFALL: Death is a competing risk for VTE in cancer cohorts. Kaplan-Meier (1-KM) with deaths censored overestimates cumulative VTE incidence, and the distortion differs between groups with different mortality (ctDNA-positive patients typically die sooner than ctDNA-negative), which can distort between-group comparisons. Simple proportions (VTE yes/no) ignore unequal follow-up. CHECK: see whether follow-up time and death/censoring status exist and what share of patients die without VTE in each group. IF FOUND: estimate cumulative incidence with the Aalen-Johansen estimator and compare with Gray's test / Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards for risk questions; use cause-specific Cox hazards (deaths censored) for the aetiological question of whether anticoagulation lowers the VTE rate; report both if they disagree. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4528617/ ; https://www.jthjournal.org/article/S1538-7836(22)08670-6/fulltext ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5326634/

label: PITFALL cancer type confounds ctDNA status and VTE risk in pan-cancer data
text: PITFALL: In a pan-cancer cohort, cancer type drives both ctDNA detectability and baseline VTE risk (e.g. pancreatic, lung, gastric cancers are high-risk for VTE), so a pooled comparison within 'ctDNA-negative' patients mixes cancers with very different baseline risks and anticoagulation rates (Simpson's paradox). CHECK: cross-tabulate CANCER_TYPE against ctDNA status and against exposure/outcome; see whether one or two cancer types dominate the ctDNA-negative anticoagulated cell. IF FOUND: stratify or adjust for cancer type (stratified Cox or cancer type as covariate) and check that the direction of the anticoagulation effect is consistent across the larger cancer types. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1182/bloodadvances.2021006484 ; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jtha.2023.03.037

label: Genotype is not a pathway-activation readout
text: PITFALL: Treating the presence of a mutation (genotype) as if it were a measurement of pathway activation. Mutation status of RAS/RAF genes is a poor proxy for MAPK output; activation is established by readouts such as phospho-MEK/phospho-ERK or a transcriptional output score (e.g. the MPAS genes DUSP4/DUSP6/SPRY2/SPRY4/ETV4/ETV5/PHLDA1/EPHA2/EPHA4/CCND1), or by functional assays of the mutant protein. CHECK: list every column of all five tables (patient: tumour site only; sample: cancer type, sample type, TMB; gene-panel matrix; MAF mutation calls; SV calls) and state explicitly whether ANY column measures pathway output (expression, phospho-protein, RPPA, drug response, functional annotation). IF FOUND that none does: say plainly that the data can show only whether the named variants exist and in which samples, not that they 'lead to activation'; split the hypothesis into (a) variants exist in iCCA samples and (b) they activate the pathway, and report which part the data can address before choosing a label. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41698-018-0051-4 ; https://doi.org/10.1158/1535-7163.mct-08-0972

label: RAF missense effect cannot be read from sequence
text: PITFALL: Assuming a missense change in a RAF-family kinase is activating because of where it sits or by analogy to BRAF V600E. RAF missense mutants fall into different functional classes: RAS-independent activating (monomer or dimer), kinase-impaired or kinase-dead mutants that still raise ERK signalling only via RAS and wild-type CRAF, and neutral passengers. The direction and mechanism of effect was only ever established by in-vitro kinase assays and pERK measurements in cells, never from sequence. CHECK: look for any functional-effect column in the MAF (the given header has Consequence, Variant_Classification, HGVSp, Hotspot, Annotation_Status and no functional/oncogenic-effect field). IF FOUND absent: do not assert gain-of-function from domain position or residue conservation; describe the variant's location only as context, not as evidence of activation. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/nature23291 ; https://www.cell.com/fulltext/S0092-8674(04)00215-6

label: Oncotator amplification-peak columns are gene annotations, not sample CNA calls
text: PITFALL: data_mutations.txt carries Oncotator columns named TCGAscape_Amplification_Peaks, Tumorscape_Amplification_Peaks, TCGAscape_Deletion_Peaks and Tumorscape_Deletion_Peaks; these are static gene/region-level annotations copied from reference databases onto every variant in that locus, NOT copy-number calls for the sample carrying the variant, so using them as evidence of focal amplification in a subtype is invalid (they also exist only for samples that happen to have a mutation in that gene). CHECK: for one gene, confirm the column value is identical across all samples/variants in that gene and unrelated to subtype. IF FOUND: do not use these columns (or ploidy) as per-sample amplification data; treat focal amplification as unmeasured in the MAF. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7350419/ (Oncotator annotates variants with variant- and gene-centric information from 14 pooled reference resources).

label: Predicted-damaging is not gain-of-function
text: PITFALL: Using Variant_Classification = Missense_Mutation, or an in-silico 'damaging/deleterious' prediction (SIFT, PolyPhen, REVEL and similar), as support for activation. These predictors score disruption/conservation, do not distinguish gain from loss of function, and perform worse on gain-of-function variants (which are often predicted benign). Under the ClinGen/CGC/VICC somatic oncogenicity SOP computational evidence is only 'supporting' (OP1, 1 point), whereas well-established functional studies are 'strong' (OS2, 4 points); a novel non-hotspot missense with only domain location (OM1, 2) + computational (OP1, 1) + absent from gnomAD (OP4, 1) reaches about 4 points, which is the variant-of-unknown-significance range (likely oncogenic needs 6 or more). CHECK: note which evidence codes could actually be scored from the supplied tables. IF FOUND that only computational/positional evidence is available: classify the variants as of unknown significance on the data alone and do not upgrade to 'activating'. SOURCE: https://www.clinicalgenome.org/site/assets/files/7465/sop_for_classification_of_oncogenicity_of_somatic_variants_version_1_0-1.pdf ; https://doi.org/10.1155/2023/8857940

label: Do not infer focal amplification from VAF or ploidy
text: PITFALL: Trying to infer focal amplifications from a somatic MAF (variant allele fraction from t_alt_count/t_ref_count, or the sample-wide ABSOLUTE ploidy) is not valid: focal amplification is defined from segmented copy-number profiles (GISTIC separates short focal events from arm-level gains using segment length and amplitude), VAF depends jointly on purity, total copy number, mutant-allele multiplicity and clonality, and amplified wild-type genes with no point mutation are invisible in a MAF. CHECK: confirm no segment-level or gene-level copy-number values exist before attempting any amplification analysis. IF FOUND (none exist): do not report a VAF- or ploidy-based 'amplification' result as a test of the hypothesis; at most mention it as an uninterpretable proxy. SOURCE: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/gb-2011-12-4-r41 and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12239336/.

label: Hotspot flag is recurrence, not function
text: PITFALL: Misreading the MAF 'Hotspot' column. It flags residues that are statistically recurrent in large pan-cancer cohorts (cancerhotspots.org); most functional alleles are rare (the long tail: about 80% of hotspots occur in 1 in 1,000 or fewer patients) and a newly described variant will normally be Hotspot=0. Hotspot=0 is therefore not evidence against function, and Hotspot=1 is evidence of selection, not a measurement of pathway activation in these tumours. CHECK: read the Hotspot value for the gene-of-interest rows but also tabulate how many rows in the whole file are Hotspot=1 to see whether the column is informative at all. IF FOUND Hotspot=0: do not use it to call the hypothesis False; IF FOUND Hotspot=1: treat it as supporting evidence of recurrence only. SOURCE: https://aacrjournals.org/cancerdiscovery/article/8/2/174/6249/Accelerating-Discovery-of-Functional-Mutant ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4744099/

label: MAF denominators and Variant_Classification filter for KIT
text: PITFALL: A MAF lists only samples that have a mutation, and the 274 MB MAF here is large enough to include silent and possibly non-coding calls, so (a) using MAF sample counts as the denominator drops unmutated samples and (b) counting every KIT row as 'KIT-mutated' counts silent/intron/UTR/flank passengers. CHECK: build denominators from data_clinical_sample.txt restricted to samples listed as profiled in data_gene_panel_matrix.txt and having a non-missing MUTATION_TYPE subtype; tabulate Variant_Classification for Hugo_Symbol exactly equal to 'KIT' (not substring, which would catch KITLG); verify one sample per patient and collapse multiple KIT variants in a sample to one mutated/not flag. IF FOUND: count a sample as KIT-mutated only for protein-altering classes (Missense_Mutation, Nonsense_Mutation, Frame_Shift_Del/Ins, In_Frame_Del/Ins, Splice_Site, Nonstop_Mutation, Translation_Start_Site), and treat profiled samples absent from the MAF as wild-type, not missing. SOURCE: https://www.biostars.org/p/102049/ and https://rdrr.io/bioc/maftools/src/R/validateMaf.R.

label: Promoter absence: first check file can contain non-coding calls
text: PITFALL: A 'mutation X is absent' claim gets labelled True (or Not verifiable) from an empty gene-symbol lookup without first establishing whether the mutation file can show promoter/non-coding variants at all; many cBioPortal-style MAFs carry only coding calls because the portal's loader skips Silent, Intron, 3'UTR, 3'Flank, 5'UTR, 5'Flank, IGR and RNA (5'Flank kept only for TERT), whereas other study files keep everything. CHECK: tabulate Variant_Classification over the whole data_mutations.txt and per sample; see whether 5'Flank, 5'UTR, IGR, Intron rows exist and in how many samples. IF FOUND: if non-coding classes are present the hypothesis is testable from the data (any promoter hit for the gene contradicts 'absent'; none in assayed samples supports it); if the file holds only coding classes, absence of promoter rows is uninformative and the claim is Not verifiable. SOURCE: https://groups.google.com/g/cbioportal/c/tqVhYFqWvwo ; https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/895

label: Find the variants robustly before concluding
text: PITFALL: Concluding a variant is absent (or present) from a brittle string match. Protein-change strings depend on the annotated transcript/isoform and format (HGVSp_Short 'p.N217I' vs HGVSp 'p.Asn217Ile'), and the named variants may have been found in samples that are not in the deposited whole-exome table (cBioPortal deposits often hold only the discovery cohort; the gene-panel matrix here says WXS for mutations and SVs). CHECK: pull ALL rows with Hugo_Symbol ARAF (also match by Entrez_Gene_Id and by Chromosome X coordinates), print Tumor_Sample_Barcode, HGVSp, HGVSp_Short, Protein_position, Codons, Transcript_ID; search the whole file for residue numbers 217 and 322; confirm every sample in the clinical table appears in the gene-panel matrix as profiled. IF FOUND that the named variants are missing: that means the key variable is not in the data (cannot settle), not that the hypothesis is contradicted; IF FOUND under a different numbering: reconcile by codon/coordinate before concluding. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/

label: Mutation burden / passenger confounding of KIT frequency across subtypes
text: PITFALL: In UV-driven cutaneous melanoma the mutation burden is very high and differs strongly between genomic subtypes (the UV-high BRAF/RAS/NF1 groups carry many passenger mutations, Triple-WT tumours typically far fewer), so a raw 'any nonsynonymous KIT mutation' frequency in the comparison groups is inflated by passengers and can mask or distort a real enrichment of driver KIT mutations in Triple-WT; Fisher-type tests also assume every tumour has the same alteration probability, which is false when burden varies. CHECK: compare TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS and UV_SIGNATURE across MUTATION_TYPE groups; list each KIT variant by subtype with its protein change, the MAF 'Hotspot' flag, UV-type context (C>T at dipyrimidines) and the sample's TMB. IF FOUND: report the result both for any protein-altering KIT mutation and for recognised activating KIT hotspots only (melanoma drivers cluster in exons 11, 13 and 17, e.g. L576P, K642E, W557/V559, D816, N822), and/or fit a logistic regression of KIT status on subtype adjusting for log TMB (Firth-penalised if cells are sparse); base the conclusion on the burden-robust analysis. SOURCE: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13059-016-1114-x and https://doi.org/10.1097/cmr.0000000000000116 and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6508748/.

label: Promoter mutations appear as 5'Flank / 5'UTR / IGR in MAF
text: PITFALL: Promoter mutations are not labelled 'promoter' in a MAF. vcf2maf maps VEP upstream_gene_variant (default within 5 kb of the transcript start) to 5'Flank, 5_prime_UTR_variant to 5'UTR, and regulatory_region/TF_binding_site/intergenic variants to IGR; searching for the word 'promoter' or only for 5'Flank misses real promoter hits. CHECK: for the gene of interest pull every row with Variant_Classification in {5'Flank, 5'UTR, IGR, RNA, Intron} near its 5' end and inspect Consequence, DISTANCE (bp to transcript for upstream variants), HGVSc (c.-N notation for 5'UTR) and cDNA_position. IF FOUND: count 5'Flank rows and 5'UTR rows close to the transcription start as promoter mutations (papers on UV-tumour promoter hotspots define them as within a few hundred bp of the TSS, which often lies inside the annotated 5'UTR); report the class breakdown instead of a single yes/no on '5'Flank'. SOURCE: https://github.com/mskcc/vcf2maf/issues/33 ; https://journals.plos.org/plosgenetics/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pgen.1006773

label: No actionability column: must build explicit rules
text: PITFALL: The study tables carry no actionability annotation (the mutation file has only a Hotspot flag; there is no ONCOGENIC, HIGHEST_LEVEL or OncoKB column in mutations, CNA or SV files), so 'clinically actionable' is not a ready-made variable and any fraction depends on a rule set the analyst builds. CHECK: confirm the column lists of data_mutations.txt, data_cna.txt, data_sv.txt and data_clinical_sample.txt; note that gene, protein change (HGVSp_Short), Variant_Classification, CNA call, fusion partners and tumour type (ONCOTREE_CODE, CANCER_TYPE) are exactly the inputs a knowledgebase such as OncoKB uses to assign a level. IF FOUND: write down an explicit gene x alteration x tumour-type rule table (OncoKB-style standard-care levels 1-2, optionally level 3), apply it per sample, state it in the reasoning, and decide deliberately whether a fraction that rests on your own rule table is firm enough to support or contradict a point claim. SOURCE: https://github.com/oncokb/oncokb-annotator/blob/master/README.md ; https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/PO.17.00011

label: Mutual exclusivity is weak and underpowered here
text: PITFALL: Using mutual exclusivity with known pathway drivers (e.g. KRAS, NRAS, BRAF, receptor-kinase fusions) as proof that a gene activates the same pathway, in a cohort of only a handful of samples. Fisher/pairwise tests assume identically distributed samples and are confounded by tumour mutation burden and subtype (most apparent exclusivity is explained by these, not by pathway structure), and with fewer than about 10 samples and 1-2 carriers the smallest attainable p-value is usually above 0.05, so the test cannot be informative in either direction. CHECK: count samples (clinical sample table) and carriers; compute the minimum attainable Fisher p-value given the margins; compare TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS of carriers vs non-carriers. IF FOUND underpowered: report the co-alteration pattern descriptively only; do not call exclusivity 'support' for activation and do not call a non-significant test 'contradiction'. SOURCE: https://www.cell.com/cell/fulltext/S0092-8674(19)30503-3 ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13059-016-1114-x

label: Small subgroup, rare event: exact test, effect size, power
text: PITFALL: The Triple-WT group is a small subtype and KIT mutations are rare, so the 2x2 table (Triple-WT vs other subtypes by KIT mutated vs not) will have small or zero cells; a chi-square test is invalid there, a non-significant p-value is not evidence against enrichment, and a significant p-value from scanning many genes is not the same as a pre-specified test of KIT. CHECK: print the full 2x2 counts and per-subtype proportions; check expected cell counts (<5 means exact methods). IF FOUND: use Fisher's exact test on the single pre-specified gene (state one- or two-sided up front; 'enrichment' is directional), report the odds ratio with an exact confidence interval (Haldane-Anscombe +0.5 if a cell is zero) and the raw proportions, and judge 'supports / contradicts / inconclusive' from direction and effect size together with the p-value rather than from p<0.05 alone. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1136/jfprhc-2013-100747 and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2852239/ and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3743540/.

label: Search promoter by coordinates and all_effects, not Hugo_Symbol only
text: PITFALL: Filtering the MAF on Hugo_Symbol == gene misses promoter variants because each variant is assigned to ONE picked transcript by severity: a variant upstream of gene A that also lies in an intron/UTR/exon of a neighbouring or antisense gene B is filed under B's symbol, and one beyond the annotator's upstream distance is filed as IGR with no useful symbol; also Entrez_Gene_Id may be 0/blank in these files so ID lookups fail. CHECK: (1) grep the all_effects column (lists every gene,consequence,transcript) for 'GENE,upstream_gene_variant' and 'GENE,5_prime_UTR_variant'; (2) derive the gene's locus from its own rows in the MAF (Chromosome, min/max Start_Position, NCBI_Build; strand from whether cDNA_position falls as genomic position rises) and pull ALL rows within about +/-5 kb of the gene's 5' end regardless of Hugo_Symbol - for a minus-strand gene the promoter is at HIGHER coordinates than the gene body. IF FOUND: count those coordinate-matched rows as promoter mutations of the gene even though Hugo_Symbol names another gene; do not use remembered hg38 coordinates on a GRCh37 file. SOURCE: https://github.com/mskcc/vcf2maf/blob/main/vcf2maf.pl ; https://forum.depmap.org/t/in-25q3-mutation-annotation-vep-distance/4528

label: Actionable fraction depends on level cutoff and KB date
text: PITFALL: The fraction of samples called 'actionable' swings several-fold with the evidence-level cutoff and the knowledgebase date: the OncoKB paper reported 41% of tumours with any potentially actionable alteration but only 7.5% at standard-care level, and re-annotating the same 47,271 tumours gave 8.9% (2017 OncoKB) versus 31.6% (2022 OncoKB) at level 1-2. CHECK: compute the fraction under at least three definitions: (a) standard-care only (FDA-label or guideline biomarker in that tumour type), (b) plus investigational/clinical-evidence level 3, (c) plus off-tumour-type (3B) and biological-evidence level 4 and resistance markers; see whether 20% sits inside or outside the range. IF FOUND: if the verdict flips between definitions, say so explicitly, prefer the definition that fits the era of the samples (panel versions IM3-IM7 and ACCESS129 indicate the era), and never report a single number without naming its definition. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10784742/ ; https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/PO.17.00011

label: Co-occurring pathway drivers confound attribution
text: PITFALL: Attributing presumed pathway activation to the gene of interest when the same tumour carries another alteration that activates the same pathway. Kinase-impaired RAF mutants in particular depend on, and co-occur with, upstream RAS activation (RAS mutation, NF1 loss, receptor-kinase activation), so co-occurrence does not refute a role and absence of co-occurrence does not prove one. CHECK: build a per-sample table of all alterations in RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK and upstream receptor-kinase genes from BOTH data_mutations.txt and data_sv.txt (fusions live only in the SV file) for carriers and non-carriers. IF FOUND a co-occurring canonical driver in a carrier: any activation cannot be assigned to the variant of interest from these data; IF none: record it as 'consistent with' only. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/nature23291 ; https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/82/1/12/674854/BRAF-Mutations-The-Discovery-of-Allele-and-Lineage

label: Subtype is a residual class from the same mutation data: choose comparison group explicitly
text: PITFALL: The subtype label (MUTATION_TYPE in data_clinical_sample.txt: BRAF hotspot / RAS hotspot / NF1 / Triple-WT style categories) is itself derived from the same mutation calls, and Triple-WT is a residual class defined by the absence of other MAPK drivers, so the choice of comparison group changes the answer: Triple-WT vs all other samples pooled, vs each other subtype, or vs samples with missing/unclassified subtype are different questions, and unclassified samples must not be folded into either side. CHECK: tabulate MUTATION_TYPE including NA/'-'/blank values and confirm the exact spelling of the Triple-WT category; compute KIT mutation frequency in every subtype separately. IF FOUND: use Triple-WT vs all other classified samples as the primary contrast, show the per-subtype frequencies as a sensitivity check (enrichment should hold against each other subtype, not only against the pooled group), and exclude samples with no subtype label. SOURCE: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13059-016-1114-x (mutual-exclusivity/co-occurrence tests are sensitive to group composition and per-tumour alteration rates).

label: Coding-only / depth / PASS filters remove promoter rows
text: PITFALL: Standard 'clean-up' steps silently delete the very rows that answer a promoter question: keeping only non-synonymous/protein-altering classes (maftools default, cBioPortal import rule), requiring HGVSp/Protein_position to be non-empty, requiring FILTER == PASS, dropping rows with a dbSNP_RS id, or requiring t_depth/t_alt_count thresholds when those columns are '.' or 0 in the file. CHECK: run the gene/region query on the raw, unfiltered table first; then look at how many rows each planned filter removes and whether t_ref_count/t_alt_count/FILTER are actually populated. IF FOUND: apply no coding-only, depth or FILTER filter for this question; if read counts are missing, state that VAF-based QC was impossible rather than discarding rows. SOURCE: https://groups.google.com/g/cbioportal/c/tqVhYFqWvwo ; https://docs.gdc.cancer.gov/Encyclopedia/pages/Mutation_Annotation_Format_TCGAv2/

label: Actionability is tumour-type specific
text: PITFALL: Actionability is tumour-type specific, so a gene-only list misclassifies: the same alteration is standard-care in one cancer and only off-label/investigational in another (e.g. BRAF V600E in melanoma vs other sites, KRAS G12C in lung, ERBB2 amplification in breast/gastric, PIK3CA in breast, IDH1 and FGFR2 fusions in cholangiocarcinoma, FGFR3 in bladder, BRCA1/2 in prostate/breast/pancreas/ovary). This cohort is mixed: mostly non-small cell lung cancer, then prostate, bladder, pancreatic, hepatobiliary, breast and many small groups, with some samples having cancer type NA or unknown primary. CHECK: join every alteration to the sample's ONCOTREE_CODE / CANCER_TYPE before assigning a level; tabulate the actionable fraction by cancer type and see whether lung drives the pooled figure. IF FOUND: apply rules per tumour type, keep in-tumour-type and off-tumour-type hits as separate tiers, and report both. SOURCE: https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/PO.17.00011 ; https://doi.org/10.1158/2159-8290.cd-22-1154

label: Absence of evidence is not contradiction
text: PITFALL: Turning 'no evidence' into 'evidence against'. With a very small case series and no measured outcome, failure to demonstrate an effect (a non-significant test, a missing variable, a variant seen in one sample) is not a contradiction of the hypothesis; equally, a claim found in the hypothesis text is not evidence for itself. CHECK: before choosing a label, write down what observable result in THESE tables would count as contradicting the hypothesis (e.g. a pathway readout that is not raised in carriers) and what would count as supporting it, and check whether either observable exists. IF FOUND that neither can be computed: the honest statement is that the tables cannot test the activation claim; reserve 'False' for a real contradicting measurement and 'True' for a real supporting one, and say which part of the claim (variant presence vs activation) the evidence covers. SOURCE: https://www.bmj.com/content/311/7003/485.full ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC351831/

label: Denominator = samples assayed for non-coding regions
text: PITFALL: The denominator for an 'absent' claim is the samples actually assayed at that promoter, not all samples in the clinical table. Exome capture targets coding exons; flanking promoter/5'UTR sequence is covered only incidentally, and GC-rich promoters are a known low-coverage class, so exome-only samples can lack calls there for technical reasons; mixed designs (e.g. GENE_PANEL 'Exome, Whole Genome', discovery vs validation COHORT) mean samples differ in what was assayed, and samples with no rows in the MAF may be unsequenced rather than wild-type. CHECK: compare sample IDs in the clinical tables with Tumor_Sample_Barcode in the MAF; per sample count 5'Flank/5'UTR/IGR/Intron rows; tabulate by COHORT, GENE_PANEL, PLATFORM. IF FOUND: when concluding absence, count only samples that have non-coding calls as informative and report that n; when hits exist, report them over assayed samples; samples absent from the MAF are 'not profiled', not 'not mutated'. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4053816/ ; https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/3067

label: MutSig table is cohort-level, not subtype enrichment
text: PITFALL: data_mutsig.txt is a cohort-wide MutSig significance table (each gene's nonsilent mutation count tested against a background mutation rate over ALL patients; columns n = nonsilent mutations, npat = patients with at least one nonsilent mutation, nsite = unique sites, nsil = silent mutations, p_cv/p_clust/p_cons/p/q), so KIT's rank or q-value says only whether KIT is mutated above background in the whole cohort and says nothing about enrichment in Triple-WT; a non-significant cohort-level q does not contradict a subtype-specific enrichment and a significant q does not prove it. CHECK: read the KIT row and compare its npat with your own count of KIT-mutated samples from the MAF as a sanity check on your Variant_Classification filter. IF FOUND: use MutSig only as a filter cross-check; the enrichment claim must be tested by the subtype-stratified 2x2 analysis from the MAF and clinical table. SOURCE: https://gdac.broadinstitute.org/runs/analyses__latest/reports/cancer/THCA-TP/MutSigNozzleReport2CV/nozzle.html and https://github.com/getzlab/MutSig2CV.

label: Variant-level, not gene-level, actionability
text: PITFALL: Counting any mutation in an 'actionable gene' overstates actionability; only specific alterations qualify (e.g. EGFR L858R, exon 19 deletions, exon 20 insertions, T790M, not any EGFR missense; KRAS G12C not G12D/G12V; BRAF V600E; MET exon 14 skipping splice/deletion variants or MET amplification; truncating/known deleterious BRCA1/2; kinase fusions of ALK, ROS1, RET, NTRK1-3, FGFR2/3; amplification of ERBB2). Variants of unknown significance and silent/intronic calls are not actionable. CHECK: filter on HGVSp_Short, Variant_Classification and the Hotspot flag for mutations; use only +2 (amplification) and -2 (deep deletion) in data_cna.txt; for data_sv.txt read Event_Info/Annotation and both gene symbols to confirm a real fusion of the right gene rather than any rearrangement or intragenic event. Compare a gene-level count with a variant-level count. IF FOUND: use the variant-level count as primary and report the gene-level count only as an upper bound. SOURCE: https://github.com/oncokb/oncokb-annotator/blob/master/README.md ; https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/

label: Driver vs passenger: VAF, chrX and TMB
text: PITFALL: Arguing driver status from allele fraction or from the mere presence of a mutation without checking passenger likelihood. VAF reflects purity, copy number and clonality together; ARAF is on chromosome X, so it is hemizygous in male tumours and expected VAFs differ by sex, and the patient table has no sex column; in a high-TMB sample any gene is more likely to carry a passenger. CHECK: see whether t_ref_count/t_alt_count are populated at all (they are empty in the first data row of the MAF); compare each carrier's TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS and total mutation count with the rest of the cohort. IF FOUND read counts empty: make no clonality or driver claim from VAF; IF FOUND the carrier is among the most mutated samples: flag the variant as more plausibly a passenger and lower confidence accordingly. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7867630/ ; https://www.cell.com/cell/fulltext/S0092-8674(19)30503-3

query: PITFALL: The supplied tables may not be the cohort the hypothesis is about. The hypothesis concerns radiation-associated sarcomas (RT-AS = angiosarcoma, RT-MPNST, RT-UPS), but the header and first rows of /biodsa-data/data_clinical_patient.txt and data_clinical_sample.txt (library read only headers

label: UV promoter hotspots: adjacent positions and DNPs; count tumours not rows
text: PITFALL: In UV-exposed melanoma, promoter hotspot mutations often occur as C>T at several adjacent bases or as CC>TT dinucleotide changes, so one hotspot shows up as SNP rows at neighbouring positions and as DNP rows whose Start_Position is one base off; exact-position matching or Variant_Type == 'SNP' filtering undercounts, and counting rows instead of tumours overcounts (one tumour can carry two rows in the same promoter). CHECK: match on interval overlap (Start_Position..End_Position) over a window around the 5' end, keep Variant_Type SNP, DNP, TNP, ONP, INS and DEL, then count distinct Tumor_Sample_Barcode / PATIENT_ID. IF FOUND: report number of distinct mutated tumours over assayed tumours and list the positions; treat a cluster of nearby positions as the same promoter event class. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-018-05064-0 ; https://docs.gdc.cancer.gov/Data/File_Formats/MAF_Format/

label: Purity/coverage/assay differences bias mutation detection across subtypes
text: PITFALL: Detection sensitivity for somatic mutations falls sharply with low tumour purity/allele fraction and low depth (e.g. MuTect about 96 percent sensitive at allele fraction 0.2 and 30x but about 59 percent at 0.1), and the cohort mixes primary and metastatic samples and possibly different assays (the gene panel matrix labels samples 'WGS' while the MAF Sequence_Source shows 'WXS'), so a subtype with systematically lower purity or coverage would have KIT mutations under-called. CHECK: compare by subtype the distribution of VAF = t_alt_count/(t_alt_count+t_ref_count) and total depth for all coding mutations, the SAMPLE_TYPE mix (primary vs metastasis), and the panel/Sequence_Source values; confirm every compared sample is profiled for mutations. IF FOUND: note the direction of the bias (under-calling in the group with lower VAF/depth), restrict to samples profiled on the same assay if assays differ, and treat a small difference as inconclusive rather than as contradiction. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3833702/ and https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/molecular-biosciences/articles/10.3389/fmolb.2020.533196/full.

label: Denominator: samples with >=1 somatic alteration across mutation, CNA, SV
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis denominator is 'samples with somatic alterations', not all samples, and cBioPortal-format files make this easy to get wrong: a sample with no mutation simply has no rows in data_mutations.txt (it was still profiled), and a sample can be altered only by a copy-number change or a structural variant. The gene panel matrix lists about 1,445 samples while the mutation file has about 7,280 rows. CHECK: build three sample sets (>=1 row in mutations, >=1 gene at +2/-2 in CNA, >=1 row in SV), take their union as 'samples with somatic alterations', and compare its size with the number of samples in data_gene_panel_matrix.txt / data_clinical_sample.txt. Compute actionable/altered and actionable/all-profiled side by side. IF FOUND: use the union as the denominator for the hypothesis as worded, report the all-samples fraction as a sensitivity check, and flag if the two give different verdicts. SOURCE: https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/5000 ; https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/

label: Absent/present is about occurrence, not driver status
text: PITFALL: Confusing 'present' with 'driver'. Recurrent promoter mutations in melanoma are frequently passenger hotspots produced by elevated UV damage at ETS-type motifs (TTCCG context), so analysts are tempted to dismiss observed promoter hits as non-functional, or to demand recurrence, significance or expression evidence before counting them. A hypothesis that says mutations are 'absent' is about occurrence only. CHECK: read the hypothesis wording; list every somatic row in the promoter window with sample, position, alleles. IF FOUND: any validated somatic promoter mutation in a tumour of the stated type contradicts 'absent' irrespective of whether it is a driver; mention passenger-hotspot biology as context only, not as a reason to change the label. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6329521/ ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-023-38265-3

label: Data layout for CRPC-by-gene analysis
text: DATA LAYOUT (headers only, no analysis): 424 patients, exactly one tumor sample each. The castration-resistance outcome is split across two files: the time is SMP_CRPC_MONTHS in data_clinical_patient.txt (months from SAMPLE COLLECTION to castration resistance or last follow-up; declared STRING but numeric, min 0, six values equal 0) and the event flag is IS_CRPC (Yes=240, No=184) in data_clinical_sample.txt; join on PATIENT_ID. Covariates available: DZ_VOLUME (high 213 / low 211), DENOVO_METASTATSIS (de-novo 275 / recurrence 149), ANDROGEN_DEPRIVATION_THERAPY = sample taken on continuous ADT (No 330 / Yes 91 / NA 3), BIOPSY_GLEASON_SCORE, PSA, TISSUE_SITE, TUMOR_PURITY (5 missing), GENE_PANEL (IMPACT341 37 / 410 154 / 468 233). data_cna.txt holds only the values -2, 0, 2 and NA; AR, SPOP and TP53 have no NA in any sample, so all 424 samples are profiled for all three genes. data_mutations.txt has no OncoKB/oncogenic annotation column (only Variant_Classification, HGVSp_Short, Hotspot, etc.).

label: Zero hits: rule of three, only meaningful if region was assayed
text: PITFALL: Zero observed events in a small cohort is weak evidence of true absence: with n assayed tumours and no hits, the upper 95% confidence bound on the true frequency is about 3/n (0 of 20 still allows about 14%). CHECK: after the coordinate-based search, record n = tumours assayed at the region and k = tumours with a hit. IF FOUND: if k = 0 and the region was assayed, the data support the claim but state the 3/n bound in the reasoning; if k >= 1 the claim is contradicted outright and no test is needed; do not run a significance test to decide between them. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.1997.10473947 ; https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjqs-2013-002246

label: Pitfall 1: crude proportions vs time-to-event
text: PITFALL: Treating 'rate of castration resistance' as the crude proportion IS_CRPC=Yes per gene group (chi-square/Fisher) ignores censoring; 184 of 424 patients are censored and follow-up length can differ by group, so crude proportions under-count events and can reverse or erase a real difference. CHECK: compare follow-up among censored patients (SMP_CRPC_MONTHS where IS_CRPC=No) between altered and wild-type groups; confirm the event flag (sample file) and time (patient file) are joined correctly. IF FOUND (it will be: censoring is present): use time-to-event methods with time=SMP_CRPC_MONTHS, event=IS_CRPC — Kaplan-Meier + log-rank, Cox hazard ratio with 95% CI, or events per person-time rate ratio; report the crude proportion only as a description. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6903828/ ; https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1912.00263

label: CNA matrix NA = not profiled
text: PITFALL: In the discrete CNA matrix NA means 'not profiled for copy number', not 'no alteration', and whole blocks of sample columns are NA (visible already in the first data row of data_cna.txt); the matrix may also not contain every sample. Treating NA as 0, or dropping samples absent from the matrix, changes both numerator and denominator. CHECK: count per sample how many genes are NA in data_cna.txt, which samples are missing from its header, and cross-tabulate that against GENE_PANEL and the cna column of data_gene_panel_matrix.txt. IF FOUND: treat those samples as unassessed for CNA (they can still be altered or actionable through mutations or SVs), do not count them as CNA-negative when describing copy-number results, and say that amplification-based actionability (ERBB2, MET) is under-ascertained in them. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/ ; https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/1702

label: CNA burden: segment rows are not alterations
text: PITFALL: Counting rows of the .seg file as 'number of copy number alterations' is wrong, because a seg file lists every segment including copy-neutral ones, so raw segment count mostly reflects noise and segmentation settings rather than biology. CHECK: for each sample compute several burden metrics on autosomes: (a) number of segments with |seg.mean| above a threshold, (b) fraction of genome altered = summed length of segments with |seg.mean| >= threshold divided by summed length of all measured segments of that sample, (c) number of chromosome arms/whole chromosomes with length-weighted mean beyond threshold, and compare them with the raw segment count. IF FOUND that the ranking of lesion types differs between raw segment count and thresholded metrics: base the conclusion on thresholded event counts and FGA, and report raw segment count only as a noise indicator. SOURCE: https://peerj.com/articles/15244/ ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41698-023-00408-6 ; https://groups.google.com/g/cbioportal/c/oTNy7Ip6xK0

label: Pitfall 2: time origin and samples already on ADT
text: PITFALL: Time zero is tumor sample collection, not ADT start, and 91 of 424 samples were taken while already on continuous ADT. Patients sampled on ADT have already used up part of their time to resistance (prevalent-user bias / heterogeneous time origin; informative cohort entry), so their sample-to-CRPC times are systematically shorter regardless of genotype. No ADT-start or diagnosis date is in the tables, so a risk-set (left-truncation) correction is not possible. CHECK: compare time to CRPC between ANDROGEN_DEPRIVATION_THERAPY Yes vs No, and cross-tabulate each gene's alteration status against that column. IF FOUND: adjust for or stratify the Cox model on ANDROGEN_DEPRIVATION_THERAPY, and run a sensitivity analysis restricted to samples taken off ADT (No, n=330); do not trust a gene effect that disappears in the off-ADT subset. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9190030/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9992002/ ; https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjmed-2024-001280

label: Restrict to stated histology and confirm hits are somatic
text: PITFALL: Counting hits in the wrong tumours or counting germline variants. The claim is about one histology; study tables may mix pure and mixed subtypes or cohorts, and promoter SNPs at common polymorphic sites can slip through as 'somatic'. CHECK: join MAF Tumor_Sample_Barcode to data_clinical_sample (CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED, ONCOTREE_CODE, DETAILED_SAMPLE_HISTOLOGY_CATEGORY, SOMATIC_STATUS) and confirm hits lie in tumours of the stated type with a matched normal; look at Mutation_Status, Match_Norm_Seq_Allele, dbSNP_RS, GMAF and ExAC_AF for each hit. IF FOUND: exclude a hit only if it has appreciable population allele frequency or is flagged germline; a dbSNP id alone is not grounds for exclusion (somatic hotspots also have rs ids); report results for all tumours of the type and, as a sensitivity check, for the pure-histology subset. SOURCE: https://docs.gdc.cancer.gov/Encyclopedia/pages/Mutation_Annotation_Format_TCGAv2/ ; https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/

label: Mixed plasma (ACCESS129) and tissue (IMPACT) samples
text: PITFALL: The study mixes two very different assays in one sample table: a 129-gene plasma cell-free DNA panel (GENE_PANEL ACCESS129, roughly 850 samples, Sample Type often 'Unknown') and tissue tumour panels of 341-505 genes (IMPACT341/410/468/505, roughly 600 samples), often from the same patients. The plasma panel covers fewer genes and plasma has lower sensitivity for fusions and copy-number changes, so the rate of altered samples and of actionable samples differs by assay, and a claim about 'the samples' may refer to only one of them. CHECK: tabulate GENE_PANEL; compute the altered-sample denominator and the actionable fraction separately for ACCESS129 and for IMPACT samples and for both pooled. IF FOUND: report all three; if the verdict differs by stratum, state which stratum you take as the study's subject and why, rather than silently pooling. SOURCE: https://www.mskcc.org/msk-access ; https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534%2822%2901721-5/fulltext
