label: CNA burden: threshold sensitivity
text: PITFALL: There is no single correct log2 threshold for calling a gain or loss from seg.mean; conventions range from 0.1 to 0.3 (cBioPortal FGA uses |seg.mean| > 0.2, some of its docs say 0.1, CNVkit suggests 0.1-0.2 with downstream filtering or 0.3 without), and a pure clonal single-copy gain is +0.585 and loss is -1.0, so the answer can flip with the cutoff. CHECK: recompute the per-sample CNA count and FGA at thresholds 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 (and a high-level cutoff near 0.5-1.0) and see whether the ordering JP vs DCIS vs IDC is the same at every threshold. IF FOUND that the ordering changes with threshold: do not report a single-threshold result as decisive; state which thresholds give which ordering and weight the conclusion on the cutoffs that sit above each sample's noise level. SOURCE: https://cnvkit.readthedocs.io/en/stable/calling.html ; https://groups.google.com/g/cbioportal/c/SqtGhn-AZ4s ; https://www.biostars.org/p/133927/

label: Pitfall 3: AR alterations acquired under ADT (reverse causation)
text: PITFALL: Reverse causation for AR. AR amplification and AR ligand-binding-domain mutations are rare in hormone-naive prostate cancer and are mostly acquired under androgen deprivation (20-57% in castration-resistant tumours versus rare before treatment). An AR alteration in a 'hormone-sensitive' sample may therefore mark prior ADT exposure or incipient resistance rather than a baseline prognostic trait, which inflates the AR hazard ratio and shortens apparent time to CRPC (times at or near 0). CHECK: count AR-altered samples (expect few); tabulate them by ANDROGEN_DEPRIVATION_THERAPY and look at their SMP_CRPC_MONTHS values, especially zeros or very short times. IF FOUND: report the AR association both overall and adjusted for/stratified by on-ADT status, state that it may reflect emerging resistance, and check that the conclusion does not rest on a handful of events within the first month. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1530/erc-16-0422 ; https://www.nature.com/articles/bjc201413 ; https://www.nature.com/articles/ng0495-401

label: cfDNA false negatives change the denominator
text: PITFALL: Plasma cfDNA samples are often uninformative: low tumour shedding gives false negatives (sensitivity for tissue-confirmed drivers 58-86% overall, near 100% only when tumour fraction is >=10%), so many plasma samples have zero detected alterations, and those that do have alterations are enriched for high-shedding, advanced disease. Conditioning on 'samples with alterations' therefore gives a higher actionable fraction than dividing by all plasma samples. CHECK: count plasma samples with zero alterations of any type; compare actionable/altered with actionable/all for plasma; look at whether altered samples differ by cancer type. IF FOUND: keep the denominator the hypothesis names (altered samples) but state the all-samples figure too, and do not read zero-alteration plasma samples as true negatives. SOURCE: https://ascopubs.org/doi/full/10.1200/PO.22.00261 ; https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534%2822%2901721-5/fulltext

label: Pitfall 4: confounding by disease volume / de novo status
text: PITFALL: Confounding by clinical phenotype. In metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, high- versus low-volume disease and de-novo versus recurrent metastatic presentation each roughly double the hazard of castration resistance (HR about 1.7-1.9), and genomic alterations (e.g. TP53) are unevenly distributed across these phenotypes. A univariable gene comparison can therefore be a disease-volume effect in disguise. Likewise the 'wild-type' reference group for one gene contains carriers of the other genes. CHECK: cross-tabulate each gene's status with DZ_VOLUME and DENOVO_METASTATSIS; fit Cox models unadjusted, then adjusted for DZ_VOLUME (and as sensitivity DENOVO_METASTATSIS, on-ADT status, and the other two genes together). IF FOUND: base the verdict on the adjusted hazard ratios (stratified or covariate-adjusted Cox), and report whether each gene's direction and size survive adjustment. SOURCE: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S107814392400526X ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6093349/

label: CNA burden: purity attenuation of seg.mean
text: PITFALL: Tumour purity compresses log2 ratios toward zero (observed log2 = log2((p*CN + 2*(1-p))/2) for purity p), so a fixed seg.mean threshold under-calls CNAs in low-purity or non-clonal lesions (benign/precursor lesions, DCIS) relative to invasive carcinoma, and a low count can mean low purity rather than a quiet genome. CHECK: estimate purity per sample from the mutation table as roughly 2 x median VAF of the higher-VAF somatic mutations, VAF = t_alt_count/(t_alt_count+t_ref_count), and look at the maximum |seg.mean| of large segments in each sample; at purity 0.3 a one-copy gain is only about +0.2 and a one-copy loss about -0.23. IF FOUND that samples differ strongly in purity: use purity-scaled thresholds (or a lenient 0.1 cutoff plus a noise filter) and say explicitly whether a lesion's low CNA count could be explained by low purity; if a lesion carries clonal mutations at decent VAF but still shows flat seg.means, the low CNA count is real. SOURCE: https://cnvkit.readthedocs.io/en/stable/heterogeneity.html ; https://doi.org/10.1186/s13029-016-0060-z ; https://www.biostars.org/p/175414/

label: Clonal haematopoiesis and germline calls
text: PITFALL: Not every listed variant is a tumour-derived somatic alteration: in plasma, clonal haematopoiesis (DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1, PPM1D, also TP53, ATM, CHEK2) and germline variants are common false 'somatic' calls unless a matched white-blood-cell normal was used, and a few samples here are flagged Somatic Status 'Unmatched'. Germline BRCA1/2, ATM or CHEK2 would wrongly add to 'somatic actionable'. CHECK: tabulate Mutation_Status in data_mutations.txt and SV_Status in data_sv.txt, and SOMATIC_STATUS (Matched/Unmatched) in the sample table; list how many actionable calls rest on ATM/CHEK2/BRCA or on unmatched samples. IF FOUND: keep only somatic calls, rerun excluding unmatched samples, and treat DNA-repair-gene hits in plasma as a sensitivity tier rather than core actionable. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8935823/ ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41416-022-01776-9

label: Pitfall 5: defining altered vs wild-type per gene
text: PITFALL: Wrong definition of 'altered'. (a) Using data_mutations.txt alone misses copy-number and structural events: AR is altered mainly by amplification (data_cna value 2), TP53 and SPOP also by deep deletion (-2) and rearrangement (data_sv.txt). (b) Direction matters by gene role: count AR amplification and AR missense as oncogenic but not AR deletion; count TP53 loss-of-function (truncating, splice, hotspot missense, deep deletion) but not TP53 amplification; SPOP drivers are recurrent missense mutations in the substrate-binding MATH domain (roughly codons 80-135, e.g. F133, Y87, F102, W131). (c) The MAF has no oncogenic annotation, so counting every nonsynonymous variant mixes passengers/VUS with drivers and dilutes associations. (d) Samples with no rows in the MAF are wild-type, not missing. CHECK: for each gene list variant classes, protein changes and CNA values among carriers; build the denominator from all 424 samples in data_clinical_sample.txt/data_gene_panel_matrix.txt. IF FOUND: define alteration = driver-type mutation OR role-consistent CNA OR SV, and rerun with the looser 'any nonsynonymous + any CNA' definition as a sensitivity check; the verdict should not flip between the two. SOURCE: https://sop.oncokb.org/static/sop/OncoKB_Curation_Standard_Operating_Procedure_v6_4.pdf ; https://academic.oup.com/oncolo/article/29/8/641/7689429 ; https://github.com/cbioportal/cbioportal/blob/master/docs/File-Formats.md

label: CNA burden: over-segmentation and small noisy segments
text: PITFALL: Exome and FFPE/microdissected copy-number data are noisy and over-segmented; short segments supported by few markers are mostly false positives, and a noisier sample gets more segments and more threshold-crossing small segments regardless of biology. CHECK: per sample tabulate the number of segments, the distribution of num.mark and segment length, and how many threshold-crossing segments have few markers (for example num.mark < 10-50) or are shorter than about 100 kb-1 Mb; check whether the sample with the most 'alterations' is simply the one with the most tiny segments. IF FOUND: filter or merge small segments (GISTIC joins segments with too few markers to the nearest neighbour; CNApp re-segments with minimum length 100 kb and merges neighbours whose seg.mean differs by < 0.16), merge adjacent segments in the same gain/loss state before counting events, and prefer length-weighted metrics such as FGA and arm-level events, which are robust to fragmentation. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5452530/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7010409/ ; https://www.genepattern.org/modules/docs/GISTIC_2.0/7/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13155139/

label: Multiple samples per patient: clustered proportion
text: PITFALL: Samples are not independent: about 1,445 samples come from about 617 patients (several plasma and tissue samples per patient, IDs like P-xxxx-T01..T10), so patients with many serial samples and a persistent driver are counted repeatedly and a naive binomial interval is too narrow. The hypothesis is worded per sample. CHECK: count samples per patient; compute the fraction per sample and per patient (patient actionable if any altered sample is actionable; also first-sample-only); get the interval by resampling patients (cluster bootstrap) or a cluster-adjusted Wilson interval. IF FOUND: give the sample-level figure as primary because the claim says 'samples', show the patient-level figure beside it, and judge the 20% claim against the cluster-aware interval. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10543393/ ; https://doi.org/10.1515/ijb-2015-0024

label: Pitfall 6: rare alterations and sparse-data bias in Cox
text: PITFALL: Sparse-data bias. AR and SPOP alterations are uncommon in hormone-sensitive disease, so a gene group may contain only a few patients/events. Standard Cox partial likelihood then gives unstable or infinite hazard ratios (monotone likelihood), asymptotic log-rank p-values are unreliable, and adding many covariates (below about 10 events per variable) overfits. CHECK: for each gene tabulate carriers, events among carriers, and events among non-carriers before modelling; flag any cell under about 10 events and any Cox fit with a huge coefficient or non-convergence warning. IF FOUND: use Firth-penalized Cox or an exact/permutation log-rank test, keep the adjustment set small (disease volume first), report the CI width explicitly, and do not over-interpret a p-value from under 10 events. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1111/j.0006-341x.2001.00114.x ; https://www.jclinepi.com/article/S0895-4356(13)00051-6/abstract ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4996851/

label: CNA burden: log2 baseline centring
text: PITFALL: A mis-centred log2 baseline makes a whole genome look gained or lost when thresholding seg.mean; median centring is only valid for near-diploid samples, and in highly aneuploid samples the commonest state is not 2 copies. CHECK: for each sample compute the length-weighted median (and the main mode) of seg.mean over autosomes; a value away from 0 by more than about 0.05-0.1, or a FGA near 100% made of many small same-sign deviations, indicates a baseline shift rather than real CNAs. IF FOUND: recentre each sample by subtracting its length-weighted median/mode before thresholding, and report results with and without recentring. SOURCE: https://bionano.com/blogs/diploid-recentering-when-why-and-how/ ; https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534(19)31432-2/fulltext ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2652209/

label: Pitfall 7: direction of effect and non-significance
text: PITFALL: Misreading the claim's logic and a non-significant result. The hypothesis is a three-part directional claim: AR-altered and TP53-altered tumours should progress to castration resistance FASTER (hazard ratio > 1) and SPOP-altered tumours SLOWER ('inverse', hazard ratio < 1). Calling it False because one gene has p > 0.05 confuses low power with contradiction (absence of evidence is not evidence of absence); calling it True from a two-sided p-value without checking the sign misses a wrong-direction effect. CHECK: for each gene report hazard ratio, 95% CI, direction, and number of events; state in advance the decision rule (e.g. all three in the stated direction with CIs largely excluding 1, in unadjusted and volume-adjusted models). IF FOUND: 'False' needs evidence against the claim — an effect in the opposite direction, or a tight CI around HR=1 with adequate events — not merely a wide non-significant CI; three tests is a small family, so a Bonferroni/Holm check is enough for multiplicity. SOURCE: https://www.bmj.com/content/311/7003/485 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9365504/

label: Judging a point claim: tolerance, nested denominators, MSI/TMB
text: PITFALL: A point claim ('20%') cannot be judged by eye, and published sentences of this type are often nested ('X% had an alteration, of which Y% were actionable'), so the same data yield different percentages for different denominators; with ~1,000 samples a binomial interval is only about +/-2.5 points, so 20% is easily excluded by a rule set that is slightly too wide or too narrow. Tumour-agnostic biomarkers held in the clinical table rather than the alteration tables (MSI_TYPE unstable, high TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS) can also move the count. CHECK: fix in advance what counts as agreement (e.g. estimate rounds to about 20% or its interval covers 20%), then compute estimate and Wilson interval for each defensible definition and denominator, with and without MSI-high/TMB-high samples. IF FOUND: if every defensible definition lands far from 20% the claim is contradicted; if only some reach 20%, report that the verdict is definition-dependent and name the definition you rely on. SOURCE: https://www.stat.cmu.edu/~brian/720/week01/Binomial-StatSci.pdf ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10784742/

label: CNA burden: tiny n, matched samples, no pseudoreplication
text: PITFALL: With only a handful of samples per lesion type (clinical table has 5 samples from 3 patients, and three of them come from one patient) no significance test can settle the comparison: rank tests cannot reach p<0.05 at these sizes, and guidance is to do no inferential statistics below about 5 independent observations per group; treating segments as independent observations (t-test or chi-square over hundreds of segments) is pseudoreplication and gives meaningless tiny p-values. CHECK: count independent patients per lesion type and identify which samples are matched within one patient. IF FOUND: make the comparison descriptive, per sample, with the matched within-patient comparison (JP vs its associated DCIS and IDC in the same patient) as the primary evidence and the unmatched samples as supporting; decide the label from the direction and size of the per-sample differences and their robustness to thresholds, not from a p-value, and do not call the hypothesis 'Not verifiable' merely because n is small. SOURCE: https://www.bmj.com/content/338/bmj.a3166 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10328100/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7814346/

label: Pitfall 8: CNA misclassification from low purity
text: PITFALL: Copy-number false negatives in low-purity or small biopsies. Targeted-panel CNA calls lose sensitivity as tumour purity falls (expected log2 ratio for a 5-copy amplification drops from 1.32 at 100% purity to 0.81 at 50%), so AR amplifications and TP53 deep deletions are under-called in impure samples, pushing true carriers into the wild-type group and biasing the hazard ratio toward 1. Sample site (prostate primary vs metastasis) also correlates with both purity and prognosis. CHECK: compare TUMOR_PURITY (5 missing) and TISSUE_SITE between altered and wild-type groups for each gene; look at the gene-level segment mean in data_cna_hg19.seg for borderline cases. IF FOUND: run a sensitivity analysis excluding low-purity samples (e.g. under 20-30%) or adjusting for purity/tissue site, and treat a null AR-amplification result in low-purity samples as weak evidence. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9302205/ ; https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534(19)31355-9/fulltext

label: CNA burden: group labels and which table is the CNA variable
text: PITFALL: The clinical table does not carry the lesion type in a usable column (CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED reads 'Invasive Breast Carcinoma' for every sample, including the benign papillomatosis samples), and the gene panel matrix lists only a mutations profile even though a segmented copy-number file exists; grouping by the cancer-type column, or concluding there is no copy-number data, both give a wrong answer. CHECK: derive lesion type from SAMPLE_ID (suffixes -JP, -DCIS, -IDC; unsuffixed samples need a judgement about which lesion they are), then confirm that the set of IDs in the seg file's ID column matches SAMPLE_ID exactly and that every sample has segments covering all autosomes. IF FOUND that a sample is missing from the seg file or covers only part of the genome: treat it as unmeasured, not as zero alterations, and normalise FGA by that sample's own measured length. Use the seg file, not TMB or mutation counts, as the variable for this hypothesis; mutation burden is a different quantity. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/ ; https://groups.google.com/g/cbioportal/c/oWO1LFXGHHs

label: Pitfall 9: proportional hazards, time-zero events, competing death
text: PITFALL: Unchecked Cox assumptions and event handling. The hazard ratio is an average that is misleading if curves cross or the effect is concentrated early (likely for AR if events cluster right after sampling); six patients have time exactly 0, which some software drops or mishandles; deaths before castration resistance (102 deaths in the cohort) are a competing event that plain censoring treats as non-informative. CHECK: plot Kaplan-Meier curves per gene, test scaled Schoenfeld residuals (cox.zph or lifelines check_assumptions), list the IS_CRPC status of the time-0 rows, and count patients who are Dead with IS_CRPC=No. IF FOUND: for non-proportionality report medians/restricted mean time or a time-split HR alongside the Cox HR; keep time-0 events (add a tiny offset if the software needs positive times) and show the result with and without them; if deaths without CRPC are numerous, confirm with a cause-specific hazard interpretation or Fine-Gray model. SOURCE: https://journal.chestnet.org/article/S0012-3692(20)30470-0/fulltext ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2376927/ ; https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2001.05709

label: CNA burden: sex chromosomes and germline/artefact segments
text: PITFALL: Sex chromosomes and germline/polymorphic or artefact-prone regions inflate CNA counts: chrX/Y log2 ratios depend on the sex of the reference, and small segments at the same coordinates in several samples are usually germline CNVs or capture artefacts rather than somatic events. CHECK: list the chrom values in the seg file (X/Y may be coded X, Y, 23, 24); look for short threshold-crossing segments with near-identical start/end in unrelated patients or in all lesions of one patient. IF FOUND: compute burden on autosomes 1-22 only, and exclude or flag recurrent identical small segments; for matched lesions of one patient, alterations shared by all lesions do not distinguish them, so also report the lesion-private alterations. SOURCE: https://cnvkit.readthedocs.io/en/stable/germline.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4015338/ ; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27999612/

label: CNA burden: event count vs FGA can disagree
text: PITFALL: Count-based and length-based CNA metrics measure different things and can disagree: a sample with a few whole-arm gains/losses has high FGA but few events, while a noisy or focally rearranged sample has many events but low FGA; the hypothesis wording 'number of copy number alterations' points to an event count, but an event count alone is the metric most sensitive to noise. CHECK: report, per sample, both the number of altered segments/arms (after merging and filtering) and FGA, plus the amplitude of the largest alterations, and see if both metrics rank the lesion types the same way. IF FOUND that they agree: the conclusion is robust; if they disagree, give priority to the merged/filtered event count and arm-level events for a 'number of CNAs' claim and say so explicitly. Background expectation from DCIS exome studies is that CNA burden rises with grade and progression (median FGA about 0.14 in DCIS, about 2.5-fold higher in high-grade DCIS), so a benign precursor having more CNAs than its associated carcinoma would be unusual and needs strong evidence. SOURCE: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/cnr2.1902 ; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2022.09.034 ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41523-021-00365-y

label: PITFALL: No measured drug-response outcome: do not manufacture one
text: PITFALL: A claim about chemotherapy sensitivity of engrafted (in-mouse) tumoroids can only be tested with a functional response measurement: tumour volume/growth under drug versus vehicle in mice, or a derived metric (TGI, mRECIST, AUC, endoluminal tumour size, survival). cBioPortal-style genomic tables (clinical attributes, mutations MAF, discrete CNA, seg, gene-panel matrix) normally hold none of this, and analysts then drift into testing something else and reporting it as the answer. CHECK: List every column of every file (the library's header read of data_clinical_sample.txt showed 27 columns: derivation age, prior therapy, derivation site, sample type/class, panel, purity, MSI, TMB, cancer type; data_clinical_patient.txt showed only PATIENT_ID and SEX) and grep column names AND cell values for response-like terms: response, sensit, resist, AUC, IC50, viab, volume, growth, TGI, RECIST, TRG, regression, pCR, xenograft, engraft, mouse, treated, vehicle. Confirm whether any variable is a per-model measurement of how the model behaved under chemotherapy. IF FOUND: If no such variable exists, the hypothesis's outcome is unmeasured in these tables: say so explicitly and choose the label by the task's own definitions (it defines 'Not verifiable' as the data holding no relevant variable, and 'False' as requiring that you can identify the relevant variables and they contradict the claim) rather than testing a stand-in variable. If a genuine response variable does exist, analyse its between-model spread (see the 'uniform' and 'pseudoreplication' pitfalls). SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7272270/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9240739/ ; https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/.

label: PITFALL: Prior-therapy column is exposure, not response
text: PITFALL: A column such as THERAPY_PRIOR_TO_DERIVATION records which regimens the PATIENT received before the tumoroid was derived (e.g. 'FOLFOX, FOLFIRI, SCRT and FUDR'). It is a treatment-exposure history, not a measure of how the patient's tumour or the engrafted tumoroid responded. Treating 'received more lines' or 'pre-treated vs naive' as resistant/sensitive is confounded by indication (regimen is chosen by stage, site and disease course) and says nothing about the mouse model. CHECK: Read the distinct values of the prior-therapy field: do they name drugs/regimens only, or do they state an outcome (responder, progression, complete response)? Check whether any value refers to treatment given to mice rather than to the patient. IF FOUND: If the field only lists regimens, do not use it as a sensitivity variable and do not count variety in prior regimens as 'heterogeneous sensitivity' or sameness as 'uniform sensitivity'. Use it only as a covariate/descriptor. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10204604/ ; https://encepp.europa.eu/encepp-toolkit/methodological-guide/chapter-5-definition-and-validation-drug-exposure-outcomes-and-covariates_en.

label: Data shape for the STAG2/ESPL1 task
text: DATA SHAPE (headers only, no analysis): /biodsa-data holds one bladder-cancer study: 99 patients, 99 samples (one per patient, all ONCOTREE BLCA = bladder urothelial carcinoma; 86 Primary, 13 Recurrence; patient SUBTYPE is Invasive/Superficial), every sample listed as profiled 'WXS/WGS' in data_gene_panel_matrix.txt, and a single molecular table data_mutations.txt (MAF, ~11.2k rows, Center BGI, GRCh37) with Hugo_Symbol, Variant_Classification, Consequence, Tumor_Sample_Barcode, HGVSp_Short; Entrez_Gene_Id, Mutation_Status and read-count columns appear empty in the first rows. There is no copy-number, structural-variant or expression table.

label: PITFALL: Genotype is not a valid surrogate for chemosensitivity in colorectal/rectal cancer
text: PITFALL: Inferring uniform or heterogeneous chemotherapy sensitivity from mutation, copy-number, MSI or TMB diversity is a surrogate-endpoint error. There is no validated genomic predictor of 5-FU/oxaliplatin/irinotecan response in colorectal cancer (candidate markers such as ERCC1 failed prospective validation; TP53 status showed no impact on cytotoxic response; MMR status did not correlate with intrinsic organoid drug sensitivity), which is exactly why functional organoid/xenograft assays exist. Genomically diverse models can respond alike and genomically similar models can respond differently. CHECK: Ask of any planned analysis: is the dependent variable a measured drug response, or a genomic feature (KRAS/TP53/APC status, CNA burden, MSI score, TMB) being read as if it were response? Check whether the conclusion would change if genotype and response were uncorrelated. IF FOUND: Do not label the hypothesis True or False on the basis of genomic heterogeneity or homogeneity alone. Genomic comparisons can describe the cohort but cannot stand in for the missing response outcome; report them as descriptive only. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8582471/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6695307/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7614625/ ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41698-021-00168-1.

label: Pitfall: TCC is the whole BLCA cohort
text: PITFALL: 'TCC' is not a column value, so an analyst may think the cohort cannot be identified and answer Not verifiable, or may wrongly subset. TCC = transitional cell carcinoma = urothelial carcinoma of the bladder, which is the whole study (all 99 samples are ONCOTREE_CODE BLCA / 'Bladder Urothelial Carcinoma'). CHECK: tabulate ONCOTREE_CODE and CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED in data_clinical_sample.txt and confirm they are constant. IF FOUND: treat all profiled samples as the TCC cohort (denominator = all 99); report the Invasive/Superficial and Primary/Recurrence breakdown only as a secondary sensitivity view, not as the main estimate. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/

label: PITFALL: Two-armed claim: model response AND clinical response both need data
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis has two parts: (a) engrafted tumoroids respond uniformly to chemotherapy, and (b) this differs from clinical observations. Validating a model against the clinic requires paired data: a per-model response readout and a per-patient clinical response (RECIST, tumour regression grade, pathologic/clinical complete response). Analysts often test only one arm, or fill the clinical arm from textbook knowledge that rectal cancer response is heterogeneous (roughly 10-30% pCR) instead of from the data. CHECK: Look for a per-patient clinical response column in the patient and sample tables (the patient table header shows only PATIENT_ID and SEX). Look separately for a per-model in-vivo response column. Record which of the two arms, if any, is present. IF FOUND: If either arm is absent, the comparison 'unlike clinical observations' cannot be computed from the tables; state which arm is missing. General literature knowledge about clinical heterogeneity is context, not data analysis, and should not be what decides the label. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41698-021-00168-1 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9913532/.

label: Pitfall: denominator must be profiled samples, count samples not rows
text: PITFALL: Using the wrong denominator for a gene's alteration frequency. A MAF has one row per mutation, so samples with no mutation in the gene (or no rows at all) are absent from it; dividing by the samples that appear in the MAF, or by the number of mutation rows, inflates or distorts the frequency (a documented cBioPortal bug gave 57% instead of the true 48% for TP53 this way). CHECK: numerator = number of UNIQUE Tumor_Sample_Barcode with >=1 qualifying mutation in the gene; denominator = number of samples marked profiled in data_gene_panel_matrix.txt (compare it with the number of distinct barcodes in the MAF and with the clinical sample table; confirm all MAF barcodes exist in the clinical table). IF FOUND: use profiled samples as denominator and count each sample once even if it carries several mutations in the gene; state n/N explicitly. SOURCE: https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/5000

label: PITFALL: Sample labels and ID suffixes are not experimental outcomes
text: PITFALL: In cBioPortal studies SAMPLE_CLASS/SAMPLE_TYPE (tumor, cell line, xenograft, organoid) and ID suffixes describe WHAT was sequenced, not the result of a treatment experiment. Sample IDs here carry undocumented infixes/suffixes (e.g. -pt, -tm, TNT, PR, RC, SP, VR, MC, PC, MP, P2m/P7m/P9m) that are tempting to read as response or treatment codes (e.g. 'PR' as partial response, 'TNT' as treated). Also an ex-vivo tumoroid culture is not an 'engrafted' tumoroid: the hypothesis is specifically about in-mouse behaviour. CHECK: Tabulate SAMPLE_CLASS, SAMPLE_TYPE, TISSUE_SITE_OF_DERIVATION and the ID suffix patterns; see whether the '#' description rows define any of them as a response or as a mouse-passaged sample. Check whether any sample is annotated as xenograft-derived and, if so, whether any treatment outcome accompanies it. IF FOUND: If the codes are not defined in the files, do not interpret them as response categories. Presence of xenograft- or passage-labelled sequenced samples shows only that engraftment happened and was sequenced; it is not evidence about uniform or variable drug sensitivity. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/.

label: Pitfall: outdated gene symbols/aliases in the MAF
text: PITFALL: Looking a gene up only by its current HUGO symbol in an old MAF. Symbols are unstable (aliases, previous symbols, Excel date-mangling), and this MAF visibly uses outdated symbols (e.g. NALP6, the previous symbol of NLRP6) and has an empty Entrez_Gene_Id column, so an exact match on 'STAG2' or 'ESPL1' could return zero rows for a gene that is actually present under another name, producing a false 'not altered' or 'Not verifiable'. CHECK: search Hugo_Symbol case-insensitively for the approved symbol AND its aliases/previous symbols (STAG2: SA2, SA-2, SCC3B, STAG-2; ESPL1: ESP1, KIAA0165, SEPA, separase), and independently confirm by genomic position (GRCh37: STAG2 is on chrX around 123.09-123.24 Mb; ESPL1 is on chr12 around 53.66-53.69 Mb) and by the RefSeq/Transcript_ID/HGVSc columns. IF FOUND: pool rows under all names for the same locus before counting samples; if a symbol is absent under every alias and no rows fall in its coordinates, that is a zero count, not missing data. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7856679/

label: Pitfall: restrict to non-silent coding variants
text: PITFALL: Counting every MAF row for a gene as an alteration. Tools define an altered sample by protein-affecting variants only (maftools default vc_nonSyn: Frame_Shift_Del/Ins, Splice_Site, Translation_Start_Site, Nonsense_Mutation, Nonstop_Mutation, In_Frame_Del/Ins, Missense_Mutation); cBioPortal stores only non-synonymous mutations. Because part of this cohort is WGS, the MAF may also contain Silent, Intron, UTR, Flank, IGR or RNA rows that carry a gene symbol. CHECK: tabulate Variant_Classification (and Consequence) overall and for the genes of interest. IF FOUND: compute the frequency on non-silent coding + splice-site variants only, and report how the count changes if silent/non-coding rows are included; do not let silent rows create an altered sample. SOURCE: https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/maftools/inst/doc/maftools.html

label: PITFALL: Answering from memory of the literature instead of from the tables
text: PITFALL: Organoid/xenograft response-versus-clinic results are widely published, so an analyst may recognise the study type and label the hypothesis from what they believe a paper reported. The task asks whether THESE data tables support, contradict or cannot settle the claim; a conclusion that cannot be traced to a column in the supplied files is not a data analysis result. CHECK: For the final reasoning, write down the exact file and column that supplies (1) the response measurement and (2) the grouping/comparison. If either slot is filled by 'known from the literature' or by an assumption, flag it. IF FOUND: Base the label only on what the supplied tables can show, and say in the reasoning which variables were searched for and not found. Keep outside knowledge to a clearly marked context sentence. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41698-021-00168-1 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11155402/.

label: Pitfall: 'altered' vs mutation-only data
text: PITFALL: Mis-handling the word 'altered' when only mutation data exist. In cBioPortal a default gene query counts mutations, structural variants/fusions, amplifications and deep deletions as alterations, but this study ships only a mutation table (no CNA/SV file). Two opposite errors follow: (a) answering Not verifiable because CNA is missing, although somatic mutation IS a gene alteration and the relevant variable is present; (b) treating a mutation-only frequency as the total alteration rate. CHECK: confirm which molecular files exist (only data_mutations.txt) and that the gene panel matrix lists every sample as profiled for mutations. IF FOUND: evaluate the hypothesis with the mutation frequency, state that it is a lower bound on total alteration frequency (CNA unassessed), and reserve Not verifiable for the case where the genes could not have been observed at all (see the chrX/coverage check). SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/oql/

label: PITFALL: 'Uniform' is a claim of no heterogeneity: a non-significant test does not prove it
text: PITFALL: If a response variable is found, 'uniform sensitivity' is a null-type claim. A non-significant difference between models in a small cohort is absence of evidence, not evidence of uniformity; conversely any nonzero spread is not automatically 'heterogeneous' because replicate mice of the same model also vary. Group-mean tests (t-test/ANOVA on pooled animals) assume a common response and hide responder/non-responder structure. CHECK: Estimate between-model variance relative to within-model (mouse-to-mouse/replicate) variance, with a confidence interval, e.g. a mixed model with a random effect for model, or the range of per-model effect sizes versus replicate noise. Check sample size and whether response categories (e.g. mRECIST-style) differ across models. IF FOUND: Support 'uniform' only with an equivalence-style argument (between-model spread demonstrably smaller than a pre-stated margin), and reject it if between-model variance clearly exceeds replicate noise or models fall into different response categories. If n is too small to do either, say the data cannot settle it. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5502906/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11090505/ ; https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/scitranslmed.adi9004 ; https://aacrjournals.org/clincancerres/article/18/16/4385/15013/.

label: Pitfall: what 'frequently altered' should mean
text: PITFALL: Judging 'frequently' by an arbitrary or too-strict cutoff. There is no universal threshold; in pan-cancer exome analyses only a few cancer genes exceed 20% of tumours of a type, and most genuine cancer genes sit at intermediate frequencies of 2-20%, so demanding e.g. >20% or >50% would reject most real recurrently mutated genes, while accepting any single mutated sample would accept everything. CHECK: before looking at the result, fix a decision rule that combines (i) n/N with a confidence interval, (ii) the gene's rank/percentile among all genes in the same cohort by mutated-sample count, and (iii) comparison with the frequencies of the established top genes in this cohort. IF FOUND: call the claim supported if each gene is recurrently mutated at a frequency clearly above the typical gene in this cohort and in the intermediate-or-higher range; call it contradicted if a gene has zero or only sporadic (about 1 sample, within background) mutations. Report both genes separately, since the hypothesis needs both. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4048962/

label: PITFALL: Pseudoreplication: several samples per patient and mice nested in models
text: PITFALL: The unit of inference for 'do models differ in sensitivity' is the patient/model, not the sample or the mouse. This study has multiple derived samples per patient (matched tumour '-pt' and tumoroid '-tm' pairs, plus several tumoroid lines or passages from one patient such as 012/012RC/012SP/012VR or 025/025TNT-P2m/P7m/P9m). Counting each as independent inflates n and can fake either uniformity (many near-identical siblings) or heterogeneity. CHECK: Count samples per PATIENT_ID and per derivation; identify sibling lines and passages. In any response data, identify how many mice or replicates belong to each model. IF FOUND: Collapse to one value per model/patient or fit a mixed model with random effects for patient and model; report n as the number of independent patients/models. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10035449/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9685207/ ; https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/.

label: Pitfall: background rate, gene length and hypermutators
text: PITFALL: Treating raw mutation frequency or rank as proof of relevance. Mutation counts per gene scale with coding length, local background mutation rate (replication timing, expression) and tumour mutation burden, so long passenger genes (TTN, MUC16, olfactory receptors, FLAGS genes) top raw-frequency lists, and a few hypermutated samples can put several mutations into almost any gene. CHECK: (1) compute per-sample mutation counts (or use TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS) and see whether the samples mutated in the gene of interest are mostly the high-burden ones; recompute the frequency excluding the top-burden outliers; (2) compare observed mutated-sample count with a simple expectation = cohort non-silent rate per coding bp x gene coding length x N (binomial/Poisson test), or use non-silent:silent ratio in the gene; (3) look at the mutation spectrum: an excess of truncating (nonsense/frameshift/splice) variants spread along the gene is the signature of a selected tumour suppressor, unlike scattered missense in a long gene. IF FOUND: describe the gene as frequently mutated only if the excess over background survives; if formal tools (MutSigCV, dNdScv) cannot be run because silent mutations or coverage are absent, say so and rely on the length-scaled comparison plus truncating fraction. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3919509/

label: PITFALL: Mixed cohorts, panel versions and purity make genomic summaries non-comparable
text: PITFALL: The genomic matrices mix study samples (RC-MSK-*-pt tumours and -tm tumoroids) with what look like a clinical MSK-IMPACT reference cohort (P-00xxxxx-T01-IM3/IM5/IM6), sequenced on different panel versions (IMPACT341/410/468). Genes absent from a panel are unprofiled, not wild-type; TMB and CNA burden depend on panel size, matched-normal availability (tumour-only calling inflates TMB with germline variants) and purity (tumoroids are near 100% tumour cells, FFPE tumours are not), and xenograft-derived DNA can carry mouse-read artefacts. Any 'tumoroid vs tumour' or 'model vs clinic' genomic contrast can be driven by these artefacts. CHECK: Split samples by ID pattern and SAMPLE_CLASS; cross-tabulate against GENE_PANEL and data_gene_panel_matrix.txt; check which samples have a Matched_Norm_Sample_Barcode; compare purity and coverage between groups; treat blank/NA CNA cells as not profiled. IF FOUND: Restrict genomic comparisons to genes common to all panels, to matched patient pairs, and to like-for-like sample classes; do not pool the reference cohort with the tumoroids. In any case these comparisons are descriptive and do not measure drug sensitivity. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9103036/ ; https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2762022 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6844030/ ; https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/.

label: Pitfall: small-sample uncertainty, use Wilson interval
text: PITFALL: Reporting a prevalence from about 99 tumours as a bare percentage, or using the Wald (normal-approximation) interval, which has poor and erratic coverage for small counts and proportions near 0. With N=99 a gene mutated in 5 samples has a 95% interval of roughly 2-11%. CHECK: for each gene compute the Wilson score (or Jeffreys / exact Clopper-Pearson) 95% interval for n/N, e.g. statsmodels.stats.proportion.proportion_confint(n, N, method='wilson'). IF FOUND: base the verdict on whether the whole interval is compatible with the pre-set 'frequent' criterion, and say explicitly when the data are too thin to separate 'recurrent' from 'sporadic'. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1214/ss/1009213286

label: PITFALL: If in-vivo response data exist: metric and control choice can flip the conclusion
text: PITFALL: There is no consensus xenograft response metric; conclusions about which models respond depend on the outcome chosen (final volume, change from baseline, AUC, TGI, mRECIST categories). Simulation work found final tumour volume and change from baseline perform best, while tumour-growth-inhibition index variants had inflated type-1 error and bias; binary responder calls depend on arbitrary, mostly unvalidated cut-offs; unequal starting volumes and dropout bias naive comparisons; response must be judged against a vehicle-treated control of the SAME model because untreated growth rates differ between models. CHECK: Confirm there is a control arm per model, baseline volumes, and repeated measurements; compute at least two metrics (e.g. change from baseline relative to control, and a categorical call) and see whether the between-model pattern is the same under both. IF FOUND: Report the conclusion only if it is stable across metrics; normalise to each model's own control and baseline; prefer continuous outcomes with a mixed model over thresholded responder counts. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9240739/ ; https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/79/17/4539/638195/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7272270/.

label: Pitfall: not profiled vs not mutated (chrX, coverage)
text: PITFALL: Reading 'no rows for the gene' as 'gene not mutated' when the gene may not have been assayable, and the reverse. STAG2 lies on chromosome X; some somatic pipelines drop or under-call sex chromosomes, and exome kits differ in gene coverage. Absence of calls is evidence of absence only if the region was profiled. CHECK: confirm the MAF contains mutations on chromosome X at a plausible rate and in genes neighbouring the loci of interest (and on chr12 near ESPL1); confirm the gene panel matrix says WXS/WGS (genome-wide) for all samples rather than a targeted panel. IF FOUND: if chrX (or the locus) is systematically empty, the STAG2 half of the claim is Not verifiable rather than False; if the region is populated, a zero or low count is real evidence against 'frequently altered'. Also note STAG2 is hemizygous in males, so tabulate mutated samples by SEX as context. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/

label: Pitfall: deposited data vs published two-stage frequencies; artefact recurrences
text: PITFALL: Assuming the deposited table reproduces a paper's headline frequencies. Cancer sequencing studies often use a two-stage design (exome/genome discovery set, then targeted prevalence screen of candidate genes in extra tumours), so published percentages may rest on a larger or different denominator than the deposited samples, and discovery-set frequencies of selected genes are subject to winner's-curse inflation. The deposited cohort here also mixes primary and recurrent tumours and two assays (WXS and WGS). CHECK: count how many samples the deposited data contain and whether mutation calls look homogeneous across samples (per-sample mutation counts by SAMPLE_TYPE / gene-panel string; identical variants repeated across many samples or carrying dbSNP_RS ids suggest germline leakage or artefacts and should not be counted as independent somatic hits). IF FOUND: base the verdict strictly on n/N in the deposited data, not on recalled literature values; report a sensitivity analysis excluding suspicious recurrent identical variants and, if assays differ in yield, per-assay frequencies. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2820387/

label: Pitfall 1: no drug-response variable; define the testable part
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis mentions CDK4/6 inhibition being 'unsuccessful', but the tables contain no drug-treatment or drug-response variable (clinical tables hold only demographics, stage, purity, subtype and mutation-burden columns), so an analyst can wrongly stop at 'no response data' or, conversely, wrongly claim a response effect. CHECK: list the clinical columns and confirm there is no treatment/response/survival field; then state explicitly which observable part of the claim the data can address (CDKN2A alteration status, RB1 protein abundance and RB1 phosphorylation are all measured per tumour) and which part they cannot (actual drug response). IF FOUND: base the label on the measurable part and say so in the reasoning; established biology used to link the two is that intact, phosphorylatable RB protein is the one consistent requirement for CDK4/6-inhibitor activity, whereas CDKN2A loss alone has not predicted benefit in trials. SOURCE: https://www.cell.com/cancer-cell/fulltext/S1535-6108(17)30516-0 ; https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5704709/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6764876/

label: Pitfall 2: CDKN2A status is more than MAF mutations
text: PITFALL: Defining CDKN2A status from the mutation file alone misclassifies tumours, because CDKN2A/p16 is inactivated mostly by homozygous deletion and promoter methylation, with point mutation the minority route, and this dataset has no copy-number table; 'wild-type by MAF' tumours can still be p16-null. Also the clinical column CDKN2A_PATHWAY_ALTERATION_STATUS is described as mutations in genes 'in the CDKN2A pathway', so it may count genes other than CDKN2A (possibly RB1 itself), which would make an RB1 comparison circular. CHECK: cross-tabulate MAF CDKN2A non-silent mutation against the clinical pathway flag and against RB1 mutation; look at CDKN2A protein, CDKN2A mRNA and CDKN2A promoter methylation (data_methylation_epic has a CDKN2A row) in the 'wild-type' group for a low/absent-p16 cluster. IF FOUND: run the analysis under at least two definitions (strict MAF CDKN2A mutation; broader loss = mutation or low p16 protein/RNA or high methylation) and report whether the RB1 conclusion is the same; do not treat the pathway flag as a pure CDKN2A call without checking. SOURCE: https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3951422/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3127263/

label: Pitfall 3: filter MAF by Variant_Classification
text: PITFALL: data_mutations.txt includes non-protein-altering rows (about 8000 Silent, plus Intron, 3'/5'Flank, 3'/5'UTR, RNA, Splice_Region), and the Mutation_Status column is empty, so counting every row for a gene as an 'alteration' inflates the mutant group; truncating (nonsense, frameshift, splice-site) and missense variants also have different expected effects on protein abundance. CHECK: filter on Variant_Classification to Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift, In_Frame, Splice_Site, Nonstop, Translation_Start_Site before calling CDKN2A or RB1 mutant; tabulate truncating versus missense; all 108 samples have MAF rows and Tumor_Sample_Barcode equals the plain sample ID (e.g. C3L-00081), so absence of a CDKN2A row means sequenced and not mutated. IF FOUND: use the filtered calls, and where group size allows report truncating and missense separately. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/imported-maf-columns/ ; https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/blob/master/docs/File-Formats.md

label: Pitfall 4: test within-group RB1 heterogeneity, not just means
text: PITFALL: Comparing only the mean RB1 protein or phospho level between CDKN2A-altered and wild-type tumours answers the wrong question. p16 and RB are reciprocally altered in lung cancer (RB-positive tumours have low/absent p16; RB-deficient tumours have abundant p16 and usually intact CDKN2A), so a mean difference is expected, but the hypothesis is about whether individual CDKN2A-altered tumours vary in RB1 status; a non-significant or significant mean test says nothing about within-group heterogeneity. CHECK: plot and tabulate the distribution of RB1 protein and RB1 phospho inside the CDKN2A-altered group (range, spread, number of tumours below a low-RB threshold such as the level seen in RB1-truncating-mutant tumours), and count co-occurrence of CDKN2A alteration with RB1 mutation or RB1-low protein. IF FOUND: report counts and proportions of CDKN2A-altered tumours with RB1-low or low-phospho status alongside any group test, and let the conclusion rest on that heterogeneity rather than on the mean comparison alone. SOURCE: https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/55/3/505/501770/Reciprocal-Rb-Inactivation-and-p16INK4-Expression ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8601419/

label: Pitfall 5: adjust RB1 phospho for RB1 protein abundance
text: PITFALL: A phosphosite or phosphoprotein log-ratio mixes two things, how much of the parent protein is present and what fraction of it is phosphorylated; a tumour with low RB1 protein will show low RB1 phospho even if occupancy is unchanged, so raw RB1 phospho differences can simply restate RB1 protein differences. CHECK: correlate RB1 phospho (data_phosphoprotein_quantification) with RB1 protein (data_protein_quantification) across samples; then compute a protein-adjusted phospho value (phospho log-ratio minus protein log-ratio, or the residual from regressing phospho on protein) and repeat the group comparison. IF FOUND: report both raw and protein-adjusted phospho; interpret raw phospho as 'amount of phosphorylated RB' and adjusted phospho as 'phosphorylation per RB molecule', and do not claim altered CDK4/6 activity from raw phospho alone. SOURCE: https://www.mcponline.org/article/S1535-9476(20)30185-7/fulltext ; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cels.2020.06.013

label: Pitfall 6: phospho table is gene-level, RB1 sites are pooled
text: PITFALL: data_phosphoprotein_quantification.txt is collapsed to ONE row per gene, not per site: the RB1 row is named 'RB1_acetylprotein' (the '_acetylprotein' suffix is a mislabel carried by every row of the phospho, acetyl and ubiquityl files) and its NAME field lists many sites together (S37, S249, T356, T373, S608/S612, S780, S788, S795, S807/S811, T821/T826). Site-specific questions cannot be answered: CDK4/cyclin D preferentially primes S807/S811 while CDK2/cyclin E completes hyperphosphorylation, and the gene-level value cannot tell these apart. CHECK: confirm a single RB1 row with grep '^RB1_' and match samples by column name (column order differs between files; phospho has 108 sample columns after 3 ID columns). IF FOUND: describe the measure as overall RB1 phosphorylation, not CDK4/6-specific site occupancy, and use cyclin D1, CDK4, CDK6, CCNE1 and CDKN2A protein rows as context for which kinase arm is likely active. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3529988/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC108786/

label: Pitfall 7: RB loss is not only RB1 mutation; use protein and E2F readouts
text: PITFALL: RB can be functionally lost without an RB1 mutation (deletion, methylation, complex rearrangement, or constitutive hyperphosphorylation, including by cyclin E/CDK2, which bypasses CDK4/6), and RB1 DNA status only partly predicts RB protein; there is no copy-number table here, so MAF-based RB1 status under-calls RB loss. CHECK: compare RB1 protein in RB1-truncating-mutant versus other tumours to see what 'RB-lost' looks like in this assay; then look for non-mutant tumours at the same low level; as a functional cross-check score E2F-target / RB-loss genes from the RNA table (e.g. CCNE1, E2F1, MCM genes, and CDKN2A itself, which rises when RB is lost) and check they track RB1 protein. IF FOUND: classify RB status from protein (and phospho) rather than from mutation alone, and note CCNE1-high tumours as a second route to CDK4/6-inhibitor resistance that RB1 protein alone does not capture. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6635068/ ; https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6664013/ ; https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.adq9495

label: Pitfall 8: tumour purity confounds RB1 protein/phospho comparisons
text: PITFALL: Bulk tumour protein and phospho values average tumour cells with stroma and immune cells, which express RB1 and p16 normally; low purity can hide RB1 loss in tumour cells, and purity often differs between mutation-defined groups and subtypes, creating or masking group differences. CHECK: correlate RB1 protein, RB1 phospho and CDKN2A protein with ESTIMATE_TUMORPURITY and TSNET_PURITY in data_clinical_sample.txt, and compare purity between the CDKN2A groups. IF FOUND: add purity as a covariate (linear model of RB1 measure on CDKN2A status plus purity), or confirm the result holds in the high-purity half; NMF_SUBTYPE is another candidate covariate. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms9971 ; https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/genetics/articles/10.3389/fgene.2021.642759/full

label: Pitfall 9: file-format traps (all-NA z-score rows, pre-logged RNA, RNA not a protein proxy)
text: PITFALL: Several files are not what their names suggest. data_protein_quantification_zscores.txt has 7983 of 11110 rows entirely NA, so using it silently drops most proteins; data_mrna_seq_fpkm.txt holds negative values, so it is already log-transformed/centred rather than raw FPKM and must not be log-transformed again; the z-score files are standardised against all samples, so z-scoring them again or thresholding as if against normal tissue is wrong; mRNA is only a modest proxy for protein in tumour proteogenomics and should not stand in for RB1 protein. Clinical CANCER_TYPE says 'Lung Adenocarcinoma' but ONCOTREE_CODE is LUSC and the column descriptions say 108 LSCC tumours (it is squamous). CHECK: read RB1 and CDKN2A from data_protein_quantification.txt (row IDs look like 'RB1|RB1') and confirm they are non-NA in most samples; check value ranges before any transform; protein table has 108 sample columns, RNA 108, methylation 103, so intersect sample IDs per analysis. IF FOUND: use the raw log-ratio protein and phospho tables as primary data, RNA only as supporting evidence, and report the n actually used. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6448780/

label: Pitfall 10: TMT missingness/batch and small-subgroup statistics
text: PITFALL: TMT proteomics has plex-level batch structure and missing values that are not random (a protein or phosphosite absent in a plex is missing for every sample in that plex, and low-abundance species go missing more often); imputing zeros or minimum values, or dropping samples unevenly, can fabricate an 'RB1-low' group, and small mutation-defined subgroups make p-values unstable. CHECK: count NA for the RB1 protein and RB1 phospho rows and see whether NAs cluster by EXPERIMENT (TMT plex) or by CDKN2A group; test whether RB1 values differ by plex; record group sizes. IF FOUND: analyse complete cases without imputation, use rank-based tests (Mann-Whitney, Spearman) and Fisher's exact test for co-occurrence, report effect sizes with confidence intervals and the group n, and do not read a non-significant result in a small subgroup as proof of no difference. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6773557/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8996546/ ; https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMsr077003

label: PITFALL gene panel coverage / RNF43 denominator
text: PITFALL: The cohort mixes MSK-IMPACT panel versions (sample IDs end -IM3/-IM5/-IM6; GENE_PANEL and data_gene_panel_matrix.txt give IMPACT341/410/468), and a gene missing from an older panel is 'not profiled', not wild-type. Of the six hypothesis genes, RNF43 is the one to suspect as absent from the 341-gene panel (library could not confirm the gene list online; KRAS, BRAF, PIK3CA, AKT1, SMAD4 are on all versions). CHECK: count RNF43 rows in data_mutations.txt and RNF43 presence/values in data_cna.txt for IMPACT341 (-IM3) samples versus -IM5/-IM6 samples; zero events across all IM3 samples while IM5/IM6 show a few percent means not profiled. Also cross-tabulate panel version by right/left side. IF FOUND: compute the RNF43 frequency and test only among samples on panels that cover it (per-gene denominators, as cBioPortal does), never over all samples. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/ ; https://groups.google.com/g/cbioportal/c/h45uoKKw0-k

label: PITFALL samples with zero mutations absent from MAF
text: PITFALL: A cBioPortal mutation file lists only samples that have at least one called mutation; sequenced samples with no mutation (or no CNA / no SV) are simply absent, so building the cohort from data_mutations.txt drops unaltered samples and inflates every frequency. CHECK: compare the set of SAMPLE_IDs in data_clinical_sample.txt / data_gene_panel_matrix.txt with the Tumor_Sample_Barcode set in data_mutations.txt and with the data_cna.txt columns; count samples missing from each. IF FOUND: take the denominator from the clinical sample table restricted to samples profiled in data_gene_panel_matrix.txt, and code samples absent from the mutation file as unaltered (not as missing). Treat a sample missing from data_cna.txt as not CNA-profiled rather than as copy-neutral. SOURCE: https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/3067 ; https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/blob/master/docs/File-Formats.md

label: PITFALL MSS cohort definition (MSI NA, POLE hypermutators)
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is restricted to microsatellite-stable (MSS) tumours, and the MSS filter strongly changes BRAF and RNF43 rates because MSI-high tumours are right-sided and carry BRAF V600E and RNF43 frameshifts; leaving MSI or POLE-hypermutated tumours in fakes a right-sided enrichment. In this dataset MSI_STATUS can be NA (first data row has MSI_STATUS=NA, MSI_SCORE=0.72 and a separate MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE column), so one column alone may not define MSS. CHECK: tabulate MSI_STATUS x MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE, and plot MSI_SCORE and TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS within each; standard MSIsensor cutoffs for MSK-IMPACT are score <3 = MSS, 3 to <10 = indeterminate, >=10 = MSI-H; POLE-ultramutated tumours have very high TMB with a low MSI score. IF FOUND: define MSS explicitly (labelled MSS, or score <3 where the label is NA), exclude MSI-H and POLE/hypermutated cases, and rerun with the stricter and looser MSS definitions to show the label does not depend on it. SOURCE: https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/PO.17.00084 ; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmoldx.2016.07.010

label: PITFALL oncogenic vs any nonsynonymous mutation
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis says 'oncogenic alterations', but data_mutations.txt has no oncogenic/OncoKB column (columns end at Annotation_Status), so counting every nonsynonymous mutation counts passengers and variants of unknown significance, which are commonest in high-TMB tumours and can distort a right/left comparison. CHECK: for each of the six genes list the distinct HGVSp_Short values with counts and Variant_Classification; see what share are known hotspots (KRAS codons 12/13/59/61/117/146; BRAF V600E and known non-V600 activating/kinase-impaired codons such as 594/596/469/601; PIK3CA 542/545/1047 and other recurrent sites; AKT1 E17K) versus rare scattered missense. IF FOUND: classify with OncoKB-style rules: for oncogenes (KRAS, BRAF, PIK3CA, AKT1) count recurrent hotspot/known activating changes; for tumour suppressors (SMAD4, RNF43) count truncating mutations (nonsense, frameshift, splice site) plus known hotspot missense (SMAD4 R361, P356, D351, G386, D537). Run the test both ways (oncogenic-only and any nonsynonymous) and report whether the conclusion holds in both. SOURCE: https://faq.oncokb.org/technical ; https://sop.oncokb.org/static/sop/OncoKB_Curation_Standard_Operating_Procedure_v6_2.pdf ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7529711/

label: PITFALL RNF43 G659fs and BRAF V600E vs non-V600
text: PITFALL: Two of the six genes have variant classes with opposite or MSI-driven behaviour, so the variant definition can flip a gene's result. RNF43 G659fs (a homopolymer frameshift) occurs almost only in MSI-H tumours (about 99 percent in one large series), while N-terminal RNF43 truncations are the MSS / BRAF V600E-associated ones. BRAF V600E is strongly right-sided, whereas non-V600 BRAF mutations do not share that pattern. CHECK: in the MSS cohort tabulate RNF43 variants (G659fs versus other truncating versus missense) and BRAF variants (V600E versus non-V600) by side; any RNF43 G659fs in a tumour labelled MSS is a flag for a misclassified MSI case. IF FOUND: report BRAF as all-oncogenic and V600E-only, report RNF43 as truncating-only, and re-check the MSI status of G659fs carriers before counting them. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1200/po.23.00411 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10777808/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5342576/

label: PITFALL include CNA and SV in alteration calls
text: PITFALL: 'Alterations' covers more than point mutations. OncoKB and the cBioPortal default query count deep deletions, amplifications and fusions/rearrangements as alterations, so a mutation-only analysis undercounts tumour suppressors that are lost by deletion (SMAD4 on 18q, RNF43) and misses BRAF fusions. CHECK: in data_cna.txt read the SMAD4, RNF43, KRAS, BRAF, PIK3CA, AKT1 rows and count values -2 (deep deletion) and 2 (amplification) (MSK-IMPACT files hold mainly -2/0/2, sometimes -1.5); in data_sv.txt count rows where Site1_Hugo_Symbol or Site2_Hugo_Symbol is one of the six genes. IF FOUND: define each gene as altered if it has an oncogenic mutation OR a deep deletion (tumour suppressors) OR an amplification (oncogenes) OR a structural variant, and report the mutation-only result beside the combined one; do not count -1/+1 or seg.mean shifts as alterations. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/oql/ ; https://sop.oncokb.org/static/sop/OncoKB_Curation_Standard_Operating_Procedure_v6_2.pdf ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10162952/

label: PITFALL sidedness definition (transverse, rectum, unknown)
text: PITFALL: There is no single definition of right- versus left-sided colorectal cancer. The common rule is cecum through transverse colon = right and splenic flexure through rectum = left, but some studies drop transverse tumours, some split the transverse colon, and some treat rectum separately; re-deriving side from the detailed site can disagree with the curated side variable. CHECK: cross-tabulate PRIMARY_TUMOR_LOCATION (Right/Left/other) against PRIMARY_SITE (cecum, ascending, hepatic flexure, transverse, splenic flexure, descending, sigmoid, rectosigmoid, rectum); count missing, 'unknown', or both/multiple-primary values. IF FOUND: use the curated PRIMARY_TUMOR_LOCATION as the main grouping, exclude samples without a clear side, and run a sensitivity analysis that excludes transverse-colon tumours (and one that excludes rectum) to show the direction of each gene's effect is stable. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7505124/ ; https://doi.org/10.20524/aog.2017.0191 ; https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/JCO.2020.38.4_suppl.188

label: PITFALL 1: chain detection needs breakpoint-pair SV data that data_sv.txt lacks
text: PITFALL: Chained-rearrangement (chromoplexy) inference needs junction-level SV calls, i.e. both breakpoint coordinates and orientations of every rearrangement plus matched copy number; tools such as ChainFinder, ClusterSV (BEDPE input) and LINX (base-pair-consistent SV+CN input) cannot run without them, and the delivered data_sv.txt has only gene symbols (Site1_Hugo_Symbol equals Site2_Hugo_Symbol; 28 rows, all Event_Info=Fusion for ERG/ETV1/BRAF) with no chromosome/position/partner columns. CHECK: read the data_sv.txt header and confirm there are no Site1/Site2 chromosome or position columns and no interchromosomal partner information; also confirm no other table holds rearrangement junctions. IF FOUND: do not claim to have modelled or detected chains; state explicitly which half of the hypothesis (interdependent rearrangements vs. cancer-gene dysregulation) each table can or cannot address, and base the label on the tables, not on prior knowledge of the literature. SOURCE: https://github.com/cancerit/ClusterSV/ ; https://www.cell.com/cell-genomics/fulltext/S2666-979X(22)00032-5 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4239675/

label: PITFALL one sample per patient, mCRC only, primary vs met
text: PITFALL: The unit of analysis must be the patient with metastatic CRC, not the sample. Sample IDs include -T01/-T02, so some patients have more than one sequenced tumour, and the sample table mixes primary and metastasis specimens and has an MCRC_TYPE column that may include non-metastatic cases; counting samples double-counts patients and breaks the independence assumed by Fisher's test. CHECK: count SAMPLE_IDs per PATIENT_ID; tabulate MCRC_TYPE, SAMPLE_TYPE and STAGE_AT_DIAGNOSIS; cross-tabulate SAMPLE_TYPE by side. IF FOUND: keep one sample per patient (a fixed rule, for example the first sample or the one on the largest panel, or call a patient altered if any sample is), restrict to the mCRC cases, and confirm by a sensitivity analysis within primary-only and metastasis-only specimens. Driver mutations in KRAS, BRAF and PIK3CA are over 90 percent concordant between primary and metastasis, so specimen type is unlikely to move the result but should be shown not to. SOURCE: https://www.thelancet.com/article/S2352-3964(19)30057-X/fulltext ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4189196/

label: PITFALL 2: balanced translocations/chains are invisible in copy-number data
text: PITFALL: Copy-number tables (seg, discrete CNA, log2 CNA) cannot see balanced or reciprocal rearrangements: when both sides of a break are rejoined there is no substantial copy-number change, so translocations and largely copy-neutral closed chains are invisible to read-depth/array-style data, and a copy-number breakpoint tells you neither its partner locus nor its orientation. CHECK: before using data_cna_hg19.seg as a proxy for rearrangements, list what it can show (unbalanced losses/gains and their edges) and verify there is no partner-locus information anywhere. IF FOUND: treat CN breakpoints as evidence about deletions only; absence of CN change is not evidence against chained translocations and presence of deletions is not evidence for them; do not count 'translocations' from CN data. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-019-1913-9 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7738216/ ; https://www.nature.com/articles/hdy2011100

label: PITFALL multi-gene claim: power, multiple testing, direction
text: PITFALL: The claim bundles six genes with very different prevalence (KRAS around 40 to 50 percent, AKT1 around 1 percent in CRC), so power differs hugely per gene; a rare gene can show a clear right-sided excess yet miss p<0.05, and testing six genes without correction can also throw up a false positive. Treating one non-significant rare gene as 'contradiction', or one nominal p<0.05 as 'support', are both errors. CHECK: for each gene build the 2x2 table (altered/unaltered by right/left) among profiled MSS patients, and report right and left percentages, odds ratio with 95 percent CI, two-sided Fisher exact p and Benjamini-Hochberg q across the six genes; note the direction of each effect and the expected counts. IF FOUND: judge the hypothesis on direction plus significance across all six genes together: support needs right-sided excess in the genes (after correction where counts allow), contradiction needs evidence of no excess or left-sided excess with CIs that exclude a meaningful right-sided effect, and a wide CI on a rare gene is 'underpowered', not 'false'. Use Fisher exact rather than chi-square when any expected cell is below 5. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3859974/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7597977/

label: PITFALL 3: interdependence must beat a sequential-independent null model
text: PITFALL: 'Interdependent' or simultaneous origin is an inference against a null of sequentially accumulated independent rearrangements, and pattern-based shortcuts have high false-positive rates (about 3.9% of simulated purely sequential genomes with 50-55 breakpoints show three or fewer copy states; breakpoint clustering and few CN states are suggestive but not conclusive). CHECK: any statistic offered as evidence of interdependence (clustered breakpoints, co-occurring deletions on several chromosomes) must be compared with a simulated/permuted null that keeps each sample's own number of breakpoints and chromosome/segment lengths, with multiple-testing correction across samples. IF FOUND that no such null can be built from the available tables, report the pattern as descriptive only and do not call it evidence that rearrangements arose together. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4239675/ ; https://www.cell.com/cell/fulltext/S0092-8674(13)00212-2 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5860217/

label: PITFALL 4: breakpoint proximity is confounded by fragile sites and recurrent loci
text: PITFALL: Breakpoints that sit close together are not necessarily mechanistically linked: fragile sites, LINE source regions and recurrently selected driver deletions concentrate independent breaks at the same loci, so a uniform-genome null overstates clustering (PCAWG notes proximity 'generally, but not always' implies linkage; LINX annotates fragile sites and LINE regions before clustering). CHECK: test whether apparent clustered CN breakpoints recur at the same genomic positions across many samples (fragile site or selection, or germline CNV/artifact) versus being sample-private; use a permutation that preserves each profile's breakpoint count and per-locus breakpoint probability. IF FOUND recurrent loci drive the signal, exclude or model them separately and do not read clustering as evidence of chained events. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-019-1913-9 ; https://www.cell.com/cell-genomics/fulltext/S2666-979X(22)00032-5 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3112242/

label: PITFALL 5: co-occurrence tests are confounded by per-tumour alteration burden
text: PITFALL: Testing whether deletions/fusions co-occur across tumours with Fisher's exact test or correlation is inflated by heterogeneous per-tumour alteration burden: genomically unstable tumours carry more of everything, so unrelated events co-occur by chance (DISCOVER found most reported co-occurrences do not exceed chance once tumour-specific rates are modelled); in addition cross-tumour co-occurrence says nothing about events arising in one step within a tumour. CHECK: compute each sample's total CN-altered fraction or breakpoint count and see whether the co-occurrence signal disappears after conditioning on it (DISCOVER-style null with sample-specific rates, or stratify by burden); note only about 56 WGS samples, so power is low. IF FOUND: report burden-adjusted results only and do not equate co-occurrence with interdependent genesis. SOURCE: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13059-016-1114-x ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3061884/

label: PITFALL 6: do not conflate chromothripsis/BFB/high CNA burden with chromoplexy
text: PITFALL: Different complex-rearrangement classes get conflated: chromothripsis gives tens to hundreds of breakpoints locally clustered on one or two chromosomes with copy number oscillating between two (occasionally three) states, breakage-fusion-bridge gives clustered inverted gains, whereas chromoplexy chains are unclustered, number in the tens, span several chromosomes and cause little copy-number change; different detection criteria also disagree on a subset of genomes. CHECK: for any sample with many CN segments, tabulate breakpoints per chromosome and the number of distinct CN states per chromosome to see whether the complexity is a one-chromosome oscillation (chromothripsis-like) rather than multi-chromosome. IF FOUND: do not count chromothripsis-like or generally high-CNA-burden samples as support for chromoplexy specifically. SOURCE: https://www.cell.com/cell/fulltext/S0092-8674(13)00212-2 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4239675/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11077613/

label: PITFALL 7: discrete CNA calls are purity-dependent thresholds, not copy numbers
text: PITFALL: Discrete CNA calls (-2,-1,0,1,2) are thresholds on log2 ratios, not purity-corrected integer copy numbers: -1/+1 only exceed a low-level noise threshold, -2 exceeds a sample-specific high-level threshold, and the observed log2 ratio of a real deletion shrinks with tumour purity and subclonality (a clonal one-copy loss gives log2((2-p)/2), about -0.23 at purity 0.3 versus -1 at purity 1). CHECK: compare data_cna.txt against data_log2_cna.txt to recover the thresholds actually used, and plot per-sample deletion calls against PURITY_ABSOLUTE / WGS_BASED_PURITY_ESTIMATION to see whether low-purity samples have systematically fewer calls. IF FOUND: for statements about cancer-gene deletion (e.g. PTEN, TP53, CHD1, NKX3-1, CDKN1B) use purity-aware thresholds or report deep deletions and shallow losses separately, and give frequencies as a sensitivity range. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/user-guide/faq/ ; https://cnvkit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/calling.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9881684/

label: PITFALL 8: seg-file breakpoints include noise, germline CNVs and purity effects
text: PITFALL: Counting breakpoints or focal deletions straight from a WGS read-depth seg file over-counts: GC and replication-timing 'wave' bias, low-mappability regions, germline CNVs and segments supported by few markers create spurious small segments, and segmentation sensitivity varies with purity and coverage, so segments-per-sample is not comparable across samples. CHECK: look at the distribution of num.mark and segment length, flag segments with few markers or tiny |seg.mean|, and flag segments whose boundaries recur at identical coordinates in many samples (germline CNV or artifact). IF FOUND: filter by minimum markers/length and a purity-scaled |seg.mean| threshold, merge adjacent segments with near-equal means before counting breakpoints, and show the conclusion is stable to those filters. SOURCE: https://cnvkit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/calling.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10858679/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3561969/

The clinical tables are split into a patient file (holding CHEMO_RESISTANT) and a sample file, and cBioPortal-format studies allow several samples per patient (e.g. primary plus metastasis, pre- plus post-chemo); samples from one patient are not independent, so a sample-level 2x2 table inflates n and double-counts resistant patients who were biopsied more often. label: Pitfall 4: use CHEMO_RESISTANT among chemotherapy-treated patients, not a survival proxy
text: PITFALL: Wrong outcome or wrong denominator for 'cisplatin resistance'. label: Pitfall 5: sparse 2x2 table needs exact or Firth methods, not chi-square or Wald
text: PITFALL: Wrong test for a rare alteration in a small cohort. With few TP53-altered patients the 2x2 table has expected counts below 5, so the chi-square test and Wald (ordinary logistic regression) intervals are unreliable, and a zero cell (e.g. no altered patient among sensitive cases) makes the maximum-likelihood odds ratio infinite and logistic regression fail to converge (separation). CHECK: print the 2x2 table of TP53 status by CHEMO_RESISTANT at patient level and its expected counts; look for a zero cell. IF FOUND: use Fisher's exact test (two-sided as the primary; mid-p or an unconditional exact test is less conservative), report the odds ratio with an exact confidence interval and the resistant fraction in each group, and use Firth penalised logistic regression (or a 0.5 continuity correction) when a cell is zero or covariates are added. label: Pitfall 6: primary site and histology confound TP53 vs resistance; stratify as sensitivity
text: PITFALL: Confounding by tumour subtype. In germ cell tumours, primary site and histology are established predictors of cisplatin-based chemotherapy failure (IGCCCG: mediastinal primary non-seminoma is poor-risk by definition; seminoma is never poor-risk), so if TP53 alterations cluster in one subtype the crude association partly reflects that subtype (Simpson's paradox is possible). label: Pitfall 7: pre- vs post-chemo sample timing is tied to the outcome
text: PITFALL: Mixing pre-chemotherapy and post-chemotherapy specimens. Chemotherapy selects surviving clones and can itself induce mutations, and post-chemo tissue exists mainly for patients with residual or resistant disease, so alterations found only in post-treatment samples may be acquired or selected rather than present at baseline, and sample timing is correlated with the outcome. CHECK: cross-tabulate SPECIMEN_COLLECTION_PRE_OR_POST_CHEMO (and SAMPLE_TYPE primary vs metastasis) with CHEMO_RESISTANT and with TP53 status. IF FOUND: report the association in all patients (the hypothesis asks only for association, not for a baseline predictor) and again restricted to pre-chemo samples; if it holds only through post-chemo samples say so, and treat it as association with (possibly acquired) resistance rather than as a pre-treatment biomarker.
