text: Scope of the claim: the study supplies only three tables (patient, sample, somatic point mutations/small indels); there is no copy-number, fusion or expression table. The hypothesis is worded in terms of mutation, and the variables needed for a mutation-significance test (somatic mutations per gene per sample) are present, so the missing copy-number table does not by itself make the claim untestable. Confirm which data types exist, restrict the conclusion to somatic SNV/indel significance, say so in the reasoning, and do not extrapolate to overall pathway alteration (amplification of ERBB2/PIK3CA or deletion of PTEN cannot be seen here).

reason: The gene-set definition is the largest analyst degree of freedom in this task and can change the label.
text: 'ERBB-PI3K pathway' has no single agreed gene list, and the result can flip with the definition: a broad database set (e.g. KEGG PI3K-Akt, hundreds of genes including collagens and laminins) dilutes signal and adds long passenger genes, while a narrow curated core (ERBB receptors, PI3K catalytic/regulatory subunits, PTEN, AKT, MTOR and similar) concentrates it. Trying several lists and keeping the one that is significant is a forking-paths error. Write down the core gene list before looking at any counts, base the label on that pre-specified core list, then rerun with one narrow and one broad definition as sensitivity analyses and say explicitly if the conclusion depends on the definition.

reason: A failed join would produce a spurious 'no mutations in the pathway' result.
text: Gene matching in data_mutations.txt: the library's header read found Entrez_Gene_Id = 0 in the mutation table, so selecting pathway genes by Entrez ID would silently return nothing. The file has both Hugo_Symbol and SYMBOL columns, and genes may appear under alias or outdated symbols (e.g. ERBB2 = HER2/NEU, ERBB3 = HER3, MTOR = FRAP1, PTEN = MMAC1). Tabulate Entrez_Gene_Id, match on Hugo_Symbol after alias resolution, compare Hugo_Symbol with SYMBOL, and list in the reasoning which pathway genes were found mutated and which had zero rows, so that a zero is a real zero and not a failed join.

reason: The number of tumours and each tumour's mutation load are inputs to any significance test; a bad join corrupts both.
text: Sample identifiers may not match between tables: the library's header read saw Tumor_Sample_Barcode values like 'NPC015D' in the mutation table but clinical IDs like 'NPC15F', 'NPC29F'; it also saw roughly 55 samples in the clinical sample table, roughly 56 patients, and 56 distinct barcodes in the mutation table (header-level observations; verify). A naive merge on ID can drop most samples, give the wrong denominator, or attach TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS to the wrong tumour. List the distinct IDs in each table, compute the exact-match overlap, try a normalised key (strip leading zeros, drop the trailing letter) and check it is one-to-one. Either build an explicit verified ID map or compute per-sample mutation load directly from the mutation table (rows per barcode); state the denominator (number of tumours sequenced) and how it was derived.

reason: These rows change both the pathway numerator and the background denominator, so the filtering choice can move the p-value.
text: Not every row of data_mutations.txt is a clean somatic coding event: the library's scan reported 68 of 1575 rows with FILTER = common_variant (population-frequency flag, possible germline leakage) and about 21 rows classed Intron/Flank/RNA/IGR; Mutation_Status and Validation_Status are empty and cannot be used to filter. Tabulate FILTER and Variant_Classification overall and within the pathway genes (look at ExAC_AF/GMAF and t_alt_count/t_depth for flagged rows). Run the test with and without the common_variant and non-coding rows, applying the same filter to both the pathway counts and the background counts, and report whether the conclusion changes.

label: PLAN
text: PLAN (bd09-team-a): Estimate the cohort median exonic somatic mutation frequency (mutations per covered Mb) per sample. Primary measure: TOTAL_PER_MB (silent+nonsilent / COVERED_BASES), recomputed from counts to verify; alternatives: nonsilent-only per covered Mb, NUM_NONSILENT/30 (TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS), missense-only per covered Mb, and MAF coding row counts as cross-check. Judge 'high' as an absolute claim against external benchmarks (paediatric medians ~0.02-0.8/Mb, adult cancers ~1-10/Mb, pan-cancer average ~4/Mb, TMB-high >=10/Mb); settled only if every definition puts the median on the same side by >3-fold. Checks: one sample per patient, SOMATIC_STATUS matched, MAF duplicates, Variant_Classification classes, samples absent from MAF/zero mutations, per-platform medians (Exome_WGA / WXS / WGS) with Kruskal-Wallis, COVERED_BASES scale for WGS, high-risk proxy via AGE>1.5y or MYCN_AMP with sensitivity dropping doubtful patients, strata by MYCN and age. Would change method if: TOTAL_PER_MB not reproducible from counts, WGS covered bases on genome scale, platform strata on opposite sides of benchmark, or unmatched samples present.

reason: It rules out the standard significance tools and determines what kind of background model is defensible on this data.
text: The mutation table is essentially nonsynonymous-only (library scan: 4 'Silent' rows out of 1575). Methods that estimate each gene's background mutation rate from synonymous mutations (dNdScv, MutSigCV-style silent-based backgrounds) cannot be run validly: with synonymous calls absent dN/dS tends to infinity and everything looks selected. Confirm by tabulating Variant_Classification. Do not compute dN/dS or a silent-based background rate; build the null from the nonsynonymous load itself (per-sample nonsynonymous count spread over the coding exome, scaled by each gene's coding length), state that this background includes drivers and ignores gene-specific covariates, and treat the resulting p-value as approximate.

reason: What counts as a 'relevant variable' for this hypothesis depends on knowing the subtypes are expression-defined; missing a hidden subtype column, or assuming one exists, would change the label.
text: The SCLC subtypes SCLC-A, SCLC-N and SCLC-P are defined by RNA or protein EXPRESSION of ASCL1, NEUROD1 and POU2F3 (RNA-seq clustering or dominant-TF calls, or IHC), not by DNA alterations. So the first step is to establish whether the data hold any variable that measures them. (a) List every supplied file and check for an expression-type table (cBioPortal names such as data_mrna_seq_*, data_expression*, *_zscores*, data_rppa*, data_methylation*). (b) Read all column names AND the '#' description lines of data_clinical_patient.txt and data_clinical_sample.txt, list the unique values of CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED, ONCOTREE_CODE, GRADE, MSI_COMMENT, SAMPLE_TYPE and the timeline NOTE/SUBTYPE columns, and search all of them for ASCL1, NEUROD1, POU2F3, YAP1, 'SCLC-A', 'subtype', 'neuroendocrine', 'IHC'. The timeline column called SUBTYPE is a treatment subtype (e.g. 'Systemic therapy'), not a molecular subtype. The library read only file headers and reported clinical, CNA, seg, gene-panel, mutation, SV and timeline files and no subtype column; confirm this yourself on the full tables. If a real subtype/IHC/expression variable exists, tabulate it among xenograft samples only. If none exists, say that the subtype variable is unmeasured and apply the task's own label definitions to that fact rather than building a call from DNA data.

reason: 'Significantly mutated' needs an explicit background model; a raw frequency or length-blind test can give the wrong call in either direction.
text: Reporting 'X% of tumours carry a mutation in the pathway' is not a significance test. A gene set with many or long genes is hit in a large share of tumours by chance alone, and tests that treat all genes as equally mutable ignore gene length. Sum the coding length (bp) of the pathway genes, compute the expected number of tumours with at least one pathway mutation given each tumour's mutation rate, and compare observed with expected. Use a length-aware null (per-gene Bernoulli/binomial with probability from coding length x background rate, as in PathScan) or an empirical null from random gene sets matched on number of genes and total coding length, rather than a raw frequency or an unweighted hypergeometric test.

reason: The choice between a pooled and a per-sample background can change whether the pathway test comes out significant.
text: Use a per-tumour background rate, not one cohort-wide rate. Pooling all tumours into a single binomial inflates significance when mutation load varies between tumours, because a few high-load tumours contribute most pathway hits; unmodelled background heterogeneity is the main source of false-positive 'significantly mutated' calls. Separately, low tumour purity (typical of nasopharyngeal carcinoma, with heavy non-malignant infiltrate) lowers sensitivity for somatic calls, so both pathway hits and background counts are under-called in low-purity tumours and raw pathway frequency is a lower bound; the sample table has TUMOR_CELLULARITY_DOMINANT_CLONE_VAF and TUMOR_CELLULARITY_PATHOLOGY_REVIEW (some 'N.A.'). Check per-sample mutation counts, whether pathway-mutated tumours are the high-load ones, and how counts relate to cellularity. Prefer a test that conditions on each tumour's own mutation count (per-sample p-values combined by Fisher/Lancaster, or a Poisson-binomial across samples), which handles both load heterogeneity and purity-driven under-calling, and report a sensitivity analysis without the top-load outlier tumours.

reason: An empty search for the three genes in the DNA tables is the most likely thing to be misread as support for the hypothesis; the teams need to know it reflects panel coverage.
text: ASCL1, NEUROD1 and POU2F3 are reported NOT to be on the MSK-IMPACT 468-gene panel (nor are INSM1 or REST), although YAP1, MYC, MYCL, MYCN, NOTCH1-4, SOX2, NKX2-1, RB1 and TP53 are. Finding no mutation, CNA or SV row for the three genes therefore means 'not profiled', not 'wild-type' or 'subtype not present'. Check: search Hugo_Symbol in data_cna.txt and data_mutations.txt and both gene columns of data_sv.txt for ASCL1, NEUROD1, POU2F3 (aliases ASH1/HASH1, NEUROD/BETA2, SKN1A/OCT11; Entrez IDs 429, 4760, 25833), and read data_gene_panel_matrix.txt for each sample's panel. Also note how data_cna.txt is coded: -2 deep deletion, -1 shallow loss, 0 diploid, 1 gain, 2 amplification; panel versions are mixed (patient IDs ending IM3, IM5, IM6 = 341, 410, 468 genes; models listed as IMPACT468), so a 0 or blank can mean 'gene not on that sample's panel' and a gene has a row only if it is on a panel (expect about panel-size rows, not ~20,000). Copy number of a gene says nothing about its mRNA or protein level. Never read a missing row or a 0 as 'TF not expressed' or 'subtype absent'; restrict any patient-versus-model genomic comparison to genes shared by all panel versions involved.

reason: Tells the team to check that the pathway-level call is robust to the null chosen and not driven by a single gene.
text: Self-contained and competitive nulls answer different questions and can disagree. A self-contained test (pathway mutated more than a background rate predicts) can be significant because of one highly mutated member gene; a competitive test (pathway mutated more than other genes of similar size) can be non-significant when many genes outside the pathway are also mutated. State which null was tested, do a leave-one-gene-out rerun and a per-gene breakdown of mutated samples, say whether the signal is spread over several pathway genes or carried by one gene, and prefer a conclusion that holds under both nulls.

reason: A team working from DNA tables alone may try to infer subtypes from MYC-family or locus copy number; this tells them that inference is not a measurement in either direction.
text: Genomic proxies cannot assign SCLC-A/N/P. MYC/MYCL/MYCN amplification, NOTCH mutations, RB1/TP53 status, YAP1 copy number or mutation, or seg-file copy number at the ASCL1 (12q23), NEUROD1 (2q31) or POU2F3 (11q23) loci have no published sensitivity or specificity for subtype: exome/genome studies of SCLC found no recurrent mutation or CNA that co-segregates with the expression subtypes, lineage-TF expression is epigenetically driven, and the only DNA-derived data shown to subtype SCLC is DNA methylation (not a mutation/CNA table). The MYC links are loose: MYC amplification is reported in only about 15-20% of NEUROD1-driven tumours and under 5% of others, MYCL/MYCN activation merely predominates in ASCL1-driven tumours, and most tumours of every subtype have no MYC-family amplification. Panel seg files also have sparse markers (see num.mark), so off-panel loci are interpolated. If such alterations are examined in the MSK_LX models, ask whether the same calls would be equally expected under any other subtype; report them at most as subtype-agnostic context and do not base either a 'present' or an 'absent' conclusion on them.

reason: The alpha/multiplicity convention can decide the label for intermediate p-values, so it must be fixed in advance.
text: Fix the significance threshold and the family of tests before computing. 'Significantly mutated' for a pathway is a p/q-value against a background model, and the threshold depends on how many gene sets were tested: a scan over hundreds of gene sets needs FWER/FDR control, while a single pre-specified pathway is judged at a nominal alpha. Mixing the two (scanning many sets then quoting an uncorrected p, or Bonferroni-correcting a single pre-specified test by an imaginary family) can flip the call when p lies between about 1e-4 and 0.05. Report the nominal p for the pre-specified core list as the primary result, say whether it would survive correction for a realistic number of canonical pathways (about 10, as in curated oncogenic-pathway templates), count any extra pathway definitions or filters you ran, and call the result borderline in the reasoning if the label depends on that choice.

reason: This sets the standard of evidence for a negative claim and stops the label being chosen from prior belief or from analyses that could not have discriminated.
text: The hypothesis is a universal negative ('subtypes are not present'). Supporting it needs a subtype-measuring assay showing none of the three TF states in any model; one confidently subtyped model would refute it; without such an assay neither direction is demonstrated, and absence of evidence must not be counted as evidence of absence. For each analysis you consider, ask: 'could this result have come out differently if the subtypes were present versus absent?' If not, it is uninformative and should not be counted toward any label. For every statement in your reasoning, name the supplied file and column that supports it; background knowledge of SCLC biology or of what the literature says about PDX/CDX models does not count as evidence from the data, and cBioPortal-format deposits often contain only the targeted-DNA part of a multi-omic study. The label must follow the task's own rule about whether relevant variables exist in the tables. If an expression/IHC variable does turn out to exist, note that subtypes are not clean bins (ASCL1 and NEUROD1 are often co-expressed, a TF-negative group exists, YAP1 is not a validated subtype), so calls need a stated dominant-TF rule and thresholds.

reason: Prevents the team from deciding the label from single-gene results and makes them qualify how informative the pathway-level result is at this cohort size.
text: Power: with roughly 56 exomes the cohort has low power for genes mutated in a few percent of tumours (most cancer genes are mutated at 2-20% and need hundreds of tumours to detect individually), which is why pathway-level aggregation is used. Per-gene tests alone therefore cannot settle a pathway-level claim; test at the pathway level. Report the observed pathway frequency with an exact binomial confidence interval, the expected frequency under the null, and the smallest frequency the test could detect at this sample size; if the pathway test is null, say whether that reflects a frequency close to background or simply lack of power.

reason: The hypothesis is about the PDX/CDX models only, so the teams must separate them from patient tumours and count them correctly.
text: The tables mix patient clinical tumours (sample IDs like P-00xxxxx-T01-IM6) with xenograft models (IDs like MSK_LX...), and several models can come from one patient (e.g. MSK_LX773A to MSK_LX773L). reason: Gives a second line of evidence that does not depend on the approximate background model and shows whether the result is sensitive to how a 'hit' is defined.
text: Counting every missense variant in a pathway gene as a pathway 'hit' mixes passengers with drivers. Expert pathway analyses count only activating hotspot mutations in oncogenes and truncating or recurrent mutations in tumour suppressors; recurrence at the same residue is independent evidence of selection that does not need a silent-mutation background. For each pathway gene list the protein changes (HGVSp_Short), the Hotspot column, Variant_Classification, and whether the same codon recurs across tumours or matches well-known activating residues. Report two tallies, all nonsynonymous and putative-driver-only, and note whether any significance rests on recurrent/known-driver events or on scattered unique missense variants.

reason: The label depends on how the two-part claim and its implicit comparator are read, and on not confusing 'small n / non-significant' with either 'supported' or 'Not verifiable'.
text: Reading the hypothesis and choosing the label. The claim has two parts and each needs its own evaluation: (1) fusion-negative rhabdomyosarcoma (FN-RMS) acquires fewer new alterations between an earlier and a later sample, where the library reads the unstated comparator as fusion-positive RMS (FP-RMS); (2) no newly acquired mutation is common, i.e. recurs across FN patients. Groups are likely to be small (around ten patients each), so a non-significant p-value is not evidence of 'no difference', and zero recurrences in n patients is still compatible with a true rate of up to about 3/n. Report direction and effect size first (for example median acquired alterations per patient, FN vs FP, with an exact Mann-Whitney or Fisher test) and significance second; separately tabulate every gene acquired in two or more FN patients, at gene level and at pathway level. An observed direction opposite to the claim counts as evidence against it whatever the p-value. 'Not verifiable' is for missing variables, not for small n: first establish whether the tables really hold multiple samples per patient and a way to tell FN from FP, and let that, not sample size, decide whether the claim is testable.

reason: FN versus FP is the grouping variable of the whole analysis; a wrong or per-sample definition moves patients between groups and can create spurious 'acquired fusions'.
text: Defining fusion status. The library reports that the tables have no fusion-status column, and histology is not a substitute: roughly 20% of alveolar RMS lack a PAX3/PAX7-FOXO1 fusion, embryonal, spindle-cell and pleomorphic RMS are fusion-negative, and a DNA capture panel can miss a real fusion in any single sample. Assign fusion status per patient, not per sample: cross-tabulate ONCOTREE_CODE / CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED against any PAX3-FOXO1 or PAX7-FOXO1 row (either gene order) in data_sv.txt across all of that patient's samples. List discordant patients (alveolar without a fusion call; fusion called in one sample of a patient but not another) and confirm every sample carries an RMS code. Treat a fusion seen in any sample of a patient as present from the start (the patient is FP in all samples and the fusion is never counted as 'acquired'). Run the FN-vs-FP comparison under both the SV-based and the histology-based definition and report whether the conclusion survives moving the discordant patients. (Details of the files quoted here are the library's description, not checked by the director: confirm them against the files before relying on them.)

reason: Counting per sample or per pair inflates n and double-counts retained gains, and dropping zero-alteration samples overstates acquisition unevenly between groups; both can change the FN-vs-FP direction and the recurrence table.
text: Unit of analysis, zeros and sample order. Patients appear to contribute two or more samples each (the library estimates about 42 samples from about 20 patients), so samples and sample pairs are not independent. Make the patient the unit: define one baseline (earliest) sample per patient, take the union of distinct alterations absent at baseline and present in any later sample, and give each patient one acquired count; drop single-sample patients from the acquisition analysis. 'Recurrent' or 'common' means the same gene acquired in two or more different patients, never in two samples of one patient. Samples with no mutations or no structural variants have no rows at all in data_mutations.txt / data_sv.txt, so build the sample list from data_clinical_sample.txt and data_gene_panel_matrix.txt (reconciled with the data_cna.txt columns), left-join counts and fill 0 for profiled samples; keep zero-acquisition patients in every denominator and test. Do not infer sample order from the ID suffix alone: use SAMPLE_TYPE (Primary/Metastasis/Recurrence) and AGE_AT_SEQ_REPORTED_YEARS together with the suffix, flag ties and contradictions, and for pairs whose order is ambiguous report 'private to each sample' counts rather than a directional 'acquired' count. (Details of the files quoted here are the library's description, not checked by the director: confirm them against the files before relying on them.)

reason: The choice of data types and of the acquisition metric (absolute vs proportional, gained vs total burden) can each flip the group comparison, so the team must fix and state them rather than default to a mutation-only or TMB-based count.
text: What counts as a 'new alteration'. 'Alterations' is broader than point mutations and indels. Literature background: FP-RMS is driven mostly by copy-number events with few point mutations, while FN-RMS carries more point mutations and a higher starting burden. Two consequences. First, counting only data_mutations.txt biases the FN-vs-FP comparison; count acquired events per patient separately in data_mutations.txt, data_cna.txt (nonzero discrete calls) and data_sv.txt, and combined, report the combined count as primary and each type separately, and say explicitly if the direction differs between data types. Second, the total or TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS of a later sample is not a measure of acquisition: never use it as the 'acquired' variable. Per patient compute baseline count, number shared, number private to the later sample(s) and number lost, and compare groups on (a) absolute acquired count, (b) fraction of patients with at least one acquired alteration, (c) acquired as a fraction of later-sample alterations. State which metric the label rests on and whether (a)-(c) agree in direction.

reason: A panel upgrade between samples manufactures 'acquired' alterations; if cross-panel pairs are unevenly split between FN and FP it biases the comparison directly.
text: Gene-panel versions within a pair. Samples of one patient may have been sequenced on different MSK-IMPACT panel versions (for example IMPACT410 / 468 / 505). A gene present only on the later panel can never be called in the earlier sample, so its alteration looks newly acquired when it is only newly assayed. From data_gene_panel_matrix.txt / GENE_PANEL tabulate the panel of the earlier and later sample for every patient. For every alteration called acquired, ask whether its gene could have been seen on the earlier panel; gene lists are not in the data, so use NA/blank cells in the data_cna.txt columns of older-panel samples and whether that gene is ever altered in any sample on the older panel. Check whether cross-panel pairs are unevenly split between FP and FN patients. Count acquired alterations only in genes assayable in both samples (or restrict to same-panel pairs as a sensitivity analysis) and report the result both ways. (Details of the files quoted here are the library's description, not checked by the director: confirm them against the files before relying on them.)

reason: Gives the sensitivity analyses needed to show the FN-vs-FP result is not produced by purity, coverage, germline contamination or synchronous sampling differences between pairs.
text: A mutation private to the later sample is not proven to be acquired. The mutation file holds only called variants, and the assay reports a call only above depth and allele-fraction thresholds (roughly depth >=20 with >=8 alt reads / 2% VAF at hotspots, >=10 alt reads / 5% VAF elsewhere), so low purity or coverage in the earlier sample turns a shared mutation into a false acquired one, and low purity in the later sample hides real gains. Single-region biopsies can also miss a pre-existing subclone, and samples without a matched normal (SOMATIC_STATUS = Unmatched) can carry germline variants that look like private somatic mutations. For each private-to-later mutation compute VAF = t_alt_count / (t_alt_count + t_ref_count); compare TUMOR_PURITY and SAMPLE_COVERAGE within each pair and between FP and FN groups; flag pairs reported at the same age or that are primary versus synchronous metastasis; flag private variants with VAF near 50% or 100% in unmatched samples. Describe the quantity as 'alterations private to the later sample' (an upper bound on true acquisition, applied equally to both groups), repeat the group comparison excluding low-purity pairs, low-VAF private calls and likely-germline variants, and state that true absence cannot be confirmed without read-level data. (Details of the files quoted here are the library's description, not checked by the director: confirm them against the files before relying on them.)

reason: Copy-number events are expected to be a large share of alterations in one group; per-gene counting and threshold artefacts could inflate acquired counts unevenly and so change the comparison.
text: Copy-number gains and losses between paired samples. Discrete gene-level calls in data_cna.txt come from fold-change thresholds, so the same amplification can be called in a high-purity sample and missed in a low-purity one, and adjacent genes in one amplicon inflate counts if each gene is a separate event. For each copy-number call private to one sample of a pair, look up the overlapping segment's seg.mean in data_cna_hg19.seg for both samples: if the partner shows a same-direction shift below threshold, treat it as shared, not acquired. Collapse co-amplified neighbouring genes on one segment into one event, count per segment/amplicon rather than per gene, and rerun the group comparison.

reason: With about ten patients per group a single outlier decides a mean-based comparison; the team needs robust statistics and an explicit with/without-outlier result.
text: Outliers and uncontrolled confounders. The number of alterations gained between samples depends on the time between them and on intervening chemotherapy or radiotherapy (treated relapses can be hypermutated), so one hypermutated or long-interval patient can dominate a group mean. Look at the acquired count per patient by group for an outlier (also check TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS and MSI_TYPE of later samples), and compare between groups the interval between samples from AGE_AT_SEQ_REPORTED_YEARS (whole years only, so coarse). Use medians and rank or permutation tests rather than means, report results with and without any outlier, and state interval and therapy as uncontrolled confounders (the library reports therapy data are not in the tables). label: PLAN
text: PLAN (bd10-team-b, Wnt vs histone acetylation in endometrial carcinoma, 95 tumours): Quantity = association between Wnt pathway activation and histone acetyl-site abundance across tumours. Wnt defined two ways: (a) CTNNB1 somatic mutation status (exon-3 hotspot vs WT) from data_mutations, (b) continuous Wnt-target mRNA score (AXIN2, NKD1, LEF1, RNF43, ZNRF3, NOTUM, TCF7, SP5, LGR5 etc. z-score mean) from data_mrna_seq_rsem. Histone acetylation = acetyl-sites on histone genes (H1/H2A/H2B/H3/H4 gene symbols) in data_acetylprotein_quantification. Method: per-site Wilcoxon (mutant vs WT) and Spearman (Wnt score), BH FDR across histone sites; also a per-sample histone-acetylation summary; permutation test of sample labels for a global statistic; compare enrichment of histone sites vs all other acetyl-sites as background. Checks: sample ID match across files, duplicates, missingness per site, TMT batch/plex confounding, adjustment for histone protein abundance, adjustment for genomic subtype (MSI/POLE/CNV-high/serous histology) and tumour purity, restricting to endometrioid. Would change method if: batch is confounded with Wnt status (then stratify/adjust), if association vanishes after subtype adjustment (report as confounded), or if histone acetyl sites are too sparse (then use protein-level acetylation summary). Label rule: True if FDR-significant histone-site associations survive adjustment and permutation; False if relevant variables exist but no association; Not verifiable only if no histone acetyl sites or no Wnt variable exist.

label: PLAN
text: PLAN (bd10-team-a): Estimate the association between Wnt activation and histone lysine-acetylation site levels in endometrial tumours. Wnt variables fixed in advance: (1) binary CTNNB1 exon-3 hotspot (codons 32-45) mutation vs wild-type (non-hotspot CTNNB1 mutants excluded in primary, included as WT in sensitivity); (2) continuous Wnt target score = mean z of AXIN2,NKD1,LGR5,RNF43,ZNRF3,NOTUM,LEF1,TCF7,SP5,APCDD1 mRNA, validated against hotspot status. Histone family fixed in advance: acetyl rows with gene ^HIST|^H1F|^H2AF|^H3F3 (136 rows, 30 genes), tumour samples only, sites with >=50% observed and >=5 mutants. Method: per-site Welch t (and OLS with covariates), BH FDR across histone sites, sample-label permutation set test (mean |t|, count p<0.05; 10000 perms) and comparison with background of all ~10.8k acetyl sites; Wilcoxon/Spearman agreement; leave-one-out for top sites. Checks: per-sample medians of acetyl table; plex balance and missingness; parent-protein adjustment; purity, proliferation, subtype/histology (within endometrioid, within CNV-low, covariates), EP300/CREBBP mutation exclusion. Decision rule: True if histone sites survive FDR or the sample-permutation set test is significant with consistent direction and it survives subtype/protein adjustment; False if variables are present, power is adequate and no association; Not verifiable only if variables are absent. Would change method if: Wnt status confounded with plex/subtype (then stratify/adjust), score fails positive control (drop score), or results driven by single samples.

label: PLAN
text: PLAN (bd07-team-a analyst, written before analysis): Quantities: (1) prevalence of TERT promoter mutations (chr5:1295228/1295250 and other 5'Flank TERT) per histology (CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED/ONCOTREE_CODE) and pooled, denominator = sequenced samples in #sequenced_samples header intersected with clinical sample table, one per patient, exact binomial 95% CIs; (2) clonality = proportion of TERT-mutant tumours whose CCF 95% interval includes 1, CCF = VAF*(p*N_T+2(1-p))/(m*p) using TUMOR_PURITY and seg-derived TERT copy number, plus purity-free check: TERT VAF / truncal driver hotspot VAF (BRAF V600E, RAS) in the same sample; (3) first check whether a PTC group exists in the tables at all (tabulate histology). Checks: sample-set consistency across files, purity calibration via driver CCF, low-VAF/low-alt-read TERT calls by specimen type (FFPE vs frozen), batch x histology x TERT stratification, matched/unmatched status, detection floor per sample, prevalence restricted to adequate purity/driver-detected samples. Criteria fixed in advance: 'highly prevalent' = pooled advanced prevalence with CI lower bound well above ~10% and majority-level in ATC; 'clonal' = majority of TERT-mutant tumours with CCF interval including 1 and TERT/driver VAF ratio near 1. Change of method: if purity column is biased (driver CCF far from 1) rely on relative VAF; if no PTC samples exist, the comparative half is not measurable in-data and the label is chosen by the task's label definitions applied to what is measurable; if TERT calls are low-VAF FFPE-only, do not call subclonal.

Label chosen: False (direction opposite to the hypothesis).

text: RESULT (bd08-team-b): In the 66-patient BRAF-mutant melanoma BRAFi cohort, PTEN loss-of-function (truncating mutation or deep deletion, n=13) is associated with SHORTER PFS (median 2.6 vs 6.2 months, Cox HR 1.97, 95% CI 1.04-3.73, p=0.038; adjusted for MEKi combo HR 2.44, p=0.010), so the hypothesis that PTEN LoF increases PFS is labelled False.

text: PLAN (bd16-team-a, TERT promoter mutation vs TERT mRNA in GBM): Quantity = difference in TERT mRNA (Entrez 7015 row of data_mrna_seq_v2_rsem.txt, log2(RSEM+1)) between samples with a TERT promoter hotspot call (5'Flank at hg19 chr5:1295228/1295250 in data_mutations.txt) and mutation-profiled samples with no call. Method = first establish whether any promoter rows / clinical TERT column exist (if none -> Not verifiable); then Mann-Whitney primary test, medians, AUC with bootstrap CI, Fisher on detectable expression; restrict to RNA-seq AND mutation-profiled (gene panel matrix) samples, one sample per patient. Checks = set intersections, call rate vs 70-80% expected, t_alt/t_ref depth, zero fraction of TERT, z-score file cross-check, IDH/G-CIMP/ATRX stratification, TERT copy number covariate, purity proxy (chr10 loss / chr7 gain seg.mean amplitude, VAF of other mutations) compared between groups and adjusted for. Change of method if: no promoter calls (label Not verifiable), call rate far below expectation (comparison group = 'no call', null not interpretable as support), purity confounding (adjusted analysis), tiny n (underpowered wording).

label: LEARNED
text: LEARNED: A pan-cancer exome analysis of 3,083 tumour-normal pairs across 27 tumour types (about 30 Mb coding sequence covered per sample) found median nonsynonymous mutation frequency varying about 1000-fold across tumour types, with paediatric and haematological cancers lowest and melanoma/lung highest (melanoma samples 0.1-100 per Mb); this was confirmed only from search snippets, because the full-text fetch returned just the author list, so the specific 4.0/Mb average rests on the director's note, not on a page I read. USED FOR: choosing the absolute pan-cancer scale as the benchmark for whether a cohort median of 0.60 mutations/Mb is 'high'. SOURCE: https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3919509/ and https://acsjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/cncr.31345

text: PLAN (bd15-team-b): Estimate per-gene mutation frequency = fraction of cSCC patients/samples with >=1 protein-altering (nonsynonymous: missense/nonsense/splice/frameshift/in-frame) mutation in EP300, PBRM1, USP28, CHUK from data_mutations.txt, denominator = all sequenced samples in data_clinical_sample.txt. Method: audit files (sample/patient ID match, duplicates, samples with zero mutations, variant classes, multiple samples per patient), count mutated samples per gene, rank each gene's frequency against all genes, and because cSCC has very high UV mutation burden, check whether frequency exceeds background expectation (compare with nonsilent/silent ratio, gene-length-adjusted rank, truncating fraction, hotspot/recurrence). Checks: all-variant vs nonsynonymous-only counting, per-patient vs per-sample, sensitivity to excluding hypermutators/low-VAF calls. Would change method if: multiple samples per patient (collapse to patient), mutation file contains non-coding/silent calls dominating (filter), samples missing from MAF (denominator), or gene aliases used. 'Frequently' judged as recurrent in a substantial fraction (>=~10%) of tumours and among top-ranked genes.

ACTION: measured the advanced-cancer half only, did not import or test any outside PTC figure, and stated the limit in the answer; label chosen on the measured half (True) with reduced confidence.

MEANS: purity-based CCF of TERT is just the TERT/driver VAF ratio, the driver-CCF calibration is circular, and in those 9 samples TERT is 'clonal' by definition. ACTION: changed the method: primary clonality evidence is the within-sample TERT VAF vs BRAF/RAS hotspot VAF ratio (45 samples with a driver), and the 9 circular samples plus 3 without purity are reported as not independently assessable (46 assessable: 39 clonal, 7 subclonal).

No TERT promoter call has VAF<5% or <10 alt reads (minimum 18 alt reads, VAF 0.066), so FFPE deamination artefacts are not driving the calls. ACTION: reported prevalence and clonality stratified by batch; conclusion (high prevalence, mostly clonal) holds in each stratum, so method unchanged.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: 7 of 58 TERT-promoter-mutant tumours have a CCF 95% upper bound below 1 / TERT VAF significantly below the BRAF/RAS driver VAF (P-0002212, P-0000415, P-0000320, s_JJ_thy_023_P, s_JF_thy_017_P, s_JJ_thy_051_P [ratio 0.32], s_JF_thy_002_P), 3 of them unmatched-normal samples; 22 have CCF significantly above 1 (TERT VAF above driver VAF, 12 mutants have |seg.mean|>=0.2 at 5p). The Hotspot column is 0 for all 564 rows and the lowest call anywhere is 10 alt reads / VAF 0.02, so subclones below the caller floor are invisible. MEANS: 'clonal' holds for the large majority (39/46 independently assessable; 39/45 with TERT/driver ratio >=0.75, median ratio 1.12) but not for all, and is 'clonal among detected mutations'. ACTION: reported the proportion with the exceptions named and did not claim all clonal; copy-number-adjusted CCF flips only 1 call (P-0001358, 5p loss).

label: PLAN
text: PLAN (bd15-team-a analyst, written before any per-gene numbers): Estimate, for EP300, PBRM1, USP28, CHUK, the fraction of cSCC samples (denominator = all samples in data_clinical_sample.txt) and of patients with >=1 protein-altering variant (missense, nonsense, frameshift, in-frame, splice site, nonstop, start site), by exact Hugo_Symbol match confirmed by chromosome location, with Wilson 95% CI. Criterion for 'frequently mutated' fixed in advance: PRIMARY = gene mutated in >=15% of samples AND in the top 5% of all genes ranked by mutated-sample fraction; LOOSER = >=10% and top 10%; STRICTER = >=20% and top 2%; all four genes must each pass (conjunction). Calibration: positive controls TP53, NOTCH1, NOTCH2, CDKN2A, HRAS, FAT1; negative controls TTN, MUC16, olfactory receptors, and random genes; compare observed vs burden-based expectation and nonsyn:syn within gene as secondary. Checks: MAF vs clinical sample set, variant classification table, TMB ratio check, multi-tumour patients and shared identical variants, subgroup (RDEB/immune/TMB strata) frequencies, Mann-Whitney of TMB mutated vs not, call-quality sensitivity filter (t_alt>=4, VAF>=0.05; possible-germline flag), +/-1 sample sensitivity, truncating share. I would change the method if positive controls come out implausibly low (pipeline error), if samples are missing from the MAF, or if mutations are confined to duplicate tumours/artefact calls. Label rests on prevalence+rank relative to controls; selection tests are reported as secondary since the cohort is underpowered.

label: PLAN
text: PLAN (bd06-team-a analyst, written before any survival result): Quantity = difference in overall survival between patients with a somatic BRCA2 mutation and those without (hazard ratio direction + two-sided p). Primary analysis, fixed in advance: mutant = patient with >=1 protein-altering BRCA2 call (Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift_Ins/Del, In_Frame_Ins/Del, Splice_Site, Nonstop, Translation_Start_Site) whose FILTER is not 'common_variant'; all other sequenced patients wild-type; OS event = 1:DECEASED; drop patients with blank OS_MONTHS/OS_STATUS; two-sided log-rank test, with KM curves, univariable Cox HR and 95% CI. Because the mutant group is expected to be small: also permutation log-rank p and Firth-penalized Cox if Cox is unstable. Checks: ID sets identical across the 3 files, one sample per patient; event indicator sum = DECEASED count; zero/negative times; list every BRCA2 row (classification, HGVSp, FILTER, ExAC, VAF, multiple hits); follow-up comparison (reverse KM) by group; cross-tab BRCA2 vs DNA_REPAIR_STATUS/TMB/stage/age. Sensitivity (labelled, not for choosing the label): truncating-only, including common_variant calls, including silent/non-coding rows, stratified by DNA_REPAIR_STATUS, restricted to NonDef, stage-adjusted Cox. Label rule: True only if primary shows HR>1 (mutant worse) AND p<0.05 robust to the exact/permutation test; False if variables are present and the primary comparison does not show significantly shorter survival; Not verifiable only if variables were absent. I would change the method if IDs do not match, if survival columns cannot be parsed, or if the mutant group has 0 evaluable patients.

text: PLAN (bd05-team-a analyst): Quantity = number of sequenced MPN patients with nonmutated JAK2 who carry a somatic CALR mutation (patient-level 2x2 of JAK2-mutated x somatic-CALR). Method: check clinical PATIENT_ID/SAMPLE_ID one-to-one and overlap with MAF barcodes; select CALR and JAK2 rows by Hugo_Symbol (plus chr19 13.049-13.055Mb backstop) with no Variant_Type/Mutation_Status filter; define JAK2 status two ways (nonsynonymous JAK2 rows; curated 'JAK2/MPL mutation' label) and flag disagreements; judge CALR somatic status from tumour allele burden vs germline allele percentage calibrated on JAK2 V617F germline signal, reporting frameshift exon 9 indels separately from other CALR rows. Decision: >=1 credible somatic CALR in a JAK2-nonmutated patient under both JAK2 definitions => False; zero among a reasonable denominator => True; Not verifiable only if CALR/indels cannot appear or no JAK2-nonmutated patients. label: PLAN
text: PLAN (bd11-team-b, ccRCC ITH hypothesis): Quantity = fraction of ccRCC tumours with evidence of intratumor heterogeneity (ITH), i.e. per-patient, among patients with >=2 spatially distinct regions of the same tumour, the share showing non-shared (subclonal) mutations/CNAs. Method: (1) audit all 9 files - cancer types/oncotree codes in clinical sample table, sample-ID overlap between clinical, mutation, CNA, seg, SV, panel matrix; (2) identify whether any ccRCC samples and any multi-region samples exist; (3) if they do, compute per-patient shared vs private variant fractions and count patients with >=1 private driver/variant; label True only if every multi-region ccRCC tumour shows ITH, False if some do not. Checks: cancer-type column values, kidney genes (VHL/PBRM1/BAP1/SETD2) frequencies, patients with multiple samples, panel differences across samples (a private mutation in a gene not covered by the other sample's panel is not ITH), duplicates. Change of method: if the dataset has no ccRCC samples or no multi-region sampling, the hypothesis cannot be tested and the label is Not verifiable rather than forcing a proxy (e.g. VAF spread in single samples).

label: PLAN
text: PLAN (bd11-team-a, written after reading headers only, before any tabulation): Quantity = proportion of ccRCC tumours in the supplied study showing intratumour heterogeneity (ITH), with its denominator. Step 1: tabulate CANCER_TYPE, CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED, ONCOTREE_CODE, PRIMARY_SITE, TISSUE_SEQUENCED in data_clinical_sample.txt and count kidney/ccRCC samples and patients; also scan the mutation file for a ccRCC-like driver profile (VHL/PBRM1/SETD2/BAP1) as a cross-check on the labels. Step 2: check ID mapping across sample table, mutation, seg, CNA, panel matrix files. Step 3: count samples per patient, classify multi-sample patients (same lesion vs primary/met vs longitudinal), check for any CCF/clonality/region columns. Step 4 (only if ccRCC tumours exist): per-patient shared vs private mutations restricted to common panel genes and power-filtered, purity-aware CNA comparison, exact binomial interval. Decision rule: if zero ccRCC samples exist, the proportion is undefined and the label is Not verifiable (no relevant population/variables); I will not transfer ITH from another tumour type. If ccRCC present with >=2 same-tumour samples: True only if all evaluable tumours show power-filtered ITH with adequate n; False only on a well-sampled credible counter-example.

text: PLAN (bd13-team-b, ULMS TP53/RB1/ATRX LoF hypothesis): Estimate the per-patient frequency of loss-of-function alterations in TP53, RB1 and ATRX among uterine leiomyosarcoma samples. Method: audit sample/patient/panel files (duplicates per patient, cancer type detailed, which samples were profiled for mutations/CNA/SV and whether each gene is on each panel version IMPACT341/410/468); count patients with truncating mutations (nonsense, frameshift, splice, start loss), all nonsynonymous mutations, deep deletions (CNA -2) and SVs per gene; frequency = altered patients / profiled patients with exact binomial CI. Checks: one sample per patient vs multiple, non-ULMS histologies excluded, samples missing from mutation file treated as profiled-unaltered only if in panel matrix, sensitivity to LoF definition (truncating only vs + missense TP53 vs + deep deletion + SV). Decision: 'uncommon' fails if frequencies are high (e.g. >20-30% each); hypothesis True only if each gene is altered in a small minority (<~10%). Would change method if gene is not covered on a panel (restrict denominator) or if multiple samples per patient (collapse to patient).

Primary numerator: LoF mutations (truncating classes for all; plus missense for TP53) per patient; secondary: union with deep deletions (-2) and intragenic SVs. label: PLAN
text: PLAN (bd20-team-a analyst): Quantity = per-patient divergence between patient tumour WGS and its xenograft WGS, unit of analysis = patient/line (max 13 pairs). Method: (1) confirm layout: WGS pairs, passage parsed from SAMPLE_ID, somatic status, targeted rows identical within patient (exclude them), read counts blank. (2) Mutations (WGS only): per pair count shared / tumour-only / xenograft-only (chrom,pos,alt), Jaccard, with and without sites recurrent across unrelated patients (germline/mouse/artefact filter); noise baseline from same-line xenograft-xenograft WGS pairs (SA501 X1A vs X5A, SA429 X2A vs X5A). (3) Copy number: re-bin seg file onto common 1 Mb autosomal bins (length-weighted), regress xenograft on tumour log2, report correlation, slope, and fraction of genome in multi-Mb runs deviating from fitted line; compare to xeno-xeno baseline. (4) Stratify by passage (X0/X1 vs later). Decision rule fixed in advance: 'True' if a majority of independent tumour-xenograft pairs show divergence clearly above the xeno-xeno baseline that is not explained by purity (i.e. tumour-only private mutation blocks and/or large CN state changes off the scaling line), including in early-passage pairs; 'False' if pairs are concordant to within baseline in the majority; 'Not verifiable' only if WGS pair data cannot carry signal. Tests across patients: sign/Wilcoxon on per-patient summaries, never pooled mutations. Would change method if: tumour/xenograft calls look like different calling regimes (direction-consistent excess, recurrent sites), or segment oversegmentation distorts bins, then lean on scale-invariant CN evidence.

text: PLAN (bd20-team-b, hypothesis: clonal selection during initial engraftment of breast tumour xenografts). Quantity: per patient, the divergence between the patient tumour (T) sample and its earliest xenograft passage (X): (a) fraction of WGS somatic mutations private to T (lost on engraftment) and private to X (gained/expanded), vs shared; (b) genome-wide log2 CNA divergence T vs X (gene-level correlation, fraction of genome with changed segment state). Method: key each mutation as chrom:pos:ref:alt, compare sets within patient for WGS T-X pairs; paired sign/Wilcoxon tests across patients on private fractions vs 0 and against a noise reference (same-sample WGS-vs-targeted, X-vs-later-X where available); CNA T-vs-X distance compared with between-patient distance and with a purity-rescaling null (X = a*T). Checks: do targeted samples carry any per-sample information (identical site lists? allele counts all NaN?); duplicates; sample-ID match across files; whether T-private calls are explained by tumour purity/sensitivity (X-private can be purity artefacts, T-private cannot easily be); passage number of the X sample (initial engraftment vs later passages). Would change method/label: if no allele counts and identical site lists make clonal prevalence unmeasurable AND WGS set differences are indistinguishable from call noise, label goes to Not verifiable; if T and X are essentially identical beyond noise, False.

label: PLAN
text: PLAN (bd19-team-a analyst, written before any analysis; only headers and 3 rows seen). QUANTITY: (1) head-to-head hazard ratio for PFS (primary) and OS (secondary) between the two GCB-enriched genetic clusters (CLUSTER column in data_clinical_sample, cross-tabulated against ANY_COO/COO_GEP/COO_LYMPH2CX to find which two clusters hold most GCB cases), in R-CHOP-like-treated patients with outcome; run for all cases in those two clusters and restricted to COO=GCB. (2) per-subset frequencies of nonsilent mutations and SVs in a pre-fixed gene list: mutsig q<0.1 genes plus SV targets BCL2/BCL6/MYC, with pre-declared candidate-target genes: epigenetic (EZH2, KMT2D, CREBBP, EP300), BCL2 (mutation/SV), PI3K pathway (PTEN, PIK3CA, SGK1), JAK/STAT (SOCS1, STAT3, STAT6, JAK), BRAF/MEK-ERK (BRAF, MAP2K1, KRAS, NRAS), NF-kB (NFKBIE, NFKBIA, TNFAIP3, CARD11), plus MYD88/CD79B as context. METHOD: log-rank (asymptotic + permutation 10k), Cox HR with 95% CI unadjusted, then adjusted for IPI (one term) stratified by COHORT; KM at 2 and 5 years; PH test; reverse-KM follow-up; numbers at risk. Fisher tests with BH over the fixed gene list, odds ratios with CIs, treated as descriptive because clusters were built from genetics. CHECKS: cluster levels and unassigned level; one sample per patient; missing outcome counts; age/IPI/cohort/treatment balance; PFS events that are deaths without progression; matched/unmatched somatic status balance; double-hit (MYC+BCL2 SV) sensitivity; each COO definition as sensitivity; landmark/truncated analysis if tail-driven. WOULD CHANGE METHOD: PH violation or crossing curves -> landmarks/RMST; imbalance in cohort/IPI -> rely on adjusted/stratified model; unbalanced matched status -> matched-only gene frequencies; fewer than ~20 events -> permutation p and report as inconclusive not contradicting. LABEL RULE: True if the two GCB subsets show a head-to-head outcome difference (HR clearly away from 1, permutation p<0.05 for PFS or consistent PFS+OS) and distinct candidate-target alterations; False if CI is tight around 1 or direction contradicts; Not verifiable only if cluster/COO/outcome variables are absent.

text: PLAN (bd21-team-a): Estimate the fraction of samples with >=1 somatic alteration (union of mutation rows, CNA +2/-2, SV rows) that carry >=1 clinically actionable alteration. text: WARNING SIGN: the pre-specified primary comparison (cluster 3 vs cluster 4, R-CHOP-like treated, PFS) rests on 18 events (13 of 23 in C3, 5 of 21 in C4): HR 2.79 (95% CI 0.99-7.87), asymptotic log-rank p=0.042, permutation p=0.049, Cox Wald p=0.052; adjusted for IPI and stratified by COHORT the HR is 2.35 (0.80-6.87, p=0.12); OS HR 2.18 (0.75-6.31, p=0.15); truncated at 60 months PFS HR 2.51 (0.79-8.03, p=0.11). ACTION: kept the pre-specified test as the basis (no switch of endpoint or subset), report it as moderate support for a difference in the claimed direction, not as a definitive result, and lower confidence accordingly. PH assumption holds (p=0.46), so no change to landmark/RMST method was needed.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: In the bd14 prostate dataset (2069 patients, 1 sample each) no file contains a community-level income variable or any proxy (no zip, census, insurance, education, socioeconomic field), and no genetic-ancestry variable; only self-reported RACE (White 1841/Black 165/Asian 63) and 8Q_ARM (Gain 752/Neutral 1192/Not called 120/Loss 5) exist. MEANS: the exposure in the hypothesis 'income associated with 8q gain adjusting for race and ancestry' cannot be built, so no model can test it. ACTION: abandoned the planned logistic regression and labelled the hypothesis Not verifiable; reported 8q gain vs race (37.4% White, 49.0% Black, 47.5% Asian, chi2 p=0.006) only as context.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: In SA501 (the only patient with WGS for T, X1A and X5A), 4 of the 8 tumour mutations 'lost' in X1A are called again in X5A, and only 7 of 30 X1A-not-in-T calls persist to X5A versus 104 of 116 shared calls. MEANS: single-sample WGS call sets have a false-negative/false-positive noise floor (roughly 3-4% of a tumour's calls can vanish by chance, and most single-sample-private calls are unstable), so small tumour-private fractions (6-9%) are not distinguishable from call noise; there is no technical replicate and no allele counts to model it properly. ACTION: did not treat mutation-set differences alone as proof; required support from CNA changes violating a purity-only monotone null and weighted the two pairs with matched purity (SA493 T-X1, SA533 T-X1: 16% of tumour SNVs lost, 2.5-4.3% of genome in >=5Mb discordant CNA runs) most heavily; lowered confidence.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: xenograft-only WGS mutations outnumber tumour-only ones in 13 of 13 tumour-xenograft pairs (sign p=0.0002; e.g. SA531 1068 vs 35) and the xenograft-on-tumour copy-number slope on 1 Mb bins is >1 in 11 of 13 pairs (up to 3.57 for SA531, 2.70 for SA534); xenograft-only fraction rises with slope (Spearman 0.53). MEANS: this is the purity signature (mouse stroma replaces human stroma), so xenograft-only mutations, TMB increases and raw log2 amplitude differences are not evidence of clonal change. ACTION: dropped xenograft-only counts as evidence; used tumour-only mutations and residuals from the fitted scaling line (scale-invariant) instead.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: copy-number divergence (share of 1 Mb bins in >=5 Mb runs deviating >0.25 log2 from the purity-scaling line) grows with xenograft passage across the 13 pairs (Spearman 0.60, p=0.03; X0/X1 pairs n=7 median 6.2%, range 0.4-13.1%; X2-X5 pairs n=6 median 18.1%), and the within-line xenograft baselines are of the same size (SA501 X1A vs X5A 5.1%, SA429 X2A vs X5A 24.1%; mutation Jaccard 0.56 and 0.61 vs tumour-xenograft median 0.60). MEANS: late-passage pairs confound engraftment with passaging, and tumour-xenograft divergence is not larger than what a few passages produce; no technical-replicate noise floor exists. ACTION: based the engraftment conclusion on the 7 X0/X1 pairs only, treated late pairs as upper bounds, and report that divergence does not exceed the passage baseline.

label: WARNING SIGN

ACTION: computed Jaccard with and without recurrent sites (change <=0.01), kept all rows.

MEANS: any 8q-gain analysis should treat 'Not called' as missing and check sensitivity to counting them as gains; it does not affect whether income is available. label: RESULT
text: RESULT (bd20-team-b): label True. Using only WGS samples (targeted samples are uninformative), first-passage xenografts differ from the patient tumour beyond a purity-only explanation: e.g. SA493 X1 loses ~0.4 log2 across chr15 (23-101Mb) and 16% of tumour SNVs; SA533 X1 gains chr9p (0-38Mb, +0.5 log2) and loses 16% of tumour SNVs; across 13 T-X pairs the tumour-private SNV fraction correlates with purity-unexplained CNA change (Spearman 0.66, p=0.014). text: WARNING SIGN: The observed direction is opposite to the hypothesis: V600E is 3.81% in MIP/SOL vs 0.00% in LEP and 0.97% in ACI/PAP (pooled comparator 0.80%; two-sided Fisher p=0.034, one-sided p for 'MIP/SOL lower' = 0.99; trend permutation two-sided p=0.026 increasing with grade). Would change method if: variants found under different numbering, samples not profiled, or a functional-effect column exists.

label: WARNING SIGN

MEANS: the 'focal amplifications' half of the hypothesis cannot be tested directly; only the KIT-mutation half is testable. label: PLAN
text: PLAN (bd25-team-b): Data are a lung squamous multi-omics cohort (~108 tumours; mutations, mRNA, protein, phospho, clinical with CDKN2A_PATHWAY_ALTERATION_STATUS). No drug-response variable exists, so I test the hypothesis via its molecular implication: among CDKN2A-altered tumours (mutation MAF + low CDKN2A mRNA/protein/methylation + clinical pathway flag), is RB1 protein and RB1 phosphosite abundance (CDK4/6 sites e.g. S807/S811, S780, T826) heterogeneous, i.e. does CDKN2A status alone fail to determine RB1 expression/phosphorylation state? Estimate: (1) difference in RB1 protein and phospho-RB1 (raw and protein-normalised) between CDKN2A-altered vs WT (Mann-Whitney, effect size, adjusted for purity/TMT plex); (2) spread/overlap of RB1/pRB within the altered group, fraction of altered tumours with low RB1 protein or RB1 mutation; (3) concordance of RB1 mRNA/protein. Checks: sample-ID matching across files, duplicates, how the pathway flag relates to CDKN2A mutation calls, missing values, TMT plex batch effect, purity confounding, sensitivity to the definition of CDKN2A alteration. Change method if: the clinical flag does not match CDKN2A mutations (then define alteration myself), phosphosite rows are mislabelled/missing, or batch drives the signal (then adjust). Label True if altered tumours show substantial RB1/pRB heterogeneity incl. RB-deficient cases; False if CDKN2A alteration uniformly determines RB1/pRB state; Not verifiable if RB1 protein/phospho are absent.

text: WARNING SIGN: AR alterations are concentrated in samples taken on ADT (19/91=21% of on-ADT samples vs 8/333=2.4% off-ADT), and only 2/27 AR-altered samples are prostate tissue. MEANS: the AR-CRPC association could partly be confounded by time-zero/ADT exposure (AR alteration as a marker of emerging resistance) rather than a baseline property. ACTION: kept Cox method but added ADT adjustment, ADT-stratified Cox and separate analyses in on-ADT and off-ADT subsets; AR HR stayed >2.4 with p<0.005 in both subsets (off-ADT HR 3.7, on-ADT HR 2.4; stratified aHR 3.2, p=2e-5), so conclusion unchanged.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: Crude CRPC-proportion comparisons (Fisher) are weak for AR (74% vs 55%, p=0.07) and SPOP (47% vs 58%, p=0.14) while time-to-event tests are strong (log-rank AR p=7e-9, SPOP p=0.012, TP53 p=9e-5). MEANS: the result depends on using time-to-event rather than crude proportions; crude proportions ignore unequal follow-up (184 censored of 424) and are the wrong estimator for a 'rate' of castration resistance. ACTION: reported Cox/log-rank as primary (time-to-CRPC), crude proportions only as secondary; direction is concordant in both for all three genes, so label unchanged.

label: RESULT
text: bd22 result (team-b): In the 424-patient mHSPC cohort, time from sample to castration resistance differs by genotype: AR altered (n=27) HR 3.6 (95% CI 2.3-5.7, p=6e-8), SPOP mutated (n=53) HR 0.59 (0.39-0.89, p=0.013), TP53 altered (n=139) HR 1.68 (1.29-2.18, p=1e-4); all persist in a joint Cox model adjusted for disease volume, de novo status, ADT at sample, age and tissue site. Label chosen: True.

label: PLAN
text: PLAN (bd25-team-a analyst): Quantity: within CDKN2A-altered LSCC tumours (strict = protein-altering CDKN2A MAF mutation; broad = mutation or low CDKN2A protein/RNA or high promoter methylation), the distribution of RB1 protein and RB1 phospho (raw and protein-adjusted), and the proportion with RB1-deficient state (RB1 truncating mutation or RB1 protein at the level of RB1-truncating mutants); plus group comparison altered vs WT. Method: complete cases from data_protein_quantification.txt and phospho gene-level row, matched by sample ID; Mann-Whitney/Spearman/Fisher with bootstrap CIs; linear models adjusting for purity, proliferation score, TMT plex. Checks: clinical columns for any drug-response field; crosstab clinical CDKN2A_PATHWAY flag vs MAF CDKN2A/RB1; whether CDKN2A protein/RNA drops in truncating mutants; NA pattern by plex; phospho vs protein correlation; purity confound; E2F/proliferation score vs RB1 protein; CCNE1-high bypass. Change of method if: gene-level CDKN2A row is not a p16 readout (then rest on mutation calls), RB1 NAs cluster by plex (complete-case only), phospho just restates protein (use adjusted). Label rule: True if CDKN2A-altered tumours show substantial heterogeneity in RB1 protein/phospho incl. an RB-deficient subset (so RB1 status carries information beyond CDKN2A status); False if CDKN2A-altered tumours are uniformly RB-intact/hyperphosphorylated making RB1 assessment uninformative; Not verifiable only if RB1 protein/phospho or CDKN2A status are absent.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: KIT enrichment in Triple_WT is driven by small counts (6/46 vs 5/270) and is not significant against the NF1 subtype alone (6/46 vs 3/28, Fisher p=1.0), whose tumours are hypermutated (mean TMB 38.7 vs 9.1 in Triple_WT) and carry KIT V559A x2 and L706F at ordinary allele fractions. MEANS: raw any-KIT-mutation frequency is confounded by mutation burden; passenger hits in high-TMB tumours dilute the contrast. ACTION: kept Fisher on given labels as primary but added a log-TMB-adjusted logistic regression (Triple_WT coefficient 2.63, OR ~13.8, p=0.0002), a hotspot-only test (6/46 vs 3/270, OR 13.4, p=0.0004), a TMB<50 restriction (5/44 vs 5/255, OR 6.4, p=0.008) and a re-derived-subtype analysis on all 344 profiled patients (9/55 vs 6/289, OR 9.2, p=8.6e-5); all agree in direction, so the conclusion on the KIT-mutation half did not change.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: in Triple_WT tumours the KIT hotspot mutations sit at very high variant allele fraction (0.50-0.98, top 0.3-18% of each sample's mutations; 4 of 7 above 0.80) and at 1.1-9.4x the sample's median read depth, whereas KIT mutations in NF1/RAS tumours have VAF 0.06-0.47 and ordinary depth. MEANS: this is indirect evidence that the mutant KIT allele is copy-gained/amplified in Triple_WT, but exome depth and VAF are not a measurement of focal amplification (LOH, purity and capture efficiency also produce it). ACTION: reported it only as indirect, consistent evidence; did not treat it as a test of the focal-amplification half, which stays untested for lack of a copy-number table.

label: RESULT
text: RESULT (bd24-team-b): In the TCGA SKCM tables, non-silent KIT mutations occur in 6/46 (13.0%) Triple_WT patients versus 5/270 (1.9%) BRAF/RAS/NF1-subtype patients (Fisher OR 7.95, p=0.0018); all 6 Triple_WT cases are canonical KIT hotspots (K642E x3, L576P, W557R+N822I, N822K). No copy-number data exist in the provided files, so focal amplification could not be tested directly. Label chosen: True, on the testable half, with the limitation stated.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: None of the five tables holds a pathway-output variable: patient table has TUMOR_SITE only; sample table has cancer type, sample type and TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS; the MAF has 46 columns with no expression, phospho-protein, oncogenic/functional-effect field, and the Hotspot column is 0 for all 212 annotated rows (FAILED for 6), including both ARAF rows. MEANS: only part (a) of the hypothesis (ARAF N217I and G322S are present in iCCA) can be tested; part (b) (they lead to pathway activation) has no observable in this dataset, so neither a supporting nor a contradicting statistic can be computed. ACTION: changed the method from a carrier-vs-noncarrier comparison of pathway activity to a descriptive genotype audit, and the label follows the task definition for missing relevant variables (Not verifiable).

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: The cohort is 8 WXS iCCA primaries with 2 ARAF carriers (ICC12 p.G322S at X:47426719 G>A; ICC18 p.N217I at X:47426130 A>T, both ENST00000377045) and only 1 sample with another MAPK/RTK alteration (ICC24 FGFR2-PPHLN1 fusion in the SV file; no KRAS/NRAS/BRAF mutation anywhere); zero overlap, but the minimum attainable one-sided Fisher p for exclusivity is 0.75. MEANS: a mutual-exclusivity test cannot be informative in either direction. ACTION: no test reported as evidence; the co-alteration pattern (neither ARAF carrier has another pathway driver; ICC12 has two ARID1A mutations) is reported descriptively as consistent-with only.

label: WARNING SIGN

MEANS: no VAF, clonality or hemizygosity argument can be made for the ARAF variants. ACTION: made no driver claim from allele fraction; checked burden instead: ICC12 (G322S) is 3rd of 8 by TMB (0.70) and ICC18 (N217I) is 7th of 8 (0.33), so neither carrier is hypermutated, which does not raise passenger likelihood but also does not establish activation.

label: WARNING SIGN

ACTION: defined hotspots by Protein_position instead; did not use peak columns, VAF or ABSOLUTE ploidy as amplification evidence. No copy-number table or column exists in the 5 files, so the focal-amplification half of the hypothesis is untestable here.

label: WARNING SIGN
text: WARNING SIGN: Triple-WT KIT enrichment is not uniform across comparators: BRAF 0/150, RAS 1/92 hotspot (2/92 any), but NF1 2/28 hotspot (V559A x2; 3/28 any = 10.7%) vs Triple-WT 6/46 = 13.0%; Triple-WT vs NF1 one-sided Fisher p=0.35 (hotspot) / 0.54 (any). Also 2 patients (TCGA-ER-A19T, TCGA-ER-A2NF) have two samples each, but only the -06 sample is classified, so the 316 analysed samples are 316 unique patients. MutSig KIT row: n=13, npat=12, nsil=4 vs my MAF count of 16 nonsilent rows in 15 profiled samples (11 samples among classified) and 4 silent rows - close but MutSig used a slightly different patient set. MEANS: enrichment holds vs pooled others and vs BRAF/RAS, but not demonstrably vs NF1 (small n, wide CI 0.9-23.5% for NF1 hotspot). label: PLAN
text: PLAN (bd17-team-a): Quantity = among trastuzumab-treated patients whose PRE-TX sequenced sample is ERBB2-amplified (HER2_IMPACT=AMP / data_cna ERBB2=2) and who have a POST-TX sample, the proportion whose POST sample is non-amplified, with Clopper-Pearson 95% CI, compared with background discordance (internal PRE-PRE pairs or ~7-12%). Method: build within-patient pairs by PATIENT_ID; exact McNemar on AMP status and Wilcoxon signed-rank on paired ERBB2 log-ratio (HER2_IMPACT_LR and seg.mean over chr17:37.84-37.89Mb); secondary unpaired contrast among trastuzumab-treated patients (one sample/patient): DIPLOID fraction POST-TX vs PRE-TX, Fisher exact. Checks: data_cna 0/NA coding vs HER2_IMPACT and seg; purity of post non-amp samples (shared-mutation VAFs, flat seg profile); clonal relatedness of pairs (shared mutations); site same vs different; the X1 sample with/without; HER2_RESPONSE to separate acquired (CR/PR/SD then progression) from primary resistance; whether IHC/FISH is specimen-specific. Change of method if: pairs lack trastuzumab documentation (then stratify), post non-amp samples are low purity (then indeterminate), or pairs too few (rely on effect size + CI and unpaired contrast). Label: False if loss clearly above background in clonally related pairs; True if at/below background with adequate n; Not verifiable only if no pairs and no unpaired contrast can be built.

label: PLAN
text: PLAN (bd17-team-b, written after file audit only, before any ERBB2 pre/post analysis): Quantity = frequency of loss of ERBB2 amplification (HER2_IMPACT AMP->DIPLOID, ERBB2 in data_cna 2->0, drop in HER2_IMPACT_LR / seg.mean at ERBB2 locus chr17:37.8Mb) in post-trastuzumab (IMPACT_PRE_POST=POST-TX) samples of HER2-positive (HER2_IHC_OR_FISH=POS, trastuzumab-treated per TREATMENT '+BIOLOGIC' / DETAILS_FIRST_LINE) patients, versus pre-treatment samples. Method: (1) paired within-patient pre vs post comparison (the 34 patients with >=2 samples): count AMP->non-AMP transitions vs reverse, exact McNemar/binomial sign test, paired Wilcoxon on ERBB2 log ratio; (2) unpaired, one sample per patient: among HER2 IHC/FISH-positive tumours, fraction ERBB2 non-amplified by sequencing in POST-TX vs PRE-TX, Fisher exact; (3) negative control: same pre/post comparison in HER2-negative / non-trastuzumab patients to check that POST-TX labelling is not generic. Checks: sample-to-patient multiplicity (use patient as the unit), panel/batch (IMPACT300 retrospective YJ samples vs prospective), tumour purity confound (low purity could mimic loss of amp: check FGA and mutation VAFs in post samples), whether POST-TX means post-trastuzumab specifically, agreement between HER2_IMPACT column, data_cna ERBB2 row and seg file. Would change method if: POST-TX is not trastuzumab-specific (then restrict to trastuzumab-treated patients), pairs are too few (then lean on unpaired comparison and report low power), or apparent loss is explained by low purity. Label rule: False if loss of ERBB2 amp is clearly enriched after trastuzumab progression; True if no enrichment with adequate power; Not verifiable only if no pre/post ERBB2 variables exist.

text: PLAN (bd29-team-a analyst): Estimate, separately for STAG2 and ESPL1, n/N = unique samples with >=1 protein-affecting somatic mutation (missense, nonsense, frameshift, in-frame indel, splice site, start/nonstop) divided by samples marked profiled in data_gene_panel_matrix.txt (all-BLCA cohort = TCC, to be confirmed by tabulating ONCOTREE_CODE). Method: Wilson 95% CI; rank/percentile of each gene among all genes by mutated-sample count; comparison with cohort top genes; length-scaled background expectation (cohort non-silent rate per bp x CDS length x N, Poisson test); burden check (are mutated samples the high-TMB ones, recompute without top-burden samples); distinct variants vs samples (artefact recurrence); truncating fraction; alias and coordinate lookup (STAG2 chrX:123.09-123.24Mb, ESPL1 chr12:53.66-53.69Mb GRCh37); chrX coverage check; Variant_Classification tabulation; barcode match between MAF, panel matrix and clinical. Decision rule fixed in advance: True if BOTH genes are recurrently mutated (roughly >=5 samples / >=~5%, top ~1-2% of genes by mutated-sample count, clear excess over length-scaled background, not driven by one repeated variant or hypermutators); False if either gene has zero or only sporadic (1-2 samples, within background) hits while the locus was assayable; Not verifiable only if genes could not have been observed. Mutation-only frequency is a lower bound on alteration (no CNA table). I would change method if assays differ in yield (per-assay frequencies), if symbols are aliased (pool), or if recurrence rests on one identical variant (report with/without).

text: PLAN (bd31-team-a, written before analysis): Estimate, per gene (KRAS, BRAF, PIK3CA, AKT1, RNF43, SMAD4), the odds ratio of oncogenic alteration in right- vs left-sided primaries among MSS metastatic CRC patients. Unit = patient (one record per patient; altered if any of their MSS mCRC samples altered; sensitivity: first sample only). Cohort: MCRC_TYPE != Early Stage Primary, PRIMARY_TUMOR_LOCATION in Right/Left, MSS defined primarily as MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE=='MSI Status' (i.e. neither MSI nor POLE) with MSI_SCORE<10; stricter (MSI_STATUS==MSS label and score<3, TMB<25) and looser (all non-MSI-subtype) sensitivity. Oncogenic definition by OncoKB-style rules: hotspot codons for KRAS/BRAF/PIK3CA/AKT1, truncating + hotspot missense for RNF43/SMAD4, plus deep deletion (-2) for TSGs, amplification (2) for oncogenes, and SVs; report mutation-only and any-nonsynonymous alongside. Test: two-sided Fisher exact per gene, OR with 95% CI, BH q across six genes. Checks: samples per patient, MSI_STATUS vs MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE vs score/TMB, RNF43 G659fs carriers, BRAF V600E vs non-V600, panel version by side and RNF43 on IMPACT341, curated side vs PRIMARY_SITE, excluding transverse and excluding rectum, primary-only and metastasis-only specimens. Would change method if: multi-sample patients are many (then collapse), panel lacks a gene (then restrict denominator), MSS label inconsistent with score (then score-based definition), or direction flips under sensitivity (then report as unsettled). Verdict rule: True if right-sided excess in direction across genes with BH-significant for the genes having adequate power; underpowered rare genes not counted as contradiction.
