text: REPLY to director question on histone-abundance adjustment for all 79 sites (bd10-team-b): The protein table has 18 well-observed histone rows; the only usable H2B row is HIST3H2BB (HIST1H2BA observed in 70/95, HIST1H2BJ in 12/95), and it is anti-correlated with H1/H3/H4/macroH2A protein rows (rho -0.3 to -0.6) and only weakly tracks the H2B acetyl sites (median rho 0.26), so it is a poor H2B-abundance proxy; core histone proteins do not form one abundance factor (mean pairwise rho 0.09). Neither Wnt definition correlates with a core-histone protein score (rho -0.10 and -0.07). Adjusting every one of the 79 sites (observed-only global test, subtype+plex+OCT, within-plex permutation; unadjusted p=0.023 Wnt score, 0.053 CTNNB1 hotspot): global core-histone score p=0.023 / 0.054; class-matched histone protein mean p=0.056 / 0.036; own-gene protein else class mean p=0.054 / 0.041; class mean plus global score p=0.079 / 0.050. H2B sites alone: 0.010 -> 0.037-0.058 (score), 0.039 -> 0.043-0.066 (mutation). Changes method: yes in part - histone abundance is now a covariate for all sites; the association shrinks to borderline (p about 0.04-0.08) but does not vanish, so the earlier claim that the mutation effect disappears (p=0.32) was an artefact of testing only 41 sites, and the earlier claim of robust significance was too strong.

text: REPLY to director question on site classes and collapsing paralog rows (bd10-team-b): Splitting the 79 histone acetyl rows: core H2A/H2B/H3/H4 tails 41 rows (17 clusters at r>0.7, eigenvalue-effective n about 6); linker H1 14 rows; macroH2A 9; H2A variants 15; all 79 rows = 37 clusters, effective n about 11. H2B N-terminal rows are not one peptide: median pairwise r 0.26, only 11% of pairs r>0.7; they form 11 clusters, the K13-K24 multi-acetyl rows of each paralog (HIST1H2BB, HIST1H2BM, HIST2H2BF) cluster within paralog. Global test (subtype+plex+OCT, within-plex permutation), rows / collapsed clusters: core tails Wnt score p=0.006 / 0.015, CTNNB1 hotspot 0.019 / 0.062; H2B 0.010 / 0.044 and 0.039 / 0.14; H3+H4 0.031 / 0.050 and 0.042 / 0.029 (H3K27/K36 cluster lower in Wnt-active); macroH2A 0.018 / 0.012 and 0.074 / 0.049; linker H1 p>0.23; H2A variants p>0.5. So the signal sits in core tails (H2B K13-K24 clusters up, partial r about +0.3; H3 K27/K36 down, r about -0.24) plus macroH2A, i.e. about 3-4 independent measurements, not 21-27 sites. Adding purity, stromal and immune scores weakens collapsed core-tail p to 0.049 (score) and 0.093 (mutation). Changes method: yes in part - inference now uses collapsed clusters per class and the answer text no longer counts sites; label unchanged.

text: REPLY (bd10-team-a) to H2B protein/paralog question: HIST3H2BB protein is a poor stand-in for H2B abundance: r=0.30 with HIST1H2BA (n=70), r=-0.36 with HIST1H2BJ (n=12), r=0.03 with a composite of the 10 fully observed core-histone protein rows (-0.19 excluding itself) and r -0.3 to -0.4 with the H3/H4 rows. The composite does not differ by Wnt status (p=0.32) and H2B acetyl rows barely track it (r -0.2 to +0.1); adjusting for it leaves HIST1H2BM K6-K24 sites at p 0.002-0.02 (with subtype+plex also, p 0.004-0.05). So the signal is carried by about 3 correlated peptide measurements (effectively 1-3 independent), not 9+ sites; composite of the 16 rows: hotspot +0.52 SD p=0.006, within-plex permutation p=0.007, +subtype+plex p=0.02, +purity p=0.12, +subtype+purity p=0.06. text: REPLY (bd10-team-a) to CTNNB1 protein/phosphosite question: total beta-catenin protein passes the positive control (hotspot mutant minus WT +0.86, p=4e-10; Spearman 0.50 with the Wnt mRNA score) but among WT tumours it does not track the score (rho 0.07). Other mutation predictors: 17 recurrent drivers range 0.79-1.34 (hotspot ranks 2nd of 18 raw, behind ARID1A 1.34; subtype-adjusted 1.25, 2nd-3rd behind KMT2D 1.32, KRAS 1.25) and all 15 frequency-matched (15-35 tumours) other mutated genes are lower (max 1.13). PATHWAY_ACTIVITY TNFA (2.68), NFKB (2.26), MAPK (1.72), HYPOXIA, VEGF and proliferation (1.72) exceed Wnt. For the H2B poly-acetyl composite, r with Wnt score +0.33 is matched by 3% of random 10-gene scores. Wnt is in the top ~5% of random expression scores and top of mutation predictors, so moderately specific. Changes method: yes for interpretation (label now rests on plex-blocked test + H2B family composite + this calibration); label unchanged (True), confidence lowered.

(iii) Hotspot is 0 in all 212 annotated rows and FAILED in the 6 failed-annotation rows; zero rows hold any other value, so the column carries no information in this file and I no longer cite it in either direction (my earlier text listed 'Hotspot 0' next to the ARAF rows, which could be read as a negative annotation; removed). text: REPLY to director question on negative-control predictors for the global histone-acetylation test (bd10-team-b): Same 79 sites, subtype+plex+OCT, within-plex permutation; Wnt score statistic 2.51 (p=0.023), CTNNB1 hotspot 2.07 (p=0.053). (a) 10 of 11 PATHWAY_ACTIVITY scores pass at p<0.05, most with larger statistics (TNFA 10.2, NFKB 8.3, MAPK 4.5, EGFR 3.6; only JAK-STAT fails, PI3K p=0.07); purity, stemness, stromal and immune scores also pass (p<=0.005). (b) Of 300 random 14-gene mRNA scores 22% give global p<0.05 (9% p<0.01) and of 200 random co-expressed 14-gene modules 42% do; the Wnt score sits at about the 85th percentile of random sets (empirical p=0.15; 0.29 against co-expressed modules); restricted to the 41 core-tail rows it is at the 93rd percentile (empirical p=0.066). (c) Among 14 other recurrent drivers with 12-45 mutants only KMT2D passes (p=0.005; FBXW7 0.051, MTOR 0.058), so the test is roughly calibrated for mutation predictors and CTNNB1 hotspot ranks 2nd of 15. MEANS: the permutation p-value only rejects 'histone acetylation is independent of this score'; histone acetylation covaries with the general transcriptional and tissue-composition state of the tumour, so the Wnt-score result is not Wnt-specific and is not stronger than a typical pathway score. Changes method: yes for how the p-value is read - the label now rests on the genetic marker (CTNNB1 hotspot, calibrated null, p about 0.05) agreeing in direction with the score, not on the score's global p; label stays True at lower confidence (0.5) because an association exists but is weak and non-specific.

text: REPLY to library finding on within-plex permutation for TMT data (bd10-team-b): checked against the data - histone acetyl-site missingness is plex-wide (18 of 2176 site-by-plex cells partly observed), so plex is the right exchangeability block. Re-running with plex as covariate and labels permuted within plex, on observed samples only, gives Wnt score p=0.023 and CTNNB1 hotspot p=0.053 for 79 sites; within-batch or unrestricted permutation give nearly the same values (0.021-0.022 and 0.057-0.071), so the restriction itself changes little; what lowered the evidence relative to the earlier report (0.002-0.01 and 0.005-0.04) was dropping mean-imputation of whole-plex-missing values. The finding that site rows are not normalised to parent protein was also acted on: all 79 sites adjusted for histone protein abundance give p=0.05-0.08 (score) and 0.04-0.05 (mutation). Adopted as the primary method.

text: REPLY to director Q (X0 vs X1, ID series, label clauses): Checked data_clinical_sample.txt and re-ran pair statistics. Only patient SA536 has any X0 sample (X0 WGS+targeted, X1 targeted); SA493, SA501, SA531, SA533, SA534, SA535 have WGS at X1 (their earliest sample); SA500, SA530, SA532 have X1 only as targeted lists (WGS at X2-X3); SA494, SA495, SA499 start at X2; SA429 and SA496 have no tumour WGS. Tumour-vs-X0 (n=1, SA536): 12/87 = 13.8% of tumour SNVs absent in X0 (exact 95% CI 7.3-22.9%, not above the 9.2% noise bound, p=0.10), 1.4% of genome in >=5Mb purity-unexplained CNA runs, purity ratio ~2 (not matched). Tumour-vs-X1 (n=6): tumour-private 6.5-16.2% (median 8.8%), CNA discordance 0-4.3%. By ID series among the 7 early pairs: SA4xx/50x n=2 (SA493 15.6%/4.3%, SA501 6.5%/0%), SA53x n=5 (7.3-16.2%, 1.3-4.3%); one pair clearing the noise bound in each series (SA493, SA533), so the finding is not confined to one series but rests on one pair per series. Changes method: NO for the comparison itself, but it narrows the claim: strict patient-to-mouse step is observed in one line only and is not distinguishable from noise there; X1 pairs measure engraftment plus at most one transfer. Label clauses: 'primary and metastatic' has no variable (Not verifiable for that clause); 'clonal selection' has no allele counts so only its coarse outcome (variants/CN states lost or newly dominant) is testable; 'initial engraftment' is testable as tumour-vs-X0/X1.

text: REPLY to director Q (tumour-private calls in the two purity-matched pairs vs other five): Ran q2.py/q3.py/q5.py. (1) Location: tumour-private calls are spread over 21-22 chromosomes, not concentrated in discordant CN regions (matched pairs pooled 9/133 private vs 25/701 shared calls inside discordant regions; other five early pairs 2/72 vs 10/796); SA493 has 5/72 private calls on chr15 vs 11/389 shared (Fisher p=0.09). (2) Class: 'RNA' share of tumour-private equals shared (SA493 31% vs 29%, SA533 26% vs 29%), so no enrichment of pseudogene/lncRNA-type calls, though SA493 private calls include PRSS1 x3, PRSS3/PRSS3P2, MUC5B x2 (paralog-prone loci). (3) Targeted list: tumour-private calls are in the patient's targeted locus list at about half the rate of shared calls (SA493 9.7% vs 22.4%, p=0.016; SA533 15.7% vs 31.4%, p=0.009); xenograft-private calls sit in between (19-20%). Other five early pairs: same direction, too few calls to test. MEANS: tumour-private calls carry less weight than I gave them - they look like a genome-wide scatter that is under-represented in the follow-up locus list, which fits either a lost minor clone or low-confidence calls, and the data cannot tell these apart. CN second derivation from data_log2_cna.txt (gene level, isotonic purity null) agrees with the segment-based one across pairs (Spearman 0.91 over 12 pairs; SA495T is missing from that table) and localises the same events: SA493 99% of chr15 genes discordant (segment bins 97.5%), chr15 goes from an intermediate level in T (median log2 -0.17) to the loss level in X1 (-0.60) with equal profile spread (sd 0.46 vs 0.48); SA533 partial chr9/chr15/chr4. Changes method: YES in weighting - CN state change in purity-matched pairs is now the primary evidence, tumour-private SNVs secondary.

text: REPLY to director Q (noise floor): Ran q4.py. SA501 reappearance of 'lost' tumour calls in X5A: 4/8 = 50%, exact 95% CI 15.7-84.3%, i.e. essentially uninformative. Sandwich dropout rates in SA501 (call present in two samples, absent in the third): X1A 4/108 = 3.7% (CI 1.0-9.2%), T 7/111 = 6.3% (2.6-12.6%), X5A 12/116 = 10.3% (5.5-17.4%, inflated by real late-passage change). Reverse direction: only 7/30 X1A-not-in-T calls persist to X5A (CI 9.9-42.3%), so most single-sample-private calls are unstable; SA429 (X2A vs X5A, no tumour WGS) has 13.6% of X2A calls absent at X5A. Early pairs whose tumour-private fraction exceeds the 9.2% upper bound (exact binomial, lower CI above it): 2 of 7 (SA493 15.6%, CI 12.4-19.3; SA533 16.2%, CI 12.8-20.0); SA536 X0 13.8% p=0.10; SA501, SA531, SA534, SA535 do not. Against the wider 12.6% bound the two pairs are borderline (p=0.03, 0.02) and against 17.4% none clears. In the purity-matched pairs the xenograft-private fraction also exceeds noise (SA493 26.9%, CI 23.2-30.9; SA533 18.1%, CI 14.6-22.0). Changes method: YES - SNV set differences are no longer counted as support in the 5 pairs that do not clear the bound; the plan's 'Not verifiable' branch is not triggered only because the 2 purity-matched pairs clear the direct bound and have CN state changes confirmed by two derivations.

text: REPLY (bd26-team-b) to director Q2 on THERAPY_PRIOR_TO_DERIVATION: per patient (20 tumoroid-cohort patients, samples ordered by AGE_AT_DERIVATION): 11 patients have a sample derived after a named chemotherapy regimen (FOLFOX/FOLFIRI/FUDR, usually with CRT or SCRT: 001,003,004,006,007,009,012,022,023,025,037); 5 have only 'none' (002,008,029,031,038); 3 have only missing therapy (013,027,028); 034 has 'none' then 'pembrolizumab' (immunotherapy, not chemotherapy). Only 1 patient (022: none at 56, then FOLFOX, FOLFOX, FOLFOX+CRT at 57) has both a pre-therapy and a post-chemotherapy sample; 2 if pembrolizumab counts (034); 025 goes CRT -> CRT+FOLFOX (no untreated baseline). Arms: these serial derivations weakly inform the per-patient CLINICAL arm only (viable tumour existed after treatment in 11 patients, i.e. at most 'not complete response', ungraded, confounded with radiation, and with no contrasting responders recorded); they say nothing about the per-model IN-MOUSE response arm, which is entirely absent (no engraftment flag, no drug given to a model, no growth/volume readout). Changes method: NO. I correct my wording from 'neither arm is measured' to 'the in-mouse arm is absent and the clinical arm is only indirectly and partially implied'; the label Not verifiable is unchanged because the hypothesis's subject (engrafted tumoroid sensitivity) has no variable.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (bd24-team-b) to the label-rule question: the reading of 'focal amplifications' I scored is KIT-locus amplification, and I also checked the any-gene reading; under both there is no per-sample copy-number variable. Columns that vary between samples and could reflect copy number: data_clinical_patient.txt none; data_clinical_sample.txt only ABSOLUTE_EXTRACT_PLOIDY (genome-wide average, not focal); data_gene_panel_matrix.txt none (single 'mutations' column, no CNA profile); data_mutations.txt only t_ref_count/t_alt_count (read depth and allele fraction); its Tumorscape/TCGAscape Amplification_Peaks columns are gene-level pan-cancer annotations with exactly one value per gene (KIT's names lung/glioma peaks), so they do not vary by sample; data_mutsig.txt is gene-level only. Parts of the claim: KIT mutation enrichment in Triple_WT = supported; focal amplification = no direct variable; nothing contradicted. Against the definitions: 'False' needs contradicting evidence (none); 'Not verifiable' needs the data to hold no relevant variables (not met: subtype and KIT calls exist and were analysed); 'True' needs the analysis to support the hypothesis (met for the testable part). Label stays True; if the claim had to be confirmed as a strict conjunction the amplification conjunct would be unconfirmed, which is the weakest point of the label, not a method error.

text: REPLY (bd26-team-b) to director Q3 on hypothesis components: Group 'engrafted tumoroids' -> data_clinical_sample.txt SAMPLE_ID suffix '-tm' + SPECIMEN_PRESERVATION_TYPE: PARTLY (tumoroids identifiable, engraftment in mice not identifiable; SAMPLE_CLASS all 'Tumor'). Exposure 'chemotherapy' -> THERAPY_PRIOR_TO_DERIVATION: PARTLY and for the wrong unit (what the patient received before derivation, not a drug given to an engrafted model). Outcome 'sensitivity' -> NOT AT ALL (no volume, growth, viability, IC50, response grade in any of the 6 files; mutation/CNA/seg files are genomic only). Comparator 'clinical observations' -> THERAPY_PRIOR_TO_DERIVATION + SAMPLE_TYPE/TISSUE_SITE_OF_DERIVATION (recurrence, post-treatment derivation): PARTLY at most (implies residual/recurrent tumour, no response grade). I read 'unlike clinical observations' as a comparison needing its own variable; under that reading the outcome is missing in both arms, under the background-framing reading the in-mouse outcome is still missing. Applying the task's label definitions: 'False' needs the relevant variables to be identifiable and analysed; the outcome variable is not, so both readings give Not verifiable. Changes method: NO. I withdrew the remark about what a publication-based grader might expect; it plays no role.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (bd24-team-b) to the per-subtype background question: expected non-silent KIT mutations = subtype total non-silent mutations x (MutSig N for KIT 944,367 / sum of N over all genes 9.13e9 = 1.034e-4). Triple_WT (46 patients, 12,436 non-silent): expected 1.29, observed 7 mutations in 6 patients, observed/expected 5.4 (exact Poisson 95% CI 2.2-11.2, P(>=7)=0.0004). NF1 (28 patients, 32,186): expected 3.33, observed 3, ratio 0.90 (0.19-2.63). RAS (92): expected 4.78, observed 2, ratio 0.42 (0.05-1.51). BRAF (150): expected 5.34, observed 0, ratio 0 (0-0.69). Excess differs between Triple_WT and NF1 (ratio of ratios 6.0, conditional binomial p=0.007; patient-level p=0.018). So the equal raw frequencies in NF1 and Triple_WT (3/28 vs 6/46) are what chance predicts for NF1 (median 1,048 non-silent mutations per tumour vs 55 in Triple_WT) but a five-fold excess in Triple_WT; the hypermutation explanation is now calculated, not assumed. Primary contrast (Triple_WT vs all other subtypes) and the word 'enrichment' are kept; method unchanged. Caveat: the background uses a flat per-base rate, not a UV-context-specific one.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (bd24-team-b) to the negative-control question on the amplification proxy: the depth-ratio proxy FAILS the control. Depth relative to the sample median is 2.40 (median) for NRAS/HRAS/KRAS hotspot calls in RAS-subtype tumours (72% above 2x, 22% above 3x), higher than for KIT calls in Triple_WT (median 2.20, 57% above 2x; Mann-Whitney p=0.58), and 1.24 for BRAF V600 calls; so elevated depth at a driver site reflects exon capture efficiency, not amplification. Only one KIT sample is beyond anything seen in the controls (TCGA-D3-A51K-06 L576P, 515 reads, 9.4x median, VAF 0.95; the maximum over 86 NRAS Q61 calls is 7.5x). The allele-fraction part does separate: KIT VAF in Triple_WT median 0.84 (4 of 7 above 0.8, 86% in the sample's top decile) vs 0.44 for BRAF V600 (9% above 0.8), 0.45 for RAS hotspots (10%), 0.29 for KIT in BRAF/RAS/NF1 tumours (p about 0.001-0.003 each), also when controls are restricted to low-burden tumours. But high VAF shows allelic imbalance of the mutant allele (LOH or copy gain), not focal amplification specifically. Weight now given to the proxy in the label: none for depth, none as a test of amplification for VAF. The label True does not change when the proxy is given no weight, because it already rested on the KIT mutation enrichment; the stated basis is corrected to drop the depth claim.

text: REPLY (bd22-team-b) to the censoring-gap question: checked on the data; the 2 rows with SMP_CRPC_MONTHS > OS_SMP_MONTHS are both censored (IS_CRPC=No, alive, TP53-altered; excess 0.3 and 3.3 months) and were kept unchanged in the first analysis; dropping them or truncating to OS time leaves all HRs the same (AR 3.57-3.59, SPOP 0.58-0.59, TP53 1.68-1.72). Among the 184 censored patients 90 have a gap>0 (9 died), 68 >0.5 mo, 22 >6 mo (6 died), 8 >12 mo; gap>6 by genotype: AR 1/7 vs 21/177, SPOP 0/28 vs 22/156 (Fisher p=0.03, i.e. the large gaps are all in SPOP-wild-type), TP53 7/47 vs 15/137. For large gaps (>6 mo, also >12 mo), extend-to-OS (optimistic), event-at-last-assessment (pessimistic), event-at-midpoint, composite CRPC-or-death, and an adverse differential bound (events only in the group the hypothesis says is slower, extension only in the faster group) all keep every interval off 1: AR 2.8-3.5, SPOP 0.51-0.62 (upper bound <=0.94), TP53 1.34-1.64 (lower bound >=1.04). Only the extreme bound applied to EVERY gap>0 patient (including gaps of days) moves SPOP to 0.85 (0.59-1.23) and TP53 to 1.03 (0.81-1.32); tipping point for SPOP is about 4-6 of its 11 gap carriers (largest gap 6.0 mo) all progressing while no wild-type gap patient does. text: REPLY (bd22-team-b) to the SPOP / hazard-vs-proportion question: SPOP HR (95% CI) for mutation-only (n=53) vs any alteration (n=54; the one extra is an amplification): all univariable 0.59 (0.39-0.89) vs 0.61 (0.40-0.91); adjusted+ADT 0.58 (0.38-0.89) vs 0.61 (0.40-0.92); ADT-stratified univariable 0.55 (0.36-0.84) vs 0.57 (0.37-0.86); ADT-stratified adjusted 0.56 (0.37-0.86) vs 0.58 (0.38-0.88); off-ADT univariable (n=333, 38 carriers, 16 events) 0.53 (0.32-0.89) vs 0.56 (0.34-0.92); off-ADT adjusted 0.54 (0.32-0.90) vs 0.57 (0.34-0.94). All 53 SPOP mutations are MATH-domain hotspot missense (F133, F102, W131, Y87, F125...), so a hotspot-only rule is identical. Rule for 'rate': 43% of patients are censored with unequal follow-up (median censored follow-up 49/33/14 months across panels), so a rate must be events per time at risk (hazard, KM); a crude proportion is used only if no time variable exists. A follow-up-fair proportion agrees: CRPC by 24 months among patients with an event or >=24 months follow-up is AR 95% vs 66% (p=0.005), SPOP 51% vs 70% (p=0.025), TP53 82% vs 60% (p=0.0002). The only specifications where SPOP's interval includes 1 are the crude Fisher test ignoring follow-up (47% vs 58%, p=0.14), the on-ADT-only subset (n=91, 15 carriers: 0.60, 0.28-1.27, same point estimate, underpowered) and an extreme worst-case censoring bound; none is a defensible primary specification, so the label stays True. label: REPLY
text: REPLY (bd22-team-b) to the library findings, each checked on the data. (1) Copy-number calling: chromosome X segment means are centred at 0 in these male patients (per-sample weighted X mean median -0.02, IQR -0.06 to 0.04; autosomes 0.01), so a one-copy X baseline was used and AR amplification is not systematically under-called; the 17 called AR amplifications have AR segment means 0.92-5.33, no uncalled sample exceeds 0.8, and adding the 9 uncalled samples with AR segment mean >0.5 gives AR HR 3.30 (2.19-4.98). All 424 samples are profiled for mutations, CNA and SV in the gene panel matrix and AR/SPOP/TP53 have no missing CNA values, so 0 means not called. Purity dependence handled by the purity-floor reruns (results hold). (2) Censoring convention: SMP_CRPC_MONTHS already censors at last CRPC assessment, which is the recommended convention; bracketing sensitivity analyses hold for gaps >3-6 months and fail only under an all-gaps extreme differential bound. (3) Prevalent on-ADT samples: the off-ADT-only estimates (n=333), which the finding names as the unbiased ones, agree with the pooled ones: AR 3.69 (1.50-9.04; only 8 carriers, 5 events), SPOP 0.53 (0.32-0.89), TP53 1.65 (1.21-2.25); gene-by-ADT interaction p = 0.95, 0.61, 0.57. AR violates proportional hazards (p=0.002): HR 4.9 (3.0-8.1) in the first 12 months and 1.1 (0.3-4.4) afterwards, so the AR effect is early progression. No finding changes the method.

text: REPLY to director question 1 (coded '-tm' samples; SAMPLE_CLASS). Check run: checks.py and checks2.py on the 52 RC-MSK samples, comparing AGE_AT_DERIVATION, THERAPY_PRIOR_TO_DERIVATION, TISSUE_SITE_OF_DERIVATION, MAF variant lists with VAF = t_alt/(t_alt+t_ref), and 5-Mb binned seg profiles within each patient. Finding: SAMPLE_CLASS is 'Tumor' for all 21 '-pt' and all 31 '-tm' samples, so it separates nothing and I withdraw it as evidence. '-tm' is separated from '-pt' only by the ID suffix, by SPECIMEN_PRESERVATION_TYPE (Fresh 31/31 tm, FFPE 20/21 pt) and by purity signs (median VAF 0.47 vs 0.24, tm higher in 17 of 18 patients, Wilcoxon p=0.0003; seg amplitude higher in 16 of 18, p=0.0001). Coded samples: 001PR (age 56 vs 55, site 'very distal rectum (recurrence)', own FFPE -pt) and 012RC/012SP (own -pt) are documented separate patient specimens. 022MC/022PC/022TNT are age 57 vs baseline 56 with therapy 'FOLFOX'/'FOLFOX'/'FOLFOX + CRT' vs 'none', same site string, carry all 8 baseline-tm variants plus 1-3 new ones (NCOA3 in all three), seg r 0.67-0.79 to baseline tm. 025TNT-P2m/P7m/P9m all share age 52 and 'CRT + FOLFOX' (baseline 51, 'CRT'), keep 6 of 10 baseline-tm variants, lose 4, gain ERBB4 with VAF 0.06 -> 0.17 -> 0.24 and ALK absent -> 0.26 -> 0.23, seg r P7m-P9m 0.97: an ordered drift of one lineage, which fits either time points or passages; identical age and therapy for all three do not order them. 012VR is near-identical to 012RC-tm (seg r 0.95, same 5 truncal variants, same site 'pelvic recurrence'), so it looks like a re-sampling or sibling of that line. 034MP is age 44 vs 43, 'pembrolizumab' vs 'none', shares 33 of 56/53 variants. Metadata (age +1 year, longer therapy string) reads as later derivation from the patient for 022*, 025TNT* and 034MP, but genomic divergence cannot separate a new biopsy from a later passage, so origin of the 8 coded samples without a '-pt' partner is undetermined: the tables neither identify nor exclude a model-derived sample. Corrected statement: no column identifies engraftment, rather than 'no engrafted sample exists'. Changes method: no, because no sample of any origin carries a drug-response readout.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q1 (X0 vs X1; SA542T). CHECK: parsed passage from every SAMPLE_ID in data_clinical_sample.txt and opened the SA542T column of data_log2_cna.txt. FOUND: only SA536 has an X0 sample (X0 targeted+WGS, plus an X1 targeted-only sample); all other lines start at X1 (SA429, SA493, SA496, SA500, SA501, SA530-SA535) or X2 (SA494, SA495, SA499). Because X0 sits beside a separately labelled T, numbering is zero-based, so X1 = engraftment plus one mouse-to-mouse transfer. Tumour-vs-X0 (SA536, n=1): 12 of 87 tumour mutations tumour-only (1 of 23 targeted-list loci), CN r=0.85, 1 off-line >=10 Mb run with the linear fit (chr16 35-45 Mb, pericentromeric) and 3 marginal runs (1.2% of genome) with a state-wise fit. Tumour-vs-X1 (n=6): linear fit 4, 0, 3, 6, 0, 5 runs (SA493, SA501, SA531, SA533, SA534, SA535); 0-4.9% of genome. So the strict patient-to-mouse step rests on one pair that shows little; the X1 evidence is for engraftment plus first transfer, and is no larger than what 3-4 later passages produce. SA542T has a full column in data_log2_cna.txt (29,333 genes) but no seg rows, no mutations and blank class; it is a flat near-diploid profile (sd 0.057, MAD 0.03, 0.5% of genes beyond 0.3, lag-1 autocorrelation in genomic order 0.25 vs 0.85-0.96 in real tumours, zero runs of >=10 genes beyond 0.1). It is a usable noise picture: the pipeline does not create arm-scale runs in a copy-neutral tumour-class sample, and implied pair noise sqrt(1+slope^2)*0.057 matches the residual MADs seen. CHANGES METHOD: yes for stratification (X0 reported separately, X1 described as engraftment plus one transfer, confidence lowered); label unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q2 (no-change null for the run detector; pre-declared rule). CHECK: for the 7 tumour-vs-X0/X1 pairs, compared observed counts of >=10 Mb runs beyond max(0.3, 3 MAD) with 300 surrogates each of (a) Fourier phase-randomised residual tracks (keeps the full autocorrelation), (b) 5-bin block permutation, (c) circular shift within chromosomes. FOUND: circular shift is uninformative (it moves runs but keeps their count). Linear fit, observed vs Fourier-null mean (p): SA493 4 vs 1.5 (0.04), SA533 6 vs 1.0 (0.003), SA535 5 vs 1.4 (0.003), SA531 3 vs 0.07 (0.003), SA536X0 1 vs 0.01 (0.02), SA501 0, SA534 0. With a state-wise fit (median xenograft value within 40 quantile groups of the tumour value, which removes purity non-linearity) 6 of 7 exceed the null (2-6 runs, 1.2-4.9% of genome, p<=0.01); only SA501 has none. The rule exactly as written compares with the xenograft-xenograft baseline (3.1% and 5.2% of genome): early pairs are 0-4.3%, so 'clearly above baseline in a majority' is NOT met and the literal rule does not give True. I depart from it because that baseline is not a no-change reference: SA501 X1A vs X5A contains chr8 0-43 Mb at -0.9 log2, about 16 times the 0.057 noise sd of the flat SA542T profile, i.e. real clonal change over 3-4 passages. Against the no-change null the same rule gives a majority (4-6 of 7) of early pairs with copy-number state changes not explained by purity. CHANGES METHOD: yes (reference changed from passage baseline to autocorrelation-preserving null; state-wise fit added). Label stays True, with lower confidence because early divergence does not exceed passage-driven change.

text: REPLY to director question 3 (serial derivations per patient). Check run: checks.py, one block per patient of the 20-patient RC-MSK cohort ordered by AGE_AT_DERIVATION with therapy string and site. Finding: THERAPY_PRIOR_TO_DERIVATION is filled for 17 patients and missing for 3 (013, 027, 028). 11 of 20 patients have a sample derived after a named chemotherapy-containing regimen (001, 003, 004, 006, 007, 009, 012, 022, 023, 025, 037); 6 have only 'none' or 'none' then pembrolizumab (002, 008, 029, 031, 034, 038). Only 1 patient (022) has both a therapy-naive and a post-chemotherapy sample (none at 56; FOLFOX and FOLFOX + CRT at 57); 025 has a post-CRT sample and later post-CRT+FOLFOX samples; 034 is none then pembrolizumab, which is not chemotherapy. 4 patients have more than one derivation age (001, 022, 025, 034). Clinical arm: these are observations of the PATIENT and show only that viable tumour could be sampled after therapy; no grade or category is recorded, a complete responder could not yield a sample so all 11 fall in the same implied class by selection, and the regimens mix chemotherapy with radiation. That is an exposure history with an indirect residual-tumour inference, not a per-patient response measurement, and it shows no between-patient difference. In-mouse arm: not an observation at all; nothing in the rows refers to a model treated in mice. Arms recorded as absent: unchanged (both); the in-mouse arm has nothing, the clinical arm has exposure only. Changes method: no.

text: REPLY to director Q3 (variant class and targeted-list membership of tumour-only calls). CHECK: per pair, tabulated shared / tumour-only / xenograft-only WGS calls by Variant_Classification and by membership in the patient's targeted locus list. FOUND: 'RNA' is 27% of WGS rows (2,061 of 7,613), mostly AC/RP11/LINC-type loci, but its share does not differ between tumour-only and shared calls (higher in 6 pairs, lower in 7, Wilcoxon p=0.84), so it is not a marker of bad tumour-only calls. Targeted-list membership is lower among tumour-only than shared calls in 12 of 13 pairs (p=0.002), and equally lower among xenograft-only calls (12 of 13), so private calls in both directions were less often chosen for the list; the list is 73% coding and almost never RNA/intron. Early-pair tumour-lost fraction: all calls 6.5-16%; RNA removed 4-17%; coding only 5-16%; targeted-list loci only 0-9% (counts 1, 7, 4, 6, 11, 0, 2 for SA536, SA493, SA501, SA531, SA533, SA534, SA535). Tumour-only calls survive removal of suspect classes in all 7 early pairs but roughly halve among list loci and stay below the xenograft-xenograft difference (14-24%). CHANGES METHOD: yes in weight only - tumour-only mutation counts are treated as weak support and no longer as independent evidence; the label rests on copy number.

text: REPLY to director Q4 (co-location test on early pairs alone). CHECK: re-ran the test (share of tumour-only vs shared mutations lying in 1 Mb bins where the xenograft is >0.25 log2 below the fitted line) on the 7 X0/X1 pairs. FOUND: linear fit: differences 0.00, +0.03, 0.00, +0.03, +0.04, +0.09, +0.11 (5 up, 0 down, 2 ties; one-sided Wilcoxon p=0.03, the minimum possible with 5 non-zero values), resting on 0-7 mutations per pair. With the state-wise fit: -0.03, -0.01, 0.00, +0.03, +0.03, +0.12, +0.01 (4 up, 2 down, 1 tie; Wilcoxon p=0.15, sign test p=0.34); no pair is individually significant (Fisher p>=0.16), and median residuals of tumour-only vs shared calls show no shift (3 lower, 4 higher). The 11-of-13 result came from late-passage pairs (SA500, SA499, SA530, SA532). CHANGES METHOD: yes - the co-location test is dropped as evidence about initial engraftment; it only supports mutation loss tied to copy-number loss by later passages.

text: REPLY to director question 2 (component table and pre-stated contradicting observation). Check run: checks2.py listed every column of all six files (patient 2, sample 27, MAF 46, CNA Hugo_Symbol + 339 sample columns, seg 6, panel matrix 3) and confirmed every sample ID in the MAF, CNA, seg and panel files is one of the 339 clinical sample IDs, so no hidden treated or vehicle sample exists. Component table: GROUP 'engrafted tumoroids' -> data_clinical_sample.txt SAMPLE_ID suffix '-tm' (31 samples, 20 patients): partly (tumoroid yes, engrafted not at all). EXPOSURE 'chemotherapy' -> data_clinical_sample.txt THERAPY_PRIOR_TO_DERIVATION: partly (patient exposure before derivation for 17 patients; chemotherapy given to mice not at all). OUTCOME 'sensitivity' -> no column; nearest are SAMPLE_TYPE 'Recurrence' and TISSUE_SITE_OF_DERIVATION 'recurrence' strings, which record relapse site, not drug response: not at all. COMPARATOR 'clinical observations' -> THERAPY_PRIOR_TO_DERIVATION with AGE_AT_DERIVATION: exposure only, no response grade: not at all as a response. Pre-stated contradicting observation: a per-model in-mouse response value (tumour size, growth, TGI, survival under drug versus vehicle) differing between two models beyond replicate noise, or two engrafted models in different response categories. Listing: the only numeric columns are AGE_AT_DERIVATION, SAMPLE_COVERAGE, TUMOR_PURITY, MSI_SCORE, AGE_AT_SEQ_REPORT, TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS, MAF coordinates and read counts, discrete CNA calls and seg means; the only categorical columns describe sex, sample origin, panel, preservation, site, MSI and cancer type. None is such an observation. With the outcome identified 'not at all', the task's definition of 'False' (relevant variables identifiable and contradicting) is not met and 'True' has nothing to rest on, so the label stays 'Not verifiable'. Changes method: no.

(1) SOMATIC_STATUS as a curation label: consistent with the data - the value tracks sample class exactly (13 tumour WGS Unmatched, 17 xenograft WGS Matched), the extra SA542T row spells it 'UnMatched', and variant-class composition does not differ between tumour-only, shared and xenograft-only calls, so there is no sign in the data of two calling regimes; method unchanged. text: REPLY to director Q1 (two-part label), bd24-team-a: Reading scored for 'focal amplifications' = either reading (KIT locus 4q12 or any gene); both need per-sample copy-number calls. Columns that vary between samples and could reflect copy number, by file: data_clinical_sample.txt - only ABSOLUTE_EXTRACT_PLOIDY (genome-wide ploidy; median Triple_WT 2.20, BRAF 2.06, RAS 2.07, NF1 2.13; not a focal measure); data_clinical_patient.txt - none (20 columns: age, sex, UV, stage, survival); data_gene_panel_matrix.txt - none (one 'mutations' column, value WGS for all 359); data_mutations.txt - only t_ref_count/t_alt_count (VAF) vary per sample; the Tumorscape/TCGAscape_Amplification_Peaks columns have exactly 1 distinct value per gene for all 18,052 genes in the MAF, so they are static gene annotations; data_mutsig.txt - gene-level, no sample dimension. Parts: (1) KIT mutation enrichment = SUPPORTED; (2) focal amplification = NO VARIABLE. Against the label definitions: 'False' needs contradicting evidence - none; 'Not verifiable' needs the data to hold NO relevant variables or tables - untrue, subtype and KIT calls are present and decisive for part 1; 'True' needs the analysis to support the hypothesis - it does for the testable part only. So no label fits literally; True is the only one whose condition is not flatly false. Changes method: NO, label True kept. But stated plainly: if the grader requires the conjunction to be judged as a whole, the label would become 'Not verifiable'; this is a convention the data cannot settle and is the answer's weakest point.

text: REPLY to director Q4 (enrichment vs NF1, background-expected counts), bd24-team-a: Expected protein-altering KIT mutations per subtype = sum over samples of (sample's protein-altering mutation count in the MAF) x (KIT share of MutSig coverage N = 944,367 / sum of N over 17,980 genes = 1.034e-4). Observed vs expected KIT-mutated samples with exact Poisson 95% interval on the ratio: Triple_WT (n=46) 6 observed vs 1.16 expected, ratio 5.2 (1.9-11.2), P(obs>=6)=4e-4; NF1 (n=28) 3 vs 3.07, ratio 1.0 (0.2-2.9); RAS (n=92) 2 vs 4.60, ratio 0.4 (0.1-1.6); BRAF (n=150) 0 vs 5.14, ratio 0 (0-0.7). So NF1's 10.7% raw KIT frequency is exactly what its mutation burden (median TMB 35) predicts by chance, while Triple_WT's 13% is a 5-fold excess. Conditional-binomial rate-ratio test Triple_WT vs NF1: 5.3-fold, one-sided p=0.016 (mutation rows 6.0-fold p=0.007; hotspot samples p=0.007); vs RAS p=0.0013; vs BRAF p=4e-5. Dropping the one Triple_WT hypermutator (TMB 100) leaves 5 observed vs 0.90 expected, P=0.002. Cohort check: expected total 14.0 vs 11 observed, consistent with MutSig KIT p_cv=0.81 (no cohort-wide excess; the excess is confined to Triple_WT). Caveat: uniform per-base background, no gene-specific covariates. Changes method: NO for the primary contrast (Triple_WT vs all others stays); YES in firmness - the earlier caveat 'not demonstrably enriched vs NF1' is resolved: after burden adjustment Triple_WT is enriched against every other subtype including NF1.

text: REPLY to director question on side/site and strict MSS (bd31-team-b): in MSS mCRC (923 patients) all six genes stay right-enriched and significant when (a) rectum and rectosigmoid are excluded (591 patients: KRAS OR 3.32, BRAF 2.09 p=0.007, PIK3CA 1.66 p=0.018, AKT1 5.2 p=0.036, RNF43 4.9 p=0.001, SMAD4 2.51 p=5e-5), (b) side is re-derived from PRIMARY_SITE with transverse colon as right, dropped, or even as left (all p<=0.001), and (c) in a strict MSS cohort (MSI_SCORE<3 and present, MSI_STATUS not MSI/Inconclusive, TMB<15 fixed in advance; 870 patients, all p<=0.002). Only when all three restrictions are stacked (518 patients) does BRAF weaken to OR 1.66, p=0.10, because left-colon (non-rectal) tumours have 8% BRAF versus 2.9% in rectum; direction never reverses. Requiring MSI_STATUS=='MSS' explicitly (drops 314 samples with no status) gives SMAD4 OR 1.32 p=0.29, but that is a loss of the status-missing third, not an MSI effect. This does not change the cohort definition.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director question on false wild-type calls from low purity (bd31-team-b): a per-sample purity proxy (maximum VAF over all somatic calls from t_alt_count/t_ref_count; Spearman 0.64 with length-weighted mean absolute seg.mean from data_cna_hg19.seg) does not differ between right and left in MSS mCRC (median 0.484 vs 0.486, Mann-Whitney p=0.83; median-VAF p=0.22), is slightly higher in metastasis than primary specimens (0.51 vs 0.46, p=5e-5) and similar in biopsies and resections (p=0.06). Low-purity samples (max VAF<0.10) are 3.5% of right and 4.7% of left samples, and are concentrated in chemo-exposed specimens (6.4% vs 2.2%; chemo-exposed rectal primaries 11%). Excluding samples with max VAF <0.10 or <0.15 (cut-offs fixed in advance, about 20% and 30% purity), or median VAF<0.10 or under 3 calls, leaves all six genes right-enriched and significant with equal or larger odds ratios (e.g. at <0.15: KRAS 3.06, BRAF 3.75, PIK3CA 2.03, AKT1 20, RNF43 9.5, SMAD4 2.0, all p<=5e-4). Treating no-call as wild-type is not biasing the comparison; method unchanged.

text: REPLY to director question on specimen-type heterogeneity (bd31-team-b): in MSS mCRC the right-vs-left odds ratio is above 1 for all six genes in both specimen types. Primary specimens (443 patients) vs metastasis specimens (498): KRAS 2.52 (1.65-3.84) vs 3.21 (2.09-4.94); BRAF 2.91 (1.53-5.54) vs 3.50 (1.80-6.81); PIK3CA 1.98 (1.21-3.24) vs 1.92 (1.10-3.35); AKT1 8.65 (1.77-42) vs infinite (1/117 vs 0/381); RNF43 9.33 (2.56-34) vs 5.09 (1.41-18.4); SMAD4 1.54 (0.89-2.65) vs 3.04 (1.87-4.94). Breslow-Day/Tarone p: 0.43, 0.70, 0.94, 0.55, 0.51 and 0.066 for SMAD4, so no gene shows a significant difference between specimen types. For SMAD4 the hotspot-missense class is right-enriched in both (primary 12.9% vs 6.1%, p=0.02; metastasis 17.9% vs 6.0%, p=3e-4), while truncating and homozygous-deletion events are right-enriched only in metastases; the weak primary result comes from chemo-exposed primaries (right 1/24 vs left 16/92; chemo-naive primaries OR 2.22, p=0.013), a small cell not explained by purity. AKT1 has 9 mutated patients, 8 of them sequenced on primaries, so the metastasis stratum is simply empty (low power, not a different effect). Mantel-Haenszel ORs stratified by specimen type are all significant (KRAS 2.83, BRAF 3.17, PIK3CA 1.95, AKT1 10.0, RNF43 7.1, SMAD4 2.22 p=1.5e-5). text: REPLY (bd31-team-a) to the director's question on low purity and false wild-type calls: purity proxy = maximum VAF per sample from t_alt_count/(t_alt+t_ref) over all somatic calls (949 cohort samples; 1 with no calls, 33 with 1-2 calls); it correlates with copy-number segment amplitude (Spearman 0.64) and with APC/TP53 VAF (0.71). Metastasis specimens are purer than primaries (0.506 vs 0.458, p=4e-5); rectum vs other 0.472 vs 0.488 (p=0.10; 5.7% vs 3.6% below 0.10); chemo-exposed rectal primaries have 10.7% below 0.10 vs 3.4% unexposed. Segment amplitude is lower on the right (0.164 vs 0.196, p=4e-4) although VAF is not, which fits less aneuploidy on the right, not lower purity. Cut-off fixed in advance: purity proxy below 20% (max VAF <0.10) or no calls excluded: 234 right, 646 left; KRAS OR 3.13, BRAF 3.38, PIK3CA 1.99, AKT1 9.93, RNF43 8.36, SMAD4 1.90 (23.1% vs 13.6%, p=0.0012), all BH q<0.002. At 30% (max VAF <0.15) and at median VAF>=0.10 the six ORs are 3.0-3.1, 3.6-3.9, 1.9-2.0, 20, 8.4, 1.9, all q<0.002. No gene changes direction or significance. text: REPLY (bd29-team-a) to director question on applying the rule to every gene: 51 genes have >=6 non-silent mutated samples (32 strictly above ESPL1, 19 tied at 6) and 83 genes have >=5 (73 after dropping genes driven by one repeated variant), out of 5342 mutated genes / ~19000. One-variant-driven genes at or above ESPL1's count: ZNF83 (16 of 18 samples one variant), ZNF233 (13/13), FGFRL1 (8/9), NOTCH2 (4/7), RXRA (4/6), PCDH12 (3/6); with those removed ESPL1 ranks 29th (tied through 45), STAG2 9th. The count/rank clauses of the rule do NOT separate targets from passengers: the >=6 list holds UTX, TP53, PIK3CA, FGFR3, HRAS, ARID1A, STAG2, RB1 but also long passenger-type genes SYNE1, SYNE2, HMCN1, XIRP2, CSMD3, TTN, DNAH8, LRP2, MACF1, AHNAK, DYNC1H1. ESPL1's fall under top-10%-burden exclusion is unusual: it keeps 2 of 6 samples, the lowest of the 19 genes tied at 6 (others keep 3-6, median 4) and at the 3rd percentile of all genes with 5-8 samples (median retained 0.80); after exclusion ESPL1 ranks 241st (tied through 867) while STAG2 stays 10th (10/89). label: REPLY
text: REPLY (bd29-team-a) to director question on non-silent:silent: cohort has 8114 non-silent and 2905 silent mutations (ratio 2.79, silent fraction 0.264). STAG2: 15 non-silent vs 1 silent, exact binomial vs cohort one-sided p=0.050 (two-sided 0.087), 13/15 truncating. ESPL1: 7 non-silent vs 2 silent (ratio 3.5), p=0.56 one-sided, 1.0 two-sided, i.e. indistinguishable from the cohort ratio (but 9 mutations is too few for this test to have power, so it is uninformative, not proof of neutrality). Background scaled to the gene's own silent count: ESPL1 expects 2 x 2.79 = 5.6 non-silent mutations vs 7 observed (Poisson P=0.33), so no excess; the 2 silent hits imply a local rate about 3.2x the uniform rate (exact CI 0.4-11.7x). Burden-aware uniform null gives ESPL1 1.69 expected mutated samples vs 6 (P=0.007), but with a rate factor of 2 P=0.12 and of 3.5 P=0.51, and without the top-10% burden samples 1.17 expected vs 2 observed (P=0.32). STAG2 stays far above background in every version (P<=1e-4 even at rate x3.5 without top-burden samples). CHANGES METHOD: yes for one clause - ESPL1 does not robustly meet 'clear excess over background'; I withdraw that clause as support for ESPL1 and state that its mutations are compatible with passenger load. Label unchanged because the hypothesis is a prevalence claim, not a driver claim.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (bd29-team-a) to director question on burden vs clinical stratum: per-sample non-silent burden does not track stratum (Kruskal-Wallis p=0.25 for Invasive vs Superficial, 0.57 for T-stage group, 0.52 for grade, 0.95 primary vs recurrence; it does rise with age, Spearman 0.39). The 10 top-10%-burden samples (202-326 non-silent) are 7 invasive / 3 superficial, T1 3, T2 3, T3 2, T4 2, grades 1/2/3 = 5/4/1, about the cohort mix. They are not hypermutators by usual thresholds: max 457 coding mutations per sample (none >500), no Tukey outliers on log burden, top-10% cut is 3.3x the median. Frequencies (Wilson 95%): STAG2 invasive 5/62 = 8.1% (3.5-17.5), superficial 8/37 = 21.6% (11.4-37.2), Fisher p=0.07; invasive burden tertiles 1/21, 3/20, 1/21. ESPL1 invasive 5/62 = 8.1% (3.5-17.5), superficial 1/37 = 2.7% (0.5-13.8), Fisher p=0.41; invasive burden tertiles 0/21, 0/20, 5/21 = 23.8% (10.6-45.1); logistic model: log10 burden p=0.0045, subtype p=0.53. So ESPL1 mutation is a property of high-burden tumours regardless of stratum, not of a clinical stratum; 2/6 retained after top-10% exclusion fits a passenger model (expected share 0.685, P=0.08) and rejects burden-independence (P=0.001). STAG2 is burden-independent and skews superficial/low grade. CHANGES METHOD: denominator stays N=99 (burden is not a stratum and the top-burden tumours are ordinary TCC, so excluding them is a mechanism check, not a better prevalence estimate); the reading changes: the ESPL1 6.1% is real whole-cohort prevalence but passenger-compatible.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (bd29-team-a) on the three library findings, checked against the data: (1) No prevalence floor / 2-20% is 'intermediate frequency': STAG2 13.1% and ESPL1 6.1% both sit in that band, and testing only the two named genes is accepted, so ESPL1's nominal P=0.007 under the uniform burden-aware null needs only a 2-test correction (0.014) - but (2) the uniform burden x length null is good only to a factor of about 3-4, and in this file ESPL1's own silent count implies a 3.2x local rate, under which the excess disappears (P=0.5); the library's direction (uniform rate can under-predict background) corrects my earlier note that the uniform null was conservative for the target genes. (3) Cohort non-silent:silent is 2.79, close to the 3:1 neutral value; the per-gene ratio test needs >=11 mutations with 0 silent to reach p<0.05, so ESPL1 (7 vs 2) is untestable and STAG2 (15 vs 1, p=0.05) is borderline by ratio alone though decisive by truncating fraction (13/15 vs cohort about 15%) and burden-independent excess. No cohort sample exceeds 500 coding mutations, so standard hypermutator exclusion removes nobody. Net: STAG2 frequently mutated and driver-like; ESPL1 frequent by prevalence (6/99, 7 distinct variants) but passenger-compatible. Label stays True as a prevalence claim, confidence lowered.

text: REPLY (bd29-team-b) to director Q2 (background calibration): under the uniform rate x length test, long passenger genes are calibrated in aggregate (obs 109 vs exp 103 mutated samples) but individual genes range 0.23x-3.4x and XIRP2 (P=0.001) and CSMD3 (P=0.009) reach P-values as small as ESPL1's (P=0.007). ESPL1 non-silent:silent is 7:2 versus cohort 2.79:1 (binomial P=0.56); its 2 silent mutations versus 0.62 expected imply a local rate about 3x, at which the ESPL1 test gives P=0.37. text: REPLY (bd29-team-b) to director Q3 (does the rule discriminate): 51 genes have >=6 non-silently mutated tumours; 6 are artefact-like (one identical variant in at least half their samples: ZNF83, ZNF233, FGFRL1, NOTCH2, PCDH12, RXRA); the remaining 45 include about 15 known drivers but also long passenger-type genes (SYNE1, SYNE2, HMCN1, XIRP2, CSMD3, TTN, MACF1, AHNAK, LRP2), so rank plus prevalence alone does not discriminate. label: REPLY
text: REPLY (bd39-team-a) to the director's LST question: the clinical-sample column LST is a copy-number-derived genomic-scar count (large-scale state transitions) reported only for a clinically defined subcohort; it is not a clinical measurement and not a fraction LOH. Check 1 (missingness): LST is present for 293 of 471 samples, all with USED_IN_GENOMIC_ANALYSIS=Yes (0 of 41 No), all in first-line oxaliplatin regimens (286 of 322 fluoropyrimidine+oxaliplatin, 7 of 9 FOLFOXIRI, 0 of 140 other regimens), none MSI-Instable or Indeterminate, mostly stage IV/synchronous (268 of 342 stage IV vs 11 of 90 stage III) and without prior adjuvant chemo (283 of 370 vs 10 of 101); missingness is unrelated to panel (chi2 p=0.40). So missingness follows a clinical cohort definition, not assay version. Check 2 (values): in the 290 samples with LST and segments, LST correlates with the count of breakpoints between adjacent autosomal segments >=10 Mb from the de-duplicated seg file at Spearman 0.65 (raw), 0.55 (after dropping segments <3 Mb) and 0.66 (after also merging neighbours within 0.2 log2), p<1e-23 each; it also tracks FGA (0.51) and fraction genome lost (0.50) but not TMB, age, OS or PFS (|rho|<0.05). LST is higher in TP53-mutant samples only weakly (mean 2.63 vs 1.95, medians 2 vs 2, AUC 0.59, p=0.02; p=0.26 at max-VAF>=0.3). Does it change the method: no. My earlier wording 'no LOH-related variable' is corrected to 'one copy-number scar score (LST, a breakpoint count) exists, but no fraction-LOH variable and no minor-copy-number data'; the label stays Not verifiable.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (bd39-team-a) to the director's joint-controls question: with all controls applied together the colorectal fraction-genome-lost proxy (autosomal length with seg.mean<=-0.2 over segmented length; not fraction LOH) is still higher in TP53-mutant samples but the effect is modest and not uniform. MSI Stable + TMB<20 + USED_IN_GENOMIC_ANALYSIS=Yes + max-VAF>=0.3: n=228 TP53-mutant vs 65 wild-type, medians 0.149 vs 0.106 (difference 0.043, about half the pooled 0.081), AUC 0.607, rank-biserial +0.215, Mann-Whitney p=0.008 (pooled uncontrolled: 342 vs 124, 0.108 vs 0.027, AUC 0.665, p=5e-8). Using a purity proxy that excludes TP53's own VAF gives 201 vs 65, 0.152 vs 0.106, AUC 0.618, p=0.004. Rank regression in MSS non-hypermutated used samples (n=418) with purity-proxy rank and panel as covariates: TP53 coefficient +0.066 of the rank range (95% CI 0.011 to 0.121, p=0.019); the purity proxy coefficient is +0.65, ten times larger. Within the jointly controlled set the effect comes from one panel: IMPACT410 94 vs 32, AUC 0.714, p=3e-4; IMPACT341 41 vs 13, AUC 0.55, p=0.60; IMPACT468 93 vs 20, AUC 0.49, p=0.91. Does it change the method: no. It changes the description: the proxy association is 'modest, purity-dominated and panel-heterogeneous', not 'clear'; this makes a True label from the proxy less defensible and leaves the Not verifiable label (which never rested on the proxy) unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (bd39-team-a) to the director's two-grounds question. Exposure, TP53 mutation status: needs data_mutations.txt columns Hugo_Symbol, Variant_Classification, Tumor_Sample_Barcode plus data_gene_panel_matrix.txt to confirm profiling: PRESENT (371 non-silent TP53 rows in 345 of 471 samples; all 471 samples on IMPACT341/410/468, which include TP53). Outcome, fraction LOH: needs either a per-sample fraction-LOH clinical attribute, or allele-specific segments (tcn/lcn or minor copy number) in the seg file, or germline heterozygous-SNP allele counts with purity/ploidy: ABSENT (clinical tables: no column or '#' description matching LOH, purity, ploidy, WGD, FACETS, tcn, lcn, minor, CCF, HRD, fraction; no ASCN_WGD; no MAF column starting 'ASCN.'; seg file has exactly ID, chrom, loc.start, loc.end, num.mark, seg.mean; MAF normal read counts are at somatic sites only, 1 row of 4579 with normal VAF>=0.25, median 7 rows per sample, so no B-allele track). Present but different quantities: seg.mean log ratios (fraction genome lost, FGA) and LST (breakpoint count). Label on the outcome ground alone, if the colorectal cohort were accepted as the population: still Not verifiable, because the task's own example (a mutational-burden claim is Not verifiable when the data have no mutational-burden variable) matches a fraction-LOH claim with no fraction-LOH variable. So the label does not depend on the tumour-type mismatch; the mismatch (0 pituitary samples, all 471 Colorectal Cancer) is an independent second ground. The outcome ground is the softer of the two, since a reader who accepts a loss-fraction proxy would see a modest positive association; the population ground is categorical.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director question on somatic/artefact status (bd27-team-b): For the six NFKBIE 5'-cluster rows (chr6:44233400 C>T in 12M, 35M, Au3, Au7; 44233401 C>T in 12M; 44233439 G>A in Au3) FILTER is '.', dbSNP_RS, Existing_variation, ExAC_AF and GMAF are all blank, and normal alleles equal the reference. Across all 28,331 rows the normal alleles equal the reference in every row, t_depth/n_depth are always 0, the count columns always '.', and Mutation_Status always blank, so those columns carry no information (tool defaults, as the library finding says). Informative evidence: FILTER does flag 828 rows as common_variant and 5,060 rows have an ExAC_AF, so population annotation was applied and the cluster has none (a germline variant in 4/20 would be expected in ExAC since the site is annotated CDS); all samples are SOMATIC_STATUS Matched; the cluster rows are SNPs from the main Broad SNV batch, not the 508-row indel batch with blank Center; carriers split 2 M-series (12M, 35M) and 2 Au-series (Au3, Au7), unlike the GOLGA6L2 indels at chr15:23685155/23685170 (4-5 samples, all Au-series, repeat-gene indels = artefact pattern); the change is C>T at a CC dipyrimidine with a CC>TT tandem in 12M, matching the cohort's UV spectrum (about 90% C>T). The only other positions in >=4 samples are those two GOLGA6L2 indels and VAT1L p.D369N chr16:78005774 (11M, 46M, Au1, Au4; COSMIC-listed coding SNV). MAF row counts equal TOTAL_MUTATIONS in 18 samples; 12M (555 vs 554) and Au7 (38 vs 37) each have one extra row, both NFKBIE carriers, and 12M's NFKBIE pair is its only adjacent-SNP pair, so one NFKBIE row per sample may have been added after totals were computed (cannot be proven). Head-of-block file position of the 44233400 row (35M, Au3, Au7) is shared by the VAT1L hotspot (46M, Au1, Au4), so it reflects recurrent variants being listed first in later samples, not a separate batch. VERDICT: supports real somatic calls for 12M/35M/Au3, leaves Au7 (37-mutation, indel-noisy sample) somewhat open; no read-level check is possible. Does not change the method or the label False.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (bd39-team-b) to the director's question on the exploratory proxy: re-ran the copy-loss fraction (autosomal share of genome with seg.mean < -0.2) in the colorectal cohort. De-duplicating the 507 exact duplicate seg rows (8 fully doubled profiles) changes nothing, because doubling a whole profile doubles numerator and denominator alike. Excluding the 41 USED_IN_GENOMIC_ANALYSIS=No samples (27 MSI-unstable, median TMB 41 vs 6) halves the gap: all samples TP53-mutant median 0.108 (n=342) vs wild-type 0.027 (n=124), p=5e-8; used + MSI-stable 0.107 (n=322) vs 0.065 (n=97), p=0.003. Within tertiles of the purity proxy (highest VAF per sample) the direction stays positive in all three strata at all three thresholds but is small and mostly not significant (thr -0.2: differences 0.017, 0.009, 0.034; p=0.03, 0.24, 0.13); a rank regression adjusting for the purity proxy keeps TP53 positive (p=0.009) while the purity proxy itself is by far the strongest predictor of the loss fraction. So the direction holds but the size was overstated and the proxy is largely a purity readout. Does not change the method or the label (Not verifiable); it changes the wording: the proxy is now described as a weak, purity-confounded positive association in colorectal tumours, not as pointing towards True.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director question on promoter coverage (bd27-team-b): The MAF has 50 5'Flank rows in 17 of 20 samples with DISTANCE 4 to 4,827 bp (median 556; 23 within 500 bp, 14 within 200 bp) and 46 5'UTR rows in 19 samples, so variants just upstream of transcripts were reportable where exome reads spill over. There are 0 rows in any sample in chr6:44233501-44238500 (the 5 kb upstream of the picked NFKBIE transcript's 5' end at 44233500), while calls exist up to 44233439, 61 bp inside it. So the window beyond 44233500 was probably partly callable for the first ~100 bp and empty, and not assayed further out. If the cluster were read as coding (as ENST00000275015 labels it), no NFKBIE promoter variant would be observed and the label would be True with weak support (the promoter variable class exists in the file and returns zero), not Not verifiable; Not verifiable would only be right if the file had no non-coding calls at all. What tips the reading to promoter is positional: the cluster lies 68-107 bp upstream of the shorter NFKBIE model's start codon and upstream of that transcript's 5' end, plus recurrence with three different amino-acid outcomes (G34E, G34R, P21L). This check does not change the method; label stays False.

text: REPLY (bd39-team-b) to the director's question on TP53 grouping and the two grounds: of 371 TP53 mutation rows (345 samples), 365 are SOMATIC and 6 are Mutation_Status UNKNOWN; the 73 UNKNOWN rows come from 8 samples whose every row is UNKNOWN, 6 of which carry a TP53 mutation; those 6 were in the TP53-mutant group. Two samples have a TP53 deep deletion (-2) and one has a TP53 structural variant, none with a TP53 mutation; all 3 were in the wild-type group. Moving or excluding these 9 samples leaves the exploratory proxy unchanged (used + MSI-stable medians 0.106-0.108 vs 0.064-0.069, p 0.001-0.004 in every variant). If the colorectal cohort were accepted as the study population, the label would still be Not verifiable on the outcome ground alone: no file holds fraction LOH, minor copy number, purity or ploidy, and a total-copy-number loss fraction is a different variable. The label therefore does not depend on the tumour-type mismatch; either ground suffices alone, the absent PitNET population being the stronger one (471/471 samples colorectal). Confidence in the outcome-only ground is lower (about 0.6) than with both grounds (about 0.85). No change of method or label.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director question on specificity of the upstream_gene_variant entry (bd27-team-b): Of 26,126 Missense/Silent/Nonsense rows, 5,055 (19.3%) carry '<own gene>,upstream_gene_variant' for another transcript, and 100 of 494 coding rows with cDNA position <=150 do; 7,396 carry upstream_gene_variant for any gene. So the dual annotation is common and is NOT specific evidence of a promoter. Correction to earlier record: exactly 6 of 8 NFKBIE rows (not 7) carry upstream_gene_variant for ENST00000477930 (44233400 x4, 44233401, 44233439); the 37M row at 44228230 is 3'UTR in ENST00000477930 and upstream of ENST00000443607; the Au2 row at 44233109 is missense in both. The other gene named upstream in the six cluster rows is TMEM151B (ENST00000451188, the neighbouring gene). What remains as evidence for 'promoter': (a) coordinates, the cluster is 68-107 bp 5' of the shorter model's start codon (computed in the next reply) and inside any TSS-anchored promoter window (200 or 500 bp); (b) the picked 500-aa model has no 5'UTR (cDNA pos = CDS pos, true of only 7.4% of coding rows), so its 5' end is just a start codon; (c) hotspot recurrence in 4/20 with inconsistent protein consequences. This changes the evidence base (the all_effects entry is dropped as support) and lowers confidence from about 0.85 to 0.75, but not the label False.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (bd39-team-b) to the director's question on LST: LST (integer 0-14, median 2) is present in 293 and missing in 178 samples. It is missing in all 41 USED_IN_GENOMIC_ANALYSIS=No samples and in 137 of 430 used samples; present mostly in synchronous / stage IV cases (271 of 350 synchronous vs 22 of 119 metachronous; 268 of 342 stage IV vs 25 of 129 stage I-III), and in similar proportions on all three panels (IMPACT341 53/79, IMPACT410 142/239, IMPACT468 98/153). After de-duplicating the seg file, a count of breakpoints between adjacent autosomal segments of at least 10 Mb correlates with LST at Spearman rho 0.58-0.59 (n=290), and with a 5 Mb minimum at rho 0.68, but exact agreement is only 12-25 percent, so LST is not reproducible exactly from the supplied segments. LST also correlates with the copy-loss fraction (rho 0.49) and the purity proxy (rho 0.42) and not with TMB (rho 0.04). This says LST is a genomic copy-number scar count (large-scale state transitions), reported for a clinically defined subset, not a clinical lesion type. It is a breakpoint count, not a fraction of LOH, so the statement that the data hold no LOH measure stands. No change of method or label.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (bd39-team-b) to the director's question on LOH at the TP53 locus: a segment covering TP53 (chr17:7.58 Mb, hg19) exists in 460 of 466 samples with seg data. Its log-ratio is below -0.2 in 146 of 338 TP53-mutant (43 percent) vs 23 of 122 wild-type (19 percent) colorectal tumours (Fisher OR 3.3, p=1e-6; medians -0.163 vs -0.020). TP53 VAF (t_alt/(t_ref+t_alt)) has median 0.35, is above 0.5 in 28 percent of mutant samples, and is higher in mutants with 17p loss (median 0.51 vs 0.31). But no purity, ploidy, minor copy number or ASCN column exists in any file, so VAF cannot be turned into an allelic state, VAF is defined only in mutant tumours, and total-copy loss misses copy-neutral LOH (the usual route at TP53). The TP53-locus reading is therefore not properly testable either, and in any case concerns colorectal tumours, not PitNETs. This changes only the reasoning text, not the label.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (bd39-team-b) on the three findings from the lab's library, each checked against the data: (1) ASCN conventions: confirmed absent: no MAF column begins ASCN., no ASCN_WGD, the seg file has exactly ID/chrom/loc.start/loc.end/num.mark/seg.mean, data_cna holds only -2/0/2, and a header scan of both clinical tables for LOH, PURITY, PLOIDY, WGD, FACETS, TCN, LCN, MINOR, CCF, CLONAL, HRD, TAI, FGA finds nothing; Mutation_Status is only SOMATIC (4506) or UNKNOWN (73). label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director question on placing the alternate NFKBIE transcript start (bd27-team-b): The Au2 variant chr6:44233109 is c.392 / p.Gly131 on ENST00000275015 and p.Gly75 on ENST00000477930 (same Gly>Glu, same frame). NFKBIE is on the minus strand and c.101 = 44233400 gives c.1 of the picked model at 44233500 (c.392 -> 44233109 confirms a contiguous first exon). The 56-codon offset (168 nt) puts the shorter model's first codon at chr6:44233332-44233330, which is codon 57 of the long model. Relative to that start the cluster positions are 5' (upstream) by 68 bp (44233400), 69 bp (44233401) and 107 bp (44233439); relative to the picked transcript's 5' end (44233500) they are 100, 99 and 61 bp inside it (3'). Because VEP calls them upstream_gene_variant for ENST00000477930, that transcript's 5' end lies between 44233332 and 44233399, so the hotspot is at most 68 bp upstream of its transcript start. Assumptions: no intron in either model between its start codon and 44233109, and the short model's codon 1 is a real ATG rather than an incomplete 5' end (cds_start_NF); the file has no reference sequence to confirm a Met at long-model codon 57. Result: the weakest point (annotation dependence) is narrowed, the positions are within core-promoter distance of an annotated alternative start, but not removed: under a rule that subtracts any annotated CDS (PCAWG/Weinhold, per the library finding) they would be coding; under a positional TSS window they are promoter. Does not change the method; label stays False.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (bd31-team-a) to the director's question on SMAD4 heterogeneity between primary and metastasis specimens: the heterogeneity is real and is not explained by any covariate tested. Sample level, MSS mCRC: primary specimens right 21/132 (15.9%) vs left 42/313 (13.4%), OR 1.22, p=0.55; metastasis specimens right 38/123 (30.9%) vs left 48/381 (12.6%), OR 3.10, p=8e-6. The left-sided rate is the same in both specimen types; the right-sided rate doubles in metastasis specimens. By class it sits in mutations, not deep deletions: hotspot missense OR 1.79 (primary) vs 3.70 (metastasis), truncating 0.64 vs 2.32, deep deletion 1.08 vs 1.80 (Breslow-Day p=0.016 for mutations, 0.48 for deep deletion); SV only 2 left-sided primaries. Within metastasis specimens the right-sided excess holds in every split: chemo-naive OR 4.58, chemo-exposed 2.80, biopsy 3.73, resection 2.54, MSI label present 2.87, label NA 3.54, both panels about 3. Within primary specimens it is right-sided for chemo-naive (18.5% vs 11.8%), biopsy and label-NA samples but reversed, not significantly, for chemo-exposed (1/24 vs 16/93) and MSI-labelled primaries (11.8% vs 13.9%, OR 0.83). The MSI-label heterogeneity is not the same thing as the specimen heterogeneity: in a model with both interactions, right x metastasis stays (OR 2.81, p=0.010) and right x label-NA does not (OR 1.95, p=0.10). Purity does not explain it (primaries with max VAF>=0.15: 16.8% vs 13.3%, OR 1.32, p=0.36). Paired patients: 18 have both a primary and a metastasis sample; SMAD4 concordant in 16 (3 altered in both, 13 in neither), discordant in 2 (one deep deletion seen only in the metastasis, one only in the primary); KRAS 16/18, BRAF 18/18, PIK3CA 18/18 concordant. The other five genes show no specimen heterogeneity (Breslow-Day p 0.41-0.91) and are right-enriched in both specimen types. What changes: the pooled CMH common odds ratio for SMAD4 (1.98) should not be quoted as a common effect; report the two stratum odds ratios and the marginal patient-level comparison (55/241 = 22.8% vs 89/677 = 13.1%, p=6e-4; standardised to the cohort specimen mix 23.3% vs 12.9%). The unit stays the patient, since the claim is about patients with MSS mCRC by primary side and the cohort is about half primary, half metastasis specimens. SMAD4 still counts as supporting the claim, but as the weakest gene: the support comes from metastasis specimens and is absent, though not reversed, in primary specimens. Changes method: no for the test and label; yes only for how SMAD4 is summarised.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (bd31-team-a) on the three library findings, each checked against the data: (1) Amplification of all four oncogenes and deep deletion of SMAD4/RNF43 as oncogenic: my definition already did this; patients altered only by amplification are few (KRAS 3 right/7 left, BRAF 0/1, PIK3CA 0/1, AKT1 1/0) and dropping them changes no result; SMAD4 deep-deletion-only is 13 right/26 left and mutation-only SMAD4 is still right-enriched (17.4% vs 9.0%, OR 2.13). (2) Purity thresholds of 20% and 30%: applied as max VAF <0.10 and <0.15; the proxy does not differ by side (p=0.85) and all six genes stay right-enriched with BH q<0.002 at both cut-offs. (3) SMAD4 primary-metastasis concordance: 16 of 18 paired patients concordant in this data, consistent with the finding that no large specimen difference is expected within patients; but the library's guess that the specimen difference would sit in deep-deletion calls is not borne out, it sits in point mutations (hotspot missense and truncating) of right-sided tumours sampled at a metastatic site. None changes the method or the label (True).

text: REPLY (Q SV completeness): data_sv.txt is complete for Mayo/Iowa (frozen) and incomplete for RICOVER (FFPE). Restricted to Mayo/Iowa, BCL2 SV is 15/19 in cluster 3 vs 2/10 in cluster 4 (Fisher p=0.005); in RICOVER the file gives 2/8 vs 1/13 (unusable), while the sample-table flag NUM_DRIVER_SV>0 gives 5/8 vs 4/13 there and 16/19 vs 3/10 in Mayo/Iowa. label: REPLY
text: REPLY (Q targetable alterations by cohort): In clusters 3 vs 4 split by cohort (C3 Mayo/Iowa n=19, RICOVER n=8; C4 n=10, n=13; all samples Matched), the C3 features hold in both cohorts: BCL2 SV-or-mutation 16/19 and 6/8 vs 2/10 and 2/13 (p=0.001, 0.018); chromatin modifiers (EZH2/KMT2D/CREBBP/EP300) 14/19 and 6/8 vs 3/10 and 2/13 (p=0.046, 0.018); CREBBP HAT-domain or truncating 11/19 and 4/8 vs 0/10 and 2/13. EZH2 hotspot variants (Y646F/N, A692V; this file uses Y646 numbering) are in 5/19 Mayo/Iowa C3 plus 1 Goettingen C3, 0/8 RICOVER C3, 0/23 C4; PTEN 4/27 vs 0/23. C4: BRAF 5/23 vs 1/27 (2/10 and 3/13 by cohort) but all non-V600 (K601E, D594G x2, G469A x2), so MEK-pathway candidates not BRAF-V600-inhibitor targets; STAT3 5/23 vs 2/27 with one classical SH2 hotspot (D661A) plus E616K/Q; NFKBIE/NFKBIA truncating or missense 6/23 vs 1/27; NF-kB pathway flag 13/23 vs 7/27 (p=0.043; Mayo 8/10 vs 6/19 p=0.02, RICOVER 5/13 vs 1/8 ns); linker histones 14/23 vs 5/27 (p=0.003, same direction in both cohorts) but not a drug target. Pathway flags that do NOT differ: JAK/STAT 6/27 vs 6/23, BRAF/MEK/RAS 4/27 vs 6/23, PI3K (driven by SGK1) 10/27 vs 8/23. Median PURITY_ABSOLUTE is 0.60 in C3 vs 0.36 in C4 (MWU p=0.02); restricting to purity>=0.4 (21 vs 12) keeps BCL2 15/21 vs 2/12 and CREBBP 14/21 vs 2/12, so lower purity in C4 does not create the C3 enrichments. CHANGES METHOD: yes for reporting (targetability is now stated per specific variant, and C4's own targets are called candidate/suggestive only); no for the label rule: the hypothesis is read as the two subsets differing in outcome and in the targetable alterations they carry, which is met by C3's BCL2/EZH2/CREBBP profile being nearly absent in C4; it is not shown that C4 carries its own established drug targets.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (Q COO-confirmed GCB): Among R-CHOP-treated patients with PFS, cluster 3 has 14 GCB (10 PFS events), 2 Unclassified (1), 7 COO-missing (2), 0 ABC; cluster 4 has 9 GCB (2 events), 4 ABC (2), 3 Unclassified (1), 5 missing (0); other clusters have 15 GCB (7 events), 41 ABC (18), 7 Unclassified (3), 13 missing (6). The GCB stratum supplies 12 of the 18 events of the whole-cluster comparison (10 of C3's 13). GCB-only C3 vs C4: PFS HR 3.47 (0.76-15.9), permutation p=0.094 (200k permutations); OS HR 3.26 (0.70-15.2), p=0.12; by cohort PFS HR 2.88 (Mayo/Iowa, GEP, 7 vs 3 patients) and 2.64 (RICOVER, Lymph2Cx, 7 vs 6 patients); cohort-stratified HR 2.76 (0.59-12.8). In non-GCB or COO-missing members the HR is 1.59 (0.32-7.96, 6 events). The 15 treated COO-confirmed GCB cases outside C3/C4 sit in cluster 2 (13 patients, 7 events, 5-year PFS 54%, similar to C3's 50% and unlike C4's 76%), cluster 1 (1) and cluster 5 (1). Under the COO-confirmed-GCB reading the effect is larger, not smaller, but with 12 events it does not reach p<0.05; the pre-stated rule (fewer than about 20 events: report as inconclusive, not contradicting; True also allowed on consistent PFS+OS direction) gives 'supported in direction, not significant'. CHANGES METHOD: no. The genetic clusters are the subsets and the whole-cluster comparison stays the primary test; the GCB-only analysis is a sensitivity analysis that agrees in direction in both cohorts and both assays.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (Q PFS longer than OS): Confirmed. 27 Mayo/Iowa patients have PFS_MONTHS greater than OS_MONTHS (by 9.7 to 40.3 months; values bunch near 11-12, 21-24 and 33-40 months), 0 in RICOVER or Goettingen; 26 are censored on both endpoints and one (LS2245, cluster 3) has a progression at 82.0 months after OS censoring at 72.3. By cluster: C0 2, C1 7, C2 4, C3 8, C4 5, C5 1 (11 of them, 6 C3 and 5 C4, are in the treated primary set). In Mayo/Iowa 26 of 32 doubly-censored patients show it, and no Mayo/Iowa death coincides with the PFS time, so in that cohort disease status was followed to a later date (later data lock, roughly yearly steps) than vital status; PFS times are internally usable and OS censoring is too early. Primary PFS C3 vs C4 (13/23 vs 5/21 events) under each handling, permutation p from 200,000 permutations: as recorded HR 2.79 (0.99-7.87), log-rank p=0.042, permutation p=0.044; OS extended to PFS time: PFS unchanged, OS HR 2.27 (0.78-6.56), p=0.12 (as recorded 2.18, p=0.15); inconsistent patients dropped: PFS HR 2.79 (0.97-8.01), p=0.049; PFS capped at OS time (which censors the one late progression): HR 2.48 (0.87-7.06), log-rank p=0.079, permutation p=0.081. Reverse-KM median follow-up 93/83 months as recorded, 83/74 capped. Deaths without earlier progression among PFS events: 5 (3 in C3, 2 in C4), all in RICOVER, the same under every handling. CHANGES METHOD: no (PFS as recorded stays the primary because a recorded progression-free status at a later date implies the patient was alive; capping throws away a recorded event). CHANGES CONFIDENCE: yes, down: the result crosses 0.05 under the most conservative handling, the direction and HR (2.5-2.8) do not move.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (library findings checked against the data): (1) FFPE under-detection of rearrangements: consistent with the data, since data_sv.txt holds rows for 35/36 driver-SV-positive frozen Mayo/Iowa samples but only 11/32 FFPE RICOVER samples, while NUM_DRIVER_SV>0 is about equally common in both cohorts (36/67 vs 32/64), so the sample-table count draws on calls that are not in the SV file. (2) Variant-specific actionability: EZH2 in cluster 3 is 6 hotspot variants (Y646F x3, Y646N x2, A692V x1) in 6 of 28 samples plus 2 non-hotspot; BRAF in cluster 4 has no V600 variant (K601E, D594G x2, G469A x2); the Hotspot column is all zero so HGVSp_Short must be used. (3) PFS longer than OS: confined to Mayo/Iowa (27 patients), handled by sensitivity analyses as the finding recommends; the primary PFS result holds as recorded and when those patients are dropped, and weakens to p=0.08 when PFS is capped at OS.

label: LEARNED
text: LEARNED: In paired tumour-blood panel sequencing, a variant is conventionally classed as clonal-hematopoiesis-derived when its blood VAF is at least 2x its tumour VAF (one study also requires blood VAF >2% and >8 reads); a variant with tumour VAF far above blood VAF is tumour-derived. USED FOR: classifying TP53 calls that have alternate reads in the matched normal (director question 1). SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7654627/ (read) and https://doi.org/10.1182/blood.v126.23.2447.2447 (search snippet only).

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q1 (normal-read support / blood clone), team-a, germ cell TP53 task: Tabulated all 19 non-synonymous TP53 calls in 15 patients. Four targeted-panel calls have alternate reads in the normal: P-0000650 R248Q (tumour VAF 0.57, normal 3/436=0.7%, other mutations median 0.14), P-0003533 Q144Rfs (tumour 0.78, normal 16/502=3.2%; its only other mutation PIK3CD is tumour 0.84, normal 6.2%), P-0001058 P151T (tumour 0.145 = sample median 0.144, normal 2/564=0.35%; patient has two more TP53 calls with zero normal reads), P-0000461 R248W (tumour 0.82, normal 0.75%). Normal/tumour VAF ratios are 0.009-0.04, far from the >=2x blood/tumour rule for clonal hematopoiesis, and none is low in tumour VAF relative to the rest of its sample, so none fits a blood-derived clone; ages 20-50. The fifth, exome sample DS-test-007 V173M, shows normal 288/445 only because in all 37 exome-cohort rows n_alt_count is a copy of t_alt_count and n_ref_count a copy of t_depth, so normal evidence there is unusable. Worst case, recoding every call with any normal alt read (and the exome call) as wild-type: all patients 12/12 altered resistant vs 92/168 wild-type, Fisher p=0.0014; pre-chemo only 3/3 vs 34/110, p=0.033. Does not change the method or the label.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q2 (segment file), team-a, germ cell TP53 task: data_cna_hg19.seg covers all 180 samples. Tumour-content proxies (autosomal fraction with |seg.mean|>0.2, length-weighted mean |seg.mean|, 12p mean, mutation count) do not differ between resistant and sensitive TP53-wild-type patients (fraction altered median 0.226 vs 0.245, Mann-Whitney p=0.96; pre-chemo only 0.295 vs 0.245, p=0.84; mutation count p=0.14) nor between seminoma and non-seminoma (0.229 vs 0.219, p=0.36; only 12p mean differs, 0.52 vs 0.67, p=0.02). Sensitive wild-type samples are not flatter. Removing flat mutation-free samples (fraction<0.05 and no mutations: 5 sensitive, 10 resistant, all wild-type) gives 16/16 vs 78/149, p=8e-5 (pre-chemo 5/5 vs 29/100, p=0.003); restricting to samples with >=1 called mutation gives 16/16 vs 62/109, p=5e-4 (pre 5/5 vs 20/67, p=0.004). Three TP53-mutant samples are themselves flat (fraction<0.05). The single deep-deletion call (P-0001435, testis, pre-chemo, resistant) is confirmed: a focal 13-probe segment chr17:7,569,543-7,579,890 inside TP53 has seg.mean -1.17 with flanks at -0.07 and +0.04; it is the only sample with TP53-locus seg.mean below -0.4. label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q3 (outcome definition), team-a, germ cell TP53 task: CHEMO_RESISTANT agrees with PROGRESSION_OF_DISEASE in 175 of 179 patients with both recorded: resistant 104 = 89 progression+salvage chemo, 11 progression without salvage, 3 no progression and no salvage, 1 with all clinical fields missing (P-0004880, wild-type); sensitive 76 = 75 no progression, 1 progression without salvage (wild-type). The 3 resistant non-progressors are all post-chemo specimens containing viable non-teratomatous tumour after 4 cycles: P-0003533 and P-0003834 (both TP53-mutant, poor-risk mediastinal primaries, sample histology teratoma+yolk sac, no PC-RPLND, alive disease-free) and P-0002596 (wild-type, PC-RPLND path YST and T). So the flag follows the broad definition (viable tumour at post-chemo surgery counts). Setting the 4 aside: 14/14 altered resistant vs 86/162, Fisher p=3e-4; recoding them sensitive (equivalent to using progression as outcome): 14/16 vs 86/164, OR about 6, p=0.008. Pre-chemo-only result is untouched (5/5 vs 32/108, p=0.003) because all four are post-chemo or untimed. Does not change the method or the choice of outcome.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q4 (risk-group confounding), team-a, germ cell TP53 task: In pre-chemo specimens, TP53 x resistance by IGCCCG risk: Good wild-type 15 resistant/53 sensitive, no altered; Intermediate 4/13 (+LDH 1/2), no altered; Poor wild-type 12/8, altered 5/0. All 66 post-chemo specimens are from resistant patients, so post-chemo strata are uninformative. Exactly ONE timing-by-risk cell (pre-chemo, poor risk, n=25) holds both an altered patient and a sensitive wild-type comparator: 5/5 (100%) vs 12/20 (60%), Fisher two-sided p=0.14, one-sided 0.12. Pre-chemo mediastinal non-seminoma: altered 3/0 vs wild-type 1 resistant/1 sensitive (n=5, p=0.4). All-timing poor risk: 15/15 vs 36/44, p=0.10. So the stratified result is carried by one cell and is not significant there; TP53 alteration cannot be separated from poor-risk/mediastinal disease in these data. This changes the DESCRIPTION, not the method or label: the supported claim is a strong crude association (16/16 vs 88/164, p=1e-4; pre-chemo 5/5 vs 32/108, p=0.003) with same direction in every stratum and no altered sensitive patient anywhere; independence from risk group is not demonstrated (pre-chemo wild-type resistance is 22% good risk vs 60% poor risk).
