text: REPLY to director Q on PDX/CDX and label rule (bd33): in data_clinical_sample.txt all 42 models have SAMPLE_CLASS=PDX, but 8 of them (8 distinct patients) have PROCEDURE_TYPE 'Blood Draw' and TISSUE_SITE 'Blood'/'blood' (case-insensitive), i.e. they are CTC-derived (CDX) models, so my earlier 'no CDX label' was incomplete; the 42 models come from exactly 29 distinct PATIENT_ID values (not 'about 30'; MSK_LX773 has 10 models); model rows are CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED Small Cell Lung Cancer 40 / Combined Small Cell Lung Carcinoma 2 and GRADE High 18, High Grade 16, high 4, unknown 2, Undifferentiated 2. label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q on single-assay claim (bd33): the models are not one uniform dataset. 36 of 42 models have mutation Center 'MSK-IMPACT341/410/468' and total seg num.mark 6285-7737 (same as patient tumours, 6261-7708); 6 models (MSK_LX973, MSK_LX773L, MSK_LX1053, MSK_LX599B, MSK_LX1127, MSK_LX736; LX1053 has 0 mutation rows) have Center 'mskcc.org', blank Sequencer and Mutation_Status, and 18779-25274 markers (about 3x), with 14-30% of their segment boundaries more than 1 Mb from any boundary position used in the other samples, so their copy number was segmented with a denser, partly off-panel marker set. Two of them carry mutation rows in genes with no row in data_cna.txt (MSK_LX1127: PHC1, CELSR2, TTN, RTEL1-TNFRSF6B; MSK_LX599B: RXRG), but 96 of 101 of their mutation rows are still in panel genes, so this is not exome-wide calling. All of it is DNA (mutations, copy number); no model has any expression or protein value, and none has a mutation row within 0.9 Mb of ASCL1, NEUROD1 or POU2F3. So 'single uniform IMPACT dataset' was wrong as a description, but the variables measured in the models are unchanged. Changes method: no.

text: REPLY to director Q on seg file at the three loci (bd33): using hg19 positions ASCL1 chr12:103.35 Mb, NEUROD1 chr2:182.54 Mb, POU2F3 chr11:120.11-120.19 Mb, a segment spans ASCL1 in 42/42 models (length 48-133 Mb, median 101 Mb, 49-1189 markers, nearest boundary 1.6 Mb away), NEUROD1 in 41/42 (68-238 Mb, median 163 Mb, nearest boundary 8.1 Mb; MSK_LX773A has a gap 179.6-183.5 Mb with no segment), and POU2F3 in 42/42 (9-133 Mb, median 133 Mb; the only boundaries within 2 Mb, in MSK_LX325D, MSK_LX1053, MSK_LX1127, MSK_LX736, sit at panel genes KMT2A/CBL about 1 Mb away, not at POU2F3). No short segment or change-point is at any of the three genes; the value is carried across tens of Mb at 0.1-1 Mb per marker. The seg file is a real DNA copy-number variable but not a 'relevant variable' in the task's sense: the subtypes are defined by expression of the regulators, and arm-level interpolated copy number (seg.mean -0.76 to +0.61 here) neither shows nor rules out expression. This agrees with the library finding. Changes method: no, it completes the record.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q1 (CDKN2A_PATHWAY flag; Unmatched samples), bd25-team-a. CHECK: tabulated the flag against the three routes, CDKN2A/CDKN2B/MTAP RNA, CDKN2A and CCND1 protein and CIN; compared RB1 by flag after removing 5 RB1-mutant and 1 CDK4-mutant tumours; reran strict comparison on the 99 Matched samples. FOUND: the flag is independent of CDKN2A point mutation (5/17 mutants flagged = cohort base rate 34/108) but covers all RB1 and CDK4 mutants; the 23 flagged tumours with no pathway point mutation are mostly deep 9p21 loss (15/23 CDKN2A RNA<0.5 with CDKN2B RNA median -1.9) and/or cyclin D1 high (flagged vs unflagged CCND1 protein 0.45 vs -0.92, p=4e-5; CDK4 protein p=0.03); CIN only slightly higher (3.48 vs 3.14, p=0.05). A rule 'RB1/CDK4 mutation or CDKN2A RNA<-1 or CCND1 RNA z>1' reproduces the flag in 80% of tumours, so it looks like a copy-number-aware pathway call (CDKN2A deletion, CCND1/CDK gain, RB1), not a CDKN2A-mutation indicator; it cannot be decoded exactly without a copy-number table. After removing RB1/CDK4 mutants flagged (n=28) vs unflagged (n=74): RB1 protein +1.00 log2 (boot CI -0.17 to +1.91, MW p=0.006), protein-subtracted phospho -0.48 (p=0.03), regression-residual phospho -0.15 (p=0.29), RB-low 1/28 vs 7/74. Strict mutation on Matched only: RB1 protein +1.26 (CI 0.31-1.79, p=0.010) vs +1.16 (p=0.004) on all 108; only 1 of 17 mutants is Unmatched. Direction and size agree with strict (+1.16), mid (+1.14) and broad (+2.51). CHANGES METHOD: no. Lead with the strict MAF definition (the claim says 'mutations'); the flag is reported as a fourth, concordant grouping.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q2 (reference for 'varies widely'), bd25-team-a. Pattern that would have made the answer False: CDKN2A-mutant tumours with RB1 protein and phospho no different from other tumours and unrelated to any RB-pathway read-out, or mutants uniformly RB1-lost, so that measuring RB1 adds nothing to CDKN2A status. CHECK: within-group SD and range of RB1 in the 17 CDKN2A mutants placed against all 8228 fully quantified proteins / 4435 phospho rows and against 1000 random groups of 17 tumours. FOUND: RB1 protein SD in mutants 1.32 (range 5.62) is at the 76th percentile of proteins in absolute terms only because RB1 is a high-variance protein cohort-wide (SD 1.64, 86th percentile); the mutant/cohort SD ratio is 0.80 (17th percentile of proteins), random groups of 17 have median SD 1.65 (13% of random groups are narrower than the mutants), and for the broader definitions the altered group is significantly NARROWER than random (n=57 SD 1.19, n=84 SD 1.24, 0/1000 random groups as narrow). Protein-adjusted phospho: SD 0.71, 48th percentile, random median 0.77. In the high-purity half the 9 mutants have SD 0.58 vs 1.69 for all high-purity tumours. So RB1 spread in mutants is equal to or smaller than every reference. CHANGES METHOD: yes. 'Varies widely within mutants' cannot separate True from False (any group passes) and is dropped as the label rule. The label now rests on between-group and joint-state evidence: mutants have higher RB1 protein (+1.16 log2, p=0.004) and raw phospho (+0.88, p=0.03), 16/17 keep RB1 above the RB1-truncating level, and RB1 loss (11 tumours, only 3 RB1-mutant, p16-high) is visible only at the protein level. Label stays True.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q3 (RB-low counts without expression-based CDKN2A definitions; purity), bd25-team-a. CHECK: recounted RB1-protein-low tumours (<= -2.10, level of RB1-truncating mutants, n=11) by MAF mutation alone and by MAF mutation or methylation-high, in all tumours and in the TSNet high-purity half; regressed RB1 protein on purity in RB1-wild-type tumours. FOUND: all tumours: mutation alone 1/17 RB-low (6%, exact CI 0-29%) vs 10/91 in the rest (Fisher p=1.0); mutation or methylation 2/44 (5%, CI 1-15%) vs 9/64 (p=0.19). High-purity half: 0/9 (CI 0-34%) vs 5/45, and 1/23 (CI 0-22%) vs 4/31. The significant depletion appears only when CDKN2A RNA-low is part of the definition (1/57 vs 10/51 p=0.003; 2/84 vs 9/24 p=1e-5), and RB-low tumours have high CDKN2A RNA (median 4.28 vs 2.50, p=0.002) and protein (2.72 vs -1.53, p=0.001), so that split was partly built in by construction. Purity: in RB1-wild-type tumours RB1 protein rises with purity (slope +0.80 log2 per unit purity, Spearman 0.21, p=0.03), so low purity LOWERS bulk RB1 in an RB-intact tumour (stroma is RB-poorer than the tumour cells here) while it would hide loss in an RB-lost tumour. The one RB-low mutant C3L-02625 (purity 0.34) sits 3.2 log2 (2.6 residual SD) below what its purity predicts, so dilution alone does not explain it, but it lacks RB-loss features (CDKN2A protein -2.81, E2F score 29th percentile, RB1 RNA 39th percentile, no RB1 mutation), so its RB loss is unconfirmed. RB-low tumours are split evenly by purity half (6 vs 5). CHANGES METHOD: yes. An 'RB-deficient subset among CDKN2A-altered tumours' is 0-2 tumours and does not robustly satisfy my earlier rule; that clause and the 9/24-vs-2/84 contrast are removed from the support for the label. Label stays True on other evidence (see Q2 reply).

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q4 (does RB1 phosphorylation carry its own information), bd25-team-a. CHECK: within CDKN2A-altered tumours (strict n=17, mutation-or-RNA-low n=57, broad n=84) Spearman of protein-adjusted RB1 phospho (phospho minus protein, and regression residual) with CDK4, CDK6, CCND1, CDK2 protein, CCNE1 RNA and phospho (no CCNE1 protein row), protein-adjusted RBL1/RBL2 phospho and the E2F/proliferation scores; then placed the RBL2 correlation against the same statistic for every gene's adjusted phospho and repeated after centring by TMT plex. FOUND: no relation to CDK4, CDK6, CDK2, CCND1 protein or to E2F/proliferation RNA scores (all |rho|<=0.26, CIs span 0, in n=57 and n=84). Structured co-variation with the other pocket proteins: adjusted RBL2 phospho rho +0.38 [0.13,0.59] (n=57) and +0.40 [0.19,0.57] (n=84), residual version +0.42 and +0.47, plex-centred +0.41 and +0.51 (p<=0.001); raw RBL1 phospho +0.35 to +0.45; Ki-67 adjusted phospho +0.50 to +0.68; CCNE1 RNA +0.25 (n=84, p=0.03); CCND1 RNA -0.31. In the 17 strict mutants every CI spans zero (underpowered). Caveat from the genome-wide reference: adjusted phospho of many unrelated genes also correlates with RB1's (95th percentile of |rho| 0.48; RBL2 sits at the 90th-94th percentile, Ki-67 at 96th-100th), so a sample-wide phospho component explains part of the structure. Also 'phospho minus protein' over-corrects (correlates -0.34 with RB1 protein); the regression residual does not. So adjusted RB1 phospho is not noise, but it cannot be tied to CDK4/6 activity, and it does not differ by CDKN2A mutation (p=0.11 subtraction, p=0.74 residual). CHANGES METHOD: yes, in how the phosphorylation half is treated: raw phospho is reported as 'amount of phosphorylated RB1' (higher in mutants, +0.88, p=0.03), the regression residual replaces subtraction as the per-molecule measure, and the claim's phosphorylation half is called supported only weakly (structured but not CDK4/6-specific). Label unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY on the two library findings, bd25-team-a, each checked in the data. (1) Purity and RB1: among 103 RB1-wild-type tumours RB1 protein rises with TSNet purity (slope +0.80 log2 per unit purity, Spearman 0.21, p=0.03), so in this dataset admixture lowers bulk RB1 in RB-intact tumours and a low-purity RB1-low call is suspect; the RB-low CDKN2A mutant C3L-02625 is still 3.2 log2 below its purity prediction but has no p16-high or E2F-high signature. (2) Gene-level phospho row: RB1 phospho correlates 0.80 with RB1 protein and the median across 3000 genes is 0.60 (IQR 0.45-0.74), so the gene-level phospho values are NOT protein-normalised; subtracting protein over-corrects for RB1 (adjusted value correlates -0.34 with protein), so use the regression residual. TMT plex explains 18% of the variance of both RB1 protein and adjusted phospho.

text: REPLY to director Q (background rate from other amplified genes), bd17-team-b: CHECK RUN: for every within-patient pre/post pair, every gene called amplified (2) in the pre sample in data_cna was followed to the post sample, with seg.mean at the gene locus. RESULT: ERBB2 lost in 2/26 pre-post sample pairs = 2/24 patients (8%); non-17q12 genes in the same trastuzumab pairs lost the call in 11/44 (25%; 6 of 14 pairs with such a call), 17q12 neighbours (CDK12, RARA) 6/26, control pairs 0/6 calls (2 pairs). Most other-gene losses are near-threshold flips (post seg.mean 0.4-0.9); complete loss of a high-level (pre seg>=2) non-17q amplicon occurred in 1/7 pairs (P-0000553 FGFR2 5.13 -> -0.07, CTNNB1 2.76 -> -0.14, metastasis->primary, no FGFR2 therapy) versus ERBB2 2/20 (Fisher p=1). Paired ERBB2 log-ratio change (median -0.29) does not differ from other amplified genes (MWU p=0.42). My earlier statement that there was no usable background rate was wrong: ERBB2 loss is NOT enriched over the background of amplification-call loss. Applying the plan's rule: 'False' needed >=6 losses of 24 against a 10% background (>=7 at 14%, >=11 at 25%); 'True' needed adequate power, which 24 pairs cannot give (0/24 has a one-sided 95% upper bound of 11.7%); so the enrichment rule yields no label at 2/24 and the submitted 'False' did not follow from that rule. CHANGES METHOD: yes for the evidence standard (label now rests explicitly on verified cases, not enrichment); label kept at False with lower confidence.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q (P-0000444 and YJ-her-010 ordering), bd17-team-b: CHECK RUN: listed private mutations and non-17q segments per sample. P-0000444: shared TP53 p.V157_R158del and CDKN2A p.V96del; pre liver metastasis private: BCL6 p.T48M (167/1818), ERBB2/CDK12 amp, 1p loss, 3q and 4q gains, 13q loss; post GEJ primary private: 9 mutations (BCL10, BRCA2, EPHB1, JAK1, MLL2 splice, NOTCH4, PGR, PIK3CA E545K, TSC1; VAF 0.06-0.20) and a 2q gain (TMEM127 amp). No cross-sample read counts exist for this prospective pair, so absence is by non-call only. Both samples carry private events, so the post primary is a separate branch, not a descendant of the metastasis; this pair cannot be ordered in time and spatial heterogeneity is not excluded. YJ-her-010 (same cardia primary, matched normal, genotyped counts): all 4 baseline mutations retained at higher VAF (TP53 0.28 -> 0.81); post private APC p.T2268S (0/419 pre -> 285/1074) and CIC p.P1082L (0/448 -> 290/766); pre private: only the ERBB2/CDK12 and FGFR2 amplicons, no private mutations; post private: many new gains/losses (1q, 2p incl. ALK/DNMT3A amp, 5q, 12q, 18q). This looks like replacement by a related subclone lacking both amplicons after treatment, with time order clear. Count of losses attributable to selection under treatment: 1 clear (YJ-her-010), 1 ambiguous (P-0000444). CHANGES METHOD: no for the paired design; yes for the count (2 -> 1 clear + 1 ambiguous); with 1-2 of 24 the plan's enrichment rule is not met, label False kept on case-level evidence only.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q (are POST-row IHC/FISH values copied from baseline), bd17-team-b: CHECK RUN: compared PRE and POST rows in 32 pre/post sample pairs. IHC_HER2 is identical in 22 of 26 pairs where both are recorded and differs in 4 (P-0000444 3+ -> 2+, YJ-her-010 3+ -> 0+, P-0001047 2+ -> 3+, P-0003981 2+ -> 3+); HER2_FISH differs in 4 of 7 pairs with both recorded (e.g. 4.0 -> 3.2, 3.3 -> 3.8, 3.5 -> 2.0) and is identical in 3 (P-0002208 has 17.65 on all three rows, which looks copied). So the field is mostly sample-specific, with at least one patient-level copy; identical IHC 3+ is uninformative. Both paired loss cases are HER2_IHC_OR_FISH=NEG on the post row, so restricting to POS post samples does exclude them, as I said. Of 11 post-only trastuzumab-treated patients, 4 are diploid: 3 are IHC 2+ with FISH 1.1-1.9 (NEG; these cannot be the baseline values that qualified them for trastuzumab, so they are probable post-treatment HER2 loss) and 1 is IHC 3+ POS but diploid (P-0004407; either a copied baseline value with loss, or assay discordance). Among IHC/FISH-POS samples of trastuzumab patients, diploid is 1/29 post vs 8/55 pre (Fisher p=0.15). CHANGES METHOD: no. Denominator stays baseline-amplified paired patients; the unpaired null stays a null and is not evidence of absence.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q (acquired vs primary resistance strata and the X1 sample), bd17-team-b: CHECK RUN: tabulated the 24 pairs by HER2_RESPONSE, HER2_TX_STATUS, TTP. All 23 with data are OFF TREATMENT. Best response: CR 3 (1 loss), PR 14 (0 losses), SD 3 (1 loss), POD 3 (0 losses), missing 1 (YJ-her-003, 0 losses). The two losses are P-0000444 (CR, TTP 25.4 months) and YJ-her-010 (SD, TTP 7.6 months), both in the acquired-resistance stratum: 2/20 CR/PR/SD (10%) vs 0/3 POD, Fisher p=1.0, so the strata comparison is uninformative. s_YJ_her_013_X1 looks model-derived (PIK3C3 p.D640Y 231/0 reads, VAF 1.00, absent 0/945 in the patient sample; minimum seg.mean -7.79; KRAS A59E 0.88); it belongs to a POD patient and stays ERBB2-amplified, so dropping it leaves 23 pairs, 2 losses, and does not touch the acquired-resistance stratum. CHANGES METHOD: no; the stratum fits the claim's setting but adds no statistical weight; confidence is not raised.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY on library findings, bd17-team-b: (1) Amplification call rule (fold change >2): consistent with data, ERBB2 AMP calls with HER2_IMPACT_LR below 1 exist (YJ-her-008 0.49, YJ-her-009 0.60, YJ-her-013 0.85), so call and segment mean are different quantities and background call loss must be stratified by baseline level, which I did (pre seg <1: 3/8 lost, 1-2: 4/26, >=2: 3/8 for other genes). (2) Amplification discordance is common: confirmed in this data (25% of other amplification calls lost between paired samples; FGFR2 5.13 -> -0.07 in P-0000553), so the 8% ERBB2 loss is not above background. (3) T-number is accession order, not collection order: confirmed, 4 pairs have a PRE-TX sample with a higher T-number than the POST-TX sample (P-0002208, P-0003536, P-0004680, P-0006112); all 4 retain ERBB2 amplification, and neither loss case is T-number-inverted, so the curated pre/post label was kept. None changes the label.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q1 (does the low-R2/spread rule separate True from False): checked on all 8,228 fully quantified proteins. RB1 is at the 98.2th percentile for variance explained by CDKN2A MAF mutation (R2 0.056 vs proteome median 0.005; rank 146; only 1.5% of 1,000 random groups of 17 match it; not proteome-wide significant, BH q about 0.9), and RB1 phospho is at the 94th percentile of 4,435 phospho rows. Within-mutant SD of RB1 protein (1.32) is ordinary: 15% of random groups of 17 are as tight (random 95% range 1.04-2.12), SD ratio at the 20th percentile of proteins. So RB1 is more tied to CDKN2A status than a typical protein, and the earlier rule (only 4-6% of variance, heterogeneous mutants) could not have given False. A False pattern would be RB1 no more related to CDKN2A than a typical protein, or lower in mutants, with no RB1-deficient cases among altered tumours. Method changed: the label (still True) now rests on direction and specificity of the higher RB1 protein/phospho in mutants plus protein-level RB1-deficient cases, not on low R2 or spread.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q2 (TSNet purity): TSNET_PURITY (108/108, rho 0.88 with ESTIMATE) correlates weakly with RB1 protein (rho 0.18, CI -0.02 to 0.38) and phospho (0.19), not with protein-normalised phospho (0.07); in the 17 CDKN2A mutants protein rho is 0.56 (CI 0.09-0.84). Mutant and other tumours have equal purity (0.53 vs 0.52) and purity-adjusted mutant coefficients are unchanged (RB1 protein 1.08, CI 0.24-1.91, p=0.012; phospho 0.84, p=0.036; normalised -0.23, p=0.35). C3L-02625 has TSNet purity 0.34 (23rd percentile) and stays 2.7 SD below its purity expectation; all 13 tumours with RB1 protein <= -2 stay at least 2.2 SD below. The count of RB1-deficient-range CDKN2A mutants stays 1/17, but that tumour has ordinary RB1 mRNA (39th percentile) and E2F score (47th), so its RB1 loss is uncorroborated. Method not changed apart from adding purity as a covariate.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q3 (does protein-normalised RB1 phospho carry information beyond abundance inside CDKN2A-altered tumours): no clear evidence. In 17 mutants every Spearman CI spans zero (E2F score -0.06, CDK4 -0.26, CDK6 -0.38, CCND1 0.16, CDK2 -0.35, CCNE1 mRNA 0.35, normalised RBL1 0.42 n=11, normalised RBL2 0.08). In 84 broadly altered tumours: E2F 0.03 [-0.18,0.23], CDK4 0.15, CDK6 -0.07, CDK2 -0.04, CCND1 mRNA -0.31, CCNE1 mRNA 0.25, normalised RBL2 0.40 [0.21,0.56]; but normalised RB1 phospho correlates 0.44 with the sample-wide median of phospho-minus-protein, and after removing that offset the RBL2 link is 0.25 (0.07 in mutants). RB1 protein itself tracks E2F (0.43; 94th percentile of proteins). Method changed: expression half of the hypothesis is supported; phosphorylation half only as abundance-driven aggregate phospho-RB1, and this is now stated. Label still True.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q4 (CDKN2A definitions): fraction with RB1 protein <= -2 is (a) MAF mutation 1/17 = 5.9% [exact CI 0.1-28.7], (b) matched-normal only 1/16 = 6.2% [0.2-30.2], (c) mutation or hypermethylation without the mRNA rule 2/44 = 4.5% [0.6-15.5], (d) pathway flag minus RB1/CDK4 mutants 2/28 = 7.1% [0.9-23.5], against 13-17% in remaining tumours. All four agree on direction (altered tumours less often RB1-deficient, RB1 protein higher: p=0.004, 0.01, 0.04, 0.003) and each has a small RB1-deficient subset. The earlier 84-tumour class (3.6% vs 41.7%) was inflated by circularity: RB1-low tumours have high CDKN2A mRNA (8% vs 41% mRNA-low) so the mRNA rule excludes them. CDKN2A_PATHWAY_ALTERATION_STATUS (34) contains all 5 RB1 mutants, the CDK4 mutant and only 5/17 CDKN2A mutants; 23 flagged tumours have no such mutation; it is unrelated to CDKN2A mutation, weakly to low CDKN2A mRNA (p=0.09), inversely to methylation, and goes with higher CCND1 mRNA, so it probably encodes copy-number events absent from the tables. Method changed: lead with MAF mutation; mRNA-based class contrast dropped. Label still True.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY on the two library findings (bd25): (1) Purity direction checked in data: among RB1-wild-type tumours RB1 protein rises only +0.9 log2 units per unit TSNet purity (p=0.11), so dilution cannot create an RB1 protein value <= -2; most RB1-low tumours have high CDKN2A mRNA (median 4.19 vs 2.50), consistent with real RB loss. (2) The gene-level phospho row is not protein-normalised: phospho-vs-protein Spearman is 0.80 for RB1, 0.58 RBL2, 0.33 RBL1; phospho minus protein is a coarse stoichiometry proxy and shares a sample-wide offset (rho 0.42 with the sample median), which should be removed before interpreting it. Neither finding changed the label (True).

text: REPLY (bd33-team-a) to director question on scope/readings: Checked data_clinical_sample.txt. All 42 models have SAMPLE_CLASS='PDX' and CANCER_TYPE='Small Cell Lung Cancer'; no column says 'CDX'. The 8 'CDX-like' models (LX1053, LX325D, LX674C, LX731B, LX736, LX761C, LX833, LX973; 8 patients) are inferred only from PROCEDURE_TYPE='Blood Draw' + TISSUE_SITE blood/Blood, so CDX status is an inference, not confirmed. Null pattern per column is identical for the 8 blood-derived and the 34 other models (same columns empty: METASTATIC_SITE, MSI_*, SAMPLE_COVERAGE, SOMATIC_STATUS, TUMOR_PURITY), and no expression/IHC/subtype variable exists for either group. 2 of 42 models are Combined SCLC (MSK_LX263, MSK_LX871; ONCOTREE CSCLC), 40 are plain SCLC; they are SCLC-family models and inside the hypothesis, but including or excluding them changes nothing. Under all three readings (each model, collection as a whole, PDX and CDX separately) the label rule gives the same result, Not verifiable, because the subtype variable is absent for every model. Does not change the method.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (bd33-team-a) to director question on label boundary: Patterns fixed per label: 'False' needs a per-model column/table of ASCL1/NEUROD1/POU2F3 RNA or protein (expression matrix, IHC/H-score column, or a subtype annotation SCLC-A/N/P) with >=1 model positive; 'True' needs the same variable with no model assigned to A/N/P; 'Not verifiable' is the absence of any such variable. Went through all nine files: clinical_patient (15 demographic/stage/survival/smoking columns), clinical_sample (24 columns), cna, seg, gene_panel_matrix (panel names only), mutations (MAF columns), sv (4 rows: RB1-PTPRG x2, DAXX, FANCA-ZNF276), timeline_specimen (1 row), timeline_treatment (3 rows; SUBTYPE = Systemic/Radiation therapy). None holds a True or False pattern. Model-row values checked: GRADE = High 18/High Grade 16/high 4/Undifferentiated 2/unknown 2 (tumour grade, empty for patient tumours); CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED/ONCOTREE = SCLC 40, CSCLC 2 (histology). The 27 non-probe data_cna.txt rows non-NaN only in models are: 21 legacy/alias or non-coding targets present in 21 older-format models (BIVM-ERCC5, C15orf23, C3orf72, CDKN2BAS, CHURC1-FNTB, EIF2C2, FAM20A, FIP1L1, FLJ42627, INSRR, LOC652276, LOC80054, LRRFIP2, NCRNA00253, OBSL1, SDCCAG8, SH2D2A, SOX2OT, TIMM8B, TOP2A, TSPAN1), 5 MSI microsatellite markers in 14 models (D17S250, D2S123, D5S346, NR-21, NR-24), and PAK5 in 4 models; none is a subtype regulator or neuroendocrine marker. Word search of all files for ASCL1/NEUROD1/POU2F3/express/RNA/IHC hits only a column description ('to express the degree of abnormality', GRADE) and gene names NCRNA00253/RMRP_lncRNA. (3) Level dates finding: applying mid-2019 Level 1-2 knowledge lowers the strict cfDNA fraction from 43.8% to 28.9% (cluster CI 24.2-33.7), confirming that knowledge-base date moves the strict tier by ~15 points; still above 20%. (4) Convention finding (1-2, 1-3A, 1-3B all used; 'clinically actionable' most often 1-3B; cross-tumour = 3B): my pan tier corresponds to 1-3B and gives 334/596 = 56.0% (50.9-60.9); my strict tier to 1-2. None of the findings changes the method or the label False.

text: REPLY to director Q on copy-number segments (bd40-team-b): using data_cna_hg19.seg (gene positions approximated from memory, hg19), 30 of 54 FN private-to-later gene-level CNA calls lie on segments already shifted >=0.3 log2 in the same direction in the first sample (threshold crossing, not a new segment): 13 chr17q genes in P-0048073 (seg.mean 0.80 to 0.98, purity 40 to 40), 9 chr16q plus 2 chr6q genes in P-0013120 (-0.54 to -0.85, purity 30 to 70), 5 in P-0074869; 4 of 6 FP calls are also threshold crossings. Collapsed to one event per contiguous later-sample segment: FN 22 segments vs FP 6 (mean 2.2 vs 0.6, MWU p=0.04); segments new relative to the first sample: FN 13 vs FP 2 (1.3 vs 0.2, p=0.04). Total new events (mutations + SVs + new segments): FN 3.2 vs FP 1.1 (p=0.08); same-panel pairs 1.67 vs 1.14 (p=0.46). Direction FN>FP holds under this definition but the gene-level count of 74 overstated it about twofold; I now use the segment-level count as the CNA measure. Label unchanged.

text: REPLY to director Q on purity and time separation (bd40-team-b): purity change later minus first is mean +11.5 in FN (n=10) and -16.3 in FP (n=8; the four blank-purity samples are all FP, in P-0060318, P-0063459 and P-0069477, and those pairs were kept in group comparisons but dropped from any purity analysis); later-sample coverage FN 522 vs FP 588. Fraction of first-sample alterations re-detected later: FN mean 0.48 vs FP 0.92. (a) Stratified by purity change FN stays higher (purity up: 5.8 vs 2.0; flat or down: 9.0 vs 1.2; within 10 points: 7.0 vs 1.0, p=0.06) and in OLS of log1p(acquired) on group plus purity change the FN coefficient is 0.86 (t=1.9) while the purity coefficient is about 0; within FN the purity correlation is only 0.10. (b) Time-separated pairs (Local Recurrence or differing ages): FN n=4 mean 9.0 vs FP n=4 mean 2.25; but only one FN pair of those (P-0050430, 1 acquired) re-detects >=50% of baseline, against 4 FP pairs (mean 2.25), so that cut cannot test the direction. In all pairs re-detecting >=50% of baseline: FN n=5 2.2 vs FP n=10 1.5 (p=0.75); new-segment definition 1.2 vs 1.1. So the direction survives purity adjustment, but in pairs where the later sample is demonstrably the same clone the groups are about equal, not FN fewer. Method unchanged in label; the claim is narrowed to 'FN not fewer, likely more'.

Clause 1 against the tumour's own baseline: FN acquired 71 vs retained 33 (Wilcoxon p=0.29), FP 15 vs 43 (p=0.02), so FN do not acquire fewer than they retain either. Proportional: acquired/later-sample events FN median 0.55 vs FP 0.35 (p=0.28; no zero denominators); acquired/baseline events FN 1.00 vs FP 0.42 (p=0.041; 1 FN and 2 FP patients with zero baseline events dropped; with +1 in the denominator 0.73 vs 0.33, p=0.14). text: REPLY (bd40-team-a) to director Q2 (could the later sample show new events): re-detection of baseline events in the later sample is LOWER in FN (pooled 23/37=0.62, patient median 0.50) than FP (21/24=0.88, median 1.00; MWU p=0.08), so FN pairs are more divergent in both directions (gain and loss), not just better sampled. Later-sample purity is blank for 3 FP patients (P-0060318-T04, P-0063459-T03 coverage 211, P-0069477-T03) and 30% for 2 more FP; only P-0006113-T02 and P-0060318-T04 have Archer-only fusion rows. Restricting to pairs whose later sample has known purity >=40%: acquired FN median 3.0 (n=9) vs FP 1.0 (n=5), p=0.012; re-detection >=0.5 and purity >=40: FN 2.0 (n=6) vs FP 1.0 (n=5), p=0.037; re-detection =1 and purity >=40: FN [2,2,4] vs FP [0,0,1]. The low-purity/low-coverage FP later samples are not what makes FP look low (the three blank-purity FP patients still show 1, 3 and 3 acquired events). text: REPLY (bd40-team-a) to director Q3 (second clause, one recurrence rule for both groups): genes/events acquired in >=2 patients. FP: none under any definition (mutations only, all alteration types, arm-level CNA events). FN: mutation table only TP53 in 2/10 (P-0051132 C176F, P-0073133 E258*); all types adds MDM2 amplification (P-0013120, P-0018770) and BAP1 deletion (P-0035844, P-0048073); arm-level 12q gain in 3, 3p loss in 2, 8q gain in 2. text: REPLY (bd40-team-a) to director Q4 (private-to-later CNA calls vs segments): of 59 gene-level calls private to the later sample (25 arm-level events: 21 FN, 4 FP), 13 events are new segments (baseline same-direction seg.mean <0.3 and < one third of the later shift) and 12 were already present at baseline below the calling threshold (e.g. P-0048073 17q gain 0.80 -> 0.98, 13 genes; P-0013120 16q loss -0.54 -> -0.85 with purity 30 -> 70, 9 genes; P-0018770 MDM2 0.84 -> 5.02). New-segment CNA events per patient: FN total 11, median 1 vs FP total 2, median 0 (MWU p=0.044); same-panel pairs FN 5 (n=6) vs FP 1 (n=7), p=0.16; cross-panel FN 6 (n=4) vs FP 1 (n=3), p=0.27. Direction holds in every subset. This DOES change the primary definition: acquired = mutations + non-fusion SVs + new-segment CNA events, minus SMARCA2 in P-0050430 (gene not on the baseline 468 panel). Result: FN median 2.5 (total 29) vs FP 1.0 (total 12), MWU p=0.17; excluding P-0051132 2.0 vs 1.0 (p=0.28); same-panel 1.5 vs 1.0 with equal totals 9 vs 9 (p=0.83). text: REPLY to director Q1 (seven calls, bd38-team-b NPC ERBB-PI3K): the seven calls are ERBB2 I767M (NPC41F), ERBB3 K329R (NPC115D), ERBB3 E919K (NPC6F), PIK3CA E545K (NPC14F), PIK3CG R784T (NPC21F), KRAS G12V (NPC3D), NRAS Q61R (NPC10F) = 6 distinct genes in 7 tumours; the 'post-hoc 5 genes' note omitted PIK3CG and was only a circular illustration, never the primary set. File annotations: CLIN_SIG=pathogenic for exactly the three hand-scored hotspots (KRAS G12V, NRAS Q61R, PIK3CA E545K; only 10 of 1550 nonsynonymous rows cohort-wide are pathogenic, Fisher P=7e-6 for 3/7 vs 7/1543); ERBB2 I767M has COSMIC id COSM51317; the Hotspot column is 0 for all rows so is uninformative. None of the seven has any ExAC/1000G frequency; the only rsIDs are the ClinVar somatic hotspot ids (SOMATIC flag 1). By contrast 356 of 1571 rows cohort-wide (23%, 82% C>T, 34% in NPC15F) have ExAC_AF>0 but only 68 are flagged common_variant, so the background contains likely germline leakage; dropping those rows lowers the expected count and strengthens enrichment (18-gene set 7 vs 1.64 expected, P=0.0016). Calls counted are unchanged; method unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q2 (spectrum, bd38-team-b NPC): six-class SNV spectrum cohort (n=1561) C>A 20.9%, C>G 9.9%, C>T 50.6%, T>A 4.4%, T>C 10.3%, T>G 3.8%; hypermutated NPC15F (n=340) C>T 69.7%, C>G 0.3%; cohort without NPC15F C>T 45.3%, C>A 23.8%. 'F' group (42 samples, 1295 rows, median load 19.5, common_variant 3.9%, ExAC>0 23.6%) vs 'D' group (14 samples, 266 rows, median 15, common_variant 6.0%, ExAC>0 19.2%): F has more C>A (27% vs 11% excluding NPC15F), otherwise similar; both groups hold pathway hits (D: KRAS G12V, ERBB3 K329R; F: the other five). Hotspot substitutions: PIK3CA E545K is C>T (dominant class, TCA context not CpG), KRAS G12V is C>A (21%), NRAS Q61R is T>C (10%). A specific base change of even the dominant class has probability about 0.5/(C:G sites) per mutation, below the any-change-in-codon uniform chance used, so the 20x allowance remains generous; no stratification needed. Method unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q3 (RAS definition, bd38-team-b NPC): burden test by gene set (obs vs expected nonsynonymous mutations, Poisson P / Poisson-binomial P for affected samples, 30 Mb exome): 18 genes with RAS 7 vs 2.13, P=0.006/0.002; 15 genes without RAS 5 vs 2.04, P=0.056/0.036; without RAS plus MTOR (MTOR A1778S in NPC30F) 6 vs 2.43, P=0.038/0.019; RAS plus MTOR 8 vs 2.52, P=0.004/0.001; curated-template set (4 ERBB receptors + 29-gene PI3K template) 7 vs 4.20, P=0.13/0.15. Dropping ExAC_AF>0 rows (likely germline leak in background) gives no-RAS P=0.022/0.014, no-RAS+MTOR 0.013/0.006, template 0.11/0.07. Hotspot test with pre-fixed lists: plan-named list (8 codons; 7 without RAS) gives 2/7 hits with RAS (P=7e-6, 0.003 at 20x) and 1/5 without RAS (P=0.003, 0.05 at 20x); a broad 45-codon list gives 4/7 with RAS (P=4e-9) and 2/5 without (P=7e-5; but ERBB3 K329 was known to me before the list was written, without it 1/5, P=0.013). Conclusion: with RAS the pathway is clearly significant; without RAS it is borderline-significant (P 0.01-0.06 depending on background cleaning); on the broad 33-gene template burden alone is not significant. The label is therefore definition-dependent in strength but every focused definition shows excess (2.4-4x) and PIK3CA E545K is a ClinVar-pathogenic hotspot in all; label False kept, with the 18-gene KEGG-style set (RAS is in KEGG ErbB and PI3K-Akt maps) still primary and the no-RAS result reported beside it.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q4 (null calibration, bd38-team-b NPC): ran the identical length-scaled burden test on 12 comparator pathways written down before counting (WNT, NOTCH, TGFB, P53/DDR, HIPPO, JAK-STAT, NFKB, MAPK, HEDGEHOG, cell-cycle/RB, other RTKs, GPCR-cAMP; 21-49 kb each). 3 of 12 reach Poisson P<0.05: P53/DDR 9 vs 1.8 (P=1e-4, TP53 x7), NFKB 6 vs 2.0 (P=0.016), NOTCH 6 vs 2.5 (P=0.044); the other nine have obs/exp 0-2.5 (P 0.05-1.0). The rejecting ones are known NPC driver pathways, so the null is not broadly permissive; pooled comparators excluding P53 and NFKB are 26 observed vs 21.1 expected (1.23x). ERBB-PI3K (18 genes) ranks 2nd of 13 by excess (3.3x, behind P53/DDR 4.9x) and 2nd by share of cases (12.5% vs 16.1%); Bonferroni x13 gives 0.08 for Poisson P and 0.03 for the Poisson-binomial P. Overdispersed null: zero-truncated negative binomial fitted to per-gene counts of 1390 mutated genes gives gamma shape 2.5 (CV 0.63); pathway P becomes 0.008 with RAS, 0.062 without RAS, 0.044 without RAS plus MTOR, 0.14 for the 33-gene template. A matched random-gene-set null could not be built because CDS lengths exist only for mutated genes. Method kept (uniform null adequately calibrated; NB null added as a check); label False kept but confidence lowered because significance without RAS is marginal.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY on library findings (bd38-team-b NPC): (1) common_variant rule checked against data: flag covers only 68 rows while 356 rows have ExAC_AF>0 and 389 carry rsIDs, so the flag does miss low-frequency population variants; none of the 7 ERBB-PI3K calls (nor MTOR A1778S) has any population frequency, but TSC1 R22W (ExAC EAS 1.2e-4) in the template set does and is dropped in the ExAC-filtered rerun. (2) Pathway membership: results reported for both readings; KEGG-style with RAS P=0.006, template-style ERBB+PI3K core without RAS P=0.06 (15 genes) to 0.13 (33 genes), so the label's strength is definition-dependent. (3) Uniform-null calibration: negative-binomial null (shape 2.5) changes P only slightly (0.006 to 0.008 with RAS; 0.056 to 0.062 without).

text: REPLY to director Q (purity / mutation check), bd32-team-b: (a) JuP3-JP has 3 mutation rows (PIK3CA E542K, SMG1 R420Q, CES1 S12A); all 3 are shared with both JuP3-DCIS and JuP3-IDC, 0 are private to JP; DCIS and IDC share 26 mutations, so JP carries 3 of the 26 truncal carcinoma mutations (DCIS-private 16, IDC-private 9). JuP1 has 6 and JuP2 has 18 mutations, all trivially private because each patient has one sample. The mutation file has no allele-count or VAF columns (t_alt_count etc. are all empty), so lesional fraction cannot be estimated as 2xVAF. (b) On the arms altered in DCIS/IDC, JP's recentred marker-weighted arm means are 1q +0.003, 6p -0.022, 6q -0.022, 8p -0.005, 8q +0.018, 16q +0.049 (DCIS: +0.35, +0.47, -0.52, -0.05, +1.37, -0.51); signs follow the carcinoma direction no more than in the unrelated JuP1/JuP2 (mean signed value +0.02 vs 0.00), and on a linear scale the carcinoma clone is at most about 1% of the JP sample (1q, 8q). (c) Largest whole-arm deviation: JuP3-JP 19p +0.19 (the same arm is +0.14 in DCIS and +0.18 in IDC), JuP1 22q +0.09, JuP2 19q +0.04; no JP sample has an arm at 0.2 or more. CONCLUSION: the data cannot fully separate 'JP has few alterations' from 'JP alterations invisible at low lesional fraction' for JuP3-JP, because no VAF exists; what is established is that JP does not contain the carcinoma CNA clone and that JuP2, which has 18 mutations including PIK3CA H1047R, is also flat at arm scale. Method unchanged; label False kept (no reading of the data supports a HIGH number in JP), confidence lowered slightly.

text: REPLY to director Q (merged events, recentring, cutoffs), bd32-team-b: After recentring each sample on its marker-weighted median (baselines JP +0.005, DCIS -0.055, IDC -0.024) and merging adjacent same-direction segments per chromosome, event counts JP/DCIS/IDC are: cutoff 0.1 total 18/14/18 (arm-scale 2/8/8, smaller 16/6/10); cutoff 0.2 total 1/7/9 (arm-scale 0/6/6, smaller 1/1/3); cutoff 0.3 total 0/7/3 (arm-scale 0/6/3, smaller 0/1/0). The ordering on total events is NOT the same at every cutoff: at 0.1 JP ties IDC and exceeds DCIS because of small events; at 0.2 and 0.3 JP is far lowest. I cannot claim 0.2 was chosen blind, so the label now rests on cutoff-independent results: (1) arm-scale events are fewer in JP at every cutoff, and JP's only two (19p, 19q at 0.1) are present at the same level in DCIS and IDC; (2) lesion-specific events (event in one lesion whose level over the same coordinates in the other lesion is below half the cutoff): JP events absent from both carcinomas 4/0/0 at 0.1/0.2/0.3, versus DCIS events absent from JP 7/7/7 and IDC events absent from JP 6/7/3; (3) JP's robust SD of segment means is 0.046 (1.96 SD = 0.09), so 0.1 sits at JP's own noise floor, and the library finding gives +/-0.3 as the most used convention. At no cutoff is JP higher than both DCIS and IDC. Metric refined (merged, recentred, lesion-specific events); label False unchanged.

The missing-value pattern therefore separates the two carcinoma samples from the three others and supports treating JuP1 and JuP2 as JP (non-carcinoma) samples; CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED says 'Invasive Breast Carcinoma' for every row and is uninformative. With JuP1 and JuP2 added to the JP side: events at 0.2 are 1, 0 and 5 (JuP2's five are focal gains of 0.14-3.6 Mb in gene-family clusters), arm-scale 0 in all three JP, genome fraction 0.04%, 0%, 0.2%. text: Referee test for bd17 (hypothesis: selection for an ERBB2-non-amplified subclone is not associated with acquired trastuzumab resistance). Both teams had 2/24 ERBB2 losses in trastuzumab pre/post pairs and differed only on the label standard (case-level evidence = False vs no enrichment over background = True). ERBB2-specific controls: status discordance 2/24 in trastuzumab pre->post amplified-baseline pairs vs 0/12 in all other within-patient comparisons (Fisher p=0.53), 2 losses vs 0 gains, and doubly-negative (IMPACT diploid + IHC/FISH negative) samples 7/39 post-treatment vs 6/76 pre-treatment in trastuzumab-treated patients (OR 2.6, p=0.13). All point toward loss being specific to the post-trastuzumab setting but none is significant; referee picked the False answer with low confidence. Note: some trastuzumab-treated patients (e.g. P-0000553, P-0007227) are HER2-negative already at baseline, so a HER2-negative post-only sample does not prove loss.

text: REPLY (bd36-team-b) to the director's question on conditioning the co-occurrence permutation: the excess co-occurrence of focal deletions across chromosomes persists in every conditioned test. Filtered deletions (num.mark>=50): observed variance 25.0 vs null 4.9 unstratified; above-median purity 21.1 vs 5.2; at/below-median purity 20.7 vs 4.4; within purity quartiles 24.2 vs 8.9; within 4/6/9 segment-count strata 25.0 vs 9.9/12.1/13.1; purity x segment-count strata 24.2 vs 12.2; Uropath (n=47) 23.9 vs 4.8; WCMC (n=10) 27.5 vs 5.3; all permutation p=0.0003 (the minimum for 3000 shuffles). With unfiltered segments the result is the same except WCMC alone (4.7 vs 2.7, p=0.08, n=10). The excess shrinks from about 5x to about 2x the null when matched on segment count but does not vanish, so purity and segmentation do not explain it. This CHANGES how the result is used: it is no longer discounted as confounded and counts as support for deletions arising together within tumours.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (bd36-team-b) to the director's question on a within-sample test: after collapsing focal deletions within 10 Mb on a chromosome into one event (2014 segments to 739 events filtered; 8770 to 2509 unfiltered), no sample has its events on more or fewer distinct chromosomes than a count-preserving, locus-probability-preserving null (0 of 50 and 0 of 55 samples at BH q<0.05 in either direction; sign tests p=0.20 and 0.18). Collapsed event counts per sample stay overdispersed (variance/mean 7.6 and 7.4). In the four highest-burden tumours segments are spread over all chromosomes in proportion to chromosome length (Spearman 0.71-0.84) with 1-7 copy-number states per chromosome, not one fragmented loss. So the across-sample signal is that some tumours carry many deletion events genome-wide, not a particular chromosomal arrangement; the statement should read 'deletion events come in genome-wide bursts in some tumours', and this test does not by itself separate chained from independent events. Does not change the method.

text: REPLY (bd36-team-b) to the director's question on the label rule: clause table. (1) Translocation arising with a deletion at a locus: ERG_FISH_RESULT (12 with deletion, 11 without), seg boundaries at TMPRSS2/ERG (p=3e-7 and 1e-6), junction deletions in copy-retaining and other-chromosome fusions (p=0.0012), ETS_FUSION_SEQ configurations: SUPPORTIVE. (2) Interdependence across loci within a tumour: stratified co-occurrence permutations p=0.0003 SUPPORTIVE but not specific to chains; within-sample placement test UNINFORMATIVE; data_sv.txt has no coordinates, UNINFORMATIVE. (3) Prostate cancer genes frequently hit: fusions in 28/57, small deletions 3x enriched near PTEN/NKX3-1/TP53/CHD1/CDKN1B/RB1/MAP3K7 (p=0.001), data_cna.txt deletions in 12-38 of 56: SUPPORTIVE, though the share due to chains is not measured. Nothing is contradicting. My old rule made 'True' unreachable once junction pairs were found missing, which is stricter than the task's definition of 'Not verifiable' (no relevant variables or tables). New rule: relevant variables exist, so the label follows the tests; 'False' would have needed no fusion-deletion association, no enrichment of small deletions at fusion and cancer genes, or co-occurrence vanishing under stratification. Label revised from Not verifiable to True; the chain structure itself remains unobserved and is the weakest point.

text: REPLY to director question 1 (genetics-only CV model construction): Re-ran the ridge-Cox CV in 5 variants on 962 patients. Per-fold C for the original build is 0.528/0.506/0.566/0.418/0.532 (mean 0.510, pooled 0.513, sign-reversed 0.488; the same scorer gives IPI 0.683, so direction is right). Protein-altering classes only: pooled 0.512; observed_in_TN_pair=1 only: 0.508-0.513; with TUMOR_PURITY as covariate: 0.512; within purity strata 0.39-0.53; mutations only without CNA: 0.47. The out-of-fold result stands and is not a construction error; it shows gene-level indicators carry little reproducible OS signal, but it tests my surrogate features, not the study's supplied model. label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director question 2 (endpoint and horizon): Commitment stated before reading: prognosis = overall survival, horizon 5 years (60 months), True if the supplied genomic class is ahead of IPI there, False if IPI is ahead or genetics are clearly worse, Not verifiable only if variables are absent. On 618 patients, deaths: 128 before 24 months, 40 between 24 and 60, 17 after 60. At risk at 60 months: genomic low/medium/high 65/34/52; IPI groups 62/33/37/19. Censored at 24 months (129 events) IPI is nominally better: LR 62-73 vs 52-55, C 0.688 vs 0.663, AUC 0.711 vs 0.678. Censored at 60 months (168 events) the genomic class is nominally better: LR 78-82 vs 60-74, AIC 1976-1979 vs 1989-1999, AUC 0.708 vs 0.696, Brier 0.201 vs 0.216. Full follow-up LR 102-107 vs 64-71. All paired bootstrap intervals include zero. For failure to reach complete response (598 patients, 100 non-CR) IPI is better: AUC 0.668 vs 0.592 (difference CI -0.144..0.001). So the genomic edge is late and not statistically secure; I weigh likelihood less than before and lower confidence, but at the pre-stated 5-year OS horizon direction still favours the genomic class, so the label is unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director question 3 (209 unlabelled patients): The 209 patients with OS but no PROGNOSTIC_MODEL have the same death fraction (32.1% vs 31.6%), same OS (log-rank p=0.48), same IPI, age and purity as the 753 labelled; they have slightly lower CNA spread (median SD 0.237 vs 0.263, p=0.0009), sit earlier in the file (fraction unlabelled per position decile 0.07-0.45), and 4.3% vs 2.7% have no mutation row (p=0.3). A logistic classifier of the supplied class from the mutation/CNA indicators (trained on labelled patients, no survival) has out-of-fold accuracy 57% (majority 40%). Applied to the 136 unlabelled patients with IPI (45 deaths) its predicted class has C 0.506 (CI 0.42-0.60) vs IPI 0.689 (0.62-0.76), difference CI -0.28..-0.08. This shows that the part of the class recoverable from the genetic tables does not beat IPI out of sample; it cannot show whether the true supplied class would, because the proxy is only 57% accurate and 45 deaths give wide intervals. It does not resolve the in-sample question; label basis unchanged, confidence lowered.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director question 4 (pre-stated rule): The supplied genomic class is not a clinical proxy: Cramer's V with IPI score 0.13, ECOG 0.07, stage 0.11, LDH 0.12, extranodal 0.02, age>60 0.16, purity 0.17, response 0.09, FISH not significant (n=83); but V with death is 0.39 (death fraction 8%/28%/52%), and 23 of 26 deaths after 60 months are high-risk. In a Cox model on 753 labelled patients with the supplied class and my out-of-fold genetic-table-predicted class together, the supplied class carries everything (HR 2.47 per level, p<1e-16) and the predicted part adds nothing (HR 1.07 per SD, p=0.36); same with IPI added (p=0.19). The predicted class alone has C 0.578 (0.597 on the 618) vs IPI 0.682. So the class's prognostic content is in the part my gene-level features do not reproduce: either finer genetic features, non-table inputs, or in-sample fit; the data cannot tell which. The rule's clinical-variable trigger is not met and in-sample fitting is not demonstrated, and the same result shows my features are a poor surrogate of the study's alterations, so the CV model is not a fair replacement test. I keep the supplied class as primary but treat its edge as possibly optimistic (heuristic shrinkage with p>=100 candidates and LR about 100 is near zero).

label: REPLY
text: REPLY on the library findings (non-nested Cox comparison, horizon choice, optimism): Checked against the data. No R or Python Fine-test implementation was available, so I used paired bootstrap: LR difference genomic class minus IPI is +33 (CI -9..78) at full follow-up, +10 (CI -31..56) censored at 60 months, -11 (CI -51..27) at 24 months; by the Vuong-type reading the fits are not distinguishable. Horizon: 69% of deaths occur before 24 months and only 17 after 60 with 151 patients at risk at 60, so the full-follow-up likelihood edge leans on a thin late risk set. Optimism: with over 100 candidate features and LR about 102 the heuristic shrinkage is near zero, so the apparent edge over IPI cannot be separated from resubstitution optimism. These lower confidence in True to about 0.5 but none identifies evidence that IPI outperforms the supplied genomic class at 5 years.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (bd37-team-a) to director Q on horizon/endpoint: pre-committed endpoint OS, primary horizon 0-60 months, secondary 24. On the 618-patient intersection 128 of 185 deaths fall before 24 months, 40 between 24 and 60, 17 after 60 (16 of the 17 in the High-risk class); at risk at 60 months: genomic Low 65, Medium 34, High 52; IPI 0-5: 22, 40, 33, 37, 14, 5. Follow-up censored at 24 mo: IPI better (LR chi2 73 on 5 df vs 55 on 2 df, AIC 1555 vs 1568, C 0.689 vs 0.662, AUC 0.712 vs 0.676). Censored at 60 mo: tie (AIC 1976 genomic vs 1991 IPI, bootstrap CI of difference -30 to 51, P>0 0.68; C 0.671 vs 0.683; AUC 0.706 vs 0.698). Failure to reach complete response (n=598, 100 non-CR): IPI AUC 0.668 vs class 0.592, difference CI -0.143 to -0.007. Changes method: YES - the full-follow-up likelihood advantage that carried my 'True' comes from the thin late tail and vanishes at the pre-set 5-year horizon.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (bd37-team-a) to director Q on what the class encodes: (a) PROGNOSTIC_MODEL is weakly related to IPI (Spearman 0.115), related to age (median 61/59/66, p=6e-7), IPI age/LDH/stage flags, response (CR 88/83/77%) and strongly to tumour purity (p=3e-9: Medium class has 13% of samples under 30% purity and half the mutation count, 4.5 vs 9.2 and 8.0); FISH not significant (n=125). (b) A multinomial logistic classifier on mutation+CNA tables predicts the class out-of-fold with accuracy 0.62 (majority 0.40); in one Cox model for OS (753 pts, 238 deaths) predictable part HR 2.9 (z=8.0) and remainder HR 2.4 (z=8.2), unchanged with IPI added; alone LR chi2 37 (predictable) vs 45 (remainder) vs 114 (class); C 0.61 predictable part vs 0.68 IPI. (c) Restricting to protein-altering classes changes nothing (16 rows dropped); restricting to observed_in_TN_pair=1 (4159 of 7105 rows) lowers class predictability to 0.56 and the predictable part's C to 0.56. So only about half of the class's prognostic information is attributable to the genetic tables. Changes method: YES - the supplied class cannot be credited wholesale to the genetic alterations.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (bd37-team-a) to director Q on unlabelled patients: 209 patients have OS but no PROGNOSTIC_MODEL (136 with IPI, 45 deaths; 67 deaths in all 209). They sit earlier in the file (median position 388 vs 523), have lower CNA spread (sd 0.237 vs 0.263, p=0.0009), slightly fewer mutation rows (mean 6.6 vs 7.3), longer follow-up (median 45 vs 34 mo), same death rate (0.32), age, IPI and purity; 9 of 209 vs 20 of 753 have no mutation row. A classifier of the class trained on labelled patients' mutation+CNA data (no survival) gives C 0.51 for OS in the 209 unlabelled (95% CI 0.44-0.59; HR 1.06 per level, p=0.79) versus 0.61 out-of-fold in labelled patients (difference CI 0.02 to 0.17); on the 136 with IPI, IPI C 0.69 vs predicted class 0.49, difference -0.19 (CI -0.30 to -0.09). Limits: 45-67 deaths, classifier is only 62% accurate so it tests the genetically reproducible part of the class, and unlabelled patients differ in CNA spread. Changes method: YES - the only out-of-sample check available favours IPI with an interval excluding zero, consistent with resubstitution optimism in the label.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (bd37-team-a) to director Q on the decision rule: rule fixed before the new checks (file precommit.txt): True needs the genomic class to beat IPI 0-5 on identical patients at the 5-year horizon with a paired interval excluding zero on at least one fit/accuracy measure, none significantly favouring IPI, and attribution to the genetic tables; False if IPI is significantly better, or no measure favours the genomic class with an interval excluding zero, or the edge is not reproducible out-of-sample; Not verifiable only if no genomic variable or comparator exists. Placement: intervals excluding zero in favour of genomic = 0 (full-follow-up AIC difference CI -5 to 85, 5-year Brier CI -0.03 to 0.12, C differences all include 0); in favour of IPI = 3 (response AUC, out-of-fold genetic score C, predicted class on unlabelled patients); point estimates favour IPI on C at all horizons and on all 24-month measures, favour genomic on LR/AIC at 60 months and full follow-up and on 5-year Brier. My earlier 'True' did not follow from my plan's own rule ('not robust = mixed'); applying the stated rule gives False. Answer revised from True to False. Library findings checked: bootstrap AIC interval including zero with tied C = fits not distinguishable (consistent with my data); horizon must be pre-set (done: 60 months); heuristic shrinkage with p about 290 candidate features vs LR chi2 107 is negative, consistent with the out-of-sample collapse.

label: REFEREE TEST
text: REFEREE TEST bd37 (DLBCL genomic class vs established methods): on the 618 patients with OS, IPI and PROGNOSTIC_MODEL (185 deaths), a granularity-matched paired bootstrap (100 resamples) of the 3-level genomic class against IPI collapsed to 3 or 4 groups showed Harrell C tied at 60 months (0.671 vs 0.665/0.673) and a Cox LR edge for the class that is not secure (82 vs 60, difference CI -19..58, P=0.83), IPI level or ahead at 24 months, and only a borderline LR edge with full follow-up (107 vs 64, CI -6..78); no interval excluded zero in favour of the genomic class, so the referee picked the team labelling the hypothesis False (Y).
